example_sentences.japanese: 子供がジュースを欲しがっています。
example_sentences.english: My kid wants some juice.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は私の親友です。
example_sentences.english: He is a close friend.

example_sentences.japanese: 風で桜の花が散ってるね。
example_sentences.english: Cherry blossoms are scattering in the wind.

example_sentences.japanese: 動物は本能のまま動くね。
example_sentences.english: Animals act purely on instinct.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は彼の要望に応じました。
example_sentences.english: I responded to his demand.

example_sentences.japanese: 目をつぶってください。
example_sentences.english: Close your eyes.

example_sentences.japanese: 風で髪が乱れたね。
example_sentences.english: The wind has messed up your hair.

example_sentences.japanese: 食べ過ぎたのでベルトを緩めたの。
example_sentences.english: I loosened my belt because I ate too much.

english: To Spill, To Drop, To Shed Tears
notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means zero, but the verb vocab version means to spill or to drop. Just imagine something that's spilling and dropping. Eventually it will reach zero." "Imagine a barrel of corn cobs, spilling and dropping out corn cobs, until they reach zero."

example_sentences.japanese: 「あんた、今カーペットに珈琲を零したでしょう？」「しまった!ごめん!」「ごめんで済んだら警察はいらないわよ！」
example_sentences.english: """Did you just spill coffee on the carpet?"" ""Oh no! Sorry."" ""If sorry fixed everything, we wouldn’t need the police!"""

example_sentences.japanese: ソファにワインをこぼした。
example_sentences.english: I spilt wine on the sofa.

example_sentences.japanese: 親に逆らうのは良くない事です。
example_sentences.english: It is not a good thing to disobey your parents.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は悪いことをしたので罰を受けたんだ。
example_sentences.english: He did something bad so he was punished.

example_sentences.japanese: ウサギが雪の上を跳ねていったよ。
example_sentences.english: The rabbit hopped through the snow.

example_sentences.japanese: 肉が焼けました。
example_sentences.english: The meat is cooked.

notes: "The thing you want to take has escaped. Meaning you failed to catch this thing. This word is to fail to catch." "The readings come from 取る and 逃がす."

example_sentences.japanese: 犯罪者を取り逃がすふりをするのは、ちょっとやり過ぎじゃない？
example_sentences.english: Don’t you think pretending that you failed to catch the criminal is a bit overkill?

example_sentences.japanese: 釣った魚を逃がしました。
example_sentences.english: I let go of the fish I had caught.

example_sentences.japanese: 支度ができたら出かけましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let's go out when we are ready.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供に昔話を聞かせてあげたの。
example_sentences.english: I read a story to the children.

example_sentences.japanese: お祖母ちゃんがお風呂場で転んだ。
example_sentences.english: My grandma fell down in the bathroom.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はパイロットの職に憧れているんだ。
example_sentences.english: His ambition is to become a pilot.

example_sentences.japanese: 人に乱暴してはいけません。
example_sentences.english: You must not use violence on people.

example_sentences.japanese: 父は今、留守です。
example_sentences.english: My father isn't at home now.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は両親から多くを教わりました。
example_sentences.english: I learned a lot from my parents.

example_sentences.japanese: 箱の角が潰れていますよ。
example_sentences.english: The corner of the box is squashed.

example_sentences.japanese: 妹は九月にアメリカの大学に入学します。
example_sentences.english: My little sister's entering college in the United States in September.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は人前で話すことが苦痛です。
example_sentences.english: It is painful for me to speak in front of other people.

example_sentences.japanese: ポスターの位置が少しずれているよ。
example_sentences.english: The poster is slightly out of position.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼を恨んではいけません。
example_sentences.english: You should not bear a grudge against him.

example_sentences.japanese: 恋する気持ちを歌にしました。
example_sentences.english: I expressed my feelings of love in my song.

example_sentences.japanese: 友人が慰めてくれました。
example_sentences.english: My friend consoled me.

example_sentences.japanese: クーラーで体が冷えた。
example_sentences.english: The air conditioner's given me the chills.

example_sentences.japanese: 犬が自分のしっぽを追いかけてぐるぐる回っている。
example_sentences.english: The dog ran round and round chasing its tail.

example_sentences.japanese: 水と油は混ざりません。
example_sentences.english: Water and oil don't mix.

example_sentences.japanese: 心配は無用です。
example_sentences.english: There's no need to worry.

example_sentences.japanese: 不必要なファイルは削除してください。
example_sentences.english: Please delete any unwanted files.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は時々意地悪な質問をする。
example_sentences.english: He sometimes raises nasty questions.

notes: "When a vocab word is a single kanji and alone, it tends to steal the meaning from the kanji. Same goes for this one too. It means above or up." "When a vocab word is a single kanji and doesn't have okurigana (hiragana attached to the kanji) it usually will use the kun'yomi. Since you learned the on'yomi reading of the kanji, we'll need to use a mnemonic to learn the reading of this vocabulary word. Above you is a huge weight. You're holding it up and struggling (it's heavy!). You look up and try to crane your neck to see how much it weighs (うえ), but you can't see the numbers on the side of it. How long can you hold it above your head like this?"

example_sentences.japanese: 上のひょうをみてください。
example_sentences.english: Please look at the chart above.

example_sentences.japanese: このフロアの三かい上にトーフグのオフィスがあります。
example_sentences.english: The Tofugu office is three floors up.

example_sentences.japanese: くつ下のかたほうは、かいだんの上にあったわよ。
example_sentences.english: One of your socks was at the top of the stairs.

notes: "As a vocab made up of a single kanji, you know that the meaning of this vocab word and the meaning of the kanji that makes it are the same: Again!" "The reading you learned for the kanji is the same as the reading for this word. You won't have to learn it ""again."""

example_sentences.japanese: 又してもおまえにやられてしまったぜ...とほほ！
example_sentences.english: You’ve deceived me again... boohoo!

example_sentences.japanese: わたしはアメリカ人です。又、わたしはフランス人でもあります。
example_sentences.english: I'm American. And also, I'm French.

example_sentences.japanese: 又来たぜ！
example_sentences.english: Here I am again!

notes: "Enter something with all your strength and you will look down to see that what you're doing is inputting data. You're inputting it right now! Into this site! The answers you enter into WaniKani with all your strength can be said with this word. Wow. Full circle already, and you're only on level 2. Look at you go!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: データの入力をおえました。
example_sentences.english: I finished inputting the data.

example_sentences.japanese: ここに王子のソーシャルセキュリティーナンバーを入力してください。
example_sentences.english: Please enter the prince's social security number here.

example_sentences.japanese: 「ローマじ入力」と「かな入力」、どちらをつかっていますか？
example_sentences.english: "Do you use ""romaji input"" or ""kana input""?"

notes: "This word is made up of a kanji with some hiragana attached, ending in an う sound. That means this word is a verb. The kanji itself means ""correct,"" so what is the verb form of that? It would be to correct." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: After you correct something for someone, you yell out ta da (ただ) very excitedly. Go ahead and imagine yourself doing this a few times to help you to remember."

example_sentences.japanese: しせいを正しなさい。
example_sentences.english: Sit up straight.

example_sentences.japanese: 王子はまちがいを正されてプライドがきずついた。
example_sentences.english: The prince's mistake was corrected and his pride was wounded.

example_sentences.japanese: あやまりを正すことができれば、ごほうびをあげるわ。
example_sentences.english: If you can correct my mistakes, I’ll give you a reward.

notes: "The 々 symbol just repeats the kanji that comes before it. You'll see it from time to time, so take note of it, even though it doesn't really have any meaning of its own. So, essentially 中々 is the same as 中中. That being said, you have something that's middle x2. When something is even more middle than middle itself, it is very or considerably something or another." "The reading for this word is the kun'yomi reading, since it's like putting two single kanji together rather than a true jukugo word. To learn the kun'yomi reading, take a look at this mnemonic: From the middle of the middle comes a sound. It is a knocking sound. Knock. Knock. Knock. You open up the walls around this thing. Then you open up the second set of walls (middle of the middle). Inside is an old man, who identifies himself as ""the knocker."" You go inside of him and find another knocker as well. That's why it's a knocker knocker (なかなか)."

example_sentences.japanese: 中々できません。
example_sentences.english: I really can’t do it.

example_sentences.japanese: あの王子も中々やりますね。
example_sentences.english: That prince is quite good, huh?

example_sentences.japanese: マリオカートをきわめることは中々かんたんではない。
example_sentences.english: It’s not very easy to make oneself a master of Mario Kart.

english: Very, Much, Greatly, A Lot Of, Very Much
notes: "When you do something with (に) big, you do it very, or with a lot of something." "You learned this reading when you learned 大きい. If you can remember that, you should be able to remember this one too!"

example_sentences.japanese: 大いにまなびましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let’s learn a lot!

example_sentences.japanese: 王は王子と王女に、「大いにこくみんのぜいきんをつかっていいぞ」といった。
example_sentences.english: "The king said to the prince and the princess, ""Go ahead and use a lot of money from the citizen's taxes."""

example_sentences.japanese: きょうは大いにのみたまえ。
example_sentences.english: Please drink a lot today.

notes: "This word is a single kanji with hiragana attached, though there is no specific clue as to what type of word it is. That means you can usually guess it's a noun, adverb or na-adjective (in this case it's a noun / adverb). The meaning of this word is pretty much the same as the kanji, though, making it fairly easy. The kanji meaning for 少 is few, and the meaning of the vocab form is a little or a few." "Did you know that this word created an English word you probably already know? Have you ever heard someone say ""just a skosh""? That's 少し! Hopefully you know this English word and therefore know this Japanese word as well."

example_sentences.japanese: ぎゅうにゅうは、少ししかありません。
example_sentences.english: There is only little milk.

example_sentences.japanese: 少ししかのこってないよ。
example_sentences.english: There are only a few left.

example_sentences.japanese: かれのプロポーズは少しあいまいだった。
example_sentences.english: His proposal was a little vague.

notes: "When something is in the middle of an action but it's stopped, this means it's put into suspension. Imagine getting frozen while you're running. It's kind of like that." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: やきゅうのしあいは、あめで中止になりました。
example_sentences.english: The baseball game was called off due to rain.

example_sentences.japanese: ざんねんですが、このきかくはいったん中止することになりました。
example_sentences.english: Sorry, but it was decided that this project will be canceled for now.

example_sentences.japanese: たのしみにしていた生ほうそうが中止になった。
example_sentences.english: The live show I had been looking forward to was canceled.

english: To Get Fat, To Gain Weight, To Grow Fat, To Become Fat
notes: "This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means fat so the verb form of that is to get fat." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You have to learn the ふと portion of this word to be able to read it. Here's a mnemonic to help you: You're getting fat so quickly that you can see your body expanding. You look down - at first you can see your foot (ふと) but then a second later you can't. You can't see your foot because you're getting fat, even when you stick your foot way out. What's going on?"

example_sentences.japanese: さいきん、たべすぎで少し太りました。
example_sentences.english: I’ve gotten a little fat from overeating lately.

example_sentences.japanese: たべても太らない人がうらやましい。
example_sentences.english: I envy people who don't get fat even though they eat a lot.

example_sentences.japanese: 太れば太るほど、わたしはおなかがすく。
example_sentences.english: The fatter I get, the hungrier I become.

english: First Of All, To Start With, Firstly, To Begin With
notes: "The kanji means previous. This is an adverb version of that word. It's a little thing you can begin sentences with. You can't start your sentences with ""previous"" but you can start it with ""First of all"" or ""to start with.""This is usually written without kanji though, so keep that in mind." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. In fact, the reading for this word is very rare, and kind of an exception. We'll use a mnemonic that uses both the kanji part and the hiragana attachment part. First of all and to start with, you have to make it through this maze (まず)."

example_sentences.japanese: 先ず、下ごしらえをします。
example_sentences.english: First, we do the prep work.

example_sentences.japanese: 先ず、その五十ねんかけてあつめた切手コレクションからだんしゃりしましょう。
example_sentences.english: Why don't you declutter the stamp collection you've been working on for fifty years first?

example_sentences.japanese: 先ずは、チキンの羽をむしりとって、それぞれの羽に名前をつけます。
example_sentences.english: First you need to pluck the chicken and then name each of the feathers.

english: In Its Entirety, Whole, Wholly, Entirely
notes: "If you go to (ごと) a circle, you need to go to it in its entirety. That means you have to circle around the whole thing. Otherwise, it isn't even a circle. It's like a line or a squiggle or something." Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You learned this reading, so you should be able to read this too!

example_sentences.japanese: わたしは、そのうたを丸ごとあんきしています。
example_sentences.english: I’m memorizing the whole song.

example_sentences.japanese: その牛、半分だけじゃなくて丸ごと一とう下さい。
example_sentences.english: Please give me the whole cow, not half.

example_sentences.japanese: このケーキには林檎が丸ごと入っています。
example_sentences.english: This cake is filled entirely with apples.

notes: "主 means main so when you add に it becomes the adverb mainly." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: You mainly spend your time talking to your master Moe. But you mainly address him like, ""Oh Moe The Great!"" (おも). That's because he's above you. Imagine yourself saying ""OH MOE THE GREAT!"" as you walk into his room, bowing low."

example_sentences.japanese: 主に日本ごをべんきょうしています。
example_sentences.english: I’m mainly studying Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: ポートランドでは、赤い車と白い車が主にうれています。
example_sentences.english: Primarily red and white cars are sold in Portland.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は研究者で、主にバナナに興味があります。
example_sentences.english: He is a researcher who is mainly interested in bananas.

english: One Breath, One Go, One Sitting
notes: "It's weird to think of having one energy. But, what gives you energy? You do it one time every couple of seconds. That would be taking breaths. So, ""one energy"" is one breath." "The reading is the same as the ones you learned with the individual kanji, though いち from 一 is shortened to いっ."

example_sentences.japanese: にがいくすりを一気にのみほしました。
example_sentences.english: I drank the bitter medicine down in one gulp.

example_sentences.japanese: 元気そうな父のかおを見たら、一気に気がぬけました。
example_sentences.english: It was such a relief to see my father, who looked well.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕のひいお婆さんは、ぎょう子を二百こ一気にたべた。
example_sentences.english: My great-grandma ate two hundred gyoza in one sitting.

notes:
"A stop that's just a rest (aka not permanent) isn't a straight up stop. You're planning on continuing again. That's why this is a pause." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

"When someone experiences a hurry death it's a very sudden death." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: わたしの大すきなバンドが、かつどうを休止しました。
example_sentences.english: My absolute favorite band is on hiatus.

example_sentences.japanese: パソコンのスリープと休止じょうたいのちがいをおしえてください。
example_sentences.english: Could you tell me the difference between sleep mode and hibernation mode on the computer, please?

example_sentences.japanese: しごとのと中で、小まめに小休止をとってエクササイズをするようにしています。
example_sentences.english: I'm trying to take little breaks and exercise frequently during work.

example_sentences.japanese: 父が急死した時、私は受けん生でした。
example_sentences.english: I was preparing to take my exams when my dad suddenly passed away.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日、上司が、のう出血のため急死しました。
example_sentences.english: My superior died suddenly of a cerebral hemorrhage yesterday.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼とはよく喧嘩になっちゃって、それが本当に嫌だったんだけど、今では喧嘩もできなくなっちゃってすっごく悲しいよ。まさか心臓発作で急死しちゃうなんて思ってもみなかったからさ。
example_sentences.english: I often argued with my boyfriend and I hated it, but I even miss the arguments now. I never expected that he would drop dead from a heart attack.

english: Shortage, Physical Shortage, Insufficient, Not Sufficient, Not Enough
notes: "You have something that's not sufficient. When something isn't sufficient, you have a shortage. Keep in mind that this is a physical shortage, not a shortage of mental ability or something like that. To remember this, just think about how 足 also means ""foot."" What is a foot? Something physical. That's why this is a physical shortage." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: おつりが不足しています。
example_sentences.english: I don’t have enough change.

example_sentences.japanese: しきん不足で中央せいふのきかくしたプロジェクトが中止になった。
example_sentences.english: Due to the lack of funds, the project that the central government planned was suspended.

example_sentences.japanese: 経験が不足しているうえにいつも寝不足なので、あなたは首です。
example_sentences.english: You are fired because you lack experience and are always sleep deprived.

notes: "A substitute task is a substitution." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: サワークリームをヨーグルトで代用しました。
example_sentences.english: I substituted yogurt for sour cream.

example_sentences.japanese: きもののこしひもは、ストッキングでも代用かのうです。
example_sentences.english: You can use stockings as a substitute for the cord you wear under your kimono.

example_sentences.japanese: 糊がないので飯粒で代用した。
example_sentences.english: We didn’t have glue so we substituted grains of boiled rice for it.

english: Viewing Cherry Blossoms, Sakura Viewing, Cherry Blossom Viewing
notes: "When you have flowers that you see you are viewing flowers. But not just any flowers. What flowers do Japanese people love viewing? That's right, this word refers to viewing cherry blossoms." The reading for this vocab is all kun'yomi, but you learned the kun'yomi readings of both these when you learned their kanji. So no worries there. You can spend the extra time viewing the cherry blossoms.

example_sentences.japanese: ことしは花見にいかなかった。
example_sentences.english: I didn’t go sakura viewing this year.

example_sentences.japanese: 北りくち方の花見の名しょをごしょうかいします。
example_sentences.english: I'm gonna introduce you to the best cherry blossom viewing spots in Hokuriku region.

example_sentences.japanese: 死ぬ前にもう一度花見をしながら宴会がしたいなあ。
example_sentences.english: Before I die, I want to have a drinking party under the cherry blossoms one more time.

english: Year Round, All Year, Whole Year, Throughout The Year, All Year Round
notes: "The year middle sounds like it should be something like ""the middle of the year,"" but it's not. Think of something that happens in the middle of the year and then all other parts of the year. It's just referring to everything within this year, which is how we get year round." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. 中 does have a strange reading, though, which is じゅう. This is basically just ちゅう changing to ぢゅう, but since nobody uses ぢ it just switches to じ and you end up with じゅう. That's called rendaku."

example_sentences.japanese: この町のそらは、年中どんよりしています。
example_sentences.english: The sky in this town is dull all year.

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグのしゃいんは、二十四じかん年中むきゅうではたらいている。
example_sentences.english: Tofugu employees work twenty four seven, year round.

example_sentences.japanese: この国では一年中雨が降るんだが、妻もまた年中その文句を言うんだ。
example_sentences.english: It rains year round in this country and my wife complains about it year round as well.

english: Absent From School, Absence From School, School Absence, Leave Of Absence
notes: "When you rest from school you are absent from school. This is only for very long absences though, not a day or a week, but months or years. Think about it like taking an extended leave of absence from school." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 大学を一年かん休学していたんです。
example_sentences.english: I’m taking a one year leave of absence from university.

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトは大学のとき、学こうを一年かん休学してじ分さがしのたびに出た。
example_sentences.english: When Viet was a college student, he took a year of leave from school and went on a journey of self discovery.

example_sentences.japanese: 「どうしてケリーが三週間も休学しているか知ってる？」「知ってるよ。ケリーは結膜炎がひどいらしいよ。」
example_sentences.english: """Do you know why Kelly has been absent from school for the past three weeks?"" ""Yes, apparently she has a really serious case of pink eye."""

notes: "When you make a task you're looking for a certain action and/or effect. What task can you make right now to get the effect of learning more kanji?" "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. Remember when you learned the kanji for 作 and we said you'll see some that take just さ instead of the whole さく? This is one of those!"

example_sentences.japanese: アルコールの作用をおしえてください。
example_sentences.english: Teach me about the effects of alcohol.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日、学こうで、作用・はん作用のほうそくを学んだ。
example_sentences.english: I learned Newton's third law of motion at school today.

example_sentences.japanese: このケーキの味がする薬には、副作用はありませんか？
example_sentences.english: Does this cake-flavored medicine have any side effects?

notes: "If you come to the party wearing something really, really old, everyone will know you're from ancient times (as if your wrinkles didn't give it away already, right?)." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: カッパは、日本古来のようかいです。
example_sentences.english: The kappa is an ancient Japanese yokai.

example_sentences.japanese: 古来、この池は、「ワニカニの池」という名まえでしられていました。
example_sentences.english: "In ancient times, this pond was known as ""WaniKani Pond."""

example_sentences.japanese: トイレは、古来から現代へと受け継がれてきた素晴らしい発明品だ。
example_sentences.english: The toilet is a wonderful invention that has been handed down since ancient times to the present-day.

notes: "When you make writing, what are you doing? Simply put, you're writing. If you want to be fancier about it, you could say this is composition." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: この作文を、中川先生にわたしてください。
example_sentences.english: Please hand this essay in to professor Nakagawa.

example_sentences.japanese: 作文のテストで百てんをもらいました。
example_sentences.english: I got 100 percent on the essay exam.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕の作文は、まだ間違いだらけです。
example_sentences.english: My essays are still full of mistakes.

notes:
"What is the ""industry of make""? Well, it's an industry where you make things, obviously. That can only be construction!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

"Plow the earth to make it ready for cultivation and farming." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

"You confused all of the ingredients to your cake by mixing them together into one weird mixture." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 工作はとくいではありません。
example_sentences.english: Construction is not my strong point.

example_sentences.japanese: アリバイ工作にしっぱいした。
example_sentences.english: I failed to set up a reasonable alibi.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は小学生の頃、夏休みの自由工作の宿題で、アイスクリームを作る機械を作った。
example_sentences.english: When I was in elementary school, I made a machine that makes ice cream for my school crafting project over summer break.

example_sentences.japanese: この土地を耕作するには許可がいります。
example_sentences.english: You need approval in order to cultivate this plot of land.

example_sentences.japanese: 色々な感情が交錯し、結論を出せずにいました。
example_sentences.english: Various emotions were mixed and we weren’t able to reach a conclusion.

notes: "You are able to stand using your self. Nobody is helping you. Nobody is holding you down. This is your independence!." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: むすこもようやく自立しはじめました。
example_sentences.english: My son is finally starting to be self reliant.

example_sentences.japanese: 自立しんけいしっちょうしょうがなおったら、自立しようとおもっています。
example_sentences.english: I'm thinking of being on my own, if I recover from autonomic dysfunction.

example_sentences.japanese: もしあなたが強くで自立した日本人女性で、男なんて必要ないというなら、これをシェアしてください。
example_sentences.english: Share this if you are a strong, independent Japanese woman who doesn’t need a man.

english: Joining A Company, Entering A Company
notes: "When you enter a company you're actually joining a company. Welcome, new recruit. Prepare to be hazed!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: この会社には、四月に入社しました。
example_sentences.english: I joined this company in April.

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグの入社しけんはグーグルの入社しけんよりもむずかしい。
example_sentences.english: Tofugu's employment exam is more difficult than Google's.

example_sentences.japanese: 大学を卒業したらすぐに、大きな金融機関に入社するか、アメリカ合衆国の大統領になれたらいいなと思っている。
example_sentences.english: As soon as I graduate from college, I hope to either join a big financial firm or be the president of the United States.

notes: "You have many parts. Look at them all. You have to choose one of the parts. You can't decide which one you want. This one? Maybe. How about this one? Hmm, maybe that one too." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: かさは、多分外にあります。
example_sentences.english: Maybe the umbrella is outside.

example_sentences.japanese: 多分、レイヤーさんなのかもしれないよ。
example_sentences.english: Perhaps, she is a cosplayer.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日の夜は多分雪になるから、雪だるまを作ろう。
example_sentences.english: It’s probably going to snow tomorrow, so let’s make a snowman.

notes:
"This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means mix so the verb version is to mix. There are similar words to this one, including 交じる which means ""to be mixed"" and 交わる which means ""to intersect."" This one is when you're doing the mixing. Like 交じる, the connotation is that the things being mixed are distinguishable from each other, like two types of fish, or books being mixed together. They don't become homogenous like paint or something would." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: You have to remember the ま portion. Who would mix things for you (like cakes and other goodies) growing up? That would be your Ma (ま)."

"This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means mix so the verb vocab version is to mix. This is when you're doing the mixing. You can remember this because ""there (ぜる) is much mixing to be done so it's best if you just do it because nobody else will.""The connotation for this word is you can't distinguish the things you're mixing, like combining paints, which become one mixed color that isn't two separate colors anymore." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: You're doing mixing like your ma (ま) taught you, which is why when you do the mixing things get done around here a lot faster.You can also use the level 5 vocab 交ぜる to help you remember as it has the same meaning and reading!"

example_sentences.japanese: トランプをよく交ぜてください。
example_sentences.english: Mix the cards up well, please.

example_sentences.japanese: どうしてたくさんの男たちの中に女を一人交ぜたんだ？
example_sentences.english: Why did you mix one woman into group with a bunch of men?

example_sentences.japanese: 豆腐と河豚を交ぜるのは危険です。
example_sentences.english: It’s dangerous to mix tofu and puffer fish.

example_sentences.japanese: 混ぜるな危険！
example_sentences.english: Don't mix it. It's dangerous!

example_sentences.japanese: トンカツソースとマヨネーズを混ぜたら最強に美味しいよ！
example_sentences.english: It's incredibly tasty when you mix tonkatsu sauce with mayonnaise.

example_sentences.japanese: ねぇ、気をつけた方がいいよ。あの男がさっきあんたの飲み物に何か混ぜてたのを見たよ。
example_sentences.english: Hey, you should watch out, I saw that guy mix something into your drink.

notes: "A vehicle that runs goes is running and it's moving you somewhere else. You're traveling!We usually use this word to describe moving or running vehicles like cars and trains. Keep an eye on those context sentences to make sure you're using it right. ;)" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたの車の走行マイルをおしえてください。
example_sentences.english: Can you tell me the mileage of your car?

example_sentences.japanese: バスの走行中にせきを立つのはきけんです。
example_sentences.english: Leaving your seat while the bus is moving is dangerous.

example_sentences.japanese: その電車は、ストライキが終わり次第、ホグワーツ魔法魔術学校への走行を再開する。
example_sentences.english: The train will start running to Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry again as soon as the strike is over.

english: Until Now, Up To Now, So Far
notes: "You know that 今 means now. What you probably don't know is that まで means ""until."" So, this word means until now." "The reading for this word is the kun'yomi reading which you learned previously when you learned the vocab word 今. You can tell this is a kun'yomi reading because it has hiragana attached. So if you know that, you should be able to read this word as well."

example_sentences.japanese: 今まで何をしていたんですか。
example_sentences.english: What have you been doing until now?

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチが今まで付きあったかの女は百万人に上るが、ようやく一人の女の人におちつきつつある。
example_sentences.english: Koichi had a million girlfriends up until now, but he is finally about to settle down with one woman.

example_sentences.japanese: お前が今までの中では一番の彼女だよ。
example_sentences.english: You are the best girlfriend I’ve had so far.

notes: "This is the kanji color repeated twice (the 々 character just repeats the kanji before it). When you have colors and colors and colors, you have a lot of variety. That's why this word means various." The reading for this kanji is just the kun'yomi reading twice. Since you've learned the kun'yomi reading already, you should be able to read this word as well. Nothing tricky about it.

example_sentences.japanese: 色々な小せつをよみました。
example_sentences.english: I’ve read various types of novels.

example_sentences.japanese: 色々考えたけっか、日よう日にたこやきパーティーをすることにしました。
example_sentences.english: After thinking about various things, I've decided to hold a takoyaki party on Sunday.

example_sentences.japanese: 私のベッドの下に住んでいるトロールには色々な種類がいます。
example_sentences.english: There are various species of trolls that live under my bed.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: After. Everything happens after. It's a cause and effect chain. One thing happens, and then another thing happens after. This is life. This is the universe. Everything is after. It's an automatic (あと) cycle that just keeps going and going and going. You can differentiate this one from 後ろ because it has a で on the end. ""Day"" (で) follows night which follows ""day"" again, automatically."

example_sentences.japanese: 後でいっしょにお茶でもしませんか。
example_sentences.english: Why don’t we have some tea together later?

example_sentences.japanese: 後で、「言わんこっちゃない」って言わせないでよ。
example_sentences.english: "Don't make me say, ""I told you so,"" later."

example_sentences.japanese: その映画を見終わった後で、もう一度それを見るために違う映画館へ向かった。
example_sentences.english: After the movie, we headed across town to watch it again in another theater.

notes: "When the thing that is exiting is blood, you are probably bleeding." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Note that the しゅつ from 出 gets shortened to しゅっ. That's a small つ there, not a big one."

example_sentences.japanese: なかなか出血が止まりません。
example_sentences.english: The bleeding won’t stop.

example_sentences.japanese: Tofuguはぜっさん出血大サービス中です。
example_sentences.english: Tofugu is providing you with a huge discount!

example_sentences.japanese: 指を抜いていれば、鼻からの出血は止まると思います。
example_sentences.english: I think my nose would stop bleeding if I kept my finger out of it.

notes: "What do you use to show that a word is lively? Conjugation! Lively things are happening, so you have to conjugate your words to match. It also has another meaning. When you want to actually use something lively you are making practical use of it. I mean, you're using it, after all. So as long as you aren't pretending to use it, it's probably practical." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は、どうしの活用をべんきょうします。
example_sentences.english: Today we will learn verb conjugation.

example_sentences.japanese: ちょこっとあいたじかんを活用して、ワニカニで日本ごをべんきょうします。
example_sentences.english: I make use of small pockets of time and study Japanese on WaniKani.

example_sentences.japanese: このデータをうまく活用して、何かできないかな。
example_sentences.english: I don’t know if I can put this data to good use.

notes:
"If you think about direct going (aka transportation) how would you make it better? You'd make it so everything was nonstop and direct. Just imagine how much nicer it would be if every airplane you took was direct and you never had to stop. So nice!" "This is a jukugo word and uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. The ちょく of 直 is shortened with a small っ, though, so make sure to take note of that."

"Remember how 直行 is ""nonstop""? Well, with 直航 it's the same thing, but more like with flying things, making this a nonstop flight." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: このひ行きは、東京に直行します。
example_sentences.english: This airplane is nonstop to Tokyo.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は、日本との会ぎの後、トーフグとのアポに直行します。
example_sentences.english: Today after the meeting with Japan, I'll go directly to the appointment with Tofugu.

example_sentences.japanese: ごめんなさい、今は話せません。トイレへ直行しているところなのです。
example_sentences.english: I’m sorry, I can't talk right now. I’m on a nonstop trip to the bathroom.

example_sentences.japanese: この船は神戸港に直航します。
example_sentences.english: This ship is on a direct voyage to Kobe Port.

notes: "When your heart is relaxed, how do you feel? What if this is after something startling happens? You would feel relief or peace of mind." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: これで安心です。
example_sentences.english: That’s a relief.

example_sentences.japanese: あの子は次の行どうがよそくできないから、安心できないのよね。
example_sentences.english: I never know what that kid will do next, so I can't get peace of mind.

example_sentences.japanese: お父さんの癌が無くなったことを聞いて、とても安心した。
example_sentences.english: I feel so relieved now that I know my dad no longer has cancer.

notes: "Remember 足りる? That is ""to be enough."" How can you make something be enough? You keep adding things to the pile until you reach that point where there are enough! That's why this verb is to add, because you keep adding until you 足りる. Maybe you add so much that someone tries to sue (す) you for that nasty pile of squirrels you keep outside." "The reading is the same as 足りる, so if you know that you can add things up to this."

example_sentences.japanese: 三足す二は五です。
example_sentences.english: Three plus two is five.

example_sentences.japanese: このスープ、もう少し水を足した方がいいんじゃないかな。
example_sentences.english: Maybe it would be better to add more water to this soup.

example_sentences.japanese: ここにもう少し文章を書き足すことはできますか？
example_sentences.english: Can you add a little more to this sentence here?

english: "Whisper In Ear, Whisper In One's Ear, Whisper In Someone's Ear"
notes: "A hit to someone's ear... you'd think that would be like yelling into their ear, but it's not. Think of it like you're hitting your mouth to their ear so that it's nice and close so you can whisper in ear." This word uses the kun'yomi readings for both kanji, but you know them both now, so you should be able to read this too!

example_sentences.japanese: かれは、わたしにこっそり耳打ちしました。
example_sentences.english: He secretly whispered in my ear.

example_sentences.japanese: ミーティングのときに、コウイチがニッカになにか耳打ちしてるのをみてしまった。
example_sentences.english: I happened to witness Koichi whispering something in Nikka's ear during the meeting.

example_sentences.japanese: 私が彼に、何かセクシーな言葉を耳打ちしてというと、彼は「テープやCDは好きかい？」と囁いてくれた。
example_sentences.english: "I told him to whisper something sexy in my ear and he said, ""Do you like tapes and CDs?"""

english: Anticipation, Anticipate, Going Ahead, Arriving Ahead
notes: "If you know of something that happens previous to something rotating (回り), you will then be in anticipation of its actions and rotations based on previous knowledge." "This consists of a couple kun'yomi readings put together. You can tell it's kun'yomi because of the hiragana sticking out at the end. In the previous level you learned both the words 先 and 回る (verb version of 回り). If you know those, you should be able to put them together to learn the reading of this word as well."

example_sentences.japanese: 先回りして、まちぶせしよう！
example_sentences.english: Let’s go ahead and ambush them!

example_sentences.japanese: リクはとてもせっかちで、いつも人の話をかっ手によそうして先回りして話すから、すごくイライラするんだよね。
example_sentences.english: Riku is very impatient, and always tries to guess what I'm going to say before I've said it, and it's been really annoying me.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は先回りをして富士山の頂上に着いており、私のことをのろまと笑った。
example_sentences.english: He beat me to the top of Mt. Fuji and then laughed at me for being slow.

notes: "This is the adverb version of 未, meaning it means the same thing: not yet." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: Someone's telling you ""not yet... not yet.... not yet..."" you have some food on your nose, but you're not allowed to eat it until your ma says it's okay. ""Not yet... Not yet..."" Why would your mom treat you like a dog like this? Oh well... maybe she'll let you eat the food soon, at least."

example_sentences.japanese: 未だ二百才まで生きた人げんはいない。
example_sentences.english: There’s still never been a person who’s lived to two hundred years old.

example_sentences.japanese: 未だ、時さボケがあるんですよね。
example_sentences.english: I’m still jet-lagged.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事が決まったのかどうかは未だ分からないんだ。向こうは未だ、十二人も面接しなきゃいけないみたい。
example_sentences.english: I’m not sure if I got the job yet. It seems like they still have to interview twelve other applicants.

notes: "本当 is reality or truth (level 5 vocab). If you go towards truth and reality, you are saying that it is really and truly true. 本当に! It is!" "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. It shares the reading with the level 5 本当 as well, but just has a particle on the end to show you're going towards reality. Really!"

example_sentences.japanese: 日本の人たちは、本当にやさしいです。
example_sentences.english: Japanese people are really kind.

example_sentences.japanese: このせいひん、本当に高くなっちゃったねー。
example_sentences.english: This product has gotten truly expensive.

example_sentences.japanese: 本当にこの道であっていますか？
example_sentences.english: Is this really the way?

notes: "When you do something that's your fault and then you say ""thanks"" after you do it, that's super-duper rude, wouldn't you say? Imagine doing something like this and then thinking to yourself after... wow, I was really rude." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 失礼ですが、日本ごははなせますか。
example_sentences.english: Excuse me, but can you speak Japanese?

example_sentences.japanese: じっさいの会話で「あなた」という言ばを使うと、失礼にきこえることが多いです。
example_sentences.english: "If you use ""anata"" in an actual conversation, it often sounds impolite."

example_sentences.japanese: もし私があなたに太いと言えば、失礼だと思いますか？
example_sentences.english: Would you think I’m rude if I told you that you’re fat?

english: Surely, Certainly, Without Exception, Always, Definitely
notes: "This word looks like a verb but it's not (sorry!). It's an adverb. The kanji itself means certain and the vocab version means all sorts of variations on that: surely, certainly, and without exception to name a few." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: Ra, the Egyptian god asks you: ""Can you do it? Are you certain you can build the pyramids?"" ""Yes I can ra (かなら). Yes I can,"" you reply."

example_sentences.japanese: かれは必ずもどってくるので、大じょうぶです。
example_sentences.english: He’ll definitely come back, so I’m okay.

example_sentences.japanese: 必ずねる前にコンタクトを外した方がいいよ。でないとし力がさらにおちるよ。
example_sentences.english: You should always take out your contacts before going to bed. Otherwise your eyesight will get worse.

example_sentences.japanese: 何があっても必ずさい後までワニカニをやりとげます。
example_sentences.english: I will certainly complete WaniKani no matter what.

english: The Heck, In The World, On Earth
notes: "Okay, so this one is really weird, sorry. Each of us only get one body in our lifetimes, right? Well what the heck! What if I want more than one body. Let's all be mad about this together. " "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. Just watch out because いち is shortened to いっ here!"

example_sentences.japanese: 一体どうなっているんだ。
example_sentences.english: What the heck is going on?

example_sentences.japanese: 「あいとにくしみはひょうり一体」って、一体全体どういういみなんだ！？
example_sentences.english: "What the heck does, ""There's a thin line between love and hate,"" mean?"

example_sentences.japanese: 一体俺が何をしたって言うんだよ？
example_sentences.english: What the heck did you say I did?

notes: "When things get all mixed up while trying  to pass through each other it becomes a mess. This can be people, cars, bikes, what have you. Anything that has to move around and pass through each other. When this happens things slow down and you get traffic." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ここでは、交通じこがよくおきるんです。
example_sentences.english: Traffic accidents happen a lot here.

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグのオフィスが入ったビルの前の通りは交通がはげしい。
example_sentences.english: There's heavy traffic on the street in front of the building the Tofugu office is in.

example_sentences.japanese: もし俺の車にヘリコプターのプロペラがあれば、空を飛んで交通渋滞を回避することができるのになぁ。
example_sentences.english: I wish my car had helicopter blades so I could fly over this traffic jam.

notes: "You enter a place. So, you have been given (or forced) admission into this place. You have been given entrance. For example, ""admission"" into a prison is something you could gain by not doing your WaniKani reviews in certain Crabigator ruled countries." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: わたしの母は、来年のはるから、かいごしせつに入所することになりました。
example_sentences.english: My mother will be admitted to a nursing home next spring.

example_sentences.japanese: こちらに入所年月日を記入してください。
example_sentences.english: Please write down your admission date here.

example_sentences.japanese: 俺の兄貴は今入所中だ。
example_sentences.english: My yakuza boss is in jail now.

notes: "When you say things that help you are giving advice, though not everyone will think it's good." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたの助言、ぜんぜん役に立たなかったんだけど。
example_sentences.english: But your advice wasn’t helpful at all.

example_sentences.japanese: かの女の助言にしたがって、コウイチはついにタバコをやめたんだよ。
example_sentences.english: In keeping with his girlfriend's advice, Koichi finally quit smoking.

example_sentences.japanese: そのチョコレートをくれたら、助言をあげるわ。
example_sentences.english: I will give you advice, if you give me that chocolate.

notes: "When you have the power to help someone, you are giving them assistance and support." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: そのせつは、ご助力をたまわりかんしゃ申し上げます。
example_sentences.english: Thank you for your assistance at this time.

example_sentences.japanese: YouTubeのどうがさい生カウントをのばすため、コウイチは助力をもとめてタランティーノに電話をかけた。
example_sentences.english: Koichi made a phone call to Quentin Tarantino seeking help to increase his YouTube view counts.

example_sentences.japanese: スパイダーマンの助力を求める必要はない。
example_sentences.english: You don’t need to request Spider-Man’s assistance.

notes: "When you stand up versus someone, you're looking to get into a confrontation. Just imagine yourself doing this to someone bigger than you. You stand up to versus them and then realize this confrontation is a bad idea." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: あととりあらそいで、兄と弟は対立してしまったんです。
example_sentences.english: The older and younger brothers are in opposition over the succession dispute.

example_sentences.japanese: 対立するんじゃなく、一しょにきょう力してがんばろうよ！
example_sentences.english: Why don't we cooperate and work hard together instead of competing?

example_sentences.japanese: もう一回俺のことを対立を避けるような人間だと言ってみろ！お前の顔面をぶん殴ってやる。
example_sentences.english: I’ll punch you in the face if you say I’m a non-confrontational person one more time.

notes: "When you meet your talk with someone else, you're having a conversation." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 男の人と女の人が、大学のろう下で会話をしています。
example_sentences.english: A man and a woman are having a conversation in the hallway of the university.

example_sentences.japanese: ペースのはやい日本ごの会話は、まだりかい出来ません。
example_sentences.english: I can't understand fast-paced Japanese dialogue yet.

example_sentences.japanese: どうして私達の会話はいつも野球についてなのでしょうか？
example_sentences.english: Why are our conversations always about baseball?

notes: "When you decide with your heart you have true determination, unlike when you decide with your mind." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Just make sure you take note of the shortened つ. So, けつ goes to けっ."

example_sentences.japanese: あなたのおかげで、せい形手じゅつをする決心がつきました。
example_sentences.english: Thanks to you, I’ve decided to get plastic surgery.

example_sentences.japanese: インスタセレブになるというトーフグの決心はトウフと同じぐらいかたい。
example_sentences.english: Tofugu's resolution to being an Instagram celebrity is as firm as Tofu.

example_sentences.japanese: ついに、あなたに、どこから私の誕生日プレゼントの酒を買ってきてもらうか決心したよ。それは…日本だ。楽しんできてね！
example_sentences.english: I’ve finally made up my mind about where you’ll be buying me drinks for my birthday... In Japan. Enjoy!

notes: "The location from which you enter is where you make your entrance. It has to do with things like ""entrance fees"" and ""entrance was not permitted,"" etc." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 会場に入場するには、チケットが必ようです。
example_sentences.english: You need a ticket to enter the venue.

example_sentences.japanese: さいしゅう入場時かんは午後五時です。
example_sentences.english: Last admission is at 5 pm.

example_sentences.japanese: ちくしょう！「確実な死への部屋」への入場門が塞がれている。
example_sentences.english: "Damn it! The entrance to the ""Room of Certain Death"" is blocked."

notes: "When you brighten your research it's like you're shedding light on it. To do that, you have to perform an investigation. This word is particularly used in academic and scientific situations." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: お前は本当にしんそうを究明するつもりがあるのか？
example_sentences.english: Are you really going to investigate the truth?

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチのおかしな言どうのしんのどうきはまだ究明されていない。
example_sentences.english: The true motive behind Koichi's strange words and deeds have not yet been brought to light.

example_sentences.japanese: 私が大学で取っている授業の一つで、現在「鳥が先か卵が先か」について究明しているんです。
example_sentences.english: One of the classes I’m taking in college is currently investigating whether the chicken or the egg came first.

english: Notice, Notification, Flier, Pamphlet, Handbill, Flyer, Leaflet
notes: "This is a strange word, so you'll have to bear with me. You know that 知 means know. But in the case of this word, what do you know? Look at the second half. らせ sounds a bit like ""race."" So, you know about a ""race."" How do you know about this race? You got a notice or notification about it." "Remember 知る? This is the same reading (し). So, if you know that, you'll be able to read this one as well."

example_sentences.japanese: あのう、お知らせしたいことがあるんですが、今、いいですか？
example_sentences.english: Excuse me, I have something that I’d like to tell you - do you have some time now?

example_sentences.japanese: 学校からのお知らせはもうよみましたか？
example_sentences.english: Did you read the notice from the school already?

example_sentences.japanese: 残念なお知らせがあります。昨夜誰かがこの家に侵入し、冷凍庫に入っていたアイスクリームを全部盗んでしまいました。
example_sentences.english: I have some bad news. Someone broke into our home last night and stole all the ice cream we had stored in our freezer.

english: One By One, In Succession, One After The Other
notes: "When something is happening next, next (next next next), it's happening in succession, or one by one. Just imagine a line of people going through to get stamps on their heads. The person at the stamp counter is saying ""Next! Next!"" and then shouting ""C'mon people, one by one, alright?""" "The reading is the same as the word 次 (so it's つぎ), but this time you do it twice. No strange rendaku or anything like that either, which makes everyone happier."

example_sentences.japanese: しんじられないような出来ごとが次々とおこったんです。
example_sentences.english: Seemingly unbelievable events were occurring one after the other.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチかんとくは、さく夜、Youtubeで次々とヒット作を生み出すゆめを見ました。
example_sentences.english: Last night, Director Koichi had a dream that he made one Youtube hit after another.

example_sentences.japanese: ヨーロッパの街は、次々と疫病に侵されていった。
example_sentences.english: One by one, the cities of Europe fell to the plague.

notes: "The anti versus... You'd think this would be a double negative, but it's like a lot of other words where you have two similar words combined... it just means the same thing as those two words. In this case, the anti-versus of something would be the opposite. Alternatively, it can be the opposition. You choose." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: その考えには反対です。
example_sentences.english: I’m opposed to the idea.

example_sentences.japanese: 不自由の男神は、アッパーわんをはさんで、自由の女神の反対がわに立っています。
example_sentences.english: The Statue of Restriction is standing on the opposite side of the Statue of Liberty in middle of the Upper Bay.

example_sentences.japanese: チェンジビルに引っ越してからというもの、あいつは昔のあいつとは正反対の人間になっちまったんだ。
example_sentences.english: He’s the complete opposite of what he used to be like ever since he moved to Changeville.

hiragana: しゅっしょ, でどころ
notes: You exit a place. It's a release from prison for you!Note: this word can also mean source or origin, often found in copyright law documents (for all you lawyers out there). "The reading follows on'yomi protocols, but you just have to be careful of the shortened しゅつ which becomes しゅっ.Note: There is also the reading でどころ which is used with the meanings origin and source. It's usually written as 出どころ when used in this way."

example_sentences.japanese: ジェニーの出所はいつですか？
example_sentences.english: When will Jenny be released from prison?

example_sentences.japanese: 出所したら、ちゃんとかしをかえしてくれよな。
example_sentences.english: When you get out of the prison, please return the favor, okay?

example_sentences.japanese: 引用部分の出所を明示してください。
example_sentences.english: Please present the source of the quoted section.

notes: "When you decide with your self, that is your own decision. That comes from you. That comes from your self determination. But the word is mainly used in Japan as a euphemism for suicide. It's kind of important that you know that." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: あのさむらいは自決した。
example_sentences.english: That samurai committed suicide.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチ社長は、トーフグは自決けんを強く心からしじするということを、何どもくりかえした。
example_sentences.english: President Koichi reiterated Tofugu's strong and wholehearted support for our right to self-determination.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は、獄中で絶望し、自決してしまったんです。
example_sentences.english: He was depressed during his imprisonment and committed suicide.

notes: "An electricity talk. What is this witchcraft? The only way to talk via electricity is with a telephone." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 電話で家ぞくと話しています。
example_sentences.english: I’m talking on the phone with my family.

example_sentences.japanese: 夜おそくに電話してごめんね。
example_sentences.english: Sorry to call you so late at night.

example_sentences.japanese: アレクサンダー・グラハム・ベルが自分の電話の着信音を何にしていたのかが気になります。
example_sentences.english: I wonder what ringtone Alexander Graham Bell had on his telephone.

english: To Be Bent, To Bend, To Curve, To Turn
notes: "This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means both music and bend. In the case of this word, we're looking at ""bend."" So, the verb form of bend is to be bent. This is when something bends on its own, not when you're doing the bending. It's just bending." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: Something, let's say a road, starts out straight. But, with some magic, a witch causes it to curve."

example_sentences.japanese: 三つ目のしんごうを、右に曲がってください。
example_sentences.english: Please turn right at the third light.

example_sentences.japanese: そのカレー色のネクタイ、ちょっと曲がってるよ。
example_sentences.english: Your curry colored necktie is a bit crooked.

example_sentences.japanese: 野球のボールが当たってから、僕の小指はちょっとだけ左に曲がっています。
example_sentences.english: Since getting hit with a baseball my pinky finger bends slightly to the left.

notes: "This is a verb because it ends with an う sound. What does the kanji mean? It's music and bend. In the case of this word, we're going with the ""bend"" version. The verb of that is to bend. This is when you're doing the bending. You can remember this because げ is the gentleman you're bending. He looked good before you bent him in half." "How did you bend this gentleman? You bent him using magic (ま). Just imagine yourself bending a gentleman with magic. Go ahead, do it in your mind."

example_sentences.japanese: 次は、右足のひざを90ど曲げてください。
example_sentences.english: Next, please bend your right knee at a 90 degree angle.

example_sentences.japanese: このYoutubeビデオでは、コウイチがスプーンを百本ひたすら曲げつづけます。
example_sentences.english: In this Youtube video, Koichi just keeps bending 100 spoons.

example_sentences.japanese: スーパーマンはなんでも曲げられます。すでに曲がっているものでさえも。
example_sentences.english: Superman can bend anything, even something that is already bent.

english: To Reevaluate, To Look Again, To Reassess
notes: "You know the word 直す from a couple levels ago. It means ""to fix."" So, when you fix what you see, what are you doing? You're reevaluating something. That's why this word means to reevaluate." The readings are all kun'yomi readings, like the vocab you've seen already. This is like two vocab words put together, which is why it's using the kun'yomi reading. The hiragana on the end is a hint!

example_sentences.japanese: もう一ど、けいかくを見直しましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let’s look at the plans one more time.

example_sentences.japanese: この間のはいひん回しゅうの日、主人が思ったよりたよりになって、ちょっと見直しちゃった。
example_sentences.english: On the last junk removal day, my husband was much more dependable than I expected and it made me look at him differently.

example_sentences.japanese: 大学の授業の選択を見直す方がいいと思うよ。だって、愚鳩を捕まえるのが、いいキャリアになるとは思えないもん。
example_sentences.english: I think you should reevaluate your choices in university classes. I don’t think catching dodo birds is a good career path.

notes: "You've seen the words 走る (to run) and 回る (to revolve). So, when you're running and revolving while you're doing it, you're running in circles. So, the verb form of that is to run around." "The readings are those like the words 走る and 回る. Make sure you know those words from before and apply that knowledge to read this word as well."

example_sentences.japanese: ニッカはいつもオフィス内を走り回っています。
example_sentences.english: Nikka is always running around the office.

example_sentences.japanese: うちの子なら、あの交通じこからもうすっかり立ち直って、元気に走り回っていますよ。
example_sentences.english: My kid completely recovered from the traffic accident and now he's just running, full of energy.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチが蜂の巣を撃った後、蜂から逃げるために約十分間走り回った。
example_sentences.english: After Koichi shot the bee hive, we ran around for nearly ten minutes trying to escape from all the bees.

notes: "I'm going to express my departure. That is my only announcement." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. The ひょう changes to ぴょう and the はつ gets shortened, though, so just about everything about this word is weird."

example_sentences.japanese: 今夜、コウイチから、重大な発表があります。
example_sentences.english: This evening there will be an important announcement from Koichi.

example_sentences.japanese: ピカチュウは、今朝、ポケモンから引たいすることを発表した。
example_sentences.english: Pikachu announced his retirement from Pokemon this morning.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日、みんなの前でSNSの研究成果について発表をしなければならないので、緊張しています。
example_sentences.english: I'm nervous because I have to give a presentation about my social media research outcome in front of everyone tomorrow.

notes: "A temporary determination is something you're not totally sure about. You've decided to think of something in a certain way, but only for now. If more information comes to light, you may change. That's why this word means assumption or hypothesis." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: でも、それはたんなる仮定の話でしょう。
example_sentences.english: But that’s just an assumption, right?

example_sentences.japanese: たとえば、一ドル百円と仮定すると、一本一ドルのコカコーラは百円になりますよね？
example_sentences.english: For example, if we say one dollar is one hundred yen, then one can of $1 coca cola is one hundred yen, right?

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女のベッドに積まれた札束のせいで、今とんでもない仮定が俺の頭の中を飛び交っている。
example_sentences.english: Since seeing that pile of money on her bed, crazy assumptions have been flying around in my head.

notes:
"Industry actions are things industries do. The actions of industry create a lot of construction, whether it be the construction of items or the construction of roads, factories, and more." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

"Please indicate this in a public way. How about a public announcement?" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: きのうてつ夜で仕事だったんですが、朝から工事の音がうるさくてぜんぜんねむれてないんです。
example_sentences.english: I worked all night last night, but I haven’t been able to sleep at all because of the loud construction that started this morning.

example_sentences.japanese: 町中で一日中工事しているので、通行止めだらけでいやになるよ。
example_sentences.english: Because there's construction going on all day, all over town, there are roads closed everywhere and I'm sick and tired of it.

example_sentences.japanese: この工事は今日終わったんですよね？
example_sentences.english: This construction finished today, right?

example_sentences.japanese: 毎年いつ頃日本の地価公示価格が公表されるのか教えて頂けませんか？
example_sentences.english: Could you tell me when Japanese land prices are announced each year?

notes: "A mutual discussion. Both sides are talking to each other and the feelings are mutual. Imagine you're discussing a problem. You want to get help with it, so you get some consultation from your friend. This discussion was very helpful." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 相談の時間は、午後六時から午後九時です。
example_sentences.english: The consultation time is from 6 p.m. to 9 p.m.

example_sentences.japanese: こ人的に相談したいことがあるんですが、ちょっとお時間よろしいですか？
example_sentences.english: If you don't mind, I'd like to discuss something with you in private. Do you have a minute?

example_sentences.japanese: 私は医者に痔の相談をした。
example_sentences.english: I consulted my doctor about my hemorrhoids.

notes: "A versus discuss is when you sit and look at another person. You are discussing something versus them, so you talk back and forth to each other. In this way, you are having a conversation." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチとスティーヴ・ブシェミのゆめの対談が実げんしました！
example_sentences.english: The dream of Koichi and Steve Buscemi talking came true!

example_sentences.japanese: ざんねんながら、そろそろこの対談をおわらせる時間になってしまいました。
example_sentences.english: Unfortunately, it's time to bring this conversation to a close.

example_sentences.japanese: 有名な作家と対談してみたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to talk with a famous writer.

notes: "It's been decided and determined. The decision has been made." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Just be sure to take note of the shortened けつ in 決. It goes to けっ."

example_sentences.japanese: クママンまんがの、アニメ化が決定しました！
example_sentences.english: They’ve decided to turn the Kumaman manga into an anime!

example_sentences.japanese: これはさいしゅう決定になりますので、その後の変更はできませんが、よろしいでしょうか？
example_sentences.english: This will be your final decision and it can't be changed later. Is that okay?

example_sentences.japanese: 君の妹の結婚式と俺の母さんの葬式、どちらに出席するかの決定は君に任せるよ。
example_sentences.english: I’ll leave the decision of whether we’re going to attend your little sister’s wedding or my mother’s funeral to you.

notes: "You exit and then make a departure. This is just a departure." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. The しゅつ gets shortened and はつ changes to ぱつ. No wonder you want to make a departure, you want to get away from crazy readings like this."

example_sentences.japanese: 出発まで五分です。
example_sentences.english: There are five minutes until departure.

example_sentences.japanese: 二週間後に、東京に出発する予定です。
example_sentences.english: I'm going to leave for Tokyo in two weeks.

example_sentences.japanese: ほとんど喋ったことのない同僚の出発の門出を祝う飲み会にお誘い頂き、どうも有難う御座います。
example_sentences.english: Thank you so much for inviting me to a drinking party to celebrate the departure of a co-worker that I rarely spoke to.

notes: "You make departure from your home off into the great beyond. You will go to see the unseen, and hopefully make a great discovery." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. You know the はつ part, which gets shortened to はっ. The 見 is unlike what you learned with 見, though. In order to remember that this is けん, imagine you're going out to make a discovery of some strange new lands. With strange new lands, there comes strange new people. This one has a samurai named Ken けん on it. He's trying to discover new things too!"

example_sentences.japanese: 自たくのベランダで、イモムシを発見しました。
example_sentences.english: I found hornworms on my balcony.

example_sentences.japanese: がんは、早き発見することがひじょうに重ようです。
example_sentences.english: It’s very important to have early detection for cancer.

example_sentences.japanese: Facebookでお金を稼ぐ方法を発見したぜ。しかも超簡単なの。まず、アカウント設定に行くだろ、それからアカウントを停止して、仕事に行くんだ！
example_sentences.english: I discovered how to make money from Facebook. It’s easy. Just go to your account settings, deactivate your account, and go to work.

notes: "A win that was an ease. That is an easy victory or an easy win. Don't hope for a lot of these, though. Hope for tough wins instead, they actually make you better." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 今回のテストは、楽勝だったね。
example_sentences.english: This test was a piece of cake.

example_sentences.japanese: 「JLPT5はどうだった？」「ワニカニのおかげで、楽勝だったよ。」

notes: "Okay, we're going to cheat a little bit to remember the meaning of this word. Let's say you take the temperature of the street. It is exactly one hundred degrees. That's exactly what it is. notes: "If you attempt a test, you're taking an examination. This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

notes: "Your body goes through tests and each time it does, it gains a little more experience. What has your body experienced? What tests has your body been through?" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

notes: "A test that tries to find truth is an experiment. This is because you don't know the truth, so the only way to find it is to try things out and test them. Thus, experiment!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

notes: "Something has been determined beforehand. What is this thing? This action? It is a plan." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 私がせっかく予定を立てても、誰もその通りに動いてくれないことが嫌です。

notes: "The sound that departs from your mouth is you talking. Imagine yourself saying things and words departing your mouth. They are bent in different ways and have different colors, highlighting your pronunciation of certain words and phrases." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: このたんごの発音を教えてください。

example_sentences.english: "Wow, the pronunciation of the Spanish word ""una casita"" sounds similar to ""I’m hungry"" in Japanese."

notes: "The action of returning. That is a reply." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: まだ返事をおくっていません。

notes: "When you hold on and preserve something you are doing the act of retention or maintenance on it. This is preservation." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは何かの世界記録保持者だと聞きました。
example_sentences.english: I heard that Koichi is some kind of world-record holder.

example_sentences.english: Tofugu will contribute our humble efforts to maintain Mars peace.

notes: "Go ahead and try an eat. How was that little try? That little sample? That little taste?" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 文句を言う前に、試食してみてよ。
example_sentences.english: Try a sample before you complain about it.

example_sentences.english: "The person who offers food samples in grocery stores is called ""Ms. Mannequin"" in the Japanese food industry."

english: Take An Exam, Take An Examination, Take A Test, Taking An Exam, Taking An Examination, Taking A Test
notes: "When you accept a test you are going in to take an exam. Good luck! A++++!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.english: My older brother is going to take university entrance exams next year.

example_sentences.english: I forgot to take the exam admission slip, but my mom dropped it off for me.

notes: "The kanji itself means temporary. When you add the に on there you're going towards temporary, which is temporarily." "The reading is kun'yomi, so here's a mnemonic to remember it: Would you mind carrying (かり) this temporarily?"

example_sentences.japanese: 仮にコウイチが『トーフグはめすだ』と言っても、多くのユーザーはそのいけんに反対するんじゃないだろうか。

example_sentences.english: What? Her boobs are made of balloons? Suppose that were true, who cares?

notes:
"This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means sell, so the verb version is to sell or to be sold." Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You learned this reading already, so you should be able to read it!

"Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means ripen so the verb vocab version is to ripen." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: If something starts to ripen too much, it gets all gross, and you're all like, ""ew (う), that's gross."""

example_sentences.japanese: このゲーム、ぜったい売れるだろ。
example_sentences.english: This game will definitely sell well.

example_sentences.japanese: その千円札、五百円でネットオークションにかけたら、よゆうで売れるっしょ。
example_sentences.english: I'd say, if you put up the thousand yen bill for online auction, it would easily sell for five hundred yen.

notes:
"When something advances and goes, it is moving forward. If you do this you will advance. You will progress." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

"If you invade with aggression that's an invasion." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

"I believe and look up to a higher power, for I have religious faith." "The reading for the 仰 portion is an exceptional one. Instead of ぎょう it's こう. Just remember, when it comes to religious faith, all you need to believe in is こういち."

notes: "When you distribute your heart around you, it's like your heart is everywhere at once, but not in your body. You feel frantic, you don't know what to do because your heart is out there. This represents the feeling you have when you have a worry or concern. 心配しないでね！" "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Take note that the ぱい in 配 got rendaku'd from はい, as well."

notes: "If you use a strong tone on certain words, then you are putting emphasis on whatever it is you're talking about it. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

notes: "When you're requesting people you're seeking workers. ""Help wanted!"" is what this word is basically saying." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: うちも、開業当時はしゃっ金だらけだったんだよ。

"When something is public open it is open to the public. You can go look at things that are 公開." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

"My behind regret is the regret from before, which is all regret. That's regret." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: どうがが公開されるのはいつですか？
example_sentences.english: When will the video be released to the public?

example_sentences.english: """I only published that picture to show people that you look much better in person, Hanako."" ""That is such a lie!"""

notes: "You revolve X number of times. Really, the times isn't so important, but the revolving is. That's why this word is revolve or rotate." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. P.S. Ever heard of ""回転ずし?"" That's the kind of sushi that's on conveyer belts, rotating around and around, bringing you delicious plates of things."

example_sentences.english: My pet hamster is vigorously rotating his hamster wheel.

example_sentences.japanese: あそこの回転ずし、もう行った？なんか、そこのすししょく人は皿がきらいらしく、すしが回転してあつくなってるコンベアベルトの上に直でおかれているらしいよ。
example_sentences.english: Have you been to the conveyer belt sushi restaurant over there? Apparently their sushi chefs hate plates there, so the sushi is directly on the rotating, hot conveyor belt.

notes: "Taking the nearby road will get you to your destination more quickly (because it's more close by!). This is a shortcut, aka the short way." "The reading is a bit weird in this one. Its kun'yomi reading for both kanji, even though it looks just like it should be all on'yomi reading. It's like you're taking a shortcut with your kanji readings and doing the native Japanese readings (kun'yomi) instead of the more intellectual Chinese ones (on'yomi). Luckily, you've hopefully seen both of these kanji as vocab already. You have ちか for 近 (short for 近い) and you have 道 (みち), just like the word ""street"" you learned before. Combine these together and you have the reading for this word. Perhaps it's like this because you're combining a couple concepts together into one word, at least when it comes to ""short + way."""

example_sentences.japanese: 上手な絵をも写する事は、上たつの近道です。
example_sentences.english: Tracing a good picture is a shortcut for improvement.

example_sentences.japanese: ワニカニで漢字をおぼえることは、本当に日本語習とくの近道になると思いますか？
example_sentences.english: Do you really think memorizing kanji on WaniKani is actually a shortcut to Japanese acquisition?

example_sentences.japanese: 「ありえねぇ！お前って本当脳みそ無いのな。なんで一方通行を逆走してるんだよ。」「近道になると思ったんだよ。」
example_sentences.english: """Oh my God! You are such an airhead! Why are we going down a one-way street?"" ""I thought it would be a shortcut!"""

notes: "The open of the start is the start or beginning." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: このゲームは、明日はいしん開始です。
example_sentences.english: This game will be released tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: Etoetoの先行予やく受付を開始しました。
example_sentences.english: We've started accepting preorders for EtoEto.

example_sentences.japanese: 現在、Tofuguは枕業界で巻き返しを図っており、新しいモデルの枕の販売を開始した。
example_sentences.english: Tofugu is currently still working to catch up in the pillow market, so they started selling new models.

notes: "This is the adverb version of the kanji, so it has the same meaning, basically. You can say this is the most or just most. You can also use it as extremely."
