"The reading for this is a reading you didn't learn with the kanji (the kun'yomi reading). To learn it, let's look at a mnemonic. Think of the most ridiculous motto (もっと) you've ever heard. Now imagine a motto that's even more ridiculous. Here are some actual totally real mottos that are the most ridiculous: ""What Can Brown Do for You?"" ""It's Not for Women"" ""If It Doesn't Get All Over the Place, It Doesn't Belong in Your Face"" and of course, ""Why Not Enjoy the Go?"""

example_sentences.japanese: げしとは、一年で最も夜がみじかくなる日のことだ。
example_sentences.english: The summer solstice is the shortest night of the year.

example_sentences.japanese: ふじ山は日本で最も高い山です。
example_sentences.english: Mt. Fuji is the tallest mountain in Japan.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼、今日の夜何食べたか知ってる？焼き肉食べ放題に行ったんだよ。最も臭いおならに備えておいた方が身のためだよ。用心に越したことはないんだから。
example_sentences.english: Do you know what he ate tonight? He went to an all you can eat yakiniku restaurant. We’d better prepare for the smelliest farts imaginable. Better safe than sorry.

notes: "This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means learn so the vocab verb version means to learn." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: You have to learn about Nara, the city of deer... lots and lots of deer. If you don't know about it, how about learning about it?"

example_sentences.japanese: 日本に来てから、いろんな言葉を習いました。
example_sentences.english: I’ve learned many different words since I came to Japan.

example_sentences.japanese: うちのむす子は、しょ道を習っています。
example_sentences.english: My son is learning calligraphy.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は、世界一のフグクッキーの作り方を習いに行くのよ。それ、子供たち大好きよね。
example_sentences.english: I’m going to learn how to make the world’s best fugu cookies today. Kids will love that, right?

notes: "So, you're sending something that revolves. It's a little transfer / transmission, going through the wires. Little messages that revolve around as they zip through the lines to get to their destination. Try to imagine this happening in slow motion, getting to the other end." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: そのメール、私にも転送してくれない？
example_sentences.english: Could you forward that email to me?

example_sentences.japanese: 海外に住んでいる日本人は、よく日本のウェブサイトから物を買って、海外の住所に転送しています。
example_sentences.english: Japanese people who reside overseas often buy things from Japanese websites and have them forwarded to the foreign addresses.

example_sentences.japanese: 郵便物をこちら住所の方へ転送して頂きたいんですが。
example_sentences.english: Could you please forward my mail to this address?

notes: "This is the adverb version of the kanji think. You can't help but think, you do it unintentionally. So put this in front of things to say that you did them involuntarily." The reading for this is the kun'yomi reading which you learned already, so you should be able to read this word as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 思わず本音を口にしてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: I spoke of my real intentions unintentionally.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチがすんげー大きな音のオナラをしたから、みんな思わず耳をふさいだんだけど、はなをふさいだ方がよかったね。
example_sentences.english: Koichi farted sooooo loudly that everybody reflexively covered their ears, but we should have covered our noses instead.

example_sentences.japanese: 美味しそうな写真を見て、思わず涎が出た。
example_sentences.english: I saw the delicious looking picture and involuntarily started drooling.

notes: "The flavor of this direction is one I'd like to follow and go in, along with you. You have a good flavor and you're going in a good direction. Will you be my ally? I'll be your supporter." "This word uses the on'yomi reading for 味 and the kun'yomi reading for 方. Luckily, you've learned them both already so you should be able to read this word!"

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグだけは、味方してくれると思ってたんだけどな。
example_sentences.english: I thought that at least Tofugu would support me.

example_sentences.japanese: 実は、コウイチは味方のふりをしたてきだったんだよ。
example_sentences.english: Actually, Koichi was an enemy disguised as a friend.

example_sentences.japanese: お前は一体どっちの味方なんだ？
example_sentences.english: Who the heck are your allies?

english: Beforehand, In Advance, Previously, Ahead Of Time
notes: The kanji and the word are almost exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: What did you do beforehand? You had a raw casual (あらかじ) encounter with a raw Cage, Nic Cage. You probably should have planned something better ahead of time."

example_sentences.japanese: こうなることは分かっていたので、予め用意しておきました。
example_sentences.english: I knew it would happen, so I prepared ahead of time.

example_sentences.japanese: ひ行きに乗りおくれないように、予め前日にオンラインでチェックインしておきました。
example_sentences.english: I checked in online a day before the flight so that I wouldn't miss it.

example_sentences.japanese: 予め予習しておいた甲斐がありました。
example_sentences.english: Preparing the lesson in advance was worthwhile.

notes: "When you pour your ideas into something, you're thinking a lot about it. You're paying close attention and using caution. You'll see this on a lot of signs marking dangerous things in Japan, so be sure to pay attention to them!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日、上しに注意されちゃったよ。
example_sentences.english: Today, I got a warning from my boss.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語で何かを読んでいる時には、おも白い語句くや文ぽうに注意を払って下さい。
example_sentences.english: When you’re reading in Japanese, pay attention to interesting words and grammar.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は彼が間違った道を進んでるんじゃないかと心配しているのよ。注意したんだけど、聞く耳持たずって感じで。
example_sentences.english: I’m worried that he’s going down the wrong path. I cautioned him, but he doesn’t listen to me.

notes: "When you compete to the point of conflict, you know that this person / entity is your competition. Gotta beat out that competition. For example, in order to beat out the competition, WaniKani has a mascot that can eat every other small furry animal that the competition has for their mascot. Case closed." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日の朝ごはんは、昨日のパン食い競争のパンです。
example_sentences.english: Today's breakfast is the bread I got from the bread eating competition yesterday.

example_sentences.japanese: 今は競争とかあんまりする気分じゃないんだけど。
example_sentences.english: I'm really not in the mood for a competition or anything right now.

example_sentences.japanese: あいつら、もうちょっと落ち着いた方がいいよ。二人共負けず嫌いのくせに、いっつも二人で競争してるんだぜ。
example_sentences.english: These guys really need to chill out. They're always competing with each other and they both hate losing.

notes: "People working together on the same thing is cooperation." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグと日清が、豆腐と河豚味のカップラーメンを、共同開発するらしいよ。
example_sentences.english: Apparently Tofugu and Nisshin are going to collaborate to make tofu and fugu flavored cup noodles.

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグは、北朝せんと共同して、金色の金正日人形を生さんしています。
example_sentences.english: Tofugu produces golden Kim Jong Il dolls in cooperation with a North Korean firm.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は共同の貯金をこっそり使い果たしてしまった。
example_sentences.english: He secretly used up our joint savings.

notes: "Teach and nurture. That's what your education is supposed to do." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日行くのは教育センターです。
example_sentences.english: The place we are going today is the education center.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本では、小学校教育と中学校教育がぎむ教育です。
example_sentences.english: In Japan, education is mandatory through elementary and junior high school.

example_sentences.japanese: 「教育があって常識がないよりも、教育がなくて常識がある方がはるかによい。」って誰の言葉だっけ？
example_sentences.english: "Do you remember who said, ""It is a thousand times better to have common sense without education than education without common sense?"""

notes: "Something is towards (に) special. That thing is especially special, wouldn't you say?" The reading is the same reading you learned for this kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: 特に病院ではしずかにしなければいけません。
example_sentences.english: You have to be quiet, especially in the hospital.

example_sentences.japanese: このメロンは特にかたいですね。まるでカボチャのようだ。
example_sentences.english: This melon is particularly hard. It's like a squash.

example_sentences.japanese: 「お夕飯は何が食べたい？」「何でもいいよ。特にこだわりはないよ。」
example_sentences.english: """What would you like for supper?"" ""Anything is fine. I’m not especially picky."""

notes: "Your heart holds a lot of feelings. They can be overwhelming and sometimes it feels like there are none in there at all, but that doesn't mean they aren't there in your heart." The readings for this word are both kun'yomi readings. You learned them when you learned the kanji, so you should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 何事も心持ち次だいだと思うんだよね。
example_sentences.english: I think it all depends on how you feel about it.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日あった男に心持ちほねっぽいねって言われたんだけど、何なのアイツ。
example_sentences.english: A guy I met today told me I'm kinda bony, what's up with that?!

example_sentences.japanese: あの子は、心持ちのよい素直な子です。
example_sentences.english: He is a pleasant, honest kid.

english: Get Even, Retaliation, Get Back At, Revenge, Get Revenge
notes: "When you return the doings of another person, you're doing it to get even (whether it's a nice thing or a mean thing)." "The readings are a bit weird, here. 仕 gets its on'yomi reading... you should be okay with that. 返し gets the kun'yomi reading, though, which is the reading you saw with the word 返す in level 9. You can tell this part uses the kun'yomi vocab reading because it has that hiragana attached to it. Just remember to distinguish between the two parts of the word to remember the readings."

example_sentences.japanese: くやしいから、なんか仕返ししたいな。
example_sentences.english: It was mortifying, so I wanna get even.

example_sentences.japanese: キャットウーマン！あんたって本当に最低の女だね！いつか仕返ししてやるわ！
example_sentences.english: Catwoman! You are so evil! I’ll get you back soon!

example_sentences.japanese: プリンを食べられた仕返しに、コウイチの大すきなヨーグルトを食べてやった。
example_sentences.english: I ate Koichi's favorite yogurt to get back at him for eating my pudding.

notes: "Your ""doing actions"" are the things you do. What do you say when someone asks ""what you do""? You tell them what your job is." "This word uses the on'yomi reading for 仕 and the kun'yomi reading for 事. Please note that 事 uses the reading こと, which you didn't learn with the kanji, but you have come across it once or twice by now, and because of the way rendaku works, it's changed to the voiced ごと."

example_sentences.japanese: この仕事は、交通ひこみですか？
example_sentences.english: Does this job reimburse transportation costs?

example_sentences.japanese: 赤ちゃんの仕事は泣くことです。
example_sentences.english: The business of a baby is to cry.

example_sentences.japanese: 「時間内に、この仕事を終えられると思うか？」「さあ、それはどうかな。」
example_sentences.english: """Do you think we can finish this work in time?"" ""Well I wouldn’t bet on it."""

notes: "The labor work is when you're doing work with your body, right? That's manual labor." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたの労働時間は週何時間ですか？
example_sentences.english: How many hours do you work per week?

example_sentences.japanese: うちの主人は年なので、肉体労働はちょっとさすがにきびしいかも。
example_sentences.english: My husband is old, so manual labor would be a bit too hard for him.

example_sentences.japanese: 俺には何が必要か知ってるかい？趣味の部屋と新しい車だよ。労働の対価をきちんと受け取る必要があるだろ？
example_sentences.english: You know what I need? A man cave and a new car. I need to properly reward myself for my labors.

notes: "The flavor of an idea, what is that? Imagine yourself licking an idea to figure out what it tastes like. What do you think you'll be tasting? Probably the meaning of said idea." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチのあの意味あり気なかおを見て。
example_sentences.english: Look at Koichi's meaningful look!

example_sentences.japanese: この目が何を意味するかは分かりますか？
example_sentences.english: Do you understand what these eyes imply?

example_sentences.japanese: 「あなたって、もっと賢いと思っていたわ。」「おい、それってどういう意味だよ!?」
example_sentences.english: """I thought you were smarter than that."" ""Hey what’s that supposed to mean?"""

notes: "This is the adjective version of the kanji new, so it means new too." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: Your parents put a newly wrapped present under the Christmas tree. You don't want to wait to see what new thing they got you so you rip it open to find they got you a raw (あら) steak. Getting a new steak is cool and all, but a raw steak is pretty gross. It's dripping blood all over the place."

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチが新たなオムツせいぞうぎじゅつを発明しました。
example_sentences.english: Koichi invented a novel diaper-making technique.

example_sentences.japanese: 九月は自分にとって新たなスタートになりそうな予かんがする。
example_sentences.english: I feel like September is going to be a fresh start for me.

example_sentences.japanese: この小説は、読み返す度に新たな発見がある。
example_sentences.english: Every time I reread this novel I make a new discovery.

english: Not Particularly, Separately, Not Really, Not Exactly, Not Especially
notes: "If someone asks if you want a separate knee (に), you'll say not particularly. I mean, you've never thought about it, but do you really need more knees? Not really..." The reading is just the reading you learned with the kanji. Well done!

example_sentences.japanese: 温かいものはふくろを別にしてください。
example_sentences.english: Can you use a separate bag for the warm stuff?

example_sentences.japanese: 別に会社で人間関係に苦労はしてないよ。
example_sentences.english: I don't really have a difficult time dealing with human relationships at work.

example_sentences.japanese: 「おお、フグ。最近どうよ？」「別に変わりないね。ワニ君、君はどうだい？」
example_sentences.english: """Hey Fugu! What are you up to lately?"" ""Nothing in particular. How about you Wani?"""

notes: "The idea you see in your head is your opinion. As the dude once said... ""That's just, like, your 意見, man.""" "The reading is all on'yomi, meaning 意 is just fine. 見's on'yomi (けん) is a reading you didn't learn with the kanji because it's so much less useful, but you do have to know it here. You've seen it with 発見 a couple levels ago, so that should help. In this case, just think about how your opinion is that Ken needs a new girlfriend. Barbie doesn't treat him right and he's always coming to the bar with new bruises... That Ken. Tell him your opinion."

example_sentences.japanese: 意見の出しおしみはしないで下さい。
example_sentences.english: Don't hold your opinions back, please.

example_sentences.japanese: いくら仲の良い友だちでも、ちょっと正直には意見しづらいよね。
example_sentences.english: Even though they were my close friends, I would probably have difficulty openly telling them about this.

example_sentences.japanese: これは俺の個人的な意見なんだけど、たまに、日本は本当に変わった国だなぁと思うんだよね。
example_sentences.english: This is just my personal opinion, but I sometimes think that Japan is a really weird country.

notes: "You pour writing onto a form. You're filling out this form to order something new for yourself. It's a formal request to get this new thing (imagine it being something you're excited about ordering right now, and imagine yourself ordering it by pouring writing onto an order form)." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: スタバの注文の仕方がいまいちよく分からないんだけど。
example_sentences.english: I don't really understand how to order at Starbucks.

example_sentences.japanese: まさか注文するのをわすれてたりしないよね。
example_sentences.english: You didn't forget to place an order, did you?

example_sentences.japanese: それは無理な注文だが、やるっきゃない。
example_sentences.english: That’s an unreasonable request but we don’t have a choice.

notes: "Your fate orders are the orders you get from above. You are ordered and commanded to carry out said orders." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチ王の命令には全てしたがわなくてはいけない。
example_sentences.english: We have to follow the every command of King Koichi.

example_sentences.japanese: はぁ？おねがいだった？ふざけんなよ。こっちには命令にしか聞こえなかったっつーの。
example_sentences.english: Huh? That was a request? That's BS! That definitely sounded like an order.

example_sentences.japanese: 「ほら！何をダラダラ待ってるの? 走って！」「俺に命令するんじゃねぇよ！」
example_sentences.english: """C’mon! What are you waiting for? Run!"" ""Don’t order me around!"""

notes: "When you have an idea for a task you are in preparation for actually doing it. Because it's still just an idea you're still getting ready." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 万が一の時にそなえて、マッチとろうそくを用意しました。
example_sentences.english: I got matches and candles ready in case of emergency.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎週金よう日はきゅう食がないから自分でおべん当を用意しないといけないんです。
example_sentences.english: Because school lunch is not provided on Fridays, we have to prepare our own lunch.

example_sentences.japanese: 出所祝いの鍋パーティーの用意は全てこちらで致しますので、あなたは保釈金の用意をお願いします。
example_sentences.english: We will do all the nabe party arrangements to celebrate the release from jail, so please take care of making arrangements for bail on your side.

notes: "When you fix a relationship you are going through reconciliation." "The readings are the kun'yomi readings. For 仲 you're fine. That's what you learned with the kanji. For 直り think back to the vocab word 直る. That's what's going on here."

example_sentences.japanese: 過去のことは水に流して、仲直りしようよ。
example_sentences.english: Let’s let bygones be bygones and just make peace with this.

example_sentences.japanese: そんなにかんたんに仲直りは出来ないよ。
example_sentences.english: I can't make up with her that quickly.

example_sentences.japanese: 一体全体、コウイチはどうやってマリオブラザーズを仲直りさせたの？
example_sentences.english: How did Koichi bring about a reconciliation between the Mario brothers?

english: Sell Cheaply, Discount, Bargain Sale, Sale
notes: "When you sell something cheap, you're selling it at a discount. Alternatively you can remember this word as sell cheaply or bargain sale. These are good deals!" "The hiragana on the end hints that the readings are the kun'yomi readings. Use your memory of 安い and 売る to help you to remember how to read this."

example_sentences.japanese: あんまり自分を安売りすると、後で辛くなりますよ。
example_sentences.english: If you sell yourself too short, it’ll be tough later.

example_sentences.japanese: このジャケット、めっちゃ好きだけど、ちょっとよゆうがないんですよね。近々安売りするよていとかってないですかね？
example_sentences.english: I really love this jacket, but can't afford it. Are there any upcoming sales?

example_sentences.japanese: そうだよ。君に売った時にはそのテレビは壊れていたさ。でも、だからこそ安売りしたんじゃないか。
example_sentences.english: Yes, the TV was broken when I sold it to you, but that’s why it was on sale.

english: Shared, Co Ownership, Joint Ownership, Share
notes: "The things you together have are the things that are shared." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 「あのヨットは素敵ですね。田中さんのですか？」 「兄貴と共有なんですよ。」
example_sentences.english: """That is a very nice yacht. Is that yours, Mr. Tanaka?"" ""I'm a co-owner with my brother."""

example_sentences.japanese: このワンピースのフィギュアは、コウイチとビエトの共有のざいさんです。
example_sentences.english: These One Piece figures are the shared assets of Koichi and Viet.

example_sentences.japanese: 子育ては、ふうふ間でじょうほうをきちんと共有した方が上手く行きますよ。
example_sentences.english: Raising a kid works better when husbands and wives share information properly.

english: Sightseeing, Sightseer, Watching, Watcher, Viewing, Viewer
notes: "If you try to see a bunch of things at once, you are probably sightseeing." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: おも白そうだから、見物してみましょう。
example_sentences.english: It seems fun, so let’s have a look.

example_sentences.japanese: オフィスのまどから、クリスマスパレードを見物しました。
example_sentences.english: We watched the Christmas parade from the office windows.

example_sentences.japanese: 母ちゃんなら、東京見物に出かけたぜ。
example_sentences.english: Mom would have gone sightseeing in Tokyo.

notes: "You know the single word 時, right? It means time. This is that twice. So you have one time, and you have another time. They are separate. Things don't happen in every of these times you have. They happen sometimes." "The reading is the vocab word 時 twice, with the second one getting rendaku'd."

example_sentences.japanese: 私は時々トーフグホテルの最上階のレストランでトーフグの記事を読みます。
example_sentences.english: Sometimes I read Tofugu articles in a restaurant on the top floor of the Tofugu hotel.

example_sentences.japanese: はま辺では、時々、そよ風がわたしのほほをやさしくなでていった。
example_sentences.english: At the beach, sometimes a pleasant breeze would gently caress my cheek.

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグって、時々お客さんともめるんだよね。あるトラブルが、死人を出すなぐり合いのけんかになったこともあるから、ほんと、気を付けた方がいいよ。
example_sentences.english: Tofugu gets into trouble with its customers at times. One time it even led to a fist fight that ended in a death, so you should be careful with them, really.

notes: "A language about things. This is a confusing one. Just think of it more like someone talking about things, anything, really. Someone who just talks about things is someone who tells stories. So, this word means tale or story or legend (not the Tom Cruise one, though)." "The reading for this is messed up. You have 物 as もの, which is fine, but 語 decides to go all crazy on you. Maybe you've heard the word ものがたり before (it's in some film names / book names). If not, think of a story being told about a great gatling (がたり) gun that wandered the land, mowing everything down in its path. It's a terrible legend, but what if it were true???"

example_sentences.japanese: 物語の主人公にでもなったつもりでいるんだろう。
example_sentences.english: I think she's acting like she's the main character of a story.

example_sentences.japanese: 竹とり物語は日本の有名な物語です。
example_sentences.english: The Tale of the Bamboo Cutter is a famous Japanese legend.

example_sentences.japanese: 今物語を書いているんです。悲しい子犬フェチの男の話です。
example_sentences.english: I’m writing a story right now. It’s about a sad guy who is obsessed with puppies.

english: The Lowest, The Worst, Lowest, Worst, Nasty, Terrible
notes: "The most low is the lowest. It's also what you call something when you think it's the worst or just plain terrible. Try yelling this out when you're disgusted about someone or something." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: よくこんな最低最あくの酒がのめるよね。
example_sentences.english: How can you drink such terrible, garbage alcohol?

example_sentences.japanese: 今までで最低のキスだったかも。
example_sentences.english: Maybe it was the worst kiss ever.

example_sentences.japanese: えぇっ！あの試験で最低点を取ったの？参ったなぁ。
example_sentences.english: Wow, I can’t believe you got the lowest score on the test. What a bummer!

english: To Compete, To Argue, To Quarrel
notes: "This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means conflict so the vocabulary means to compete or to argue. Your views conflict with someone else's so you're going to compete with them to see who's right." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: You're starting to compete with your rival. You're yelling, and punching each other in the faces, causing a huge scene, and making people call the cops on you. Because of your quarrel, you have both now been arrested (あらそ) and are now spending time in prison. This isn't the perfect reading, but it hopefully can get you to the correct reading with a few tries. Try to make the connection."

example_sentences.japanese: わたしの事で争うのはよして！
example_sentences.english: Please don't argue about me!

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグの社いんたちは、社長のざをねらって争っています。
example_sentences.english: Tofugu workers are competing with each other for the position of president.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたって本当に落ち着いているし楽しいし、あなたと遊ぶのは最高だわ。しかも、私たち言い争ったこともまだ一度も無いわよね。それってすごくない？
example_sentences.english: You are so chill. It’s great hanging out with you. You know what? We’ve never had an argument yet, either. That’s crazy, isn’t it?

notes: "This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means compete so the verb vocab version means to compete." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: You have to compete for kisses (きそ) from that boy/girl you like. Imagine yourself doing this, competing with a rival."

example_sentences.japanese: 子どもたちは、新しい先生の所に競うようにかけよった。
example_sentences.english: The children raced over to the new teacher.

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグはユニークすぎて、競う相手がいないんですよ。いわゆる一人勝ちってやつですね。
example_sentences.english: Tofugu is so unique that there is nobody else to compete with. They are the so-called sole winner.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチとビエトは、年に一度トーフグオフィスで開かれる剣道の大会で、優れた腕前を披露しようと競い合いました。
example_sentences.english: Koichi and Viet competed with each other to demonstrate their prowess at the annual Kendo competition held in the Tofugu office.

notes: "Something outside your normal idea of how things work will come as unexpected to you." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 意外にも、父はすぐにさん成してくれました。
example_sentences.english: Unexpectedly, my dad approved of it right away.

example_sentences.japanese: ゆですぎのやわらかいパスタをこのんで食べるのは、カナダの意外な文化でした。
example_sentences.english: Liking soft pasta that's been cooked too long was an unexpected aspect of Canadian culture.

example_sentences.japanese: フグは物凄く走るの速いよ。海ではあまり良いスイマーじゃなかったってことと、大学に入るまで陸上での競技に出たことがなかったってのは、本当に意外だよ。
example_sentences.english: Fugu is a really fast runner. The surprising thing is, he was never a good swimmer in the sea and never raced on land until he was in college.

notes: "A place that sells merchandise is a business." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. You've learned them both already!

example_sentences.japanese: 一しょに商売して一もうけしようぜ！
example_sentences.english: Let's go into business and make a fortune together!

example_sentences.japanese: 最近はあのコンビニのせいで、商売あがったりだね。
example_sentences.english: My business has dried up recently because of that convenience store.

example_sentences.japanese: 学校卒業後に商売を始めたんですが、すぐに商売をすることは簡単ではないことを学びました。
example_sentences.english: After leaving school I went into business for myself, but I soon learned that running a business is no easy task.

notes: "The sound reading. What could this be...? Wait a sec, think to Japanese and kanji. What's the reading that uses sounds from another place, specifically China? That's the Chinese reading, aka the on'yomi. Sounds familiar?" "The reading for 音 is the 音読み. 読み uses the kun'yomi, though, strangely. Way to mess up the one word that should be all on'yomi, Japan. Way. To. Go."

example_sentences.japanese: この漢字の音読みって何だっけ？
example_sentences.english: What was the on'yomi for this kanji again?

example_sentences.japanese: 初めて見た地名はふ通は音読みしちゃうよね。
example_sentences.english: We usually read place names that we see for the first time with on'yomi.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語の音読みと訓読みの違いは何ですか？
example_sentences.english: What’s the difference between the Chinese reading and the Japanese reading in the Japanese language?

notes:
"What is something that will first extinguish something and then change it? One thing I can think of is your body. It takes in food, extinguishes it in your stomach, then changes it into things your body can use (and then excrete). That's why this ""extinguish-change"" process is your digestion." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

"You're chanting and you're singing and you're having a gay ol' time. You're singing all your songs and even the chanting sounds like singing. It's so fun." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: このくすりは、消化をそく進してくれます。
example_sentences.english: This medicine will stimulate your digestion.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは下り気味だから、消化の良いものを食べさせてあげてね。
example_sentences.english: Koichi's having a touch of diarrhea, so please have him eat something easy to digest.

example_sentences.japanese: 昼に食べたラーメンをまだ消化しきっていない。
example_sentences.english: I haven’t finished digesting the ramen I ate for lunch.

example_sentences.japanese: 愛国唱歌は聴きたくないね。
example_sentences.english: I don’t want to listen to the patriotic school song.

notes: "For a period of time you have to wait. During this waiting period, you are expecting or anticipating something to happen. Waiting, expecting, waiting, expecting..." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: あの大学院生には、もっと期待してたのに。
example_sentences.english: I expected more from the grad student.

example_sentences.japanese: この前わざわざ日本からとりよせた新しいおやつは期待外れでした。
example_sentences.english: The new snack that I bought and had sent all the way from Japan the other day was not as good as I anticipated.

example_sentences.japanese: ウォール・ストリートは常にトップレベルの人材を求めていますが、コウイチならきっとそこでも期待に応えられると思います。
example_sentences.english: Wall Street always needs top-level talent and I’m pretty sure that Koichi will be able to live up to those expectations.

notes: "Climb a mountain. That is mountain climbing." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Note this uses the alternative と reading, not to be confused with とう (actually, very confusing, sorry!). Just imagine you cut your toe off with an ice pick while mountain climbing. You know it's a short と because your toe is now short. And さん becomes ざん thanks to our old friend rendaku."

example_sentences.japanese: ふじ山に登山してみたいです。
example_sentences.english: I want to try climbing Mt. Fuji.

example_sentences.japanese: もう登山はこりごりです。
example_sentences.english: I never want to climb a mountain again.

example_sentences.japanese: 「登山に行くってのはどう？」「さあ、どうしようかなあ。」
example_sentences.english: """How about we go mountain climbing?"" ""Well I don’t know about that."""

notes: "Something you wear, and wear again, is something you steadily wear. You do it so often, it's reliable. Also, if you wear something this much it's steadily wearing away too." This word uses on'yomi readings of the kanji you learned, twice. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: その会社員は、いつも着々と仕事をこなしていた。
example_sentences.english: That office worker always got tasks done steadily.

example_sentences.japanese: プロジェクトは着々進んでいるようだね。
example_sentences.english: It seems like you're making steady progress on the project.

example_sentences.japanese: 手はずは着々と整っていますよ。
example_sentences.english: The arrangements for it have been moving along steadily.

english: The First, First, Number One, Best
notes: "The ordinal number prefix one refers to the first thing. This is the number one place you can get. In fact, it's simply the best." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 自分のけんこうが第一ですよ。
example_sentences.english: You should put your health first.

example_sentences.japanese: 第一きぼうは二月十四日で、第二きぼうは二月二十一日です。
example_sentences.english: My first preference is Feb 14th and my second preference is Feb 21st.

example_sentences.japanese: あの有名なフグ一家の第一印象はどうでしたか？
example_sentences.english: What was your first impression of the famous blowfish family?

hiragana: りゅうこう, はやり
notes: "Where the stream is going is where everyone's going. That's what tends to be the trend of things. Imagine a trend going on in your society right now. Imagine it going down a stream with everyone following it." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近、アメリカの女せいの間でアジアの化しょうひんが流行しています。
example_sentences.english: Asian cosmetics are a recent craze among American women.

example_sentences.japanese: ポケモンGoはPeopleしで2016年度に最も流行したものの一つにえらばれました。
example_sentences.english: Pokemon Go was selected as one of 2016's Fads of the Year by People Magazine.

example_sentences.japanese: ねぇ、フグ。魚達向けに、流行のヘアスタイルを掲載した雑誌を出版したらどうかなって思ってるんだけど、あなたはどう思う？
example_sentences.english: Hey, Fugu. I’m thinking of publishing a magazine that catalogues trendy hairstyles for fish, what do you think about that?

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it should use the kun'yomi reading. When learning the kanji, you didn't learn that reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you with this word: You are going on your trip but you need to bring your little tabby (たび) cat with you to keep you company. This cat keeps you calm and lets you leave your house, but the airlines won't let you take it on this trip. What to do?"

example_sentences.japanese: 世界中を旅するのがゆめです。
example_sentences.english: My dream is to travel around the world.

example_sentences.japanese: さいふとパスポートをぬすまれるは、ひ行きに乗りおくれるは、マジで最悪の旅だったよ。
example_sentences.english: My wallet and passport were stolen and I missed the plane. It was the worst trip ever.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はもうすっかり旅支度ができているよ。
example_sentences.english: I’m already prepared for our trip.

notes: "Your feelings are in your heart. When your feelings are in your heart they are pure feelings. You can be happy for people and feel admiration for their successes. This is a great feeling to have in your heart." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 感心なお子さんですね。
example_sentences.english: You have such an admirable child.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日休まずに部屋をそうじするなんて、感心、感心。
example_sentences.english: You earned my admiration by cleaning your room every single day.

example_sentences.japanese: ケイティは、真面目で熱心な働きと細かい気配りで、同僚たちを感心させた。
example_sentences.english: Katie earned the admiration of her co-workers with her hard work and attention to detail.

notes: "When you arrange something according to reason, the result is an arrangement." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: このアパートの住民の部屋はみんなきちんと整理されています。
example_sentences.english: This apartment's residents' rooms are all neatly arranged.

example_sentences.japanese: 整理整とんすることは大切です。
example_sentences.english: Organizing well is important.

example_sentences.japanese: 別れた彼氏の写真を整理しました。
example_sentences.english: I adjusted the picture of my ex-boyfriend.

notes: "A dark kill is an assassination. It's done by someone who is in a ninja outfit and dark, hiding in the shadows for his moment to strike." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: そのヤクザの組長は暗殺されてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: That yakuza boss ended up getting assassinated.

example_sentences.japanese: もう暗殺教室の映画は見ましたか？とってもおも白いですよね〜。
example_sentences.english: Have you already watched the Assassination Classroom movie? It was fun, isn't it?

example_sentences.japanese: ねぇ、ビエト！どうやってこんなに面白い暗殺計画を思いついたの？
example_sentences.english: Hey, Viet! How did you come up with such a unique assassination plan?

notes: "It's all nature out there. It's entirely nature and not at all city. This word is weird. It means two opposite things. Thanks Japanese! Just look out for a negative word after the 全然. If it is negative it's ""not at all"" if it's not negative it might be ""entirely.""" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ハリケーンとの天気予ほうがあったのに、全然雨がふらなかった。
example_sentences.english: Even though the weather forecast said there was a hurricane, we didn't get any rain at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 「すみませんが、ちょっとたのみ事をしてもいいですか。」「はい、全然いいですよ！」
example_sentences.english: """Excuse me, but may I ask you for a small favor?"" ""Sure, of course!"""

example_sentences.japanese: 「分かりましたか？」 「申し訳ないのですが、チンプンカンプンで全然分かりません。今言ったことをもう少しゆっくり言っていただけませんか？」
example_sentences.english: """Did you get that?"" ""I’m sorry. I’m completely lost. Could you say that again more slowly?"""

english: For The First Time, First Time
notes: "You know that 初 means ""first"" This word means for the first time. Think of めて as ""meet."" Then think ""when we met for the first time ____ happened.""" "This word uses the kun'yomi, which you didn't learn with the kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you out. What are you beginning? You are beginning Haj (はじ). (Haj is the fifth pillar of Islam, and is a pilgrimage to Mecca during the month of Dhu al-Hijja)."

example_sentences.japanese: 初めてオバマ大とうりょうと会ったしゅんかんから意気投合した。
example_sentences.english: Since the first time we met, President Obama and I have gotten along very well.

example_sentences.japanese: 初めての銀行業むに四苦八苦しています。
example_sentences.english: This is my first time dealing with banking and I'm really struggling.

example_sentences.japanese: 「もしかして、日本はこれが初めて？」「はい。そうなんです。」「そうなんだ。日本はどう？」「かなり気に入ってるわ。」
example_sentences.english: """Is it possible this is your first time in Japan?"" ""Yes, it is."" ""Oh really? How do you like it?” ""I really like it!"""

notes: "You're trying to determine the concept behind something but you have to test your hypothesis first. You have your assumptions, but you're not entirely sure you're right yet because all you have is the concept to go off of." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: あの手がたくさんある神様の絵がここにかざられることを想定しています。
example_sentences.english: We assume the picture of the many-armed deity will be hung here.

example_sentences.japanese: まだ手に入れていないものを、手に入れたとの想定で行動するのは良くない。
example_sentences.english: It's not good to act on the assumption that you'll have something before you actually do.

example_sentences.japanese: 地震を想定した避難訓練を行います。
example_sentences.english: We will now conduct the disaster drill assuming there is an earthquake.

notes: "In the dark if you try to write down something it won't work very well. You can't see. So, how can you ""write something down"" in the dark? You write it down in your mind. This is memorization! Recognize this word? The SRS application ""Anki"" comes from this word, I'm guessing!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 短期間で丸暗記しても、すぐわすれてしまうだろう？
example_sentences.english: Even if you use rote memorization to memorize them in the short term, you'll forget them again quickly, won't you?

example_sentences.japanese: さくら木さんは、円しゅうりつを何けた目まで暗記していますか？
example_sentences.english: How many digits of pi can you remember, Sakuragi?

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はクラスのお調子者で、いつもボケているが、暗記力はすごい。
example_sentences.english: He's the class clown and is always playing the fool, but he is very good at memorization.

english: Orderly, Systematic, Well Organized, Natural Order
notes: "When you arrange things in the way that nature intended, you're doing things in a quite orderly fashion. This is the natural state of things, nice and arranged and natural. Orderly!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 東京は人が多いけれど整然としています。
example_sentences.english: Even though there are many people in Tokyo, it is well organized.

example_sentences.japanese: ダリンはいつも理路整然としたせつ明をしてくれます。
example_sentences.english: Darin always provides well-reasoned explanations.

example_sentences.japanese: Tofuguオフィスの棚に整然と並べられていたワインボトルを、マミが全部空けてしまった。
example_sentences.english: The neatly arranged wine bottles on the shelves of the Tofugu office were all emptied out by Mami.

notes: "Your truth feeling is when you feel something is true. You have the realization this is a real feeling!" "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. The reading for 実 gets changed to じっ so be careful!"

example_sentences.japanese: この売り上げ表を見ると、ワニカニが売れているんだなと実感できます。
example_sentences.english: When I look at this revenue chart I really feel like WaniKani is selling well.

example_sentences.japanese: 母が死んだという知らせを聞いても、すぐには実感がわかなかった。
example_sentences.english: Even when I heard the news that my mother died, it didn't feel real at first.

example_sentences.japanese: アメリカへ行って初めて、日本はなんと小さい国かと実感した。
example_sentences.english: Only after I went to America did I realize how small Japan really is.

notes: "You think about the concept of a certain number of times, each time thinking of each time you've thought about this concept before. Each time you look back, that is retrospection on that concept. You look back more and more times until there are no more times to look back on." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: この映画のこの回想のシーンがすごくすきなんだよね。
example_sentences.english: I really like this retrospective scene in the movie.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチはえんがわでネコと一しょにとりとめのない回想にふけっていた。
example_sentences.english: Koichi was reminiscing incoherently with his cat on the veranda.

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトが時々、仕事中にヤクザ時代のことを回想しているのをわたしは知っている。
example_sentences.english: I know that Viet sometimes reminisces about his yakuza days during work hours.

notes: "How can you solve your study problem? With a little extra scholarship and studying." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 学問と文学は切っても切れない関係にある。
example_sentences.english: Scholarship is always associated with literature.

example_sentences.japanese: こ人てきには、大学って学問する所じゃなくて、「大そつ」っていうしかくを取りに行くための所だと思ってるんだよね。
example_sentences.english: "I personally think that universities aren't a place to learn, but a place to obtain the qualifications of a ""university degree."""

example_sentences.japanese: 学問を疎かにしてはいけない。
example_sentences.english: You must not neglect your studies.

english: Special Selection, Special Choice, Special Prize
notes: "If something is special you choose it. That makes it a special selection of yours and it gets a special prize that only you could give!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 親分の絵が、コンクールで特選に入賞したぞ！
example_sentences.english: The picture of our boss won the special prize at the contest!

example_sentences.japanese: こちらが、特選されたコスプレイヤーの方々です。
example_sentences.english: Here are the specially selected cosplayers.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは、毎晩寝る前に特選の極上黒大蒜を食べるそうだ。
example_sentences.english: I heard that Koichi eats the best, specially selected black garlic before going to bed every night.

notes: "A self kill is when you kill yourself. That's suicide." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 東アジアの国の中で最も自殺りつが高い国はかん国です。
example_sentences.english: South Korea has the highest suicide rate among East Asian countries.

example_sentences.japanese: 「Blue Wale (シロナガスクジラ)」という名前のSNSゲームで、十代のロシア人少年少女たちが130人以上も自殺したそうです。
example_sentences.english: "Apparently, over 130 Russian teenagers committed suicide as a part of a social media game called ""Blue Whale."""

example_sentences.japanese: 日本の自殺名所のリストを、メールで送ってもらえますか？あと、ファイルを送る際に圧縮して頂けると助かります。
example_sentences.english: Could you email me that list of famous suicide spots in Japan? I’d appreciate if you could compress the file before you send it to me too.

english: Sympathy, Same Sentiment, Concurrence, Agree, Empathy
notes: "When you have the same feeling as someone else, you have sympathy for them, because you know how they feel. How kind of you!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: わたしはコウイチの意見に同感ですね。
example_sentences.english: I empathize with Koichi's views.

example_sentences.japanese: 今までにこんなに同感したことがないぐらい、思いっきり同感しています。
example_sentences.english: I've never agreed with someone so much.

example_sentences.japanese: 「私、フグのこと嫌い。」「同感だわ。」
example_sentences.english: """I hate Fugu."" ""I feel the same way."""

notes: "You have feelings of apologizing. Strangely, this word means thanks and gratitude, though. Perhaps someone did something so nice for you that you want to apologize for how many nice things they're doing for you. You are this grateful to them!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 感謝祭の日にはみんなに感謝しましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let's show our gratitude to everyone on Thanksgiving Day.

example_sentences.japanese: 言葉には出さないけど、つまにはいつも感謝しているんです。
example_sentences.english: Although I don't say it, I always appreciate my wife.

example_sentences.japanese: 私達のお客様全員に感謝したいと思います。私達は、皆さん無しには、ここには居られません。
example_sentences.english: I would like to express my gratitude to all our clients. Without you, we would not be here.

english: To Foster, To Raise, To Rear
notes: "This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means foster so the verb vocab version is to foster." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: You're offering to raise some girl as your own. After the paperwork is over, you can finally say: ""Yah, she now (やしな) is my kid!"""

example_sentences.japanese: ワニカニがトーフグを養っているの？それともトーフグがワニカニを養っているの？
example_sentences.english: Does WaniKani foster Tofugu or does Tofugu foster WaniKani?

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチのにんじゅつにだまされない目を養う必要があります。
example_sentences.english: We need to keep our eyes peeled so we won't be deceived by Koichi's ninjutsu.

example_sentences.japanese: たまにはご主人にも感謝しろよ。あいつだって、立派に家族を養ってきたじゃないか。
example_sentences.english: You should thank your husband sometimes. He has done a good job raising your family, hasn’t he?

english: To Look Back At, To Look Back On, To Look Back
notes: "Your seeing is returning on something. This is when you look back at something you've already looked at before. This word means to look back at." "The readings are just 見 and the vocab word 返る, combined together. So long as you know both of those you should be able to combine them into the reading for this word."

example_sentences.japanese: か去を見返ってるひまはないんだよ。
example_sentences.english: I don't have time to look back on the past.

example_sentences.japanese: 赤さまの見返るおすがたがただただかわいすぎてモエまくっておりまする（*´▽｀*）
example_sentences.english: The figure of the baby looking back at me is just too cute and totes adorbs.（*´▽｀*）

example_sentences.japanese: ガシャーンと大きな音がして、私は思わず後ろを見返った。
example_sentences.english: There was a huge crash and I involuntarily looked behind me.

notes: "When your bone gets folded like paper, or something, you can bet you have a broken bone or fracture." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Just watch out because こつ is shortened to こっ here."

example_sentences.japanese: これはふくざつ骨折ですね。
example_sentences.english: This is a compound bone fracture.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは去年ひどい自動車事こにあってね。足を骨折しただけじゃなく、頭まで失くしてしまって、今はロボットになっちゃったんですよ。
example_sentences.english: Koichi had a bad car accident last year. Not only did he break his legs, but he lost his head and now he's a robot.

example_sentences.japanese: しばらくみんなで一緒に会ってないよね〜。最近どうしてるの？私は足の小指を骨折した以外は特に変わりないよ〜。（笑）
example_sentences.english: It’s been a while since we all got together. How have you been? Things are pretty much the same with me except I broke my pinky toe. Lol.

notes: "When something has become perfect it has reached completion." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 完成前に起こしてもらえますか？
example_sentences.english: Can you get me up before it's completed?

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグはこの数日間で、かなりのりょうを完成させた。
example_sentences.english: Tofugu has accomplished a great deal in the last few days.

example_sentences.japanese: 我々の新しい日本語学習アプリは、あと一ヶ月程で完成します。
example_sentences.english: Our new Japanese learning app will be completed in a month or so.

notes: "A perfect finish is when everything is at total completion. Nothing is left over and all is done." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 作戦完了！
example_sentences.english: Mission complete!

example_sentences.japanese: この町でしばらくつづいていたさい開発工事がようやく完了した。
example_sentences.english: The redevelopment that's been ongoing for a while in this town has finally been completed.

example_sentences.japanese: 携帯の充電が完了してから折り返してもいいかな？
example_sentences.english: I’ll call you back when my cellphone battery has finished charging, okay?

notes: "When you have gentle cooperation nobody has their way. You're very gently coming towards the middle, coming to a compromise. (Whether you like it or not.)" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 妥協したくないの。
example_sentences.english: I don't want to give in.

example_sentences.japanese: うまく妥協することができなくて、ちょっとせい神的に参っちゃったんだよね。
example_sentences.english: I couldn't compromise very well and everything came apart at the seams.

example_sentences.japanese: この仕事に、妥協は許されないよ。
example_sentences.english: At this job, compromise is not allowed.

notes: "There is a reason for this fee that you have to pay to get in here. We are doing cooking and cuisine for you to eat while you're watching the show. If we weren't doing cooking, we probably wouldn't charge you this fee!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: メニューには魚料理がたくさんございますが、みなさんどれになさいますか？
example_sentences.english: There's a lot of fish on the menu. What is everyone getting?

example_sentences.japanese: マミは、カリフラワーを白いブロッコリーだとかんちがいして料理しました。
example_sentences.english: Mami mistook the cauliflower for white broccoli and cooked it.

example_sentences.japanese: 簡単な料理しかできません。
example_sentences.english: I can only cook simple cuisine.

notes: "The hope you request is your desire. Just imagine yourself hoping and requesting some higher power for something you really want. What is this? It's your desire or wish." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 世界が平和であってほしいと強く願望しています。
example_sentences.english: I wish so strongly for world peace.

example_sentences.japanese: 「お金をためて早期リタイアして毎日一日中ゲーム三まいというゆめを見ました。」「ゆめは願望の表れって言いますよね。それがあなたの願望なんですよ。」
example_sentences.english: """I had a dream where I retired early and played video games all day, every day."" ""They say dreams reflect your desires. That must be what you desire."""

example_sentences.japanese: 結婚願望はあるんだけど、なかなか理想通りの相手が見つからなくてさ。
example_sentences.english: I want to get married but can’t find anyone that’s up to my standards.

notes: "There is fault in your hope. It breaks, and everything falls apart. You feel massive disappointment and despair." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ホイップクリームたっぷりでって言ったのに、全然たっぷりじゃなくて失望しています。
example_sentences.english: I'm disappointed that there isn't a lot of whipped cream in this even though I asked for extra.

example_sentences.japanese: あの先生は、期待していたよりも英語が上手じゃなくて失望しました。
example_sentences.english: That teacher isn't good at speaking English like I thought they'd be, so I'm disappointed.

example_sentences.japanese: マジ、自分に超失望中だよ〜。ノースリーブのシャツが着たいんだけど、ポッチャリ二の腕が気になってさ。しかも、腰まわりもたるんできたし。彼氏は私のポッチャリした指が好きだとか言うんだけど、そんなの全然嬉しくないってのさ。
example_sentences.english: I’m really disappointed. I want to wear sleeveless shirts, but my chubby arms bother me a lot. My waist is getting flabby, too. My boyfriend tells me that he likes my pudgy fingers, but it doesn’t make me happy at all, you know?

notes: "This has almost the same meaning as the kanji it comes from. Instead of just simply being ""example,"" though, it's for example. So, you could start a sentence with this and be all like ""例えば, I am using 例えば in a sentence.""" "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: Using all kinds of ""for examples"" like this, you were taught (たと) many things throughout your life. For example, you were taught about..."

example_sentences.japanese: 例えば、昔はすごく人気があったけど、今は落ちぶれてしまった人がいたとしましょう。
example_sentences.english: For example, let's say there was a person who used to be very popular but isn't at all anymore.

example_sentences.japanese: 例えば、舌をかみそうになった時、コウイチなら何て言うと思う？
example_sentences.english: For instance, what do you think Koichi would say when he almost bit his tongue?

example_sentences.japanese: なぁ、さくらちゃん、例えば、週に一度や二度ぐらい、うちに来ないか？
example_sentences.english: Hey, Sakura, why don’t you come over to my house, like, once or twice a week or something?

notes: "An attempt to join together isn't just any get together. Imagine two people boxing. They attempt to knock each other out when they join together. That's why this word is game or match. Did you watch the 試合 today? No! Don't tell me what happened, I recorded it on the VHS." "This word uses the on'yomi し for 試 and the kun'yomi あい for 合. You learned both of these readings already, so you should be able to put them together!"

example_sentences.japanese: 良かったらもう一試合しませんか？
example_sentences.english: If you don't mind, why don't we play another game together?

example_sentences.japanese: けん道の試合の結果はどうでしたか？
example_sentences.english: What was the outcome of the kendo match?

example_sentences.japanese: 「あの野球の試合は本当にひどかったね。」「本当にそうだね。」
example_sentences.english: """That baseball game was really terrible."" ""Yeah, tell me about it."""

notes: "What your thoughts request inside your head, nonstop like a crazy person, are your heart's desires." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは、世界の平和を念願して、出家しました。
example_sentences.english: Koichi earnestly wished for world peace and became a priest.

example_sentences.japanese: ついに長年の念願だったアフリカ旅行を実げんしました。
example_sentences.english: I finally realized my long-awaited dreams of traveling in Africa.

example_sentences.japanese: やったー！ついに念願の彼氏ができたよー！やっぱ一生懸命願えば叶うもんだね！超幸せー！
example_sentences.english: Yay! After all this waiting, I finally got a boyfriend. I guess if you wish hard enough, you really can get what you want. I’m so happy!

notes: "You've hopefully seen how 登る means ""to climb."" So, if you're climbing a mountain what is that? It's mountain climbing." "The reading comes from combining 山 and 登る together to form one word, 山登り. If you know the readings of those two words you know the reading of this word too."

example_sentences.japanese: 山登りがしゅ味なんですか？
example_sentences.english: Is mountain climbing your hobby?

example_sentences.japanese: ものしずかな友人と、山登りに行ってきました。
example_sentences.english: I went to climb a mountain with my quiet friend.

example_sentences.japanese: お互い色々あったんだけど、山登りをしながらじっくり話し合ってさ。なんと復縁することになったよ。
example_sentences.english: Both of us have been through a lot, but we had a long talk while climbing a mountain and decided to get back together.

notes: "One circumference is one time around. How many times will you go around the moon? Just 一周?" "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Note that the いち becomes いっ as it often does when being used in a counter (一階, 一回, etc.)."

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは、最後の一周で十人のランナーをゴボウぬきした。
example_sentences.english: Koichi passed ten runners on the final lap.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチはグラウンド一周を三分台で走ります。
example_sentences.english: Koichi can run one lap of the track in three to four minutes.

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグチームは世界一周旅行に出かけるので、オフィスは約一年間不在となります。
example_sentences.english: The Tofugu team is going to make a trip around the world, so the office will be closed for about a year.

notes: "The remainder of time that you work at the ol' business is extra time that you're working (above the normal work hours). This is overtime!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ちゃんときゅう料が支はらわれるなら、残業してもいいですよ。
example_sentences.english: If I get paid properly I don't mind working overtime.

example_sentences.japanese: 残業中に、材木がおちてきて、九死に一生をえることになりました。
example_sentences.english: While I was working overtime, the wood fell and I narrowly escaped death.

example_sentences.japanese: 残業後にイタメシ屋でお一人様しちゃったよ〜。なかなか寂しかったぜぃ(笑)
example_sentences.english: After working overtime I went to an Italian restaurant alone. I felt pretty lonely lol.

notes: "A beforehand promise is a promise you've made beforehand. This is a reservation or appointment. Makes sense, right?" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: パーマとカットの予約をしたいんですけど。
example_sentences.english: Could I make an appointment for a haircut and a perm?

example_sentences.japanese: 2020年に日本へ行くなら早めに予約した方がいいですよ。その年は東京オリンピックがありますから。
example_sentences.english: If you're planning to go to Japan in 2020, you'd better book early because that's the year of the Tokyo Olympics.

example_sentences.japanese: ただ今、コウイチのサイン入りブロマイドの先行予約を受け付けております。予約された方の中から抽選で三名の方にコウイチのファンミーティングinハワイのVIPチケットをプレゼントいたします。皆様どしどしご応募ください！
example_sentences.english: We are currently accepting advance reservations for Koichi's picture with his autograph. Among the people who made a reservation, we will offer three of you VIP tickets for Koichi's fan meeting in Hawaii. Please don't wait to reserve your spot!

notes: "A diagram everyone joins together to see is a sign!" "This word uses the kun'yomi reading for 合 and the on'yomi reading for 図. You know them both now, so you should be able to read this too!"

example_sentences.japanese: わたしが合図をしたら、大声で「エイドリアーン！」とさけんでください。
example_sentences.english: "When I give the signal, yell, ""Adrian!"" loudly."

example_sentences.japanese: わたしに、売りか買いかの合図の出し方をおしえてくれませんか？
example_sentences.english: Can you teach me how to give the buy or sell signal, please?

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は彼に、秘密の合図を送った。
example_sentences.english: She sent a secret signal to him.

english: To Make Someone Wait, To Keep Someone Waiting, To Make Wait, To Keep Waiting
notes: "This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means wait so this word has something to do with waiting. Use the たせ as a hint. Someone ""tossed"" a ball off into a ditch, and then they had to find it. They made you wait for them to get the ball too, even though it's a cheap piece of crap. Feel upset about this." "You learned this reading from 待つ, congrats!"

example_sentences.japanese: 先ぱいを待たせるのはよくないよ。
example_sentences.english: It’s not okay to keep your senpai waiting.

example_sentences.japanese: 一体何時まで待たせるつもりですか？
example_sentences.english: How much longer will I have to wait?

example_sentences.japanese: お待たせしてすみません。いや〜バスにえらく長いこと待たされましてね。
example_sentences.english: Sorry for making you wait so long. I had to wait for the bus for such a long time.

english: To Warm Up, To Warm, To Heat Up, To Heat
notes: "Have you seen 温かい (warm) yet? Probably. If you have, you can guess that the verb version is to warm up or to warm." "The reading is the same like 温かい. As long as you know that word, you should be able to associate that reading with this word."

example_sentences.japanese: その器は電子レンジで温めないでください。
example_sentences.english: Please don't heat that bowl in the microwave.

example_sentences.japanese: 夜ねる前に牛にゅうを温めてホットミルクにして飲むのが好きです。
example_sentences.english: Before I go to bed, I like to heat up milk and drink it.

example_sentences.japanese: 水に入れて温めると、昆布のうまみ成分がしみ出てきます。
example_sentences.english: Kombu seaweed releases its sweet flavor when it’s soaked in water and heated up.

notes: "The place you wait to join other people is a waiting room or a meeting place." "The readings for this word are both kun'yomi readings, but it's like the hiragana that normally sticks out is stuffed in. 待ち → 待, 合い → 合 and is pronounced the same too. I know it's confusing, but once you get it down you'll never forget!"

example_sentences.japanese: 合図をしたら、待合でスクワットを始めてください。
example_sentences.english: Start squatting in the meeting place on my signal.

example_sentences.japanese: 待合する場所がさむすぎて、ぼうこうえんになりました。
example_sentences.english: The waiting room was so cold that I got a bladder infection.

example_sentences.japanese: 病院の待合でばったり久しぶりに友人に会って、昔話に花がさきました。
example_sentences.english: I ran into a friend from a long time ago in the waiting room of the hospital and we chatted about the old days.

notes: "When it comes to building and constructing, the thing that puts them all together into one is architecture. If you don't have any architecture, who knows what the building will look like." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: あの会社が建築したビルは、たいしん基じゅんをみたしていません。
example_sentences.english:
The building constructed by that company doesn't meet
current quake-resistance standards.

example_sentences.japanese: この建築ひ用の内わけを教えてもらえますか？
example_sentences.english: Can I see a breakdown of these construction costs, please?

example_sentences.japanese: 多くの人が京都や奈良に残る日本の伝統建築に魅了されますが、私もその一人です。
example_sentences.english: Many people are fascinated by the traditional architecture found in places like Kyoto and Nara and I’m one of them.

notes: "The noun form of request (don't be tricked by the い on the end, it's not an adjective). So, request goes to a request." "The reading is the same like お願いします. Hopefully you're able to read that by now so you're able to read this too."

example_sentences.japanese: お願い！手伝って！
example_sentences.english: Please! Help me!

example_sentences.japanese: 「ちょっとお願いがあるんだけど……。」「もちろん。言ってみて。」
example_sentences.english: """Can you do me a favor...?"" ""Of course. Name it."""

example_sentences.japanese: 中小企業は小回りが利くから、こういう仕事をお願いしても平気だろう。
example_sentences.english: Smaller companies take on new challenges more rapidly, so they probably won't mind if we request a job like this.

notes: "When you measure and then calculate something, you are making a calculation. For example, you measure the length of a frog, then you calculate how many frogs you'd need to reach the moon. What is that? A calculation, of course." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトは今、飲み放題のパーティーにかかるひ用を計算しています。
example_sentences.english: Viet is calculating the cost of the all you can drink party now.

example_sentences.japanese: ああ見えて、コウイチは計算がものすごく速いんです。
example_sentences.english: Koichi is very quick at calculations, though he doesn't look it.

example_sentences.japanese: お母さん！こんなに沢山の計算をしたら、数学の天才になるかわりに逆に頭がおかしくなっちゃうよ。
example_sentences.english: Mom! If I do all of these calculations, instead of becoming a math genius, I’ll just lose my mind.

notes: "Change and change equals even more change." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは、天こうの変化にとてもびん感で、雨の日はよくへん頭痛をわずらっています。
example_sentences.english: Koichi is very sensitive about changes in the weather and he often gets migraines on rainy days.

example_sentences.japanese: 十年前におとずれた時とくらべて、東京はずいぶんと変化しましたね。
example_sentences.english: Tokyo has changed a lot since I visited ten years ago.

example_sentences.japanese: うわ！すごいね。既に変化が現れているのが分かるよ。
example_sentences.english: Wow! This is amazing! I can see the change already.

notes: "When you believe in your self you have plenty of confidence (or self confidence). This is a good thing to have!" "How much 自信 do you have that you know how to read this word already? I bet you have some, at least! This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well."

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは大変な自信家です。
example_sentences.english: Koichi is quite the self-confident person.

example_sentences.japanese: もっと自信を持った方がいいよ！
example_sentences.english: You should have more confidence in yourself.

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトは、誰よりもコウイチのことをよく知っているので、誰よりもうまくコウイチの顔を描ける自信があると言っていた。
example_sentences.english: Viet said he was sure he could draw Koichi’s face better than anyone else because he knew him better than anyone else.

notes: "Think about a part of the district. Separate them out in your mind (these parts). Each part is a division of the district. You can also take each division and create a classification of them. Go ahead and classify each one." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: この町では、校区が三つに区分されています。
example_sentences.english: In this town, the school district is divided into three divisions.

example_sentences.japanese: これは予算区分の問題なので、私にはどうしようもありません。
example_sentences.english: This is a problem of budget classification, so I have nothing to do with it.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は、テロ行為と合法的な戦争を区分する必要は無いと思います。
example_sentences.english: I don’t think it’s necessary to distinguish terrorism from legitimate warfare.

notes: "What you believe in your heart, and not in your head, is your faith. This is something that doesn't follow logic, it's all heart belief, it's all faith." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Just note that しん changes to じん."

example_sentences.japanese: 私の母は仏教を信心しています。
example_sentences.english: My mother believes in Buddhism.

example_sentences.japanese: 信心ぶって他人をひはんしてくるから、あの子のことあんまり好きじゃないんだよね。
example_sentences.english: I don't really like her because she sanctimoniously criticizes people.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の家族はとても信心深くてスピリチュアルなので、他のお酒を飲まずにスピリッツだけ飲みます。
example_sentences.english: His family is very religious and spiritual, so they don't drink any alcoholic drink other than spirits.

english: Newly Built, New Building, New Construction
notes: "Something that's newly constructed is something that's newly built." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 新築の家でも買えば、気分が晴れるよ。
example_sentences.english: Buying a newly built house will cheer you up.

example_sentences.japanese: 新築のマンション以外には住みたくありません。
example_sentences.english: I don't want to live anywhere other than a new apartment building.

example_sentences.japanese: 悲しいことに夫に捨てられちゃいました。新築の一軒家を買ったばっかりなのに。話を聞いてほしいんだけど。
example_sentences.english: I’m sad. My husband left me even though we just bought a newly built house. I need someone to talk to.

notes: "When poison is put inside of something, that is a poisoning." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 食中毒でかこきゅうになり、きゅうきゅう病院へはん送されました。
example_sentences.english: I hyperventilated from food poisoning and had to be taken to the emergency room.

example_sentences.japanese: ガス中毒にならないよう気を付けてくださいね。
example_sentences.english: Be careful not to get gas poisoning.

example_sentences.japanese: フグは麻薬中毒から逃れようとしてリハビリセンターに行ったが、結局また麻薬中毒になってしまった。
example_sentences.english: Fugu tried to rid himself of drug addiction and went to rehab, but eventually ended up relapsing.

notes: "You gotta believe it will return. What are you believing in returning? The reply. You made a request for something (come up with something you want really bad but have to ask for). Now you wait for the reply." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: やばい、返信するのわすれてた。ちょっと大変なことになってしまうかも。
example_sentences.english: Oh no, I forgot to reply. What have I gotten myself into?

example_sentences.japanese: き読になったのに、いつまでたっても返信が来ないんだよね。
example_sentences.english: "It said ""read,"" but I never got a reply."

example_sentences.japanese: お疲れ〜。返信したつもりだったんだけど、どうやら力尽きて、送信ボタンを押す前に寝てたみたい。ごめんね、許して〜。
example_sentences.english: How’s it going? I thought I sent a reply to you, but it seems that I was too tired and fell asleep before pressing the ’send’ button. Sorry. Forgive me.

english: Serious, Terrible, Very, Difficult, Hard, Hectic
notes: "A big change is a really serious thing. And people don't like change, either, making it a terrible event. Also, in more recent history this has come to mean very as well." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語を習とくするのは大変ですが、がんばってくださいね。
example_sentences.english: Acquiring Japanese is difficult, but do your best!

example_sentences.japanese: 大変丈夫な子供が生まれました。
example_sentences.english: They had a very healthy child.

example_sentences.japanese: 災害時は、電話回線もネット回線も混み合って、繋がりづらくなるので、ブログの更新が大変です。
example_sentences.english: When there's a disaster, the phone and Internet circuits are overloaded and it gets hard to connect to them, so it's difficult to upload new blog posts.

notes: "If you're moving towards (に) simple, you're saying simply or merely. This is one of those words that come at the beginning of a sentence. ""Simply... """ If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは単に大変な努力家なだけですよ。
example_sentences.english: It's simply because Koichi is a very hard worker.

example_sentences.japanese: 「トーフグは、私にとっては単にお金をかせぐためのものではないんです。トーフグこそが私の人生なんです。」と、コウイチは言った。
example_sentences.english: "Koichi said, ""To me, Tofugu is not merely for earning money. It's my life."""

example_sentences.japanese: 剣道では、単に相手を倒すことだけではなく、自らの心を鍛えることも重要です。
example_sentences.english: In kendo, it’s important not simply to defeat your opponent but also to train your own mind.

english: To Be Fond Of, To Like
notes: "You know that 好き is ""like."" Although 好き is kind of like a verb already, this is definitely a verb. It can be to be fond of or to like." "The reading is a strange one, different from anything you've learned, kanji on'yomi or vocab kun'yomi. The reading is この, so think of this. What is it that you're particularly fond of? Getting a cone (この) with your ice cream (which you're also fond of, who isn't?). Think of all the different cones you can get: waffle cones, sugar cones, oreo cones, yum!"

example_sentences.japanese: この日本酒は、大変酒好きだった私の父が生前に好んで飲んでいたものです。
example_sentences.english: This Japanese sake is what my heavy drinker of a father liked when he was alive.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは、黒ニンニクを好んで食べます。
example_sentences.english: Koichi likes eating black garlic.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチさん、申し訳ありませんが、好むと好まざるとに関わらず、あなたの秘密は暴露されてしまうかもしれません。
example_sentences.english: I’m sorry, Mr. Koichi. Whether you like it or not, your secrets might get revealed.

english: To Fire, To Hit, To Break Wind, To Let Loose, To Set Free
notes: "This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. You already learned the verbs 放す and 放れる but this one is a little different. This is a specific kind of releasing. It means to fire an arrow, or to hit a baseball. It even works when you're releasing a fart. Yes, it means to break wind too. What a great word!" Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You learned this reading already so you should be able to read it!

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは、するどく変化するサーブを放つバレーボール選手として知られている。
example_sentences.english: Koichi is known for being a volleyball player that can serve a very sharp curveball.

example_sentences.japanese: その選手は、ホームランを放ったしゅん間、くさいオナラも放った。
example_sentences.english: That player let out a stinky fart as soon as he hit a home run.

example_sentences.japanese: この鳥をいつか籠から放つつもりですか。
example_sentences.english: When are you thinking of letting this bird out of the cage?

english: To Look Back At, To Triumph Over
notes: "When you want to see something one more time before you have to return it, you need to look back at it. It might be your last chance to look at it, you know?" "The readings are from the words 見 and 返す put together."

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグの社長になって、コウイチを見返してやるぞ！
example_sentences.english: I will be the Tofugu president and show Koichi, who looked down on me, what I can do.

example_sentences.japanese: 子猫にイワシをあげたら、「本当にいいの？」って感じの顔でマジマジと見返してきたのがマジかわいかった。
example_sentences.english: "When I gave the kitten some sardines, she looked back at me with a face that was like, ""Is this really for me?!"" and it was super cute."

example_sentences.japanese: 答案は提出する前に見返したほうがいい。
example_sentences.english: You should look back over your test before you submit it.

notes: "When you join all your measurements together you have yourself a total." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトのさぎにひっかかったひがい者の合計は、百人になった。
example_sentences.english: The total number of the victims who were fished by Viet's scam came to one hundred.

example_sentences.japanese: 合計金がくを出してもらっていいですか？
example_sentences.english: Can you come up with the total for me, please?

example_sentences.japanese: 何度も足し算をしたんですが、その度に合計が違ったんですよね。私、馬鹿なんでしょうか？
example_sentences.english: I added the numbers over and over again and got a different sum each time. Am I stupid?

english: Traffic Light, Signal, Traffic Signal, Stoplight, Semaphore
notes: "If you believe in the numbers, there will be no traffic because the traffic light will be functioning properly. Traffic lights are based all off of traffic data and numbers. You just have to believe and hope it all works out in terms of these traffic lights." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 赤信号で止まって、青信号でわたるのよ。
example_sentences.english: You stop at a red light and cross the street at a green light, okay?

example_sentences.japanese: あぶないから、信号をむししてはいけませんよ。
example_sentences.english: It's dangerous to ignore traffic lights, so don't do that okay?

example_sentences.japanese: いいか、よく聞けよ。六つ目の信号で左折した後、八つ目の角まで歩いて右折したら、そこで会った人に向かってお尻を振るんだ。それが秘密のサインだからな。そしたら、奴はお前を俺たちのアジトまで連れて行ってくれるさ。
example_sentences.english: Listen carefully. Turn left at the sixth traffic light, walk another eight blocks, turn right and shake your butt toward someone you will meet there. That’s the secret sign, okay? Then, he will take you to our hideout.

notes: "A strange death is one that doesn't seem right. It's an unnatural death, and probably an accidental death (ie wasn't caused by natural causes)." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: けいさつは、コウイチの変死についてちょうさしています。
example_sentences.english: The police are investigating Koichi's unnatural death.

example_sentences.japanese: 「なんかパニクってるけど、どうしたの？」「コウイチは変死して、トーフグがとうさんするって聞いたんだよ。最悪だよ。」
example_sentences.english: """You look upset. Is everything alright?"" ""I just heard that Koichi died an accidental death and Tofugu went bankrupt. It’s a nightmare."""

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチが謎の変死を遂げたというニュースは、全国民を震撼させた。
example_sentences.english: The news that Koichi met a mysterious and unnatural death shocked the nation.
