notes: "If you are able to enter the gate then you have gained admission and entrance to the facility." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは有名な剣道の先生のところに入門するそうですよ。
example_sentences.english: I heard that Koichi is going to be a pupil of the famous kendo master.

example_sentences.japanese: 入門手つづきをまだ終えていません。
example_sentences.english: I haven't completed the admissions procedure yet.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語に馴染みのない私にとっても、テキストフグは絶好の入門書だと思う？買った方がいいかな？
example_sentences.english: Do you think that TextFugu is the best introduction to Japanese, even for someone like me who’s unfamiliar with it? Should I buy it?

notes: "You dare to do something risky. It's adventure time! Imagine yourself daring yourself to do risky things. Is this an adventure? If not, make it so!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトは仕事を残したまま、冒険に出かけた。
example_sentences.english: Viet left the work unfinished and went on an adventure.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日からの冒険のために、力を残しておいた方がいいよ。
example_sentences.english: We should reserve our energy for our adventure tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: 私たち、ナイル川を遡るっていう冒険旅行をしたんだけど、彼氏が西ナイル熱にかかっちゃってさあ。未だに病院で入院してるんだよね。
example_sentences.english: We went on an adventure trip up the Nile River, but my boyfriend caught West Nile Virus and he is still in the hospital.

english: Complete Recovery, Healed, Fully Recovered, Fully Recover, Healed Completely, Heal Completely, Completely Cured, Fully Cured, Fully Healed
notes: "All cured! That means you've made a complete recovery! You're healed!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 医者には、全治するのは難しいと思う、多分後いしょうが残るだろうって言われました。
example_sentences.english: The doctor told me that it's difficult to recover completely and I'd probably have some permanent damage left over.

example_sentences.japanese: 交通きそくをきちんと守っていたのに、トラックにはねられて全治一年の大ケガをしました。
example_sentences.english: Although I was observing the traffic rules strictly, I was hit by a truck and got a bad injury that would take a year to heal completely.

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトが暴力団抗争で全治六カ月の重傷を負った時、コウイチは特殊治癒能力を使ってその傷を治した。
example_sentences.english: When Viet suffered severe cuts from a gang war that would have normally taken six months to heal completely, Koichi healed him with his special healing powers.

notes: "A connection related to another connection obviously has some kind of connection, at least between all those meanings." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトはヤクザだが、そのはんざいには関係してないとだん言できます。
example_sentences.english: Viet is a yakuza, but I can say for sure that he is not connected to that crime.

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトは、ヤクザとの関係をたってトーフグの仕事に専念するかどうかまよっています。
example_sentences.english: Viet is wondering if he should cut his connections with the yakuza and just focus on his work at Tofugu.

example_sentences.japanese: 「彼は前に結婚していて、子供も3人もいるのよ。」「知ってるわよ。でも、それとこれとは関係ないでしょ。」
example_sentences.english: """He’s been married before and has three kids."" ""I know, but that has nothing to do with it."""

english: Covering An Event, Collecting Data, Data Collection, Interview
notes: "Your job is to take materials from a bunch of different people because you're covering an event. This data collection needs to be thorough, so you try to take all the materials you can from as many people as you can find." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 取材にご協力いただけませんか。
example_sentences.english: I'm wondering if you would allow us to get an interview?

example_sentences.japanese: テレビの取材を受けた時に、金が全てではないと答えたところが、ニュース番組に使われていました。
example_sentences.english: The clip where I was interviewed by a TV crew and I said that money isn't everything was used for a news program.

example_sentences.japanese: 無理は承知なんですが、どうにかご主人を取材させてもらうことはできないでしょうか？もし何とかして頂ければ、本当に本当に感謝します。
example_sentences.english: I know it’s difficult, but isn’t there any way that I could collect some data on your husband? If you could help me set up the interview, I would really really appreciate it.

notes: "Far feet are feet that have gone on long excursions. These feet have been on some trips, man. They've seen some things." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 学校の遠足で、動物園に行きました。
example_sentences.english: We went on a school trip to the zoo.

example_sentences.japanese: 春になったら、海に遠足しようよ。
example_sentences.english: When spring comes, let's go on an outing to the ocean.

example_sentences.japanese: 遠足で阪神甲子園球場に野球観戦に行って、阪神タイガースを応援しました。
example_sentences.english: We went on an excursion to Hanshin Koshien Stadium to watch a baseball game and root for the Hanshin Tigers.

notes: "Things that hurry and go faster than the other things are express. This is often used with trains or subways, so look out for it if you're looking to get somewhere in a hurry. Also be careful in case it doesn't stop at your stop, because 急行 trains don't stop at every station (which is what makes them express!)." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: けいさつは、はんざいげん場へ急行しました。
example_sentences.english: The police officer hurried to the scene of the crime.

example_sentences.japanese: 私にやさしくしてくれた人たちに、急行便でお礼の品を送りました。
example_sentences.english: I sent thank you gifts express to the people who were nice to me.

example_sentences.japanese: あーーーしまったーーーー。急行列車が行ってしまった。ってことは私の遅刻も確定だ。コウイチから受ける処罰がすんごく怖いんですけど。
example_sentences.english: Oh noooooo! The express train left. Now I'm going to be late. I’m really scared of being punished by Koichi.

notes:
"Evidence that something will be preserved is a form of guarantee, at least as long as the evidence is strong enough. Also, 保 also means guarantee, so use that to help you to remember this word." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

"Preserve your current state and avoid any hindering of you. That is our guarantee and security." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: うまく組しきを固められる保証はありませんよ。
example_sentences.english: There is no guarantee that I could strengthen the organization well though.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はワニカニのライフタイムメンバーですが、トーフグが五年後もあるなんて保証はないから本当にライフタイムでワニカニが使えるなんて思っていませんよ。
example_sentences.english: I am a lifetime member of WaniKani, but I don't really think I can use it for a lifetime, as there is no guarantee that Tofugu will still be around in five years.

example_sentences.japanese: 恐らく灰色熊が近寄ってくるかと思いますが、とても安全なのでご安心ください。ご保証致します。
example_sentences.english: The grizzly bears will probably approach you, but don’t worry. It’s very, very safe. We guarantee it.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本にはどんな社会保障がありますか。
example_sentences.english: What kind of social security is there in Japan?

notes: "We try to preserve anything we want to exist with preservation. Want a special sea creature or bird to exist? Up conservation efforts! And, if you want to save data (like on a computer), you can use this word for that kind of saving, as well." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチのデスクのかぎのかかった引き出しに、重要文書が保存されています。
example_sentences.english: Important documents are being stored in the locked drawer of Koichi's desk.

example_sentences.japanese: 母乳は、れいとうすれば保存がききます。
example_sentences.english: Breastmilk can be preserved for a long time, if you freeze it.

example_sentences.japanese: 「このベーコンは、着色保存料を一切使用しておりません。」「ってことは、本当のベーコンではありませんね。」
example_sentences.english: """This bacon contains no food coloring or preservatives."" ""Well, then it really isn’t bacon."""

notes:
"Is the evidence bright enough to convince me? Is this really proof enough?" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

"Illuminate and make things bright, my illumination!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: クリステンが正真正めいの箱入りむすめであることが証明された。
example_sentences.english: We have verification that Kristen is truly the well-protected daughter of a respectable family.

example_sentences.japanese: 何か身分を証明できる物は持っていますか？
example_sentences.english: Do you have something to verify your identity?

example_sentences.japanese: テキストフグとワニカニの各コースが修了するごとに、修了証明書のようなものが受け取れた方がいいですか？
example_sentences.english: Would you rather receive some sort of certificate proving you finished the TextFugu and WaniKani courses?

example_sentences.japanese: 照明器具の周りを蠅が2-3匹ブンブン飛び交っている。
example_sentences.english: A couple of flies are buzzing around the lighting equipment.

notes: "A laughing face is a  smiling face (or just a smile!). 笑顔s all around!" "The reading for this word won't make you smile, though. You were smiling, but then you heard about the reading of this kanji. It made you yell out ""EH??"" (え)."

example_sentences.japanese: あの笑顔がコウイチのせい実さを証明しているよね。
example_sentences.english: That smiling face proves Koichi's integrity, eh?

example_sentences.japanese: この国の王子は笑顔で国民を殺すとてもひどい男です。
example_sentences.english: The prince of this country is a very terrible man who kills his citizens with a smile.

example_sentences.japanese: この笑顔の素敵な男は俺の連れで、コウイチっていうの。
example_sentences.english: This smiling, lovely guy with me is Koichi.

notes: "You detain your study and take it away to a foreign place. That foreign place is having you study abroad." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. The reading for 留 is the りゅう version. You can remember this because Ryu (りゅう) from street fighter is doing a study abroad program to learn more karate."

example_sentences.japanese: 「兄は親の言いつけを守らず、留学してしまいました。」「留学先はどこなんですか？」「アメリカです。」
example_sentences.english: """My older brother didn't obey the orders of our parents and left to study abroad."" ""Where is his study abroad destination?"" ""It's in the U.S."""

example_sentences.japanese: 留学先で、日本語を自然にしゃべる練習をたくさんしました。
example_sentences.english: When I studied abroad, I practiced speaking Japanese naturally a lot.

example_sentences.japanese: 約束を来週の日曜日に変更していただけませんか？土曜日に、留学の書類を取りに日本総領事館に行かなければならなくなってしまって。
example_sentences.english: Could you reschedule my appointment for next Sunday? On Saturday I have to go to the Japanese Consulate General to get some study abroad documents.

notes: "If you go towards something and hurry while you do it, you are doing it suddenly." "The reading is the same as what you learned with the kanji. Suddenly you can read a new word!"

example_sentences.japanese: 急に空からマッチ箱が一箱ふってきたんです。
example_sentences.english: A matchbox abruptly dropped from the sky.

example_sentences.japanese: えっ、クリステン！急にそんなことを言われても、困るよ...。
example_sentences.english: Oh, Kristen! Even if you tell me something like that immediately, I'm at a loss...

example_sentences.japanese: ファミリー・ガイは、急に馬鹿げた回想シーンを使うことで良く知られている。
example_sentences.english: Family Guy is famous for its random and stupid flashbacks.

notes: "You know that 日光 is sunlight so when you add bathe you get ""sunlight bathe"" ... but that sounds dumb, so let's call this word sunbathe instead!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: トトロの大きなおなかの上に乗って日光浴がしたいです。
example_sentences.english: I want to sunbathe on Totoro's big belly.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は平日は日光浴だけで入浴はしない主ぎなんです。
example_sentences.english: My policy is not to bathe, but to sunbathe on weekdays.

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグのワンコは、ベランダで日光浴をするのが大好きです。
example_sentences.english: The Tofugu dog loves to sunbathe on the balcony.

notes: "Evidence that you say is testimony. Hopefully you won't have to give too much of this in your lifetime." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 全トーフグ社員が、コウイチがビエトのミートボールを食べるのを見たと証言しました。
example_sentences.english: All of the Tofugu workers testified that they had seen Koichi eat Viet's meatball.

example_sentences.japanese: マイケルだけは、コウイチに不利な証言はしたくないと言って、証言を拒否しました。
example_sentences.english: Only Michael refused because he didn't want to testify against Koichi.

example_sentences.japanese: フグが先生の林檎に河豚毒を塗ったと疑われた時、クラスメート全員が彼は無実だと証言した。
example_sentences.english: When Fugu was suspected of placing some puffer fish poison on the teacher’s apple, all his classmates testified that he was innocent.

english: To Know, To Be Aware Of
notes: "This is like a fancy and humble way of saying to know. Sure, the kanji means suppose, but think of it this way... When you say ""I suppose"" it's like a humble way of saying ""I know."" You're not being as direct about it this way, and in Japanese, that makes you more humble and polite. So, that's why 存じる means to know." The reading is the same as the one you learned with the kanji. If you remember the kanji reading, you'll have no problem remembering this vocabulary reading as well!

example_sentences.japanese: 社員たちがしょうきゅうを要求していることは存じておりました。
example_sentences.english: I was aware that workers were making demands for a pay raise.

example_sentences.japanese: つまが弟にお金の返さいを要求していたことは存じませんでした。
example_sentences.english: I didn't know that my wife had demanded that my brother pay the money back.

example_sentences.japanese: 年末でお忙しいとは存じますが、この記事を読んで頂ければ嬉しく存じます。
example_sentences.english: This article will be posted during the busy end of the season, but I would appreciate it if you could read it.

notes: "This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means hard so the verb vocab version? To make hard. You need to differentiate this from 固まる, though, which means ""to harden"" (the hardening happens on its own). This word means ""to make hard,"" because you're doing the hardening. You can remember this because you want to make something hard. And to do that, you send special ""mail"" (める) to this thing you want to make hard, and this mail does that for you." "Since the reading for 固 (かた) is different than the one you learned with the kanji, here's a mnemonic to help you out. A caterpillar (かた) forms a cocoon. The caterpillar's cocoon is hard and the caterpillar made it that way. Keep this in mind and you too will blossom into a beautiful butterfly."

example_sentences.japanese: ねん土は熱で固めることができるよ。
example_sentences.english: You can harden clay with heat.

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトは毎朝一時間かけてリーゼントをワックスで固めます。
example_sentences.english: Viet takes an hour to make his pompadour hard every morning.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは、日本に軍隊を派遣する決意を固めた。
example_sentences.english: Koichi decided to fortify his position and send his troops to Japan.

notes: "When a seat is lacking the person it's supposed to have in it, there is an absence. Where is Johnny? Another absence? Ugh. Johnny. C'mon." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Note that the けつ is shortened to けっ as つs often are when in a situation like this."

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は薬学はかせは欠席なんですね。
example_sentences.english: The pharmacy department is absent today, eh?

example_sentences.japanese: 無だん欠席が三回つづいたので、首にしました。
example_sentences.english: I fired him because he no call no show'd three times in row.

example_sentences.japanese: 大変申し訳ないのですが、急な出張が入ってしまったので、今夜の同窓会は欠席させて頂きます。
example_sentences.english: I’m terribly sorry, but an urgent business trip has come up, so I’ll be absent from the reunion party tonight.

notes: "Absolutely an injustice! We must absolutely punish the perpetrator, by all means." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: また是非日本にお来しくださいね。
example_sentences.english: Absolutely, please come back to Japan.

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグのパーティーには是非出席させていただきたいと思っています。
example_sentences.english: I'd absolutely like to attend at Tofugu's party.

example_sentences.japanese: Tofuguの製品に興味がありそうな人を知っていたら、是非私達に知らせてくださいね。
example_sentences.english: By all means, notify us if you know someone who may be interested in Tofugu products.

notes: "Something that goes towards normal is something that happens ordinarily." "The reading is the kun'yomi reading, which you didn't learn. In order to learn it, think of this: Ordinarily, I tune (つね) my violin, but today I just said ""screw it"" and didn't tune it. So, now I sound like crap. Imagine this compared to how I ordinarily sound."

example_sentences.japanese: うちの母は、常に父に愛情を持っているわけではなさそうでした。
example_sentences.english: My mom didn't always seem to be attracted to my dad.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近は、常に十時にはねていますね。
example_sentences.english: Lately, I'm usually asleep by ten.

example_sentences.japanese: 自分の親が常に正しいわけではないことを知るのに、時間がかかる子どももいます。
example_sentences.english: It takes some kids a while to realize their parents aren’t always right.

english: As Usual, As Ever, The Same, As Before
notes: "A mutual change you make with other people will go so smoothly that it will seem like everything is working as usual. It will be like everything is the same as it was before because the change was mutual." The readings for this word are both kun'yomi readings. You've learned both of these readings by now so you should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 相変わらずかっこいい鼻輪をつけてるね。でも、今日は鼻毛が出てるよ。
example_sentences.english: As usual, you've got a cool nose ring, but I can see your nose hairs today.

example_sentences.japanese: 相変わらず面白いことをしてるね。
example_sentences.english: It’s interesting, as usual.

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトは相変わらず、つぶやくような小声で、ヒドイことを言いまくってるね。
example_sentences.english: Viet is muttering an oath under his breath as usual, yeah?

notes: "The people who exit their seats at the end of the show are the number of people who showed up, not counting empty seats. This is the true attendance." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Just note the しゅつ gets changed to しゅっ, as many つs do in this situation."

example_sentences.japanese: 申しわけありませんが、出席は不定期になると思います。
example_sentences.english: I'm afraid that my attendance will probably be irregular.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチのたん生日パーティーには、出席しない予定です。
example_sentences.english: I'm not planning to attend Koichi's birthday party.

example_sentences.japanese: 別の便に乗せていただけますか？どうしても、主要国首脳会議に出席しなくてはならないんです。
example_sentences.english: Could you put me on another flight? I really have to attend the annual G8 leaders summit.

notes: "The discerning you do with your ideas shows your awareness. It shows you're consciously thinking, because you not only know that you have ideas, but you think about them and discern them." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 道をわたる前に、車が来てないことをかくにんするよう意識してください。
example_sentences.english: Please make it a habit to check that there aren't any cars coming before you cross.

example_sentences.japanese: 果物や野さいはけんこうに良いので、意識して食べるようにしています。
example_sentences.english: I consciously eat fruits and vegetables since they are good for your health.

example_sentences.japanese: サーモンは、フグが他の女の子に興味を示そうものなら、意識を失う。
example_sentences.english: As soon as Fugu shows any attention to other girls, Salmon loses consciousness.

english: "Bottom Of One's Heart, Bottom Of My Heart"
notes: "The heart bottom is the bottom of one's heart. Do you want to learn kanji? Do you want to learn it from 心底? Okay, fine, you can move onto the reading then." This word uses the on'yomi reading for the first kanji and the kun'yomi reading for the second kanji. You've learned them both already, so you should be able to read this too!

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチの不治の病が治って、心底うれしいよ。
example_sentences.english: I'm sincerely happy that Koichi's incurable disease actually has been cured.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチには心底からきらわれていると思います。
example_sentences.english: I think Koichi hates me from the bottom of his heart.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい部署、優しい人がいっぱいで、心底ホッとしたよ。
example_sentences.english: There are a lot of nice people in my new department and I feel tremendously relieved.

notes: "The original cause is how you got into this mess. Forget all the things it caused, the first cause is the origin and source of what's going on right now. You can pinpoint one thing that caused all of this!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 愛情からではなく金のためにけっこんしたのが原因で、けんかがたえず、結局りこんしてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: Since we married for money, not for love, we fought a lot and ended up getting divorced.

example_sentences.japanese: 原因不明の山火事で、町は大変なことになっています。
example_sentences.english: Due to the wildfire of unknown origins, the town has been in such a chaotic situation.

example_sentences.japanese: 心配ないよ。ビエトがすでに不具合の原因を突き止めて、現在修復作業中だよ。
example_sentences.english: Don’t worry. Viet has already uncovered the cause of the bugs and is fixing it right now.

notes: "The perfect way to tie up a research paper is with a conclusion." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: この小説は、次号で完結する予定です。
example_sentences.english: This novel will be concluded in the next edition.

example_sentences.japanese: しつ問しようと思ってたけど、勝手に自こ完結しちゃったんだよね。
example_sentences.english: I was about to ask a question, but I ended up coming up with the conclusion by myself.

example_sentences.japanese: この漫画はまだ完結していません。
example_sentences.english: This manga hasn’t been completed yet.

notes: "You can memorize with your self and your self is memorizing things. It's remembering them for later use, which means you have reached a state of consciousness that animals cannot achieve. They just think about things, they don't memorize like you do." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ぎ理の母から、母親としての自覚が無いって言われて、すっごくはらが立ちました。
example_sentences.english: My mother-in-law told me I lack an awareness for maternal responsibilities and that made me super upset.

example_sentences.japanese: 自分がすばらしいワニカニユーザーなんだという自覚を持って、日本語の勉強にはげんでください。
example_sentences.english: Please try to be conscientious about being a great WaniKani user and study Japanese hard.

example_sentences.japanese: 禁煙して三ヶ月になるけど、まだ時々煙草を吸いたいという衝動に駆られるね。興味深いことに、煙草が吸いたくなる時、自分ではそれをあまり自覚してないんだ。自分の人差し指を噛みしめているのに気づいて、ようやく自覚するんだよ。
example_sentences.english: I’ve stopped smoking for three months now, but I still get the urge to smoke a cigarette every once in a while. Interestingly, when I really want to smoke, I’m not really aware of it. I only just realize it when I find myself chewing on my index finger.

notes: "When you make your theory bright (and clear and easy to understand) you must have come up with an explanation for it. Before it was dark and murky in everyone's mind. But, when you give your explanation, it gets bright and easy to understand! Yay!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 電車のスピードを急に落とした理由を説明してください。
example_sentences.english: Please explain why you suddenly slowed down the train.

example_sentences.japanese: あんな無茶苦茶な説明で、よく会社の社長がつとまるよな。
example_sentences.english: How could he be fit to be company president with a terrible explanation like that?!

example_sentences.japanese: ごめん。さっぱり分からないよ。要約すると、説明の趣旨は何なの？
example_sentences.english: I’m sorry, I don’t understand at all. What does your explanation mean?

notes: "A fault and a failure, all in one. This must have been one big failure and mistake you've made." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. The 失 gets shortened, though. Don't make that 失敗."

example_sentences.japanese: こっちの選手はバントを失敗したと思ったら、今度はこっちの選手がとうるいに失敗したんだよ。
example_sentences.english: When this player failed to bunt, this other player was caught stealing.

example_sentences.japanese: 失敗して後かいする方が、何もせずに後かいするよりマシだと思うんだ。
example_sentences.english: I think failure is still better than doing nothing at all and then regretting that you didn't even try.

example_sentences.japanese: 正直言って、君が作ったこの映画は失敗作だね。でも、一度失敗したからといって、くよくよしてちゃ駄目だよ。誰かも、「成功とは、失敗から失敗へと熱意を失うことなく進んでいける能力である」って言ってただろ？
example_sentences.english: To be honest, this movie you made is a flop. However, you can’t let it get you down just because you failed once. Someone said that success is the ability to go from one failure to another with no loss of enthusiasm, right?

notes: "The fault of romance isn't the romance itself, it's when everything falls apart. It's when you experience heartbreak. Have you ever felt the fault of romance? If so, remember back to that time, and think about how terrible of a fault it is." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ぺちゃんこの赤い鼻が原因で、失恋しました。
example_sentences.english: My heart was broken because of my flat, red nose.

example_sentences.japanese: 失恋なんて、日常茶飯事だよ。
example_sentences.english: Heartbreak is an everyday occurrence for me.

example_sentences.japanese: 失恋しちゃって、超切ないよ。ストレス解消に買い物に行きたい。今週末バーゲンに行ってお昼も一緒に食べようよ。
example_sentences.english: I’m heart broken and it really hurts. I want to go shopping to get rid of my stress. Why don’t we go to the sale this weekend and have lunch together?

notes: "If you can do nothing within reason, then what you're trying to do is unreasonable and probably downright impossible. If you still try, you're probably just overdoing it." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. As long as you know the readings for these kanji, you should be able to read this word just fine.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチはニンニクは便ぴを治す薬だって言ってたけど、ニンニクで便ぴを治すのは無理でしょ。
example_sentences.english: Koichi said that garlic is a cure for constipation, but I'd say curing constipation with garlic is impossible.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチが無理なん題をふっかけても、トーフグチームは無理してなんとかやってのける。
example_sentences.english: Even though Koichi makes unreasonable demands, the Tofugu team manages to meet them by overworking themselves.

example_sentences.japanese: 自分の肘を舐めるのは無理です。
example_sentences.english: It’s impossible to lick your own elbow.

notes: "Okay, so you guess but you also kind of know. You can make an inference as to what the answer is... You're not 100% sure, but you think you know, even though you're guessing." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Note that 察 gets shortened to さっ."

example_sentences.japanese: 昨夜、ビエトがコンピューターの不正利用を察知しました。
example_sentences.english: Last night, Viet detected unauthorized use of the computers.

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトと手下たちは、警察の手入れがあることを事前に察知していたようだ。
example_sentences.english: Viet and his foot soldiers seemed to have sensed that the police would raid them.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕達の赤ちゃんは、母親であるサーモンの感情や不安をすごく敏感に察知するんです。
example_sentences.english: Our baby is very sensitive to the emotions and anxieties of his mom, Salmon.

notes: "When you're fording a stream, and you suddenly feel dry feelings around you, that doesn't make any sense for something wet. This dryness is an interference. It's an intervention trying to stop you from fording." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは、私生活への干渉はしないよう社員たちに注意しました。
example_sentences.english: Koichi warned workers not to interfere in his private life.

example_sentences.japanese: 両国とも、ぶ力干渉はさけたいはずだと思うよ。
example_sentences.english: I assume that both sides want to avoid armed intervention.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは、どんなことにも干渉してくるタイプの上司ではありませんが、何故かビエトが何をしているのかについては口出しするのが好きなようです。
example_sentences.english: Koichi is definitely not the type of boss to interfere, but it seems he likes meddling in what Viet is doing for some reason.

notes: "When you have romance and love all in the same package. Well, that is love! Ah, love! This is the word used when talking about love, though. You don't use this to say ""I love you.""" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 恋愛したら、相手に対していつも愛情を感じすぎてしまうんだよね。
example_sentences.english: When I'm in love, I'm usually way too into them.

example_sentences.japanese: うちの子は、最近恋愛小説ばかり読んでいます。
example_sentences.english: My kid has been reading romance novels all the time lately.

example_sentences.japanese: 恋愛での別れ際は、切なくて甘酸っぱい。
example_sentences.english: Parting from someone you love is always painfully bittersweet.

notes: "When you ford into the thick of things and mix everything up, you're getting involved in a negotiation. That's what negotiations are though, right? You gotta get right in there, fording through the muck. Then, you gotta mix things up and compromise between both parties." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: クリステンは、交渉のプロです。
example_sentences.english: Kristen is a professional negotiator.

example_sentences.japanese: なんとか交渉してみますが、期待はしないでくださいね。
example_sentences.english: I'll try negotiating, but please don't expect anything.

example_sentences.japanese: 新婚旅行の際、フグはサーモンが値段の交渉が得意だということを知ってとても感心した。
example_sentences.english: On their honeymoon, Fugu was very impressed to find out Salmon is very good at negotiating on prices.

notes: "If you love your self that is self love. Some would call too much self love selfishness as well." The readings are the ones you learned with the kanji, you self lover you.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は自愛デーにすることに自分で決めたので、一日中自愛しまくっちゃいます。
example_sentences.english: I've decided all by myself that today is self love day, so I'm gonna spoil myself all day long.

example_sentences.japanese: 自愛をぎせいにして成り立つものを生きがいにするべきではないと思うんです。
example_sentences.english: I don't think you should make it your purpose in life, if it only works out at the cost of your self care.

example_sentences.japanese: 時節柄、お風邪など召しませぬよう、くれぐれも御自愛くださいませ。
example_sentences.english: I sincerely hope you’ll take good care of yourself and don't catch a cold or anything like that in times like these.

notes: "When you write your name for a government office, they require you to write out your signature. Printing won't do for official government office business." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ここに署名をお願いします。
example_sentences.english: Can I get your signature here, please?

example_sentences.japanese: このたん願書に、一万にんの署名を集めることが目標です。
example_sentences.english: Our goal is to collect 10,000 signatures for this petition.

example_sentences.japanese: 細則を読まずに契約書に署名しない方が良かったことは分かってたんですが、一見したところ大家さんがいい人そうだったので、つい。
example_sentences.english: I knew I shouldn’t have signed the contract before reading the fine print, but the landlord seemed like such a nice person.

english: To Be Defeated, To Be Unsuccessful
notes:
"This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means failure, but ""to failure"" doesn't make sense. What happens when you experience failure, though? Well you get defeated, and you're also unsuccessful. So, this verb is to be defeated and to be unsuccessful." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: You have been defeated. You lay there on the ground, and the fans around the stadium are disgusted with your performance. Some hipster walks up to you and says: ""Yah, Boo"" (やぶ) referring to how poorly you did. ""No boo!"" you reply back. ""Yah boo"" they say again."

"If 破る is ""to tear"" or ""to rip,"" then this is to get torn or to get broken or to get ripped." "The reading comes from 破る."

example_sentences.japanese: ブルージェイズは、レッドソックスに三対一で敗れました。
example_sentences.english: The Blue Jays lost the game to the Red Socks with a score of 1-3.

example_sentences.japanese: みんなが予想していた通り、コウイチは今回ものど自まんコンテストで敗れてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: As we all expected, Koichi was defeated again in the singing contest.

example_sentences.japanese: オリンピックの予選第一回戦で敗れた日本代表のアイスホッケーチームに、怒ってカレーを投げつけた男の話聞いた？
example_sentences.english: Did you hear that a guy got upset with Japan’s national hockey team when they were defeated in the first round of a preliminary game for the Olympics and threw some curry at them?

example_sentences.japanese: ズボンのお尻の部分がいつも最初に破れるんだけど、どうしてだろう。
example_sentences.english: Why do my pants always start wearing out in the butt area first?

english: To Be Encouraged, To Be Lively, To Be In High Spirits, To Cheer Up, To Be Excited, To Be Inspired
notes: "This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means courage so the verb version is what happens when you have lots of it. Someone with courage is probably the kind of person to be lively and to be encouraged." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: Who is the one person who always seems to be encouraged and excited? Isabel (いさ)! She's so positive and always cheers everyone, including herself, up."

example_sentences.japanese: あんなに勇んでたら、あの馬は買えないなぁ。
example_sentences.english: That horse is acting too lively for me to bet on it.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチとビエトは、勇んでオフィスに入って来ました。
example_sentences.english: Koichi and Viet came into the office in high spirits.

example_sentences.japanese: 少年は、喜び勇んで旅に出発した。
example_sentences.english: The boy left for his trip in high spirits.

notes: "This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means sad so the verb form of that is to be sad. Boohoo." "If you're going to be sad about something right now, it will be kana (かな). Don't use kana when you're trying to learn kanji! You'll be sad forever if you're stuck using kana your whole life, so don't let that habit start now, friend."

example_sentences.japanese: かの女は失れんしてとても悲しんでいます。
example_sentences.english: She got dumped and she's very sad.

example_sentences.japanese: 人間だけではなく、動物も仲間の死を悲しみます。
example_sentences.english: Animals, as well as humans, are saddened by the deaths of their friends.

example_sentences.japanese: そう悲しむなって。お前の日本語は今はそれで十分だよ。ただ、勉強することを投げ出さずに、少しずつ上手くなればいいさ。
example_sentences.english: Don’t be sad. Your Japanese is good enough for now. Just don’t stop learning and you’ll improve little by little.

notes: "This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means dry so the verb vocab version is to dry." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: Why do you need to dry something off? Because someone used a hose (ほす) and got everything all wet. Ugh, you shouldn't leave that hose out anymore..."

example_sentences.japanese: セーターはかんそうきに入れないで、干してねって言ったじゃない。
example_sentences.english: I told you not to put the sweater in the dryer but to hang dry it.

example_sentences.japanese: あの芸人、ぜっ対最近干されてるよね。
example_sentences.english: I think that comedian has definitely been deprived of any chance to appear on television recently. Don't you agree?

example_sentences.japanese: 洗濯物を外に干したかったんだけど、物干し竿が壊れちゃって。
example_sentences.english: I wanted to put our laundry outside to dry, but our clothesline just broke.

english: To End, To Be Finished, To Be Exhausted, To Die
notes: "If you tear (てる) up a fruit, its life is going to end. Fruit can't go on when they've been beaten up so much. " "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: The fruit's life is about to end and you laugh, ""Hahahaha (は)!"" And then you start tearing at it more! What's wrong with you? Weirdo..."

example_sentences.japanese: 三日もねてないから、つかれ果てたよ。
example_sentences.english: I haven't slept for three days and I'm exhausted.

example_sentences.japanese: こんなところで果てるわけにはいかないと思ったんです。
example_sentences.english: I thought, I must not die here.

example_sentences.japanese: いつ果てるともなく続く会議に、社員は全員ウンザリしていた。
example_sentences.english: The meeting continued without any sign of ending and the employees were getting fed up.

english: Advance Notice, Forward Notice, Prior Notice
notes: "If you announce something beforehand you will have advance notice. Advance notice is always nice to give." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 大丈夫だよ、コウイチは予告なしにかいこしたりしないよ。
example_sentences.english: You'll be alright. Koichi won't fire you without prior notice.

example_sentences.japanese: 三ヶ月家ちんをたいのうしてしまい、立ちのきを予告されました。
example_sentences.english: I left my rent unpaid for three months and then I was given an eviction notice.

example_sentences.japanese: 殺人予告を告げる手紙が、Tofuguオフィスに届けられた。
example_sentences.english: A letter giving advance notice for a murder arrived at the Tofugu office.

notes:
"When you announce something to a wide audience, you're just throwing your message out there for everyone to hear. This is just a big wide advertisement." "Sorry, you learned the kun'yomi reading with 広. So, think of it this way when you need to remember this word's meaning: You're advertising something. It's a big advertisement to advertise how terrible a person こういち is. Come up with some terrible things he's done so that you can imagine this crazy Koichi advertisement you made and ran on national TV."

"A public announcement is a public notice." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 図書館から借りた本に、スーパーの広告が一枚はさまっていました。
example_sentences.english: In a book I borrowed from the library, there was a grocery store advertisement stuck between the pages.

example_sentences.japanese: クーポンが付いた広告を忘れたので、家にもどらなければいけません。
example_sentences.english: I have to go back home because I forgot the ad with the coupon.

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトはコウイチに、アヤがTofuguの広告にものすごく変わった絵を描いたことを告げ口しました。
example_sentences.english: Viet informed Koichi that Aya created the strangest picture ever for Tofugu’s advertisement.

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグの決算公告、もう見ましたか。
example_sentences.english: Did you already see Tofugu's public, financial announcement?

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグは、日本せいふの官報にコウイチについての重大な公告をのせることにしました。
example_sentences.english: Tofugu decided to put up an important public notice about Koichi in an official telegram.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本には、電子公告規則という法律がありますが、あなたの国はどうですか？
example_sentences.english: There is a law in Japan called the Electronic Public Notice Regulation, do you have anything like that in your country?

notes: "The task of borrowing something is when you're borrowing something. It's also when you get a loan." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: これで、借用金が百万円に達してしまった。
example_sentences.english: My debt has now reached one million yen.

example_sentences.japanese: ちゃんと借用証を書いてくれるんだったら、お金をかしてもいいよ。
example_sentences.english: If you write me an IOU, I don't mind loaning you some money.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語には、別の言語から借用された言葉がたくさんあります。
example_sentences.english: In Japanese, there are a lot of words that have been borrowed from other languages.

notes: "Give your brain a nice wash. No! Wait! It's not as nice as it sounds. This is brainwashing." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 洗脳という言葉は1950年代に生まれた。
example_sentences.english: "The word ""brainwashing"" originated in the 1950s."

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグで最初に受けるトレーニングの中には、トーフグマインドへの洗脳もふくまれている。
example_sentences.english: The training you receive at Tofugu when you start working there includes brainwashing into the Tofugu hive mind.

example_sentences.japanese: 多くの日本のネット住民は、日本のテレビ番組に韓国コンテンツが急増していることを洗脳行為のようなものだとなぞらえる。
example_sentences.english: Many Japanese netizens liken the surge of Korean content on Japanese TV to an act of brainwashing.

notes: "You know how 留守 means ""absence"" or ""away from home""? Well, now that you're absent from your home, it's someone else's  turn to come to your home and take care of it. This person is the caretaker, someone who's looking after one's house." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Knowing 留守 will be important as well."

example_sentences.japanese: 一日二万円で留守番の仕事を引き受けた。
example_sentences.english: I took a housesitting job for 20,000 yen a day.

example_sentences.japanese: アメリカでは小さい子どもだけで留守番させるのはい法です。
example_sentences.english: In America, it's illegal to let small kids look after their homes alone.

example_sentences.japanese: ２ヶ月間旅行したければ、留守番を雇う必要があります。
example_sentences.english: If you want to travel for two months, you need to hire a caretaker.

notes: "A wash that washes cars is a car wash." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Don't confuse this with the same-sounding 戦車 though... unless you're washing your 戦車 in a 洗車..."

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチの車の洗車をしたいという方がいたら、hello@tofugu.comまでメールしてください。
example_sentences.english: If there's someone out there who wants to wash Koichi's car, please email us at hello@tofugu.com.

example_sentences.japanese: 洗車が終わるのを待っている間、ガソリンスタンドのバイトがずっとダラダラ話しかけてきて、かなりウザかった。
example_sentences.english: While I waited for the car wash to finish, the part-timer kept yacking at me and it was really annoying.

example_sentences.japanese: 誰がマネー・ロンダリングするのに洗車ビジネスなんて買うっていうのさ？
example_sentences.english: Who would buy a car wash business to launder money?

notes: "You take a type of something and break it off into a part. This part is the classification of that item." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグの社員をお笑いのレベルで松、竹、梅に分類してください。
example_sentences.english: Please classify Tofugu employees into three grades using pine, bamboo, and plum, based on their level of comedy.

example_sentences.japanese: 動物うらないで、コウイチは自分が羊に分類されたことに大喜びした。
example_sentences.english: Koichi was delighted by the fact that he was classified as a sheep during animal fortunetelling.

example_sentences.japanese: テロリストは人質の扱い方の違いで大きく2つに分類されます。「フレンドリーな奴」と「フレンドリーじゃない奴」です。
example_sentences.english: Terrorists generally fall under two categories according to how they treat hostages: the friendly kind and the unfriendly kind.

notes: "You can often associate ""good"" or ""pure"" things with the color white. So when you announce something that's white (and pure) it's a confession. You're getting out the evil and making yourself white and pure with your announcement." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 「どうして告白にそんなに時間がかかったの？」「告白の仕方が分からなかったんだ。」
example_sentences.english: """Why did you take so long for the confession?"" ""Because I didn't know how to do it."""

example_sentences.japanese: ジャマルはずっとドラクエファンだと公言していたのに、最近ついにファイナルファンタジーのかくれファンだったことを告白した。
example_sentences.english: Jamal has been publicly declaring that he is a fan of Dragon Quest, but recently, he finally confessed that he is a secret admirer of Final Fantasy.

example_sentences.japanese: 会計事務所でのアシスタントの仕事を得た後に、彼女は実は数学があまり得意ではないことを告白した。
example_sentences.english: After getting an assistant position in a finance office, she confessed that she is actually bad at math.

notes: "The money (and gold) you borrow is your debt. Be sure to pay it back before the yakuza come for you." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. The しゃく gets shortened to しゃっ though, so beware. Just think of that like the little bit that you lost to the yakuza, because they weren't happy you didn't pay back your debt. *cut*"

example_sentences.japanese: 新しいけいけんをしてみたくて、借金を作りました。
example_sentences.english: I wanted to have new experiences, so I got myself in debt.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは、ビエトに五千万円借金している。
example_sentences.english: Koichi owes Viet 50,000,000 yen.

example_sentences.japanese: 失敬、失敬、通らせて。借金取りに追われているんだ。
example_sentences.english: Excuse me, excuse me. I’m trying to get through here. I’m running away from a debt collector.

notes: "When you take something and separate it into parts, you want to be especially careful not to give anyone an unequal share. This is especially important because we're dealing with money, and people will flip out and shoot you under the table if you aren't especially accurate." "The readings come from the words 取る and 分ける. So long as you know those words you should be able to read this one as well."

example_sentences.japanese: 取り分けコウイチがどなっている時に、ビエトは一人静かに笑っていました。
example_sentences.english: Viet was chuckling softly to himself, especially when Koichi was yelling.

example_sentences.japanese: ついにJLPT1に合格したんですが、トーフグには取り分け感謝しています。
example_sentences.english: I finally passed JLPT N1 and I'm especially appreciative of Tofugu for that.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は取り分け寒いという訳ではない。
example_sentences.english: It’s not especially cold today.

notes: "Stop! That's prohibition (prohibited)! When something is prohibited and you're forced to stop, that thing is obviously forbidden. If you see this you should probably not do the thing it's telling you not to do." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトは手下たちに、とばくは禁止だと言い聞かせた。
example_sentences.english: Viet admonished his soldiers because gambling is forbidden.

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグは、Youtubeのけんえつによって動画の公開を禁止されました。
example_sentences.english: Tofugu was banned from publishing videos by the Youtube censors.

example_sentences.japanese: 宇宙服を脱ぎっぱなしにするんじゃない！禁止事項の一つだろうが！
example_sentences.english: Don’t take off your spacesuit! It’s one of the things that’s prohibited.

notes: "A news report that covers things beforehand (before they happen) is a forecast. For example, a weather forecast is a 天気予報." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は午後から雨の予報だったことをすっかり忘れていました。
example_sentences.english: It slipped my mind that the forecast had said that it would rain in the afternoon.

example_sentences.japanese: お天気お姉さんは、明日から暑くなるって予報してたけどね。
example_sentences.english: The weather girl said the forecast is calling for hot weather, starting tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: 天気予報によると、カナダは今年はずっと雪が降る見通しです。
example_sentences.english: According to the weather forecast, this year Canada is expecting snow all year round.

notes: "When writing just happens to ""fall"" on the wall (whoops, wasn't me who did that, how strannnnge) it's writing that's not supposed to be where it is. This kind of writing is graffiti." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. 書, however, is kun'yomi in this case and also has rendaku. So just remember that it's read as が for this vocab and you'll be fine."

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチの落書きは今やオークションで百万ドルで落札されるまでになった。
example_sentences.english: Koichi's sketches have increased in value by as much as a million dollars at auctions.

example_sentences.japanese: 新宿駅の地下道には、昔、たくさんの落書きがしてありましたが、今はほとんど見当たりません。
example_sentences.english: There used to be lot of graffiti along the underground passages at Shinjuku Station a long time ago, but we rarely see them now.

example_sentences.japanese: スプレーでの落書きアートは既に少し時代遅れです。新しい芸術家達は、壁の汚れをゴシゴシ擦って洗い落としながらアートを創りだします。
example_sentences.english: Spray-painting graffiti is already a bit old-fashioned. The newer artists create works of art by scrubbing the dirt off the wall.

notes: "Happiness is happiness!" "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You haven't learned this reading yet so here's a mnemonic to help you:If your life is filled with nothing but happiness, every time someone says something to you, all you can do is say, ""Sigh, what (さいわ)?"" You sigh and say what. Because you're too happy to really listen. You're just sighing all day and not paying attention."

example_sentences.japanese: 幸いなことに、ちょうど空車のタクシーがやって来ました。
example_sentences.english: Luckily, an empty taxi just came.

example_sentences.japanese: お役に立てたようで、幸いです。
example_sentences.english: I'm happy that I was able to help you.

example_sentences.japanese: 幸い命に別状はありませんでした。
example_sentences.english: Fortunately, it was not life-threatening.

notes:
"Strike your head against the floor to show your subservient respect by doing the kowtow bow. This is the most respectful bow you can possibly do. (Thank you China, for bringing this word into Japanese and thank you Japanese for bringing this into English.)" "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You haven't learned this reading for 頭 yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you:They used to make you kowtow every single time you came to とうきょう. That's full on head to floor kowtowing in front of everyone who is already in とうきょう to prove that you appreciate being there. They might even make you do it these days too, if you're not being respectful enough while you're there."

"Tall inflation of prices means that there was a sudden price jump and it's waaaay more expensive than it used to be." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 叩頭とは、いわゆる日本の土下座のことです。
example_sentences.english: """Kowtow"" is what is called ""dogeza"" in Japan."

example_sentences.japanese: 部屋の中にいた全員が、王に向かって叩頭した。
example_sentences.english: Everyone in the room kowtowed toward the king.

example_sentences.japanese: その男は、叩頭を拒否したため、刑務所に入れられた。
example_sentences.english: Since the man refused to kowtow, he was put into a jail.

example_sentences.japanese: どうして株価がこんなに高騰しているんだ。
example_sentences.english: Why do stock prices suddenly jump like this?

notes: "The instruction reading may not make a lot of sense, but you've heard this word before. Jump to the reading and you'll know what the meaning of this word is." "The reading is the word 読み (like 読む) and the reading you learned for 訓 combined, making くんよみ. Sounds familiar? It's that kun'yomi reading you've heard so much about."

example_sentences.japanese: この漢字は、訓読みでも音読みでも読めます。
example_sentences.english: This kanji can be read with either the kun'yomi or on'yomi readings.

example_sentences.japanese: この漢字は、訓読みすることができますか？
example_sentences.english: Do you know this kanji's kun'yomi?

example_sentences.japanese: いつも訓読みと音読みを間違えてしまう。
example_sentences.english: I mix up kun’yomi and on’yomi all the time.

notes: "At least way back in the day, things that teach instructions to people are things that teach a lesson or moral. Back in the day, lots of learning was done through storytelling, and storytelling taught lessons and morals, thus, this word." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチの話から、どんな教訓がえられましたか？
example_sentences.english: What moral can you draw from Koichi's story?

example_sentences.japanese: この教訓を無だにはしません。
example_sentences.english: I'll keep this lesson in mind.

example_sentences.japanese: 前職から学んだ最大の教訓を教えてください。
example_sentences.english: Tell me about the biggest lesson you learned from your previous company.

notes: "The way of news is to do lots of news reports." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 同りょう達は、みんなその報道のことをすでに知っていました。
example_sentences.english: All of my coworkers knew about the news report already.

example_sentences.japanese: 今回のテロのことは、日本ではどのように報道されていますか？
example_sentences.english: How will this terrorist attack be reported in Japan?

example_sentences.japanese: 報道によると、本日早朝に起きた玉突き事故で、20匹の魚が地域の病院へ運ばれたそうだよ。
example_sentences.english: According to the news report, twenty fish were transported to a local hospital after a pileup that occurred early this morning.

notes: "If smoke is prohibited you probably shouldn't smoke. Aka no smoking, okay?" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ここが禁煙スペースだってこと、忘れてるわけないじゃない。
example_sentences.english: How could I forget that this is a no smoking area?

example_sentences.japanese: 毎週月曜日は禁煙の日って決めているんです。
example_sentences.english: I've decided to make every Monday a no smoking day.

example_sentences.japanese: 母親に禁煙するように言ったんですが、逆に母親から、禁煙したらおそらく気が狂って、父親と離婚することになると言われました。
example_sentences.english: I told my mom to quit smoking and she told me that if she did, she would probably go crazy and my parents would get divorced.

notes: "I permit that it is possible. So, go ahead, do it. I give you permission." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ワニカニの例文を他で使いたいならマミの許可を取ってくださいね。
example_sentences.english: If you want to use WaniKani's example sentences somewhere else, please get Mami's permission.

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグのコアなファンとのインタビューの許可が下りました。
example_sentences.english: I got permission to interview one of Tofugu's hardcore fans.

example_sentences.japanese: もしコウイチと一緒に写真を撮りたいなら、ビエトの許可が必要です。
example_sentences.english: If you want to take a picture with Koichi, you need permission from Viet.

notes: "You pray and request. This is your prayer." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 無事にビザが取れるよう、祈願しています。
example_sentences.english: I'm praying for my visa to be issued without any issues.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは、火星人の戦勝祈願のおどりをおどることができます。
example_sentences.english: Koichi can do the war dance of the Martians.

example_sentences.japanese: 「サーモンの手術が上手くいきますように！」と、フグは神様に祈願した。
example_sentences.english: """May Salmon’s surgery go well,"" Fugu prayed to God."

notes: "Your thoughts are prayers. These pray thoughts are prayers." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 世界中の全ての人が、祈念しています。
example_sentences.english: All people around the world are praying.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日は原ばくぎせい者いれい平和祈念式典に出席します。
example_sentences.english: I'll attend the peace memorial service for atomic-bomb victims tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: Tofuguの益々の発展と繁栄を祈念して、乾杯！
example_sentences.english: Let’s pray for more and more growth and prosperity for Tofugu, cheers!

notes: "You take your practice and you wash it. Slowly chunks fall off and it becomes more and more simple. You are washing away the gunk on the outside to attain refinement and polish yourself, via practice." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチの洗練されたおもかげを、二度と忘れることはないでしょう。
example_sentences.english: I'll never forget the look of Koichi's refined face.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは十月に行われる詩のコンテストのために下書き中の詩を洗練しようとしている。
example_sentences.english: Koichi is trying to polish a rough draft of his poetry for the poem contest in October.

example_sentences.japanese: サーモンがあんな風に洗練された日本語を話すなんて知らなかった。
example_sentences.english: I didn’t know that Salmon spoke in such refined Japanese like that.

hiragana: しゃくや, しゃっか
english: Renting A House, House For Rent, Rented House
notes: "When you borrow a house you are renting a house. Also, this is a house for rent." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji, but in this case the second kanji can be read as either the on'yomi or kun'yomi. You haven't seen the kun'yomi for 家 yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you:If you're renting a house, someone has to give you the keys and let you in and stuff. You're only renting, after all. So when they let you in they'll say, ""Here's a shack for yah! (しゃくや) Enjoy!""By the way, in the secondary reading, the しゃく goes to しゃっ. You'll see しゃくや more often, though."

example_sentences.japanese: 借家をたん保にお金を借りることは出来ませんよ。
example_sentences.english: You can't borrow money on a rented house.

example_sentences.japanese: 借家けんって、単じゅんに、「借家するけん利」のことでしょう？
example_sentences.english: """Tenants' Rights"" simply means you have the right to rent a house, right?"

example_sentences.japanese: 家を買う代わりに借家を借りる提案をサーモンに切り出そうとしてるんだけど、彼女、その話題には触れないようにしてるみたいなんだよね。
example_sentences.english: I’m trying to talk to Salmon about renting a house instead of buying one, but she kind of keeps skirting the issue.

notes: "Something below your writing isn't what you want to necessarily publish to the world. It's below your writing, after all. This is merely a rough draft." "The reading is all kun'yomi vocab reading, as you can maybe guess from the hiragana sticking out. If you know the readings of the words 下 and 書く separately, you should be able to combine them into one reading."

example_sentences.japanese: いい記事を書くためには下書きをすることが大事です。
example_sentences.english: In order to write a good article, it is important to make a rough draft.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチのオフィスのつくえの引き出しには、高校の時に書いた自作の詩の下書きが大切にしまってあるって知ってる？
example_sentences.english: Did you know Koichi keeps the rough draft for a poem he wrote in high school in his desk drawer in the office?

example_sentences.japanese: アヤって、いつも最初に鉛筆で下書きしてるのかな。それとも、下書き無しで絵を描いてるのかな。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if Aya usually makes a rough pencil drafts first or if she just draws freehand.

notes: "The correct way to sit is this way: traditional Japanese sitting (this is when you sit on your legs and your feet, kneeling). You can also call it seiza. Learning the reading will help with the meaning." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 何でそんなに長い間正座できるの？
example_sentences.english: How can you sit seiza for that long?

example_sentences.japanese: 正座させられると思っていましたが、仏僧のように心が広いコウイチは、私のちこくを許してくれました。
example_sentences.english: I thought Koichi would make me do seiza, but he was as generous as a Buddhist priest and excused me for being late.

example_sentences.japanese: 法要の間長時間正座をしていたので、足がすごく痺れています。
example_sentences.english: I knelt in seiza for so long during the Buddhist memorial service that my legs were completely numb.

notes: "If you consume smoke you are smoking." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグの社員には、喫煙する人が一人もいません。
example_sentences.english: None of Tofugu's employees smoke.

example_sentences.japanese: 喫煙室はどこにあるかご存知ですか？
example_sentences.english: Do you know where the smoking room is?

example_sentences.japanese: やばーい！ちょっと面白すぎっしょ〜！何で鼻で喫煙できるなんて思っちゃったわけ？爆笑してるんですけど。
example_sentences.english: Oh my gosh! That was just way too funny! Why did you think you could smoke with your nose? I am laughing so hard right now.

notes: "Everything is quiet and stopped. The world is still and everything is at rest." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: カナさんの言葉に胸をハッとつかれて、思わず静止してしまいました。
example_sentences.english: I was startled by what Kana said and couldn't help but stand still for a moment.

example_sentences.japanese: これはただの静止画像なのに、びみょうに動いて見える不思ぎな絵です。
example_sentences.english: This is just a still frame, but it looks like it's moving a little. What an interesting picture.

example_sentences.japanese: 弓道では、矢を放つ前に、弓を引ききった状態で一瞬静止する必要がありますが、西洋のアーチェリーも同じですか？
example_sentences.english: In Japanese archery, you need to stand still for a moment with the bowstring fully drawn back before releasing the arrow. Is it the same in Western archery?

notes: "When the sun cooks something, and that something is you, it is giving you sunburn." "The readings here are the vocab kun'yomi readings. You have ひ for 日 and や for 焼け (which you learned with the vocab). Combine it with some sunscreen and hopefully you'll prevent the sunburn."

example_sentences.japanese: どうやらうちの娘は、あの日焼けした青年への恋に胸をこがしているようです。
example_sentences.english: It seems like my daughter is deeply in love with that tan young man.

example_sentences.japanese: 日焼けでせ中が真っ赤になってるよ。
example_sentences.english: Your back is super red from that sunburn.

example_sentences.japanese: ハワイでは強い日焼け止めが必需品で、人達を日焼けから守るのにシートで覆ったりもします。
example_sentences.english: In Hawaii, strong sunscreen is essential and covers are also used to protect people from getting sunburned.

notes: "This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means announce so the verb vocab version is to announce." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: I'd like to announce... we're not having one baby, we're having two (つ) babies!"

example_sentences.japanese: 恋人に別れを告げました。
example_sentences.english: I bid farewell to my girlfriend.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日の朝会で、コウイチは明日からじで入院することを社員に告げた。
example_sentences.english: Koichi announced to his employees that he would be hospitalized for hemorrhoids from tomorrow on.

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトはコウイチに、マミはみんなの想像の斜め上を行く変人だと告げた。
example_sentences.english: Viet told Koichi that Mami is much weirder than everyone imagined.

english: To Cut Off, To Cut Out
notes: "If you cut and take something, you are going to cut it right off. So, this verb is to cut off." "The readings come from 切る and 取る. So, know those words separately and you can combine them into this word."

example_sentences.japanese: このキャベツのしんを切り取ってもらえますか？
example_sentences.english: Can you cut out this cabbage's core?

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は、一枚の紙から、星の形を切り取る方法をお教えします。
example_sentences.english: Today, I'll teach your how to cut a star out of a piece of paper.

example_sentences.japanese: 使わないのにどうしていちいち新聞から割引券を切り取るのさ？
example_sentences.english: Why do you bother clipping coupons from newspapers if you never use them?

notes: "This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means prohibition so the verb version means to prohibit." This has the same reading as the kanji you learned, meaning you know the reading!

example_sentences.japanese: これは、コウイチが自分の禁じられた恋について書いた私小説です。
example_sentences.english: This is an autobiographical novel that Koichi wrote about his own forbidden love.

example_sentences.japanese: 医者は、にんぷにアルコールときつ煙を禁じた。
example_sentences.english: The doctor forbade the pregnant woman from alcohol and cigarettes.

example_sentences.japanese: この部屋では、私語を禁じる。
example_sentences.english: In this room, whispering is prohibited.

notes: "This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means news report so you could try to say ""to news report"" but that doesn't make sense. What does make sense is ""to report on,"" however." The reading doesn't seem like it's the kanji's on'yomi reading, but it is. What an oddity! Do you think it's worth doing a news report on it? Koichi, reporting in on this strange reading that is readable by you right now. Signing off.

example_sentences.japanese: スーパーマンの死去が報じられ、全米が涙した。
example_sentences.english: The entire United States wept when they broke the news that Superman had died.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチの無事が報じられて、胸をなで下ろしました。
example_sentences.english: I felt relieved when they reported that Koichi is safe.

example_sentences.japanese: Tofuguは、初音ミクの独占取材を報じた。
example_sentences.english: Tofugu covered an exclusive interview with Hatsune Miku.

notes: "If you take your writing and fix it, you are taking your writing and rewriting it. This word means to rewrite, because the fixing is really heavy, so regular revisions won't do." "The readings come from 書く and 直す. Know those and you'll know how to read this word too!"

example_sentences.japanese: 主人公をコウイチからビエトに変こうして、この話を書き直してください。
example_sentences.english: Please change the protagonist to Viet instead of Koichi and rewrite this story.

example_sentences.japanese: 試験終了間ぎわになって、受験番号が間ちがっているのに気づいて、あわてて書き直しました。
example_sentences.english: I noticed that I wrote the examinee's number wrong at the very end of the exam period and rewrote it in rush.

example_sentences.japanese: 「これを書き直す時間があると思う？」「私はそうは思わないね。」
example_sentences.english: """Do you think we have enough time to rewrite this?"" ""I don’t think so."""

notes: "You've got your instruction and you have your practice. Time to start your training." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日、トーフグのオフィスで、火さい訓練をしました。
example_sentences.english: We had a fire drill at the Tofugu office yesterday.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は学校で、おはしの使い方を訓練しました。
example_sentences.english: We practiced how to use chopsticks at school today.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語の訓練所を破壊する秘密組織があると聞きました。
example_sentences.english: I heard there's a secret organization that destroys Japanese language training camps.

notes: "When you transmit something and you attain it on the other end, you've done a transmission." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 伝えたかったことが、ちゃんと伝達されたのか心配です。
example_sentences.english: I'm worried about whether what I wanted to say was conveyed properly.

example_sentences.japanese: 伝達事こうは以上です。
example_sentences.english: That's the only message I have.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は、人々が新しい言語を学んでいる時の、ニューロンの信号伝達について研究しています。
example_sentences.english: I’m researching the neural signal transmissions that occur while people are learning a new language.

notes: "When you announce something to warn somebody, you're warning them. Sometimes you're just trying to give them some helpful advice." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 借りた金を早く返すよう警告した。
example_sentences.english: I advised him that he should pay back money he borrowed soon.

example_sentences.japanese: あの選手はどの試合でも必ず警告のイエローカードを出されるね。
example_sentences.english: That player gets a yellow card warning in every game.

example_sentences.japanese: 警告を無視するつもりなのか？
example_sentences.english: Do you intend to ignore this warning?

notes: "There's a riot and everything's getting all mixed up! Within that, there is of course a ton of confusion." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: はん人は、混乱にまぎれてにげてしまった。
example_sentences.english: The culprit escaped in the confusion.

example_sentences.japanese: その町は、山火事で大混乱となっていた。
example_sentences.english: The wildfire brought utter chaos to the town.

example_sentences.japanese: 申し訳ないけど、そんな中途半端なやり方じゃ新入社員が混乱しちゃう気がします。
example_sentences.english: I’m afraid that your half-baked policy may cause confusion among the new employees.

notes: "You're comparing something to another thing, each versus one another. When you do that, you look at both sides. You contrast each and then you come up with a comparison." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: りょうしは、二ひきの魚を対比してみました。
example_sentences.english: The fisherman compared the two fish.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本の生活とアメリカの生活じゃ、いい対比にならないよ。
example_sentences.english: Japanese life and American life aren't a good comparison.

example_sentences.japanese: 誰がコウイチの鼻の写真を撮ったの？その光と影の対比がすごく好きなんだけど。
example_sentences.english: Who took the picture of Koichi’s nose? I really love the contrast between the light and the shadows.

notes: "The wealth you borrow is your debt." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Make sure you remember ざい over さい, though. Why? Because you got all this debt trying to buy your way into Zion."

example_sentences.japanese: 返す目どが立っていないのに、借財をするのは良くないよ。
example_sentences.english: It's not good to take out debt if you don't know how to pay it back.

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグが多がくの借財をかかえているというのは本当ですか？
example_sentences.english: Is it true that Tofugu has a large amount of debt?

example_sentences.japanese: フグが暗殺された後、サーモンに残されたのは借財だけだということが明らかになった。
example_sentences.english: After Fugu’s assassination, it became clear that the only thing he left behind for Salmon was debt.

notes: "When you renew something and it ends up morally good it's definitely an improvement." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: この絵はまだ改善のよ地があると思うんだよね。
example_sentences.english: I think there's still room for improvement on this painting.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは、トーフグの体しつ改善を図っています。
example_sentences.english: Koichi has been trying to improve Tofugu's constitution.

example_sentences.japanese: 私達のサイトに関して、何か改善すべき点などがございましたら、どうぞご連絡くださいませ。
example_sentences.english: If you have any suggestions for the improvement of our site, please contact us.

notes: "If you enter a group you are going to join or enlist." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 入団するための申しこみ書は、細かい活字でいんさつされていました。
example_sentences.english: The application for the enrollment was printed in small type.

example_sentences.japanese: その教団に入団しても、何の得にもならないよ。
example_sentences.english: You won't gain anything out of joining that religious organization.

example_sentences.japanese: 十月二十三日金曜日、Tofugu野球チームは、Tofuguオフィスで入団テストを実施します。
example_sentences.english: The Tofugu baseball team will hold tryouts at the Tofugu office on Friday, October 23rd.

notes: "If you have mixed blood, some people might say you're of mixed race. Own it!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 動物は、別の種が混血することはめったにありません。
example_sentences.english: It's rare for animals to mix breeds with one another.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは日本人とアメリカ人の混血です。
example_sentences.english: Koichi is a mix of Japanese and American.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本人の新生児の三十人に一人は混血だそうですね。
example_sentences.english: Apparently, one in thirty newborn Japanese babies is of mixed parentage.

english: One After Another, Successively, In Succession
notes: "When you continue and then you continue again (that's the repeater kanji), you get things happening one after another. Continue continue continue!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: オフィスの出口から社員が続々と出てきた。
example_sentences.english: Employees came out of the office exit, one after another.

example_sentences.japanese: ワニカニのサブスクリプションを申し込みたいという人が続々と集まってきて、うれしいけどちょっと困っています。
example_sentences.english: There are a lot of people subscribing to WaniKani, one after another, and we're happy about it, but we're having some issues with it as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ワニカニに新しい単語が続々と登場する日が待ち遠しい。
example_sentences.english: I can’t wait for the day when new words pop up one after another on WaniKani.

notes: "A big mix of folks forming a kind of riot. You'd think this would be something more violent, but it's really just an orgy. Lots of mixing, I guess, and not very much organization on the orgy-organizer's part, at least according to this kanji sequence." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: かの女は、乱交のと中で、舌をだらりと出して気ぜつしてしまったんです。
example_sentences.english: Her tongue lolled out and she passed out during the orgy.

example_sentences.japanese: いい加減、乱交するのは止めなよ。みんなドン引きだよ。
example_sentences.english: Hey, it's about time you quit it with the promiscuity, you've been putting everybody off.

example_sentences.japanese: 「何か今日の俺、マジでイケてる。ひょっとしたらアイツらの乱交パーティにも誘われちゃうかも。」「ははは〜。そうだといいね。」
example_sentences.english: """I look so good today, I may be asked to join an orgy."" ""Haha. You wish!"""

notes: "When you participate, adding yourself to the activity, that is participation. Well done, you earn a gold star for participating!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: やっと順番がまわってきて、ゲームに参加することができました。
example_sentences.english: My turn came at last and I was able to participate in the game.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたもトーフグの忘年会に参加しませんか。きっと楽しいですよ。
example_sentences.english: Why don't you participate in Tofugu's end-of-year party? It will be fun!

example_sentences.japanese: 久々の飲み会参加でエンジョイしちゃってまーす。今日は超リア充って感じだよ〜。
example_sentences.english: It’s been a while since I participated in a drinking party and I’m really enjoying it. I’m feeling super-charged!

notes: "This is a tough one. When you compare examples (in this case of numbers) you are figuring out the proportion / ratio. A ratio, for example, has one number on top of another. They are examples being compared. Same with proportions. Without two things to compare, proportion doesn't make sense. That's why when you compare examples, you are dealing with proportions or ratios." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 芸能人は比例代表選のシステムを利用して政治家になるケースが多い。
example_sentences.english: Celebrities become politicians by utilizing the proportional representation of the electoral system.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチの美しさに比例してワニカニユーザーの数もふえるってこと、ちゃんと自覚してくださいね。
example_sentences.english: Please be aware that your beauty is in direct proportion to the increase in the number of WaniKani users, Koichi.

example_sentences.japanese: 外国語能力は、いつでも時間変化率に比例するという訳ではない。
example_sentences.english: Foreign language ability doesn’t always improve in proportion to the rate of change.

english: Really, As Was Expected, Just As I Thought, As Expected
notes: "So this doesn't really make much sense in terms of the kanji and word, but it is what it is. Let's remember it this way:The kanji is fruit so the meaning is really? Like, really really? Because it sounds like you made that up. I really doubt it means really.It can also mean as was expected or just as I thought, but usually we use it as a way to say, ""Really? I don't really believe you...""" "To remember the reading, just imagine yourself snorting out a sharp ""HA!"" (は) right before saying the phrase: ""HA! Just as I thought."""

example_sentences.japanese: この決だんは果たして正しかったのだろうか。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if this is really the right decision.

example_sentences.japanese: 外に出ると、果たして見覚えのある風けいが広がっていた。
example_sentences.english: When I went outside, there was the familiar sight, just as I'd expected it.

example_sentences.japanese: あのカフェでコウイチに会えるかもしれないと思っていたら、果たしてその通りになった。
example_sentences.english: I thought I might be able to meet Koichi at the cafe, and sure enough, I did.
