notes: "If you take along some things that are related, you'll be able to understand their relation better." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: IT関連の仕事をしています。
example_sentences.english: I do IT related work.

example_sentences.japanese: この問題に関連したメールは、全部コウイチに回してください。
example_sentences.english: Please assign all emails related to this matter to Koichi.

example_sentences.japanese: 大気汚染と異常気象の関連を調査する仕事をしています。
example_sentences.english: My job is to investigate the relationship between air pollution and abnormal weather.

notes: "Renew and make something correct. When you do this, you are doing a revision. Ah, much better now." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 四月から、JR山手線のダイヤが改正されます。
example_sentences.english: The schedule for the JR Yamanote Line will be revised in April.

example_sentences.japanese: インターネットの改正料金、もうチェックしましたか？
example_sentences.english: Have you checked the revised Internet rates?

example_sentences.japanese: 市民団体は、公共の場でおならを禁止する法律の改正を求めた。
example_sentences.english: Citizen groups demanded a revision of the law banning farting in public.

english: Run Wild, Run Out Of Control
notes: "Violent running... sounds like a marathon gone wrong. No, this is when you run around and you're all violent. A better way to describe this would be to say ""run wild"" or ""run out of control.""" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: フグは最近ちょっと暴走気味だよね。
example_sentences.english: Fugu has been running a little wild recently, hasn’t he?

example_sentences.japanese: 暴走しているコウイチをビエトはやさしくつつみこんだ。
example_sentences.english: Viet gently embraced Koichi who had been out of control.

example_sentences.japanese: 暴走したトラックが、トーフグオフィスに突っ込んで来る夢を見た。
example_sentences.english: I had a dream that a runaway truck crashed into the Tofugu office.

english: To Be Entangled, To Be Tangled, To Pick A Fight, To Be Involved With, To Get Entangled
notes: "This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means entangle so the verb vocab version is to be entangled. This is when something is entangled on its own (you're not directly doing the entangling). You can remember this because of the む, which is you saying move (む) out of the way, I have to take care of this entanglement mess that just happened on its own." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: The entanglement mess you're fixing is a couple of kids that got their hair tangled up. They were doing some sparring in their からて class and one thing led to the other and suddenly both their hair was entangled together."

example_sentences.japanese: よっぱらって絡んでくるやつが大きらいなんだよ。
example_sentences.english: I hate people who get drunk and then pick fights.

example_sentences.japanese: かみにボタンが絡んじゃって取れないの。
example_sentences.english: My hair got tangled around the button and I can't get it out.

example_sentences.japanese: 最悪！ネチャネチャの風船ガムが釣り糸に絡んじゃった！どうやって取ればいいんだろう。
example_sentences.english: Oh no! Sticky bubblegum got tangled around my fishing line! How can I get it out?

english: Total Failure, Huge Mistake, Big Mistake, Debacle, Massive Failure, Epic Fail
notes: "You know how 失敗 is a mistake? Well, a large mistake is going to be a total failure or a huge mistake. So terrible!" "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. It will help to know 失敗 on its own as well."

example_sentences.japanese: 静けさの中でおならをするという大失敗をおかしてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: I made the big mistake of farting during the silence.

example_sentences.japanese: マミにコウイチのベーコンを見ていてもらうというアイデアは大失敗でした。マミがコウイチのベーコンを全部食べちゃったんですよ。
example_sentences.english: Our idea of having Mami watch Koichi's bacon was a total failure. She ate every single piece.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日の会議で、シャークの奴大失敗しちゃったんだよ。もしかすると今のポジションから降ろされちゃうかも。
example_sentences.english: In the meeting yesterday, Shark really made a huge mistake. I think he might lose his position.

notes: "When something is moving towards emergency (非常), it is something that is very, extremely bad. Like, exceedingly so. It's nuts." "The reading comes straight from the word 非常, which you hopefully know okay by now!"

example_sentences.japanese: イチゴは今季節外れなので、非常に高いんです。
example_sentences.english: Strawberries are out of season now, so they are very expensive.

example_sentences.japanese: 舌は非常に重要な発声器官です。
example_sentences.english: The tongue is an exceedingly important speech organ.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチ大統領の支持率は非常に高い。
example_sentences.english: President Koichi’s approval ratings are extremely high.

notes: "There is much deliberation and theory exchanging when you are trying to present an argument. Of course, it's a very nice one. Lots of thinking and stuff, you know? That's why there's deliberation and theories instead of just screaming. That kind of ""argument.""" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチ達は、日本まで飛行機で行くか船で行くかで議論してるんだ。
example_sentences.english: Koichi and the others are discussing whether we should take a plane or a boat to Japan.

example_sentences.japanese: マイケルが書いた記事は、大いに議論を呼んでいます。
example_sentences.english: The article that Michael wrote drew controversy.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチとビエトは、夕飯に何を食べるかについて数時間に渡って議論に議論を重ねたが、結論には至らなかった。
example_sentences.english: Koichi and Viet argued on what to eat for dinner for hours without reaching a decision.

notes: "Say you give birth to a baby. Then, after that everything falls apart and your life is overthrown. You lose it all because of this baby (babies are expensive). When you have your baby and everything is overthrown, you yourself are thrown into bankruptcy." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 会社が倒産すると知った時、空を見上げたら、きれいな飛行機雲が見えたんです。
example_sentences.english: When I learned my company would go bankrupt, I looked up at the sky and saw a beautiful contrail.

example_sentences.japanese: あの会社には、倒産の嫌疑がかかっている。
example_sentences.english: That company is under suspicion of bankruptcy.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨年はこの街だけで100余りの企業が倒産した。
example_sentences.english: Last year there were more than a hundred bankruptcies in this city alone.

notes: "This is an adverb, but it has the same meaning (basically) as the kanji. It means certainly, and it can also mean surely." "The reading for this one is certainly weird. To remember the reading for this word, just think how you're certain that if you stash the treasure, nobody will find it here."

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチが百メートルほど飛ぶのを、この目で確かに見ました。
example_sentences.english: I'm certain I saw Koichi fly about one hundred meters with my own eyes.

example_sentences.japanese: この機械をそう作するのは確かに難しそうだね。
example_sentences.english: It seems like it might be difficult to operate this machine.

example_sentences.japanese: 確かにTofuguは、伝統的な日本語学習業界にダブルパンチを食らわせました。
example_sentences.english: Tofugu has certainly delivered a one-two punch to the traditional Japanese language learning industry.

notes:
"A difficult injustice to take from someone is a criticism. Ugh, what a pain to be criticized! So difficult, and besides, it's an injustice, because I'm perfect!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

"Dodge a difficult situation by getting away from it. Do an evacuation to get out of there!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: その夫は、妻のことを家事ができないと言って非難してばかりいた。
example_sentences.english: The husband was always criticizing his wife for not being able to do housework properly.

example_sentences.japanese: その記事によって、トーフグは世間の非難にさらされることになった。
example_sentences.english: Because of the article, Tofugu opened themselves up to public criticism.

example_sentences.japanese: 君に非難の目つきで見られることは予想していたけど、それでもやっぱり悲しかったんだ。
example_sentences.english: I had already expected a critical look from you, and even without it, I felt bad.

example_sentences.japanese: その避難梯子はひどく痛んでいるので、交換する必要があります。
example_sentences.english: The fire escape is badly damaged, so we need to replace it.

notes: "You dislike someone so badly that it turns to disgust and hate." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You haven't learned this reading for 悪 yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you:When you feel disgust for someone all you can manage to say when you see them is, ""Oh... (お), it's you."" Feel the anger when you see their face, ""Oh, you again. Bleh."""

example_sentences.japanese: クリステンはクイン・ベリルを嫌悪している。
example_sentences.english: Kristen hates Queen Beryl.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは嫌悪の目で私をにらんできた。
example_sentences.english: Koichi glared at me with a look of disgust in his eyes.

example_sentences.japanese: あいつの顔を見るだけで、嫌悪を催す。
example_sentences.english: Just seeing his face makes me seethe with hatred.

notes: "I exist, I suppose... this is the kind of existence I have. I'm not really sure either way, and I don't care. Existence is futile, I suppose." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: そもそも、この町には水害防止対さくが存在していなかったんだよ。
example_sentences.english: There were no existing flood-control measures in this town to begin with.

example_sentences.japanese: じゃあ、最初はオゾンそうに穴は存在していなかったんですか？
example_sentences.english: So does that mean there were no holes in the ozone layer originally?

example_sentences.japanese: 「コウイチさんが存在するとは思えない…」とフグは言った。
example_sentences.english: """I can’t believe Koichi exists..."" Fugu said."

notes: "Through various tests over the passage of time, you have gained much experience. Time and testing is all it takes." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は、飛行機で旅行をした経験がありません。
example_sentences.english: I've never had the experience of traveling by plane.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達を助けようとしたら、今度は非難のほこ先が自分に向いてしまうという経験をしたことがある人はいますか？
example_sentences.english: Has anyone else had the experience where you try to help a friend and then you get blamed instead?

example_sentences.japanese: 「そうだ、結婚カウンセリングは試してみたの？」 「もちろん、とっくに経験済みだわよ。でも、上手くいかなかったわ。」
example_sentences.english: """Oh! Have you tried marriage counseling yet?"" ""Of course. We experienced that a long time ago but it went badly."""

english: Fire Prevention, Fire Fighting, Fire Proof
notes: "Trying to prevent fire? Better get into fire prevention." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 私なりの防火の心得を文章にまとめました。
example_sentences.english: I put my knowledge of fire prevention in writing.

example_sentences.japanese: 木材にぬると完全防火すると料を発明することができれば、大金持ちになれますよ。
example_sentences.english: If you can invent a paint that makes woods 100% fireproof, you'll be super rich.

example_sentences.japanese: Tofuguはどのくらいの頻度で防火訓練を実施しますか？
example_sentences.english: How often does Tofugu have fire drills?

notes: "When your chest is cooking and burning, you have what's known as heartburn." "The readings are the kun'yomi vocab readings (hint is that there's hiragana sticking out there). So, just make sure you know the word 胸 and 焼く. If you do, you can combine that knowledge into this word, and hopefully not get any heartburn in the process."

example_sentences.japanese: 胸焼けしている時に、なわとびで何回飛べますか？
example_sentences.english: How many times can you jump rope when you're suffering from heartburn?

example_sentences.japanese: 年を取ったせいか、あげ物を食べると胸焼けがするんです。
example_sentences.english: It may be because of my age, but I get heartburn when I eat deep-fried food.

example_sentences.japanese: 朝からカツ丼なんて、胸焼けしないの？
example_sentences.english: Don’t you get heartburn from eating katsu-don in the morning?

notes: "A place where people meet and do deliberation. Sounds boring, but also sounds like some kind of meeting or conference." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 会議中に、おなかが減ってきました。
example_sentences.english: I started getting hungry during the assembly.

example_sentences.japanese: 会議をサボって連ドラを見てるとは、何事だ！
example_sentences.english: You ditched the conference to watch a serial TV drama!? What the heck!?

example_sentences.japanese: この会議の目的は、我々の現状と新しい計画についての話し合いをすることです。
example_sentences.english: The purpose of this meeting is to discuss our current situation and go over new plans.

notes: "Something that obstructs and also does damage is an obstruction. No obstruction is ever good and if left too long it really will cause damage and interference as well." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: これ以上妨害するのを止めないと、えい業妨害でうったえるぞ！
example_sentences.english: If you don't stop interfering, I'm going to sue you for obstruction.

example_sentences.japanese: ここまで来れば、てきの妨害の危険はほぼ無いだろう。
example_sentences.english: Since we've come pretty far, the risk of being intercepted by the enemy should be almost zero.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はいつか映画のように公務執行妨害で逮捕されてみたい。
example_sentences.english: Someday I want to be arrested for interfering with police officers, like in the movies.

notes: "To prevent beforehand is still prevention." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 危機かん理がもっとしっかりしていたら、この事故は事前に予防することができたはずだ。
example_sentences.english: If we had a better risk management, we would have been able to prevent this accident.

example_sentences.japanese: その国に行くなら、事前に必ずマラリア予防の薬を飲んでください。
example_sentences.english: If you go to that country, please make sure to take medicine to prevent malaria beforehand.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本人も十年ごとに破傷風の予防接種を受けるのですか？
example_sentences.english: Do Japanese people get a tetanus vaccination every ten years, too?

notes: "To prevent and stop someone from doing something is prevention. It's good to have prevention instead of letting something bad happen." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 警察がこの町の犯罪の拡大を防止してくれています。
example_sentences.english: The police have prevented crime from spreading in this town.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は学校で、地球温だん化防止について話し合いをしました。
example_sentences.english: Today we discussed the prevention of global warming at school.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本の通貨は、世界一優れた偽造防止技術が使われていることで知られていますが、ビエトはそれを打ち負かそうとしています。
example_sentences.english: Japanese currency is known for incorporating the world’s most advanced counterfeit prevention technology, but Viet is planning to defeat it.

notes: "Quiet quiet! Do it quietly, please." "You know how 静か is しずか? Well, this is the same reading as that. Say it in a whisper with me: ""しずしず."" Shhh!"

example_sentences.japanese: 私の母は、いつも静々と機械的に家事をこなしていました。
example_sentences.english: My mom always did housework quietly and mechanically.

example_sentences.japanese: いかりくるう妻の横を尻目に、ぼくはただ静々とそうじをしていた。
example_sentences.english: I was just ignoring my super-angry wife and calmly cleaning our place.

example_sentences.japanese: 公爵夫人は静々と部屋に入って、公爵にキスをした。
example_sentences.english: The duchess gracefully entered the room and kissed the duke.

notes: "The truth is that you exist in reality. Well, that makes sense, I suppose." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 穴ぐまって、実在するんですね。
example_sentences.english: Badgers really exist, huh?

example_sentences.japanese: どんな時に、神が実在すると感じますか。
example_sentences.english: When do you feel that God really exists?

example_sentences.japanese: Tofuguの顔は、実在の人物をモデルに作られたという噂があります。
example_sentences.english: There’s a rumor that Tofugu’s face was modeled after a real person.

notes: "The place you're detained is where you exist. As long as you're in this place, this will be your residence. Note: mainly means ""residence"" in the broader sense and is parts of words like ""residence card"" or ""foreign residents.""" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本在留のアメリカ人と友達になりました。
example_sentences.english: I became friends with an American who was residing in Japan.

example_sentences.japanese: 在留期間をえん長するには、一たん国外に出ないといけません。
example_sentences.english: In order to extend your residency, you have to leave the country and then come back.

example_sentences.japanese: ビザと在留資格は別物です。

example_sentences.english: The train was derailed, but nobody was injured.

english: Evaluation, Appraisal, Verdict, Valuation, Assessment, Rating
notes: "Let's evaluate the value. What is this also known as? An evaluation." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 私のホームドクターは、いつも急いでいて、自分の症状について調べてきた患者の話を聞かずにけんもほろろに追い出すので、評価が低い。
example_sentences.english: My family doctor has a low rating because he is always in a rush, is unwilling to listen to patients who have researched a medical problem they have, and often dismisses their worries.

notes: "This is a single kanji with an い on the end, which means you think it ought to be an adjective, but it's not, it's a noun :( What's the noun form of force? It's also force." "This is a rough one. There is much force behind you, so when you come at me I scream: ""EEK! OI! (いきおい), Get away from me!"""

example_sentences.japanese: 私達の犬は、誰と競争している訳でもないのに、いつもすごい勢いでミルクボーンに向かって行きます。
example_sentences.english: Our dog always bolts towards the milk-bone even though he isn’t racing anyone.

notes: "The plan inside this piece of paper is the guide you'll be using. It's a plan. It's inside. Use it as your guide!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 「二人なんですが、席は空いていますか？」「お席にご案内するまで少しお待ちください。」
example_sentences.english: """Do you have a table for two?"" ""It will be just a moment before I will guide you to your seats."""

notes: "You have a thought on a particular view. This is your idea or notion on it." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は芸術においては素晴らしい美の観念を持っているのに、どうしてあんなに不細工な男性と付き合っているのかが理解できない。
example_sentences.english: She has a keen sense of beauty for art, so I don’t understand how she’s dating such an ugly guy.

notes: "Use your finger to indicate some things. These are your instructions. Okay, do this (point), do that (point), and then finally do this (point)." The readings are the on'yomi readings. You've learned them both already, good for you!

example_sentences.japanese: 指示を無視するのはよくありませんが、指示待ち族にはなってもらいたくはありません。私の言っている意味が分かりますか？
example_sentences.english: Ignoring orders is not good, but I don’t want you to be someone who can’t work without instructions. Do you know what I mean?

notes: "A noon sleep is sleep you do during the day, also known as a nap." The readings for this word are both kun'yomi readings. You learned them when you learned the kanji, so you should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチはただ今昼寝中です。おかけになって少々お待ちください。
example_sentences.english: Koichi is napping at the moment. Please be seated and wait for a moment.

notes: "So this doesn't quite make sense in terms of the meaning of the kanji... but you'll be okay. This means on purpose. Perhaps when you do something that has the  appearance of doing what you wanted to do you're doing it on purpose." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: ""You did that to me on purpose? Whazapp with that?"""

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は、彼に態と気のないふりをした。
example_sentences.english: She pretended to be indifferent toward him on purpose.

notes: "You sleep like a monk, as in you never stop sleeping (because you sleep while you meditate). When you sleep like a monk like this you constantly oversleep, probably because you're up late doing sutras or something. I have no idea why monks wake up late, but figure something out to make this stick in your brain cage." These are the readings you learned with the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: あいにくですが、トフグのオフィスには今、ご対応できる者がおりません。社員がみんな寝坊してしまったのです。
example_sentences.english: I’m afraid no one in the Tofugu office is available at the moment. Every worker overslept today.

notes: "Your appearance is strange. You're abnormal. Oh, and you're a pervert because you look so abnormal. Though you could just be a caterpillar going through your metamorphosis to become a butterfly. You just look really weird while the changing is going on." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 実は、ちょっと恥ずかしい話なんだけど、俺の親父めちゃくちゃ変態で、児童ポルノの一斉捜査で捕まっちゃったんだよね。
example_sentences.english: Actually, it’s sort of an embarrassing story, but my father is so perverted that he was caught in a massive child porn ring.

notes: "Go ahead and put a rank on something. This one is rank #1, so its position is up higher. Then you put a rank #67 on something. That one's position is lower." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 位置について、用意、ドン！
example_sentences.english: On your mark, get set, go!

english: Presentation, Submission, Filing, Handing In, Turning In
notes: "Go ahead and present then exit. This will be your presentation of the materials." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: トフグライターへの応募者の提出物について教えて頂けますか？また、必要なスキルは何ですか？
example_sentences.english: Could you tell me what a Tofugu writer applicant needs to submit and what skills are required?

notes: "Please present your plan in the form of a proposition." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 「提案はどうだった？」「うーん。まあまあって感じかな。」
example_sentences.english: """So what did you think of the proposal?"" ""Well, I think it was just okay."""

notes: "When you give up and just try to enjoy the view, that's resignation. You know things aren't going well, and you know you can't do anything about it now, so you resign yourself to what's to come." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 父は、様々な経験の後に諦観に至った。
example_sentences.english: My father's various experiences led to his resignation.

example_sentences.japanese: やる気はやがて、諦観となった。
example_sentences.english: Motivation became resignation before long.

example_sentences.japanese: 君は諦観するにはまだ若い。
example_sentences.english: You are too young to be resigned.

notes:
"Let's go view some sunlight! Oh wait, we can't do that here. We will have to go sightseeing to go see this amazing sunlight thing." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

"You use your daring and just go! You made a decisive action by just going like that! It was go or not go and you chose go!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 観光案内のパンフレットありますか？
example_sentences.english: Can I have a sightseeing brochure?

example_sentences.japanese: 本当にこの作戦を敢行するつもりですか。
example_sentences.english: Do you really intend to carry out this strategy?

notes: "You must respond with aid in order to show your support for someone who needs it. You can usually show your support if you root for them." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: あの熱心に声を出す応援者はいったい誰なんだ？
example_sentences.english: Who the heck is that enthusiastic and vocal supporter?

notes: "To support and aid is to support." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 心あるオナラ臭い支援を有難うございます。
example_sentences.english: Thank you for your hearty and farty support.

notes: "To undress your taxes is to throw them away. Just throw it out, who needs 'em? I'm not going to pay these taxes, therefore I am committing tax evasion." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は小さい頃、両親から親切な人になるよう教わりましたが、二人は脱税容疑で逮捕されました。
example_sentences.english: My parents taught me how to be a kind person when I was little, but they were arrested on charges of tax evasion.

english: To Run A Business, To Manage A Business
notes: "The kanji means manage, but when you manage something, what are you usually managing? How about a business? So this word means to run a business even though the kanji is manage." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: You have to run a business. Your business is to make people eat who don't want to eat. ""HEY, YOU EAT NOW!"" (いとな)."

example_sentences.japanese: 私の両親はマッサージ業を営んでいるので、私はそこで「マッサージ受け放題」なんです。
example_sentences.english: My parents run a massage therapy business, so I can get ’all-you-can-take-massages’ at home.

notes: "Unite and join together. It is unification time. Integration!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. Put'm together.

example_sentences.japanese: 全ての国が一つの政府に統合される日がいつかやってくると思いますか。
example_sentences.english: Do you think the day will one day come when all countries are united under one government?

notes: "You suck something in and obtain it. Shhheewwwwww! When you suck something in and obtain it into your body, you have done absorption because it's been sucked inside of you." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 植物が水分を取り入れる時って、どれくらいのスピードで吸収するんですか？
example_sentences.english: When plants get water, how long does it take for them to absorb it?

notes: "Your performance skill allows you to be great at acting and doing awesome performances." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: あの女優の演技力は素晴らしい。
example_sentences.english: That actress’ acting ability is magnificent.

notes: "The present time is the time you're actually in. You aren't really in any other time, because that's not how time works!" This has the same reading as the kanji you learned, meaning you know the reading!

example_sentences.japanese: 現にさっきそう言ったじゃありませんか。
example_sentences.english: Didn’t you actually say that a while ago?

notes: "When you've finished solving something, you've come to a point of comprehension and understanding. Also, used in (often radio) communication to signify you know what's up. It's like saying ""roger!""" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は弱々しいうなずいて了解の意を示して、立ち去った。
example_sentences.english: He expressed his understanding with a weak nod and walked away.

notes: "When you go to carry out something, you are carrying it out. That's why this is carry out (that is しこう). Alternatively, when you go carry out something, you are making sure something is getting done. You are doing enforcement on that thing that you're carrying out on." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Another alternative reading is せこう, which is more often used when talking about something law related."

example_sentences.japanese: この法律の施行の責任を誰が負っていたのか覚えていますか？
example_sentences.english: Do you remember who is responsible for the enforcement of this law?

notes: "When you express something that's of the present time, you are saying something that only people of the current time understand. These are expressions or figure of speech. You say these things during the present time, not the future, not the past, the present time. Otherwise nobody would understand." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨夜の夢で、私たちの赤ちゃんに「乳歯が抜けそうだった時、言葉では表現できないほど痒かった」って言われたの。
example_sentences.english: Last night in my dream, our baby told me that it’s time for her baby teeth to come out and she can’t express in words how itchy they are.

notes: "An anti rule is when you break the rules. It's when you do a foul." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: つけ睫毛を付けるなんて反則だよ。ほとんど別人みたいじゃないか。
example_sentences.english: Wearing false eyelashes isn’t fair. Don’t you think you almost look like a different person.

notes: "Ugh, time to request employment again. Time to go job hunting." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 失業なんて気にするなよ。俺なんてかれこれもう約二年間も求職活動中だぜ。
example_sentences.english: Don’t worry about being unemployed. I’ve been job hunting for almost two years now.

notes: "When you perform above the stage it's a performance. This word is usually used for musical and theatrical performances." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: ライオンキングの上演時間を教えて下さい。
example_sentences.english: Can you tell me the time of the Lion King performance?

english: Power Outage, Cutoff Of Electricity, Power Cut
notes: "When you halt electricity you experience a power outage. Makes sense. When the electricity stops you don't have any more power." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: どうしてまだ停電してるって分かってるのに、電気のスイッチを何度も付けたり消したりしちゃうんだろう。
example_sentences.english: Why do I keep flipping light switches on and off if I know that there is still a power outage.

notes: "I will provide you with the standard things you need. You can use these for your preparations. It's what everyone gets and it's what you will get too. If it helps, imagine getting some actual things, and use them to prepare for something else. Imagine everyone else getting these standard things to prepare with too." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: おはよう。朝ご飯の準備ができてるわよ。
example_sentences.english: Good morning, your breakfast is ready!

notes: "It was superior previously, so we need to go back there. That, amongst all the other things, is our highest priority." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 我が社は新しいベーコンフレーバーの開発を優先するべきだ。
example_sentences.english: We should put priority on developing a new flavor of bacon.

notes: "Divide then join something back together. When you join it back together, it won't be whole again, but you can see the two parts you divided apart. You can also compare them and see which is bigger and by how much. You can easily find the ratio this way, too." This word uses the kun'yomi readings for both kanji. You've learned them both already, so you should be able to read this already!

example_sentences.japanese: 日本では、蕎麦粉の割合が100%の蕎麦を十割り蕎麦と呼びます。
example_sentences.english: In Japan, noodles that contain one hundred percent buckwheat flour are called Juwari-soba.

notes: "If you quit your place of employment, you are quitting, aka putting in your resignation." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 上司にはっきりと「あなたの代わりはいくらでもいる」と言われたので、その会社を辞職しました。
example_sentences.english: My boss told me flat-out that I was disposable, so I left the company.

notes: "The law of movement is governed by rhythm. Imagine moving around to a boss beat. As you move, you start to feel the rhythm in your step. Go ahead and walk around your room and feel this rhythm. Note that リズム is probably going to be more common of a word to use for rhythm, but this is a kanji learning site after all. One thing you will see more often is 律動的 which means ""rhythmic.""" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 今朝、たくさんの兎が庭で律動的に飛び跳ねているのを見ました。
example_sentences.english: This morning, I saw a lot of rabbits jumping rhythmically in my garden.

notes: "Halt and stop. When something does this, it's in a stoppage." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の兄は一度心肺停止にまで至ったんですが、外科医が心臓マッサージを施した後に、心臓が再び脈動しだしたんです。
example_sentences.english: My brother once went into cardiopulmonary arrest, but his heart started beating again after the surgeon performed a cardiac massage.

english: To Know, To Understand, To Be Aware Of, To Consent, To Agree
notes: "Remember how you learned that 心得 means ""knowledge""? Well the verb version of that is to know. (You know it deep in your heart.)" The readings for this word are both kun'yomi readings. You learned them when you learned the kanji, so you should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: このお方をどなたと心得るか。
example_sentences.english: Does anyone know who this woman is?

notes: "If 演 is performance then the verb version of this would be to perform." The reading looks weird, but it's actually just the reading you learned with the kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: こんな大役を演ずることができて、とても光栄です。
example_sentences.english: I am very honored to be able to play such an important role.

notes: "You're going to get judged times two. Judge and judge again. Once by the judge and another time by the jury. This is a whole trial here." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. The はん goes to ばん though, so be careful."

example_sentences.japanese: この貯金箱には小遣いからためた80ドルが入っているんだけど、裁判を起こすには到底足りないと思うんだよね。
example_sentences.english: This piggy bank contains the eighty dollars I’ve saved from my allowance, but I guess it is not close to enough to file a lawsuit.

notes: "The superior person wins. They will win the championship and be able to claim victory over all others." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ジャイアンツは去年はボロ負けだったが、今年はリーグ優勝を果たした。
example_sentences.english: Although the Giants got their butts kicked big time last year, they won the championship this year.

notes: "Above mentions are above mentioned. Look above to see where I mentioned it, okay?" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 上述のように、雇用者、従業員のどちらも、いついかなる理由においても契約を終了することができる。
example_sentences.english: As stated above, both employees and employers can terminate an employment contract at any time for any reason.

notes: "Transport of blood. Only time you do this is during a blood transfusion." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はちょうど東京に向かおうとしていた矢先に交通事故に巻き込まれ、現在病院で輸血を受けている。
example_sentences.english: She was in a car accident when she was just about to head off to Tokyo, and now she is getting a blood transfusion in the hospital.

notes: "You lose. Because of that, you have to carry this burden and responsibility." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 10キロのお米を持ち上げることは、彼の腰の負担となった。
example_sentences.english: Lifting 10kg of rice was a burden on his lower back.

notes: "Your versus plan is to attack back. They've already attacked you once, so now it's time for your counter plan." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: コーヒーを入れようとしてボタンを押したら、コーヒーメーカーが火を噴いたの。不具合の原因を見つけて、再発防止対策を講じなきゃいけないわ。
example_sentences.english: I was making a cup of coffee, I pressed a button, and the machine caught on fire. We have to find the cause of the defect and take measures to prevent its recurrence.

notes: "Write down and mention what happened. When you do this you're writing a description and account of what happened." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: もしその男に関する記述が誤植だったら、間違った人を逮捕してしまうかもしれないよ。
example_sentences.english: If your description of the man is inaccurate, we might arrest the wrong person.

notes: "You make a distinction between people and based off that you separate the people. This is terrible! Why so much discrimination?" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は偏見や差別は好きではありませんが、そういう冗談は好きです。
example_sentences.english: I don’t like prejudice or discrimination, but I do like those types of jokes.

notes: "When you transport things and they exit from your country, you are exporting them." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 出張の際にヘロウィンを密輸出しようとしたため、彼は試験期間のうちに契約を打ち切られた。
example_sentences.english: He was terminated during his probation period because he tried to smuggle heroin on a business trip.

notes: "Remember 寝坊 and how it means oversleep? Someone who oversleeps in the morning is someone who's a late riser." "The reading is the vocab words 朝 and 寝坊 put together into one. So long as you know them separately you should know them together too!"

example_sentences.japanese: 私は朝寝坊だが、妹は私と違って早起きだから、君の犬の散歩に行けるかもしれないよ。
example_sentences.english: I’m a late riser but my sister is an early riser, she might be able to walk your dogs for you.

notes: "Things you sell that pass through the world to get to you are probably mail order. You order them and they get zoomed off to you, passing through all kinds of space to arrive at your door." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 今まで通販で買い物したことないけど、ちょっとやってみるよ。
example_sentences.english: I’ve never bought anything through mail order before, but I’ll give it a shot.

notes: "The pipe of reason. Imagine someone holding this pipe. It always leads to the correct decision because it is the pipe of reason. Those who have this pipe are in a higher rank than you. They are the management, and by using this pipe of reason they're able to make good management decisions." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 時間管理法の授業の講師が遅刻しているなんて、信じられない。
example_sentences.english: I can’t believe the lecturer of the time management strategy class is actually late.

notes: "A place where you manufacture and make is a place where manufacturing and production are done. So many things getting made." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 村田製作所は、電子部品を製造している日本の会社です。
example_sentences.english: Murata Manufacturing Co., Ltd. is a Japanese company that manufactures electronic components.

notes: "When you present something to your servant you're doing them a favor. You're kindly giving them an offer. Or, because they're a poor student, maybe you're offering program sponsoring to them. You know, because you're so nice." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本で臓器提供者になる同意書にサインをするには、どうすればいいですか？
example_sentences.english: How can I register to become an organ donor in Japan?

notes: "A quality problem is worth a question. A low quality problem however... don't ask the question. There are stupid questions, after all." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はある観客からの予想外の質問にたじろいだ。
example_sentences.english: He flinched at the unexpected question from an audience member.

notes: "Please write down and publish this so we have a record of it." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 小論文を提出したが、日付を記載するのを忘れてしまった。
example_sentences.english: I turned in my essay but I forgot to record the date on it.

notes: "Sell, sell, sell. This is the attitude you need if you want to work in sales or do sales. You have to work on your selling." This is a jukugo word, which means you need to know the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You know them both, hurray!

example_sentences.japanese: 我が社の販売員の多くは、八月に休暇を取ります。
example_sentences.english: Many of the salespeople at our company are taking time off work in August.

notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means burn and the verb vocab version is to burn something (or to burn)." "This is when you're burning something. To remember this meaning, you have to remember the も part. So, just think of your friend Moe (も), and how you're going to burn him... uh... just a little bit."

example_sentences.japanese: 何かを完全に灰になるまで燃やすことが大好きだ。
example_sentences.english: I really like burning things until they’re reduced to ashes.

notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means carry so the verb vocab version is to carry. This has to do with carrying something literal, unlike 担う which is not necessarily literal (you'll learn it later). And in this case, you carry it on your shoulder(s). You can remember that it's literal from the reading mnemonic, which has you carrying literal cats on your shoulders." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: You love to carry things, especially cats (かつ). You hoist them up onto your shoulders and carry them all around town."

example_sentences.japanese: 日本に行ったら、お祭りで神輿を担いでみたい。
example_sentences.english: If I go to Japan, I’d like to carry a portable shrine in a parade.

notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means celebrate, so the verb vocab version is to celebrate. When you burn this word, you should 祝う!" "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: When you celebrate something, you have to yell out your celebrations. Yell out いわう three times! It's kind of like a combination of the word いい (good) and ""wow."" いいwow! いいwow! Just make sure the いい gets shortened, because it's getting combined."

example_sentences.japanese: 日曜日におじいちゃんの還暦を祝うために、中華を食べに行きます。
example_sentences.english: We are going to a Chinese restaurant to celebrate grandpa’s 60th birthday on Sunday.

english: To Mention, To State, To Explain
notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means mention so the verb vocab version is to mention." "I have to mention this thing... ""NO,"" (の) you quickly respond. I don't want you mentioning that here and now."

example_sentences.japanese: 上司に全く正反対の意見を述べるのは気が引けます。
example_sentences.english: I don’t feel like explaining to my boss that I have a completely different opinion than he has.

english: Touch, Feel, Touch Sense, Sense Of Touch
notes: "Your feeling of touch is your touch sense (or simply just touch)." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: このストールの感触、シルクみたい。
example_sentences.english: This scarf feels like silk.

notes: "You want to transport something by sending it? Well that's transportation." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 輸送コストを教えて下さい。
example_sentences.english: Please tell me the transportation cost.

notes: "To expand and open. Just imagine something happening like this. This is when something is unfolding or in development." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 中小企業が海外展開をする利点とは何でしょうか。
example_sentences.english: What are the advantages of small businesses expanding overseas?

notes: "I've announced I'm going to sue you. The accusation and charge I have against you for suing you? Uh... You suck." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎月きちんとお金を払って頂けるなら、告訴はしません。
example_sentences.english: I won’t take legal action as long as you pay me every month.

notes: "When you apprehend and catch someone, that leads to an arrest / capture." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ラッシュ時の電車内で痴漢行為を働いたとして、危うく誤認逮捕されるところだった。
example_sentences.english: I was almost arrested by mistake for molestation on the rush hour train.

notes: "A place where something belongs is where it is attached. It's where it's attached to. It belong(s) to that place." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 所属部署に病欠のための診断書を提出しておいた方がいいよ。
example_sentences.english: You should turn in doctor’s notes for sick days to your own department.

notes: "When you search and inspect things, you are probably part of a criminal investigation." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 本日は捜査に関する重要書類を作成する予定です。
example_sentences.english: I’m going to draw up some important documents for a criminal investigation today.

english: Death By Strangling, Strangled To Death, Strangling
notes: "A strangle kill is when you are strangled to death. Try to avoid this." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 「あんた、もう少しであの男を絞殺しかけたのよ！」「ごめん。やりすぎたよ。」
example_sentences.english: """You almost strangled that guy to death!"" ""I’m sorry. I went too far."""

notes: "Divide that price and pull it apart. You only have to pay for one part! What a discount." "The readings are the ones you learned with the kanji. き from ひき kind of just gets stuffed into the 引き and hidden away like that strange collection of fingernails you have hidden in your closet drawer inside of a 35mm film container. Also remember that the reading gets changed to びき here because of that pesky rendaku."

example_sentences.japanese: ちょうどホームページへ割引クーポンの追加をしようと思ってたところだよ。
example_sentences.english: I’ll set about adding a discount coupon to the website.

notes: "An anti echo is still an echo! It's just going back and forth with a normal echo. Together they get a weird reverberation going." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: この記事への反響はとても大きかった。
example_sentences.english: The influence of this article was huge.

notes: "Include your ideas here, but think about the implications they will result in too, especially considering you're just including them now. They have implications!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 誰にとっても、含意を汲み取るのは難しいことだ。
example_sentences.english: It’s difficult for everyone to understand the implied meaning.

notes: "If you sue and bring about a lawsuit, you are bringing about a lawsuit." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: その訴訟に関する書類は、弁護士によって全てきちんとファイルされている。
example_sentences.english: The documents related to the lawsuit have all been neatly filed away by the lawyer.

notes: "Your limit is determined. It is where it is. It is your limit after all." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: お母さん、あの限定販売のTofugu人形が欲しいんだけど、百万ドルくれない？
example_sentences.english: Mom, I really want the limited edition Tofugu dolls, so can’t you give me one million dollars?

notes: "Obese and full. Probably not a good idea to eat until you're full if you're obese. That will lead to obesity." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: あの肥満上司が、私たちに対する全権限を持っていて、先週は二名を解雇しやがったんだよ。
example_sentences.english: That obese boss has authoritative power over us and he terminated two workers last week.

notes:
"Set up and become something. When you set up and care for something like this you're doing organization of this thing. The configuration is so nice." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

"Again you have life! Either this is a rebirth of some kind, or you have received resuscitation and another shot at life. Whatever it is, you have life again, so that's great!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: この映画は二部構成になっている。
example_sentences.english: This movie is composed of two parts.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は自分の息子は更生の見込みがあると信じている。
example_sentences.english: She believes that there is hope of rehabilitation for her son.

notes: "You hide away but you're alive. You've lived your life, so now it's time to hide and live the rest of it out until you're not alive. You've reached the age of retirement." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: お前は本当に隠居したいのか？
example_sentences.english: Do you really want to retire?

notes: "If 呼ぶ is ""to call"" then this is something similar. This is when you are called by someone (and you're not doing the calling). This word is to be called." "The reading is shared with 呼ぶ, so remember that and you'll be able to read this too."

example_sentences.japanese: おばちゃんと呼ばれる年になってしまったことがちょっと悲しかった。
example_sentences.english: I was a little sad to reach an age where I can be called a middle-aged woman.

english: To Store, To Achieve, To Score, To Finish, To Come Into Power, To Dedicate
notes:
"When you obtain something you need to keep it safe, so you decide to store it somewhere. Then you can always go back and look at the thing you managed to achieve and no one can take it from you." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You haven't learned this reading yet so here's a mnemonic to help you:You need to store all of the old saws (おさ). You were able to finish and to achieve everything you wanted with them, so it's time to put them away so they'll be safe."

"Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means supply so the verb version is to supply." "So you're supplying something... let's say nuclear warheads... to Osama Bin Laden. You gonna be in soooo much trouble, especially since it's zombie Osama Bin Laden."

example_sentences.japanese: 争いを収めるにはどうすればいいのだろう。
example_sentences.english: What should I do to finish the fight?

example_sentences.japanese: 血税の使い道が理にかなってさえいれば、政府に税金を納めるのは私は一向に構いませんよ。
example_sentences.english: I don’t mind paying the tax to the government as long as they spend it on reasonable things.

notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means supplement so the verb vocab version is to supplement." "Oh, gee, now (おぎな) you're going to supplement it? That would have been helpful earlier. Might help to say ""oh gee now"" with a ぎ sound instead of ""ji"" sound out loud, too. This is a tricky reading, won't be learned too easily, so think about it a bit now."

example_sentences.japanese: 欠員を補うために、ボーリングゲームに参加しました。
example_sentences.english: To compensate for the empty spot, I joined the bowling game.

english: To Surpass, To Outstrip, To Excel
notes: "This is the verb version of the kanji superior, so it means to surpass. Someone who is superior is always going to surpass and to excel beyond others. That's what makes them so superior in the first place!" "Remember how 今すぐ means ""at once""? Well that's the key to surpassing others. You have to do everything 今すぐ!!!"

example_sentences.japanese: あのころは、景子先輩より優れている人はだれもいなかったの。
example_sentences.english: Nobody outstripped Keiko senpai back then.

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグはユニークさにおいて、他の日本語学習教材より優れています。
example_sentences.english: Tofugu surpasses the other Japanese learning materials in terms of uniqueness.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは納豆の模型を作るのに優れている。
example_sentences.english: Koichi is excellent at making plastic natto models.

notes: "This is the adverb version of 再, so it shares the meaning again and also has the meaning once again." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: Once again, you put a footer in your note because you can't remember the reading to this word because the mnemonic is so bad (sorry!)."

example_sentences.japanese: もしできるなら、再び肘を舐めてみるべきだ。
example_sentences.english: If you can, you should lick your elbow again.

notes: "A compare and contrast will give you a comparison of something." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 偽物のダイヤと本物のダイヤを直接比較してみれば、どっちがどっちだかすぐに分かるよ。
example_sentences.english: If you directly compare a false diamond with a real one, you’ll know which one is which right away.

english: Congratulation, Congratulations, Celebration, Festival, Congratulatory Gift
notes: "This is the noun version of the kanji celebrate, so when you put a お before it to raise it up, it means congratulations! When someone has something to celebrate you should congratulate them." Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You learned this reading already so you should be able to read it!

example_sentences.japanese: 引っ越しお祝いを渡さなくちゃいけないわね。
example_sentences.english: You have to bring a moving gift.

notes: "I'm going to  chastise you about this theory. When I do this, this is a debate. Doesn't it feel like you're being chastised when people are debating with you sometimes, especially with your own theories? I think so." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は給与削減と年金減額に関する討論に加わった。
example_sentences.english: I participated in the discussion about salary cuts and the reduction of pensions.

notes: "When one person is in a position to judge everyone alone by themselves, they're definitely a part of a dictatorship. One person should never be alone to judge everyone because that's how dictators are made and they're not so great." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 俺は世界一の独裁者になるんだ。
example_sentences.english: I’ll become the best dictator in the world.

notes: "There is damage that hinders you from doing things normally. This is a disability." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 障害があることがバレて、内定が取り消された。
example_sentences.english: When it leaked out that I have a disability, the job offer I had was cancelled.

notes: "You must obey your business. When you're in this situation, you've found employment through them, which is why you must obey them (if you weren't employed, you wouldn't have to listen to them)." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ここの従業員たちは、大阪支店の従業員たちより楽観的なようだ。
example_sentences.english: Employees here seem to be more optimistic than their Osaka-branch counterparts.

notes: "Some fierce encouraging is what you need. Some encouragement!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: テレビ番組が放映された後、何百にも及ぶ激励の電話が、数時間に渡って掛かってきた。
example_sentences.english: After the TV show, hundreds of calls offering encouragement came pouring in for hours.

notes: "Create it and stand it up. This is your establishment, your founding." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 電車に乗り遅れて、会社の創立記念のイベントに遅れそうだ。
example_sentences.english: I’ve missed my train and I’m running late for my company’s anniversary event.

notes: "The transport of things that enter your country are imports." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 兄の会社が輸入家具マーケットにビジネスに広げるのですが、私はそのプロジェクトマネージャーに抜擢されました。
example_sentences.english: My brother’s company is going to expand its business in the import furniture market and he chose me as the manager for the project.

notes: "Alone I stand. I have independence!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 会社を辞めて独立した人で成功した人は多くないって言うなら、そのデータやその人たちの計画、そしてどうしてそれが失敗したのかを示してくださいよ。
example_sentences.english: If you say not many people who left the company and went independent succeeded, show me the data, their plans, and how they failed.

notes: "Our faces have adjoined in this one room to talk. You did the telephone interview where you didn't show the face of your face. Now you're showing it, so we can begin the real interview." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 面接の合否に関して、印刷物の郵送は行っておりません。
example_sentences.english: We don’t send out any hardcopy materials for the interview results.

notes: "The circumstance is that the thing you're using is a hinderance. Usually it's a help, but now it's out of order and has a malfunction." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: あのファックス機は故障中だよ。
example_sentences.english: That fax machine is out of order.

notes: "Manufacture and create. That is manufacturing." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 織り物の製造元でアメリカで事業を拡張しているところがいくつかあるって聞いたんだけど、一体どうやって拡張してるのか知ってる？
example_sentences.english: I heard some textile manufacturers are expanding their operations in the United States. Do you know how they’re doing it?

notes: "A person who is different from the person you thought it was is a mistaken identity. Whoops, sorry, I thought you were someone else. 人違い!" "The readings are 人 and 違い put together."

example_sentences.japanese: はい、私達も結合双生児ではありますが、申し訳ありませんがあなたは人違いをしていると思います。
example_sentences.english: Yes, we are also conjoined twins, but I’m afraid you are mistaking us for a different set of twins.

notes: "You are alone in what you occupy. Nobody but you occupies it. You have a monopoly." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: うちの家族の場合は、父がテレビを独占しています。
example_sentences.english: In my family’s case, my father monopolizes the television.

notes: "You are alone in what you are able to create. Nobody else can create like you, because you have originality and creativity on your side." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼が独創性に欠けていることは非常に残念です。
example_sentences.english: It’s so disappointing that he is lacking in originality.

notes: "Again you build it. This is rebuilding." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Just don't forget that extra い!"

example_sentences.japanese: 潰れかかった会社を再建するまで、彼は毎日規定よりも長い時間働いた。
example_sentences.english: To rehabilitate his almost-bankrupt company, he worked longer hours than he was supposed to every day.

notes: "Renew it by creating something anew. This is remodeling because you're creating something and changing something that exists already, renewing it." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 言うのは恥ずかしいんですが、あの改造バイクに乗ってるのは私の兄です。
example_sentences.english: This is embarrassing to say, but the guy riding the modded motorcycle is my brother.

notes: "Again it is opening. This is the reopening." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Just don't forget that extra い!"

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチとビエトの交渉は、近々再開される予定だ。
example_sentences.english: Negotiations between Koichi and Viet will be reopened soon.

notes: "Restore what you learned with reviews. That's what you do on WaniKani, right?" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 予習と復習はどちらも大切です。
example_sentences.english: Preparation and review are both important.

notes: "Depart and then restore yourself back to your original departure spot. If you do this (departing and coming back) you have a round trip." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ここから大阪まで、往復でいくらですか？
example_sentences.english: How much is a round trip from here to Osaka?

notes: "Your savings gold is your savings. You'd be good to have gold right now in your savings, actually. Melt it down into bars, manngggg." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

notes: "This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means narrow, so the verb version is to narrow." example_sentences.english: Can you narrow the width a little more here?

notes: "担ぐ is more like when you're carrying something physical. 担う is when you carry a responsibility, which is why this word means to assume responsibility. You can remember this because YOU (う) are responsible for this. You assume this responsibility." "What is your responsibility? To raise this girl named Nina (にな)."

example_sentences.english: My company’s profits soared 70% over last year and I played an important part in achieving that.

notes: "The movement that has to do with shakes is vibration and oscillation." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.english: I like feeling the vibration of an engine in a car.

notes: "If you're anti- something in a way that's different from the norm then you'll be in violation of the law! The laws that the ""not"" different people made. Either way, those people will give you a hard time for your anti-stance against the thing they like, and say it's a transgression." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You haven't learned this reading for 違 yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you:If you find yourself in violation of the law just pull out your pet eagle (い). Eagles are so majestic, they'll forget all about your transgression and let you go. If you're going to go be anti-something make sure you bring that eagle. People seem to care more about animals than other people like that."

example_sentences.japanese: スピード違反で捕まった。
example_sentences.english: I was caught speeding.

notes: "When you want to know what the circumstances are around you, you have to ask why. Why do things happen around you? Asking why is very important if you want to understand the world." "The reading for this is an exception. The reading for 何 is just the first な from なに. You can remember the second part this way:No one knows quite how or why that big zeppelin (ぜ) crashed in the 1930s. People are still asking today and no one has any answers. We have to keep asking until we get some."

example_sentences.japanese: 何故復讐しようと思ったんですか。
example_sentences.english: How do you think you’ll get your revenge?

example_sentences.japanese: 果てしなく続く空の下で、生徒たちは果てしなく長くて退屈な校長の話を聞かなくてはならなかった。
example_sentences.english: Beneath the endless sky, students had to listen to the principal’s endless and boring speech.

example_sentences.english: """I’ve had several job interviews, but I haven’t received any job offers yet.” “Join the club.”"

notes: "Step by step. If you take step by step, you're moving up gradually, taking steps." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.english: """Guess what? I got a promotion at work!"" ""Really? That’s awesome! Congrats!"""

example_sentences.english: Why don’t you leave school early with me?

example_sentences.english: Nobody found their way out of the maze.

example_sentences.japanese: 後で、今日習った日本語での両替の仕方について復習したいと思います。

example_sentences.japanese: そろそろYoutube界を引退しようと考えてるんだ。
example_sentences.english: I intend to retire from the Youtube world soon.

english: To Be Misguided, To Be Led Astray, To Be Perplexed, To Be Puzzled
notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means misguided so the verb vocab version is to be misguided." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: If you are going to be misguided you're going to be mad (まど) about it, most likely. Nobody likes to be misguided, so imagine how mad you feel when you are."

example_sentences.english: The perplexed deer was spinning in circles, so we shot it in the neck.

english: To Carry To Extremes, To Carry To The Extreme, To Take To The Extreme, To Take To An Extreme, To Carry To An Extreme, To Take To Extremes, To Master
notes:
"Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means extreme. The verb vocab version isn't ""to extreme"" because that wouldn't make sense. Instead, you carry it to extremes, making this word to carry to extremes." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: When you go to carry to extremes, you're going too far, so there has to be a key word (きわ) that you say to make the other person stop. ""CACAO! CACAO!"""

"極める is ""to carry to extremes."" If you carry something to the extremes (aka the end), and then you see it to the extremes while doing it, you're going to see through whatever you're doing." "The readings come from the words 見る and 極める put together. See through this word and learn it."

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語を極めるのは、生易しい事ではない。
example_sentences.english: It is no easy task to master the Japanese language.

example_sentences.japanese: 自分のこの目で真実を見極めたいんです。
example_sentences.english: I want to see the truth with my own eyes.

notes: "Remember how you learned that 渡す means ""to hand over?"" Well you can use your actual hand to hand over something too! " The readings for this word are both kun'yomi readings. You learned them when you learned the kanji, so you should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: プレゼントを手渡す勇気はありません。
example_sentences.english: I don’t have the courage to hand him the present.

notes: "You know 抜く from before, it's to extract. Then you have 出す which is to remove. So, if you extract and remove something, you are moving to extract something. By extracting it you are also going to select it as well." "The readings are from 抜く and 出す, combined together. Know those two and you'll be able to read this word as well."

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は背広から銃をそっと抜き出した。
example_sentences.english: He secretly started to pull a gun out of his business suit.

example_sentences.english: """Kinnikuma yells a lot."" ""Yeah, but don’t worry. His bark is worse than his bite."""

notes: "This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: Who do you need to stoop and to bow before? Takeshi Kaga (かが), that's Chairman Kaga to you! Before you can start cooking for him in Iron Chef, you must bow! Otherwise you'll be disqualified for being rude."

example_sentences.japanese: 屈むと腰が痛いんです。
example_sentences.english: I get a pain in my lower back when I bend down.

notes: "Your specialty, which you focus on with aggression, is your major in college (your college major). Study hard, young grasshopper." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はファイン・アートを専攻しています。
example_sentences.english: I’m majoring in fine art.

notes: "Shift your dwellings! Everyone shift! Somewhere else, please. Time for a migration." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: それはあなたがこの国に移住して来るか来ないかによります。
example_sentences.english: That depends on whether or not you will move to this country.

notes:
"Line up and go together. If lines did that, they'd be parallel." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

"Flatten out your equilibrium and you'll have perfect balance." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 複数の言語を並行して勉強することは、ひとつだけを学習するよりも効率的だと聞いたことがあります。
example_sentences.english: I heard that studying multiple languages at the same time is more efficient than only studying one.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は突然体の平衡を失い、ひっくり返った。
example_sentences.english: She suddenly lost her balance and toppled over.

notes: "The profit is really a benefit. Let's make more profit then." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: この新しいタイプの下着が、莫大な年間利益を上げることを予想しています。
example_sentences.english: We are expecting that this new type of underwear will yield a large annual profit.

notes: "Climb up and record your information here. This is registration. It's work to get yourself registered (from the climbing) and even if you get your name recorded on there, you may not get in. So record your information, wait, and hope you get in." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 三宅結花です。携帯電話を変えたので、新しい電話番号とメールアドレスの登録をお願いします。
example_sentences.english: This is Yuka Miyake. I’ve changed my phone, so could you register my new number and email address in your address book, please? Thank you.

notes: "Discipline is the reason why you're able to do a repair on things. It takes a lot of time to fix something, and takes a lot of studying. That discipline is what you need, and you have it. Thus, it was repaired!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 「おい、修理屋。これはすぐに直せるか？」「って、君たちの関係ってこと？悪いけど、それはできないよ。」
example_sentences.english: """Hey, repairman. Can you fix this right now?"" ""You mean, you guys’ relationship? Sorry. No can do."""

notes: "A record of sound is a sound recording of some kind. Might be minidisk, might be CD, might be digital. Whatever it is, it's still the record of sound." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 誰かがいびき録音用枕の特許を取得したというのは本当ですよ。
example_sentences.english: Someone actually got a patent for a snore recording pillow.

notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means frozen, so the vocab version is to freeze." "The reading actually comes from the word 氷, which means ""ice."" You can kind of see where the origins of these words come from, now... really cold frozen things. So, think back to こおり, then change the り to a る and put it outside the kanji. That makes the reading for this こおる, in all (or most) of 氷's glory."

example_sentences.japanese: オレンジジュースを凍らせて氷を作ったことはありますか。
example_sentences.english: Have you ever made ice cubes by freezing orange juice?

notes: "Sharpen your discipline, whatever that might be. Could be kanji, could be baseball, could be curling. Whatever it is, when you sharpen it, you have to study. You have to do training. It's the only way to get better." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: その研修は午後3時に始まる予定です。
example_sentences.english: The training session is set to begin at 3 p.m.
