notes: "We're going to deal with it by putting this up your butt and giving you the treatment you need. Kancho!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 誰か彼に応急処置ができる人はいませんか。
example_sentences.english: Is there anyone who could give him first aid?

notes: "Conserve those letters with abbreviation and it's... an abbreviation! By using omission you were able to abbreviate that word into a smaller word." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 時間の都合上、今は詳細については省略せざるを得ませんが、また後ほどご説明させて頂きます。
example_sentences.english: I have to omit the details for now due to time constraints, but I’ll explain it to you later.

notes: "Append and attach this document to your email. It's an attachment." "The reading for 添 is what you'd expect. The reading for 付 is the on'yomi reading, which you've never learned. It's ふ, but for this word it becomes ぷ from the rendaku fairies. Just think of an attachment where instead of a document or something, you get an attachment of poop (ぷ). What a gross attachment. Your friend who likes to send poop attachments is dumb."

example_sentences.japanese: 人事部長様、 恐れ入りますが、このEメールに添付された履歴書にお目通し頂けますでしょうか。お忙しいとは存じますが、よろしくお願い申し上げます。
example_sentences.english: Dear hiring manager, please have a look at the resume attached to this email. Thank you for your time.

notes: "When something collapses and breaks, it is when a collapse happens. When this happens, it is destruction. It is also probably something that was already crumbling apart." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の祖父母の家はとても古いので、雪の重みで倒壊しかねません。
example_sentences.english: My grandparents’ house is so old that it could collapse under the weight of the snow.

notes: "To break it all is to break everything. Everything is broken. Complete destruction!!!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: マイホームを持っていたんですが、台風で全壊しちゃったんですよ。
example_sentences.english: I had my own house, but it was completely destroyed by the typhoon.

notes: "When you approach to give something, you are probably giving a contribution." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: Tofuguが世界平和に寄与していることを知っているかい？
example_sentences.english: Did you know that Tofugu is contributing to world peace?

notes: "If you approach a building and attach some stuff to it, you're making a contribution. They get to keep it, after all. " This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎年少しだけ、母校へお金を寄付しています。
example_sentences.english: I contribute a little money to my alma mater every year.

notes: "You need something so you request it. But, since it's such a strong need, it's not really a request, it's more of a demand." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 労働組合は賃上げを要請した。
example_sentences.english: The labor unions demanded a wage increase.

notes: "You request then you request again. This is starting to turn into more of a demand if you ask me. Also can refer to a claim or a charge as well." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 請求書の金額が間違っているように思うので私はその請求を取り消す。
example_sentences.english: I’m going to cancel that bill because I think we were invoiced for the wrong amount.

notes: "I'm going to cut off the part of me that I'm trying to diagnose... well, not literally cut off, but cut off my diagnosing. I have come to a conclusion. A diagnosis!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の息子は四歳の時に喘息だと診断されました。
example_sentences.english: My son was diagnosed with asthma when he was four.

notes: "極める is ""to carry to extremes."" So, 極めて is something similar. It's used to refer to something that's extremely _______." "The reading comes from 極める."

example_sentences.japanese: 君がこの問題の解決方法について具体的には何も考えていないというのは、極めて明白な事実だ。
example_sentences.english: It’s extremely obvious that you don’t have any idea how we can solve this problem.

notes: "A dry cup of liquid is one that's worth cheering to. This is the Japanese way to say ""cheers!"" or ""toast"" or whatever else you say before drinking something." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: さあ、乾杯、乾杯！それ、ぐいと一杯、飲み干したまえ。
example_sentences.english: Alright, cheers cheers! Hey, bottoms up!

notes: "You examine then search. These are the steps you take in order to perform a lookup of some kind (or, as the case may be in modern times, do an internet search)." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 後でネットで検索してみるよ。
example_sentences.english: I’ll look it up on the Internet later.

notes: "I'm going to diagnose you and then make a guess as to what's wrong with you during this medical exam." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生は診察の予定がみっちり詰まっています。
example_sentences.english: The doctor has a jam-packed medical exam schedule.

english: Nap, Doze, Dozing, Nodding Off, Dozing Off
notes: "Sometimes even though you're very much awake and alive you need to sleep for a little bit, so you take a nap. But you're not dead! You're totally alive, so let's hope no one thinks you're doing anything but dozing off." The readings for this word are both kun'yomi readings. You've learned both of these readings by now so you should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 運転中に居眠りしてたみたいなんだ。
example_sentences.english: It seems like they dozed off while driving.

notes: "When you sponsor an announcement, you're allowing those you're sponsoring to create some kind of notification for all those they want to get in contact with." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: サラ金から、借金の返済を求める催告状が何度も何度も届いています。
example_sentences.english: A consumer credit company has been sending me notification letters over and over, demanding that I pay back my debt.

english: Observation, Monitor, Keep Watch Over, Surveillance
notes: "You oversee and look at all that is in your domain. You are keeping an observation over everything." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 監視カメラは持ってるんですが、まだテープを確認した事はないんですよね。ちゃんと撮れてるのかな。
example_sentences.english: I have a surveillance camera, but I haven’t checked the tape yet. I wonder if it’s working properly.

english: One Cup, One Cup Of Liquid, A Drink, One Drink
notes: "One cup of liquid is equal to one cup (or one cup of liquid)." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 「ちょっと一杯飲みに行かない？」「いいね。」
example_sentences.english: """Let’s go for a drink."" ""Sounds like a plan."""

notes: "I request and then I request again. So many requests, but nobody will listen to me. My last hope is to get a bunch of people who have the same ideas together and make a petition." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: もしご迷惑でなければ請願書に署名して頂けませんでしょうか。
example_sentences.english: If you wouldn’t mind, would you please sign this petition?

notes: "A search search is a more intense search, like the ones for a missing person." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 警察は捜索活動を続けています。
example_sentences.english: The police are continuing to work on the investigation.

notes:
"The master who sponsors you is the one who provides your sponsorship. Without this person, you wouldn't have sponsorship at all, which is why you call them ""master"" (plus, that was one of the rules with the sponsorship)." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

"The master manager rules over all of the other managers and he's in charge of their supervision. If anything goes wrong it will be blamed on him! He has to keep a close watch on them!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 競馬場の芝についてのシンポジウムが市当局の主催で開かれた。
example_sentences.english: The racetrack turf symposium was able happen because of city government sponsorship.

example_sentences.japanese: いつか自分の劇団を主宰するのが夢です。
example_sentences.english: I dream of supervising my own theater troupe someday.

notes: "The one who oversees and coaches is the one who gives the supervision and direction. I see it all! I coach!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: あの映画監督の名前が思い出せないんだけど。何て名前だっけ。もうここまで出かかってるんだけどな。あー、気持ち悪い！
example_sentences.english: I can’t remember the name of that movie director. What was his name? It’s on the tip of my tongue though. Uhg, crap!

notes: "I fear it. It is scary. It is pure terror." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ヤクザにお釣りが百円足りないと言われた時に、とてつもない恐怖を感じました。
example_sentences.english: When a yakuza told me that the change I gave him was 100 yen short, I felt an incredible amount of fear.

notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means abbreviation, so the verb vocab version is to abbreviate." "The reading is, strangely, the same as the reading you learned with the kanji. りゃくす."

example_sentences.japanese: 日本の若者はすぐ単語やフレーズを略したがる。
example_sentences.english: Young Japanese people tend to abbreviate words and phrases.

english: To Accumulate, To Get Piled Up
notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means accumulate and the verb version is to accumulate." "If something accumulates, you can start with one, but you need at least two (つ) things to say it has accumulated. If you don't, then there's nothing accumulating at all."

example_sentences.japanese: 体重を減らすために、日常の食事の量を極端に減らす必要はないよ。それよりも、バランスの良い、健康な食事を取ることの方が重要だ。ちりも積もれば山となるって言うじゃないか。
example_sentences.english: You don’t have to drastically decrease the amount of food you normally eat to lose weight. It is more important to have a balanced, healthy diet. It’s said every little bit counts.

english: To Anger Someone, To Anger, To Provoke, To Offend Someone
notes: "Remember how you learned that 怒る means ""to get angry?"" Well this is when someone else gets angry and it's because YOU made them angry. It means ""to anger someone.""" "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You learned this reading when you learned 怒る, so you should know this one too!"

example_sentences.japanese: 父さんを怒らせると後が面倒よ。
example_sentences.english: You’ll be in trouble after making dad mad.

english: To Get Lost, To Be Lost
notes: "Remember 迷う? It means ""to get lost."" If you get lost on a road, you are still lost, wandering around looking for the correct turn. This word means to be lost or to get lost." "The reading comes from the words 道 and 迷う."

example_sentences.japanese: 私は道に迷うのが得意です。
example_sentences.english: I’m good at getting lost.

english: To Get Mad, To Get Angry
notes: "What's that feeling when your belly stands up? It's that feeling where something jumps up into your throat (in this case your belly) and you get all pissed off. This word means to get mad. " "The readings are 腹 plus 立つ put together. The たつ becomes だつ, though."

example_sentences.japanese: そんなに腹立てるなって。大したことじゃないじゃん。放っておきなよ。
example_sentences.english: Don’t get so upset about it. It’s not that big a deal. Let it go.

notes: "I'm so for this I'm willing to sponsor you. I am going to urge you to do this until you do it, so much so I'll give you money. This is one great urge and press for you to do this!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: どうすれば顧客に未払分の支払手続きを丁寧かつ強く催促することができるのでしょうか。
example_sentences.english: How can I press a customer to take action on his overdue payment politely but also strongly?

notes: "You are floating above everything, at least that's how your spirit feels. You're having an affair, and feel like nothing will catch you but... wait, what's that? Is that your wife? Oh no... not floating anymore, you're not." This kanji uses the kun'yomi read for the first kanji, and the on'yomi reading for the second. You've learned them both already, so you should be able to read this too.

example_sentences.japanese: 「彼は浮気をして、それを携帯電話を持っていないあなたのせいにしたってこと？」「要約するとそんなところね。」
example_sentences.english: """So he had an affair and then blamed it on you for not having a cellphone?"" ""That about sums it up."""

english: A Look, A Glance, List, Table
notes: "One look at... just one. A little one. Just a look. Just a glance. That's all I want.It also has another meaning! When you're talking about computers and you want to see everything in one look, you will arrange it into a nice list or table. That way you only have to look at the data one time!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 連絡先の一覧から中々上司の名前が見つからないんだけど。
example_sentences.english: I’m struggling to find my boss’s name on my contact list.

notes: "You change again. This is more along the lines of an alteration, because you changed once in order to get to where you are, and then you get changed again to become altered, which is why it's an alteration (though change works too)." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 上司に、もっとお互いのメリットを強調するような企画書に変更するように言われました。
example_sentences.english: My boss told me to alter the business proposal so that it emphasized the mutual benefits more.

notes: "Deposit your gold here in the bank. When you do that, it is a bank deposit." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は帆立の養殖で稼いだ金は全て預金している。
example_sentences.english: He deposits all the money he earns from raising scallops.

notes: "The kanji and the word are almost exactly the same, but instead of just meaning again it also means furthermore and moreover. This is one of those good paragraph-starting essay words!" "The reading is a bit different from what you learned with the kanji, though. Just think about how again he dropped the 皿 (さら). Wow, what a screw up. Again and again."

example_sentences.japanese: 留学後、更に英語を上達させるには、ネイティブスピーカーと喋り続ける必要があります。
example_sentences.english: After studying abroad you need to continue speaking to native speakers to further improve your English.

notes: "We are lacking and things are scarce. We have a lack and scarcity of resources." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ビタミンDが欠乏しているかどうかはどうすれば分かりますか。
example_sentences.english: How can I know if I’m deficient in Vitamin D?

notes: "Something is leaking and whatever is leaking is exiting what it was in before. This is when a leak out occurs." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 原油の海への漏出事故を防ぐために、どんな手段を講じていますか。
example_sentences.english: What kind of measures does your company take to prevent accidental leakage of crude oil into the sea?

notes: "Let's bind this marriage up with a marriage. No better way to make a marriage happen than a marriage, right?" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 「シャーク、私がフグと結婚したってどうして分かったの？」 「ただ人づてに聞いただけさ。」
example_sentences.english: """Shark, how did you know that I got married to Fugu?"" ""You know. I just heard it through the grapevine."""

notes: "When you request marriage with someone else, you are doing a marriage proposal. Will you marry me, Brad Pitt?" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ホタルは、どの求婚者にも、結婚の条件として無理難題を突き付けた。
example_sentences.english: Hotaru sets impossible tasks for any man who wants to marry her.

notes: "Back in the day, you'd use shadows to photograph things. Now it's all fancy and digital. So, with that in mind, a photograph shadow was someone doing a photoshoot of some kind. And, in even more modern times, it has become a movie shoot as well. More simply, it can be photographing or filming as well. Basically, if it has to do with taking photos or video, 撮影 is your dude." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: お待たせして申し訳ございません。それでは、撮影を始めましょうか。
example_sentences.english: I’m sorry to have kept you waiting. Let’s start shooting now.

notes:
"Steal what other people make? Wow. Way to go. That is plagiarism." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

"When your confused urges overthrow normal thoughts and feelings it's a perversion. Some are harmless, but some are not." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 他人の作品をパクったら、盗作で訴えられるかもしれないよ。
example_sentences.english: If you stole someone else’s work, you could be sued for plagiarism.

example_sentences.japanese: 倒錯思考はまず現実否定から始まる。
example_sentences.english: Perverse thoughts first negate reality.

notes: "Prolong it for a long while. We need more time. We need a prolonging or  extension of some kind." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 延長コードがごちゃごちゃになっているのが許せないの。
example_sentences.english: I can’t stand how extensions cords get tangled up.

notes: "If you exit that edition out of your hands and into the world, you've gotten something published! That is publishing." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: その本を出版するのに二年もかかりました。
example_sentences.english: It took me two years to publish the book.

notes: "When your subscription enters into effect, you have made your purchase. This one's a bit weird because it seems like it should refer to a subscription, but I guess it is a one time subscription, and your subscription lasts your whole life?" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: この店で偽のシャネルN°5を購入しました。
example_sentences.english: This is the store where I bought the fake Chanel Number 5.

notes: "If you create subscriptions to buy things, you're probably in the purchasing department. It's your responsibility to set up subscriptions and buy everything for everyone else because you're the purchasing person." "The reading is on'yomi, which is great for 購 but not as great for 買. Luckily, the reading for 買 is buy (ばい), which is the same as the meaning, which is a pretty awesome coincidence."

example_sentences.japanese: 私は消費者の購買意欲について研究をしています。
example_sentences.english: I’m researching customers’ purchasing motivations.

notes: "And again it has become new! It was old, but now it's all nice. This is quite the renewal." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 先方は、いくつかの修正を伴う契約更新を提案してきているんだが、あまり気が進まないんだよね。
example_sentences.english: They are proposing an updated contract with several alterations, but I’m still reluctant.

notes: "Stealing photographs of you. Wait, you didn't know you were being photographed / filmed? That's secret photography or secret filming Creeeeeepy." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 電車内で居眠りしているところを盗撮されたんです。
example_sentences.english: Photos were taken of me in secret while I was napping on the train.

notes: "A subscription has been read. Each magazine that comes in you read. This is your subscription." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Since you didn't learn the on'yomi for 読 (どく) with the kanji, here's a mnemonic to help you out. You just got a subscription to dock (どく) magazine. It's all about docks and dock related things. How exciting."

example_sentences.japanese: 全アメリカ人がTofuguのニュースレターを購読しているという噂が、日本中に広まった。
example_sentences.english: The rumor that all American people subscribe to the Tofugu news letter spread throughout Japan.

english: To Be Fragrant, To Smell Good
notes: "This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means scent or fragrance so the verb version is to be fragrant or to smell good." Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You learned this reading with the kanji, so you should be able to read it already!

example_sentences.japanese: この香水は、全く匂わない。
example_sentences.english: This perfume doesn't smell at all.

example_sentences.japanese: その工場からは、チョコレートの香りが匂います。
example_sentences.english: It smells like chocolate from the factory.

example_sentences.japanese: 春の花畑では、色んな種類のチューリップが匂い、人がたくさん訪れて香りを楽しみます。
example_sentences.english: In spring, different kinds of tulips are fragrant at the flower garden and people visit to enjoy the smells.

notes: "冷たい is ""cold."" This is the verb version, so you're making something cold. This word is to chill something." "To Chill something, you need to apply cold, not heat (ひ)."

example_sentences.japanese: 指をドアで挟んじゃって、今氷で冷やしてるの。
example_sentences.english: My finger got caught in the door and I’m chilling it with ice now.

notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means decorate. The verb vocab version is to decorate." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: To decorate something, you don't really need a cause (かざ). You should just do it, just because."

example_sentences.japanese: クリスマスツリーの飾り付けをするのが好きです。今年はツリーを暖炉の横に飾りました。
example_sentences.english: I like decorating the Christmas tree. I put it beside our fireplace this year.

english: To Feel Embarrassed, To Be Shy, To Be Embarrassed, To Feel Shy
notes: "If you illuminate the things I've done, I start to feel embarrassed. Please don't embarrass me. :(" "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: The thing you feel the most embarrassed about is your 手 (て). It's all blue and scary looking."

example_sentences.japanese: えっ、有り難う。照れるなぁ。
example_sentences.english: Oh, thank you. I’m blushing!

notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means push so the verb vocab version is to push." The reading is the one you learned with the kanji, actually!

example_sentences.japanese: すみません。今朝タイムカードを押し忘れちゃったんですが、どうすればいいですか？
example_sentences.english: I’m sorry I forgot to punch my timecard this morning. What should I do?

notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means steal, so the verb vocab version is to steal." "What are you going to steal? How about a noose (ぬす)? Wait, why are you stealing a noose? That sounds like trouble to me..."

example_sentences.japanese: あいつは絶対に中途半端なことはしない奴だから、3106カラットのダイヤモンドを盗むための壮大な計画を立てているに違いない。
example_sentences.english: He’s the kind of guy who never does something halfway, so he must have a magnificent plan to steal the 3106 carat diamond.

english: To Wet, To Moisten, To Dampen, To Soak
notes: "This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means wet or damp, so the verb version is to wet or to dampen something." Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You learned this reading with the kanji, so you should be able to read it already!

example_sentences.japanese: 髪をよく濡らしてから、シャンプーをするといいですよ。
example_sentences.english: It's good to wet your hair before shampooing.

example_sentences.japanese: 大事なUSBなので、コーヒーや水で濡らさないで下さいね。
example_sentences.english: This USB is important, so please be careful not to get it wet with coffee or water.

example_sentences.japanese: 先輩にフラれてから、毎日涙で枕を濡らしています。
example_sentences.english: Since I was dumped by my senpai, I've been soaking my pillow with tears.

notes: "If you view and look at something, you are viewing that thing, or seeing it." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: TofuguTVの撮影現場を観覧しました。
example_sentences.english: I watched the TofuguTV shooting.

notes:
"A leak of water is a water leakage." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

"An elderly person in decline is someone who is old and in decline. They are experiencing senility or senile decay." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: どんなに値段が高くても、その漏水検出器を買うべきだと思います。
example_sentences.english: No matter how expensive it is, we should buy the water leakage sensor.

example_sentences.japanese: 母親が老衰で亡くなったとき、妻が「厄介者がいなくなってせいせいした」と独り言を言っているのを私は聞き漏らしませんでした。
example_sentences.english: "When my mother died from old age, I didn’t fail to hear my wife mutter, ""that parasite is gone, good riddance,"" to herself."

notes: "I'm so surprised it caused me to sigh. This is like when you run into a movie star, and you go in surprise shock. Then, you breathe out in a sigh because of your great amount of admiration and wonder for this person." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: その太陽光発電所の規模に驚嘆しました。
example_sentences.english: I was amazed at the size of the solar power plant.

notes: "One of the meanings is the same as the kanji, previously, but it can also mean already." "The reading is different from what you learned with the kanji. But as I told you already, I'll be there on Su-day (すで). It's like Sunday, but not quite the same. Imagine your confusion when someone says this over and over, but you don't know what Suday is."

example_sentences.japanese: 私が電話した時、彼は既に退社してしまってました。
example_sentences.english: He had already left his office when I called him.

notes: "When someone determines something, it's probably okay. But, when the model determiner determines something, that is the best determination ever. That is the appraisal of someone with an expert opinion." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: お前が赤ん坊の本当の父親かどうかを調べるために、DNA鑑定を受けた方がいいんじゃないか。
example_sentences.english: You should take a DNA test to find out if you are his real father.

english: A Stroll, A Walk, Stroll, Walk
notes: "Scatter around the ground and walk. When you walk in a scatter all around, you're going for a walk or a stroll." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. The ほ goes to ぽ, though."

example_sentences.japanese: 散歩をする時は、小銭しか持ち歩きません。
example_sentences.english: I bring change with me when I go for walks.

notes: "Something that's flat and equal to everything around it, all those flat things around it, are average. They're the mean (same as average)." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 2014年のセンター試験の平均点が出ました。
example_sentences.english: The average grade for 2014’s National Center Test for University Admissions was revealed.

notes: "Untie and scatter everything. This will cause a breakup and dissolution of whatever is being untied then scattered." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 私達にとって、衆議院を解散するメリットとデメリットは何ですか？
example_sentences.english: What are the advantages and disadvantages of dissolving the House of Representatives?

notes: "Sweep and exclude all that dirt from the floor, please. When you do this a lot, it becomes cleaning." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. For this one though, you have to remember to read the 除 part as じ. Just keep in mind that cleaning (cleanliness) is next to godliness and so is Jesus (じ). So, Jesus is like cleaning. Easy."

example_sentences.japanese: まずやるべきことをやらなくてはね。部屋の掃除から始めようか。
example_sentences.english: First things first. Let’s start by cleaning your room.

notes: "Detach from your marriage. This is a divorce." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 「彼とは離婚するつもりなの。」「ちょっ…早まらないで。決断する前によく考えて。」
example_sentences.english: """I’m going to divorce with him."" ""Don’t be so rash. Think about it more before you make a decision."""

notes: "Knit and gather everything back together, which you knit. When you do this to fix things and bring it back together, this is an edit." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: どうしてブログ記事を編集するのに一時間もかかったんですか。
example_sentences.english: Why did it take you an hour to edit a blog article?

notes: "Exclude this one and put it outside what we're considering. This is the exception." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: その馬はソエにより競争除外となりました。
example_sentences.english: The horse was excluded from the race due to shin soreness.

notes: "Dissolve your resources, because you need to pay back your financing and loans now." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 銀行の融資を受けるのは思っていたよりも難しかったです。
example_sentences.english: Getting a bank loan was more difficult than I thought.

notes: "Dissolve and then join together again to create a reaction, a fusion reaction." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 俺たちのバンドは、ジャズとロックが融合した音楽を演奏しています。
example_sentences.english: Our band plays music that is a fusion of jazz and rock.

notes: "How many occurences is just another way of asking how many times." The reading is a combination of kun'yomi and on'yomi readings. That being said, both readings for both kanji are the readings you learned with the kanji so you should be able to read this.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は、幾度失敗しても、諦めなかった。
example_sentences.english: Even though he failed many times, he didn’t give up.

notes: "This has the same meaning as the kanji, specifically the how much meaning. To remember this, just think about how Ra, the Egyptian God, is always asking ""How much will it cost to build this pyramid?"" Ugh, too much, let's hire some slaves." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 送料が幾らになるのか教えて頂けませんでしょうか。
example_sentences.english: Could you tell me how much the shipping will be, please?

notes: "You're taking reality and trying to resemble it. To do this, you have to do an impersonation." "This word uses the kun'yomi reading for 真 and the on'yomi reading for 似. You've learned them both already, so you should be able to read this on your own."

example_sentences.japanese: 四歳になる娘が、見るもの全てを真似するので困っています。
example_sentences.english: I am having trouble because my four-year-old daughter imitates everything she sees.

english: Private Detective, Private Investigator, Detective, Sleuth, Investigator
notes: "You look for things and you spy on people. Your job isn't as glamorous as it sounds. You're a private detective." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は結局探偵になりました。
example_sentences.english: She ended up becoming a private detective.

notes: "When you inquire about a problem, you tend to do questioning about said problem. Why is it like this? What happened? Is it bigger than a breadbox?" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 警察は関係者全員を尋問しました。
example_sentences.english: The police questioned everyone who was involved.

notes: "Look for something. Research answers. This is research." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 我々はその原因を探究している。
example_sentences.english: We’re researching the cause.

notes: "Inside spying is when you get inside enemy territory and spy on them. This is scouting and reconnaissance." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 警察はどんな時に内偵捜査をするのですか。
example_sentences.english: When do the police conduct their secret internal investigation?

notes: "If you take apart and detach it from the group into its own separate group, that's just segregation, isn't it?" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: クリームを牛乳から分離させる方法をググってみるよ。
example_sentences.english: I’m going to google how to separate cream from milk.

notes: "A sigh breath is a sigh." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 他人よりも自分がずっと短足だと気づいた時、彼は深々と嘆息して、日本短足協会へと向かった。
example_sentences.english: When he realized that his legs were much shorter than other peoples’ he sighed deeply and headed to the Japan Short Leg Association.

english: To Be Rich, To Be Wealthy
notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means rich so the verb vocab version would be to be rich." "Think about the richest person you know. That person is Tom (む). Imagine Tom as being super rich. If you don't know a Tom, think of a famous Tom, like Tom Cruise, who definitely is pretty rich."

example_sentences.japanese: カナダはカナディアンベーコンに富む。
example_sentences.english: Canada is rich with Canadian bacon.

english: To Be Scared, To Be Afraid Of, To Fear
notes: "怖い is ""scary."" This is a verb version, making it to be scared or to be afraid of." "The reading comes from 怖い."

example_sentences.japanese: 私の主人は逆さ睫毛の手術を受けるのをとても怖がっていたんですよ。
example_sentences.english: My husband was very scared of getting surgery for his ingrown eyelashes.

english: To Kill Off, To Let Die Out
notes: "絶える is ""to die out."" 絶やす is ""to kill off."" You know this because if something is to die off, you'd say ""no."" But if you're the one doing the killing off, you'd say yes (やす)." "The reading comes from 絶える."

example_sentences.japanese: 夜の間、火を絶やさないように気をつけるんだぞ。
example_sentences.english: Make sure the fire doesn’t go out during the night.

notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means knit so the verb vocab version is to knit." "When you start to knit, you always end up with the same thing every time when you're done, no matter what you're trying to make: The letter ""A"" (あ). It's so frustrating that you can't knit anything else."

example_sentences.japanese: ブラジャーを編んでみようと思ったきっかけはなんですか。
example_sentences.english: What inspired you to knit bras?

notes: "The word 迷う means ""to go astray"" but this word is to lead astray. You are doing the astraying to someone or something else. You know this because the other person was (わす) just fine until you came along to lead them astray." "The reading comes from 迷う, so use that so you aren't lead astray too."

example_sentences.japanese: もし俺の娘を路頭に迷わすようなことがあったら、一生許さないぞ。
example_sentences.english: If you lead my daughter astray, I’ll never forgive you.

english: To Pile Things Up, To Accumulate
notes:
"積もる is ""to accumulate."" Now you're doing the accumulating, and in order to do that you must go to pile things up. More and more and more. How do you know that this verb is when you're doing the accumulating? It's because you are piling up cows (む). Wow, a cow piler." "The reading comes from 積もる, so pile up your knowledge and remember it that way."

"Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means pluck so the verb vocab version is to pluck or to pick or to prune, like with plants." "You are going outside to pluck some tulips (つ)."

example_sentences.japanese: それじゃあ2人組を作って、トラックに七面鳥を積み始めて下さい。
example_sentences.english: Now please grab a partner and begin loading the truck with turkey.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は薔薇の花びらを一枚一枚丁寧に手で摘んでいきます。
example_sentences.english: She carefully picks each rose petal by hand.

notes: "If you eat vegetable food you practice vegetarianism." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 菜食主義者の人は偽善者が多いっていう意見に賛成してくれる人はいますか。
example_sentences.english: Does anyone else agree that vegetarians tend to be hypocrites?

notes: "It has become that we agree. We have agreement!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本が新たな移民を受け入れることには賛成ですか。
example_sentences.english: Do you support Japan accepting new immigrants?

notes: "A fire wound is a burn or scald you got from fire (or other hot things). Ouch!" "The reading for this is unlike anything you've seen with these kanji. Try to think about a burn (on your arm) being caused by a yakky dodo (やけど) bird (which is a dodo bird that has yak-like features). Take a look at how weird it is, and wonder why it is burning you. Feel the pains."

example_sentences.japanese: カレーを零して、手に火傷を負った。
example_sentences.english: I spilled curry and got a burn on my hand.

notes: "If 騒ぐ is ""to make noise,"" then a big version of this is even louder. It's a clamor and an uproar." "This is word that uses the kun'yomi readings of the kanji, which you should know already because 大 is pretty familiar to you by now (I hope) and you just learned 騒ぐ as well! Put them together, with a little tweaking at the end, and you have your reading. Ta-da!"

example_sentences.japanese: どこかの国で、子供用の股の部分が開いたセクシー下着が販売されて大騒ぎになっていたことがあったよね。
example_sentences.english: I remember that selling crotchless panties for kids created an uproar in some country.

notes: "For this word, the 便 comes from 便所, which you know as ""toilet."" A toilet secret is one you take with you to the bathroom, one that you don't want people to know about. This is constipation." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. The ひ changes to ぴ because ""P"" stands for ""Poop."""

example_sentences.japanese: 便秘がひどくてさぁ。もう一週間以上ウンコしていないんだよ！
example_sentences.english: I’ve been constipated. I haven’t pooped in a week!

notes: "When you make a duplicate copy you are copying things. You are making a duplication." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 一枚目はお手元にお持ちください。私達は複写の方を頂きますね。
example_sentences.english: You can keep the original, but we’ll take a copy.

notes: "Your intention for your hope is what you want. It's not just a hope. You have intention behind it. This is your desire. This is your ambition." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: この仕事を志望する動機は何ですか？
example_sentences.english: What is your motivation for applying for this job?

notes: "English translate is an English translation." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語から英訳することしかできません。
example_sentences.english: All I can do is to translate from Japanese to English.

notes: "The feeling of dye, covering your body, is the feeling of nasty germs and diseases penetrating your skin, getting inside of you. This is an infection, and it's gross." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 歯周病は感染症の一種だとは知りませんでした。
example_sentences.english: I didn’t know that periodontitis is a type of infectious disease.

notes: "If you let words pass through you, and as they do you translate them, you are doing interpreting." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: もし私が全能の神だったら、この会話を通訳してあげることができるけど、そうじゃないから無理だわ。ごめんよ。
example_sentences.english: If I were omnipotent, I would be able to interpret this conversation for you, but I’m not, so I can’t. Sorry.

notes: "Remember how 和 represents Japan? Now, take that and add translate to it. With that, you have Japanese translation." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: いくつか小さな間違いはあるものの、うまく和訳できていると思いますよ。
example_sentences.english: Aside from some minor mistakes, I think your Japanese translation was pretty good.

notes: "A dirty dye that's all throughout the sky and makes things gross when it touches them is pollution. If it's bad enough it really is like a dye, too, making your white clothes brown, yuck." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 自国のPM2.5汚染レベルはどうすれば分かるのでしょうか。
example_sentences.english: How can I find out about PM2.5 contamination levels in my community?

notes: "In secrecy you must announce this information. It's not for anyone to hear, it's secret information." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. The みつ goes to みっ."

example_sentences.japanese: とある会社の脱税について、税務署に密告したいと思ってるんです。
example_sentences.english: I’d like to inform the tax office about a company’s tax evasion.

notes: "A secrecy meet is a secret meeting. You know the password?" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 私達は密会によくこの部屋を利用しています。
example_sentences.english: We often make use of this room for secret meetings.

notes: "Self defense is when you protect yourself. It's self defense." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 自衛のための殺人は合法なのでしょうか。
example_sentences.english: Is it legal to murder someone in self defense?

notes: "A secrecy transport is when you transport something in secrecy. If you don't want people to know what you're transporting, you'll have to resort to smuggling." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 俺は一度麻薬の密輸をする話を持ちかけられたことがあるよ。もちろん断ったけどね。
example_sentences.english: I was asked to smuggle narcotics once.  Of course I refused.

english: Strictly Forbidden, Strictly Prohibited, Strict Prohibition, Ban
notes: "Something with strict prohibition is strictly forbidden / strictly prohibited." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 従業員同士の私語は厳禁です。
example_sentences.english: Private conversations with coworkers are strictly prohibited.

english: To Be Happy, To Be In High Spirits, To Feel Happy
notes: "浮く is ""to float."" This more describes the feeling you get when floating, which is to be happy or to be in high spirits. You know this because you really care (かれる) about how you feel, and to feel happy is great!" "The reading comes from 浮く, so if you know that you' are going to be happy."

example_sentences.japanese: たくさんの人がオリンピックに浮かれすぎている。
example_sentences.english: Many people get too carried away by the olympics.

notes: "If you secret something, you are trying to keep secret something. That, or you're trying to conceal it." "The reading is the same as the one you learned with the kanji, strangely enough. Nothing to conceal about this reading, you gots it."

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は内に秘めるタイプなので、心配しています。
example_sentences.english: I’m worried about him because he tends to hide his feelings.

notes: "If you go to wound something, you are going to damage it. Ouch!" "When you damage something, though, how does it feel? Does it hurt, like 痛い? Wait, what's the reading of this? It's いためる, just like 痛い's reading. That should be easy to remember, unless I accidentally damage your brain with these mnemonics or something."

example_sentences.japanese: 染毛剤は髪の毛を傷める。
example_sentences.english: Hair dye damages your hair.

english: To Feel Hot, To Flush, To Burn
notes: "If fire illuminates your face, you're going to feel hot. Sometimes you start to flush when you're embarrassed and it just feels like there is fire making your face light up." "The readings for this word are both kun'yomi readings. You haven't learned this reading for 火 yet, but it's easier to remember this with a mnemonic for the whole thing:When are you going to feel hot? When is your face going to flush? When I ask you to go to a hotel (ほてる) with me!"

example_sentences.japanese: 高熱で体が火照っています。
example_sentences.english: My body feels hot from this high fever.

notes:
"Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means go beyond so the verb vocab version is also to go beyond." "The reading can come from 越える. So if you know that you know this too!"

"Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means ultra or super so the verb version is what happens when do something ultra or super much. You start to exceed the amount you were meant to do it. If you ultra drive a car, you exceed the speed limit. If you ultra study, you exceed your brain capacity. Get it?" "Who likes to exceed everything? Your 子 (こ)! Or you, when you were a 子. No bedtimes, parents, or other limitations could stop you! You were able to go over them all!"

example_sentences.japanese: どうすればNBA選手のように身長が6.5フィートを越すのでしょうか。今、6フィートなのですが、6.5を越したいのです。
example_sentences.english: How can I be taller than 6.5 feet like NBA players? I’m 6 feet now and I want to surpass that.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はあまり自分の気持ちを言葉で表さない人なので、度を超す程私に執着していることを隠していました。
example_sentences.english: He’s not really the kind of person who talks about their own feelings, so he hid that he was excessively obsessed with me.

notes: "It's now again? Well, if it's already now, then it's now. It's also too late to do what you want to do... if it was the past, then maybe it would have been okay." "The reading is the vocab words 今 and 更に's 更 put together."

example_sentences.japanese: 今更ですが、マイ箸を持ち歩き始めました。
example_sentences.english: It may be a little late, but I started carrying around my own pair of chopsticks.

notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means translate so the verb version would be to translate." "The reading for the kanji part is surprisingly the やく you learned with it, even you wouldn't expect that. I suppose that's the kind of thing you have to look forward to if you were to go into translating."

example_sentences.japanese: この単語を訳すのは難しい。
example_sentences.english: This word is difficult to translate.

notes: "I gather things and use them. The things I've gathered, are the things I use." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: よくあるように、その会社は女性は顔で採用するそうですよ。
example_sentences.english: As is often the case, they say that company only employs attractive women.

notes: "When people gather and decide things, they decide together, usually by voting." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: じゃあ、多数決で採決しよう。夕食にてっちり（ふぐ鍋）が食べたい人は？
example_sentences.english: OK, let’s take a vote. Who wants Fugu-nabe for dinner?

notes: "What you want and request are your wants and desires. You want these things so you request for them. I wants them!" "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. よく goes to よっ, so be careful not to want the wrong reading."

example_sentences.japanese: 私の妻は、頻繁に欲求不満になります。
example_sentences.english: My wife is constantly sexually frustrated.

notes: "A loyalty announcement is the kind of announcement you give to someone who you're loyal to. To this type of person, your announcement would come in the form of advice or maybe admonishment, if you're upset with what they've done." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の忠告を侮るでないぞ、さもなくば命を落としかねんぞ。
example_sentences.english: Don’t make light of his advice, if not you might lose your life.

notes: "The most important part of your military attire are your arms (not the ones attached to your body, your guns and stuff). Arms are what make you a real military person." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: どうやら、武装勢力に襲われたようだ。
example_sentences.english: It seems that they were attacked by armed insurgents.

notes: "Take your body and manipulate it around for exercise. This is Calisthenics or gymnastics." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: この体操は見た目よりもずっときついんですよ。
example_sentences.english: This exercise is actually a lot harder than it looks.

notes: "No! I will not determine that. I refuse. I am in denial." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: その女優はダイエット中であることを否定した。
example_sentences.english: The actress denied that she was on a diet.

notes: "Change your attire to look like someone else. This is a disguise." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 変装教室にギリギリ間に合いました。
example_sentences.english: I made it to the disguise class at the last minute.

notes: "Go ahead and extend it and stretch it. That's how we'll do this enlargement." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. Of course, just to be dirty, the people who made up this word decided to use a kanji that read as かく. Dirty old monks that could see the future and speak English, ugh."

example_sentences.japanese: どうやってそんなにピアスの穴を拡張したの？
example_sentences.english: How did you expand your ear piercing hole that much?

notes: "This attire is put inside this equipment, where it's changed into something else. This attire device is strange and interesting. Imagine something that it does to your attire." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は電気制御装置の使い方を学びました。
example_sentences.english: I learned how to use an electrical control unit today.

notes: "真似 is ""impersonation."" Actually, this word is too. It's also impersonation." "The reading is 物 plus 真似 put together."

example_sentences.japanese: 「いつも何してるの？」「毎日一日中物真似の練習をしてるよ。」
example_sentences.english: """What do you do every day?"" ""I practice impersonations all day, every day."""

english: Opening And Closing, Opening And Shutting
notes: "Opened and closed things are opening and closing." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 開閉時刻の変更は、小さな混乱と誤解を招いた。
example_sentences.english: Changing the opening and closing times caused a little bit of confusion and misunderstanding.

notes: "When you enter your supply into the machine, that is your payment for the day. Every day you have to enter your supply, otherwise they crack down on you." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 授業料の納入期限はどこに書いてありますか。
example_sentences.english: Where is the due date for the tuition payment written?

example_sentences.japanese: 急に大きいお金を準備できなかったから、分割納入制度を利用しました。
example_sentences.english: Because I couldn't prepare a big chunk of money immediately, I used the installment payment system.

example_sentences.japanese: 五日以内にその製品を納入して頂きたいのですが、可能でしょうか。
example_sentences.english: I want you to deliver the product within five days, is that possible?

notes: "You proclaim things by saying them. This is a proclamation or declaration." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼のお気に入りのアイドルが、年末に引退するって宣言したから、彼も他のファンもショックを受けちゃってるのよ。
example_sentences.english: His favorite idol shocked him and other fans by announcing that she will retire at the end of this year.

notes: "All the things the leader proclaims is transmitted to the people. It's all propaganda, which is why you transmit it." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: Tofuguの広告宣伝費はいくらぐらいですか。
example_sentences.english: How much money does Tofugu spend on advertising?

notes: """No"" is the decision I've made. Sorry, but this is rejection." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 今朝新聞で上院は議案を否決したって読んだよ。
example_sentences.english: I read that the senate rejected the bill in the newspaper this morning.

notes:
"Rent it and I will lend it to you. This thing that is being lent and rented? It's a rental." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You just have to remember that 貸 is read as たい for this one. What is your rental? It is a tie (たい) fighter. Sweet."

"Sink and stagnate. Imagine something is doing just that. It is in the state of stagnation and inactivity." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 友人が賃貸のアパートを探してるんですが、どこかいい物件を知りませんかね。
example_sentences.english: My friend is looking for an apartment to rent, don’t you know any good places?

example_sentences.japanese: 景気の沈滞により、たくさんの労働者が首を切られました。
example_sentences.english: A lot of laborers were laid off due to business stagnation.

notes: "You are revered and you have my respect. This is respect." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の事、知れば知る程尊敬するのよね。
example_sentences.english: The more I know him, the more I respect him.

notes: "To become ripe(n) is to ripen and mature." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 成熟した女性の脳と成熟した男性の脳の相違点について、論文を書いています。
example_sentences.english: I’m writing a paper about the differences between the mature female brain and the mature male brain.

notes: "I don't know why a mud pole is a robber, but for some reason it is. Just imagine a robber covering himself in mud and standing behind a pole to hide, then jump out, then rob you of everything you've got." "The reading is 泥 plus the reading for 棒 put together."

example_sentences.japanese: 泥棒になるためのトレーニングは、ブートキャンプ並にハードです。
example_sentences.english: The training to become a burglar is as hard as boot camp.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. You learned this reading with the kanji, so you should be able to read it already!

example_sentences.japanese: サイラスというあの男は、実はロボットだという噂がある。
example_sentences.english: There are rumors that the man named Cyrus is actually a robot.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたって本当、噂をするのが好きね。
example_sentences.english: You really like to gossip, don't you?

example_sentences.japanese: ネットで噂の「加賀屋」っていう居酒屋に行かない？
example_sentences.english: "Do you wanna go to the izakaya ""Kagaya"" that everyone's talking about online?"

notes: "When you obtain supply, you have to put it all together somewhere. You have to put it in storage." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の部屋にはあまり収納スペースがないので、ちょっとした工夫が必要です。
example_sentences.english: There isn’t much space to store things in my room, so it requires a little ingenuity.

notes: "A closed shop is when a store's status is store closed or closed store." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 「営業時間は何時から何時までですか？」「午前10時開店で、午後8時閉店となります。」
example_sentences.english: """What are your business hours?"" ""We are open from 10 a.m. to 8 p.m."""

notes:
"If something is steaming, it makes the room all humid, making this word to be humid (because you're not doing the humiding)." "What is making things to be humid? That would be that cow. Every time he says, ""Moo"" (む) he spurts out a ton of steam making the room all humid."

"Remember how 群れ is a flock? This is the verb version, and means to flock or to crowd together with a bunch of other people." "The reading is the same as 群れ, so if you know that you can flock together the two memories in your brain."

example_sentences.japanese: この靴、可愛いんだけど、足が蒸れて臭うんだよね。
example_sentences.english: These shoes look cute, but they make my feet sweaty and stinky.

example_sentences.japanese: どうして日本では、不良少年少女は、コンビニの前で群れる傾向があるんでしょうか。
example_sentences.english: I wonder why delinquent kids tend to hang out in front of the convenience stores in Japan.

notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means dangle so the verb vocab version is to dangle or to dangle something. You're doing the dangling." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: What are you trying to dangle? You're dangling a taco (た) in front of a hungry person. He just wants the taco, and you keep dangling it like that."

example_sentences.japanese: あの娘が涎を垂らしながら一服しているブルドッグの絵を描いたんだけど、それがすっごく可愛くってさ。
example_sentences.english: She drew a picture of a bulldog drooling while napping and it was really cute.

english: To Heap Up, To Serve Food
notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means heaps, so the verb vocab version is to heap up. It can also mean to serve food, as in you're heaping on food onto someone's plate." "Please keep heaping up the food. I want more (もる), more, more."

example_sentences.japanese: 日本人の中には、不幸や悪霊を追い払うために玄関先に塩を盛る人がいます。
example_sentences.english: Some Japanese people heap up salt on their doorsteps to drive away misfortune and evil spirits.

notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means manipulate, so the verb vocab version is to manipulate." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: A guy using eye arts (あやつ) isn't a great guy, it's the type of guy who might try to manipulate you via hypnosis of the eyes."

example_sentences.japanese: クマが裏でみんなを操っている黒幕だっていう噂があるんだ。
example_sentences.english: There is a rumor that Kuma manipulates everyone behind the scenes.

notes: "The things an author makes is writing and other bits of authorship." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は少なくとも五十は著作があります。
example_sentences.english: She has no less than 50 books published.

notes: "Extend the lens nice and big to zoom in on the subject, please." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 写真を拡大した時に、彼氏の鼻毛が出てることを発見しちゃったんだよね。どん引きだったわ。
example_sentences.english: I enlarged the photo and found out my boyfriend’s nose hairs were sticking out. I was turned off.

notes: "I recognize your consent. It is approval of what I'm doing." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 委員会から承認を得られる自信はあまりありません。
example_sentences.english: I don’t have enough confidence to get approval from the committee.

notes: "It is a delight that you come so I welcome you. This delight welcome is a welcome." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: カウンターの上に「チップ大歓迎」と書かれた箱がありましたよ。
example_sentences.english: "I saw a box on the counter that had ""tips welcome"" written on it."

notes: "Take your finger and brandish it to command the troops. " The readings are the on'yomi readings, so if you know those you may take command of this vocab word.

example_sentences.japanese: アメリカ軍を指揮している司令官に一度会ってみたいな。
example_sentences.english: I’d like to meet the commanding officer of the American army.

notes: "The things you pass through on your way to work are the things you see and run into during your commute." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 通勤は時間を浪費するので、私は職場の近くに住む方がいいですね。
example_sentences.english: Commuting can eat up a lot of time, so I prefer to live near my office.

notes: "You consent and know everything that's going on. You consent and know about all this." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: わしの娘がお前と結婚することは承知できん。
example_sentences.english: I can’t consent to your marrying my daughter.

notes: "When something rots and eats away at something, that is corrosion. Not a good thing." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: ステンレスは腐食作用への耐久性があるんじゃなかったっけ？
example_sentences.english: Stainless steel is supposed to withstand the corrosion, isn’t it?

notes: "Your loss comes from damage done to you. This is damage." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: トラックの衝突で積荷がダメージを受けたが、小さな損害で済んだ。
example_sentences.english: The truck crash damaged the cargo, but it was only minor damage.

notes: "The rot failure is when something rots and fails itself away. It disappears. It is decomposition or decay." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 多くの人々が腐敗した政治組織にうんざりしています。
example_sentences.english: Many people are tired of the corrupt political ring.

notes: "I will determine what you are inferring via an estimate." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: そのサバンの男は群衆の規模を534人と推定したのだが、実際の数とピッタリ当っていた。
example_sentences.english: The guy, who is a savant, estimated the scope of the crowd to have 534 people and he was exactly right.

notes: "You say a reason for your actions, but really it's just an excuse." "The reading is 言う and 訳 combined."

example_sentences.japanese: 分かってもらえることを願って、言い訳を書いたEメールを送りました。
example_sentences.english: I sent her an explanation email and I hope she can understand.

notes: "Normal work is work you do all day long, 8-hours a day, 5 days a week. That is full time employment or full time." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 子どもがもうちょっと大きくなるまでは、常勤でのお仕事はちょっと無理かな。
example_sentences.english: I won’t be able to work full-time for now until my child gets a little older.

notes: "Descend off the (train) car. You are getting off a train, or a bus, or anything else with wheels." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 「あのジェットコースター、どうだった？」「すっごく良かったから、降車した瞬間にゲロっちゃったよ。」
example_sentences.english: """What did you think of that roller coaster?"" ""It was so intense that I threw up right after getting off."""

notes: "A big loss is a heavy loss." "The reading is the おお reading of 大 coupled with the on'yomi reading for 損. Just keep in mind that the そん changes to ぞん and you'll be good here."

example_sentences.japanese: 大儲けするつもりでパチンコに行ったが、結局大損してしまった。
example_sentences.english: I went to a pachinko parlor in the hopes of making a lot of money, but I ended up with a heavy loss instead.

notes: "A mistake in what you calculate is a miscalculation." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は英語がペラペラだと思ったが、とんだ誤算だった。
example_sentences.english: I was wrong in thinking that she would speak decent English.

notes: "A mistake in what you solve... wow, sorry, I thought I was supposed to solve this, not that. What a terrible misunderstanding." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 君は誤解しているよ。あれは俺の姉貴だよ。
example_sentences.english: You’ve got the wrong idea. She’s my older sister.

notes: "A mistake in use is a misuse." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 薬の誤用は命に関わることがあります。
example_sentences.english: Misuse of medicine can be fatal.

notes: "It releases and shoots out of the bomb. It's not fire. It's radiation, and it sticks around a long time once it has been released." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 放射冷却のせいで今朝起きた時はものすごい冷え込みだったよ。
example_sentences.english: It was very cold when I got up this morning because of radiational cooling.

notes: "To infer reason is to have reasoning." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 日付の書き方から、その脅迫状はアメリカ人によって書かれたものだと推理しました。
example_sentences.english: I inferred that the intimidating letter was written by an American due to the way the date was written.

notes: "To infer and recommend something is to give a recommendation. What do you recommend?" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたを、優秀な屁こき野郎として、屁こき大会に推薦しておきましたよ。
example_sentences.english: I recommended you as a good farter for the fart competition.

notes: "Shrink what you have into something small. It was big, now it's small. This is a reduction." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: うちの会社、他社との競争に勝つために、利鞘を縮小することを検討しているんだ。
example_sentences.english: Our company is thinking of reducing our profit margin to be competitive with another company.

notes: "You shoot yourself at a mirror, and it is the anti-you. It is your reflection." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 雪野原は、巨大な鏡のように、冬の太陽の光をキラキラと反射します。
example_sentences.english: The field of snow brightly reflects the winter sunlight like a giant mirror.

notes: "As for myself? I recommend this product. It is a self recommendation. You make it of yourself!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 今回のモデルへの応募について、自薦・他薦は問いません。
example_sentences.english: We accept both self recommendations and direct applications for this modeling position.

notes: "When you shoot something into someone that you actually have to pour (aka a liquid), you're shooting them up with a needle, giving them a shot / injection." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 腰が痛かったんですが、お医者さんが痛み止めの注射を打ってくれました。
example_sentences.english: My lower back was sore so the doctor gave me shot of painkillers.

notes: "I am going to descend my participation in this conflict. I am going to descend all my weapons to the ground. I am going to surrender." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はまだ降参していません。
example_sentences.english: I haven’t given up yet.

english: To Apply, To Submit An Application
notes: "I would like to say humbly in this crowded place that I am going to apply. If there are a lot of other people applying, you feel humbled, so you say humbly you want to apply." "The readings come from 申す and 込む, stuck together... humbly."

example_sentences.japanese: 私は麻疹に免疫がないので、病院に麻疹の予防接種を受けるための申込をしました。
example_sentences.english: I’m not immune to the measles, so I submitted an application for the measles vaccine at the hospital.

english: To Fill Out, To Write In
notes: "You write something on this paper but it is crowded. Why is it crowded? Because there are little boxes for you to write things in. You are filling out a form, which makes this verb to fill out or to write in." "The reading comes from 書く and 込む combined into one."

example_sentences.japanese: 急いで申込書に書き込んだ方がいいよ。あと十分で事務所は閉まっちゃうんだから。
example_sentences.english: You better hurry up and fill out an application. The office will close in ten minutes.

english: To Get Thin, To Lose Weight
notes: "This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means thin so the verb version is to get thin." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You haven't learned this reading yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you:If you want to get thin, just join the Yankees (や). They run their players around those four bases so much they all get thin quicker than you can throw a ball."

example_sentences.japanese: 「痩せたい」と、言い始めてから二年が経ちます。
example_sentences.english: "It's been a couple years since I started saying, ""I want to lose weight."""

example_sentences.japanese: 私の村にいる野良犬のほとんどは痩せていますよ。
example_sentences.english: Most stray dogs in my village are skinny.

example_sentences.japanese: 会話が途切れて気まずくなった時は、とりあえず「最近、痩せた？」と言うことにしている。
example_sentences.english: "When it gets silent and awkward during conversations, I make it a rule to just say, ""Have you lost weight lately?"""

notes: "To do loss to something means you are doing something to make something have loss. This is to harm or to injure." "In order to harm your opponent, you go way overboard. You soak (そこ) them in acid. Soaked head to toe. Too far man, too far."

example_sentences.japanese: 働きすぎてあんたが健康を損なうんじゃないかって、心配してるのよ。
example_sentences.english: I’m worried that you may ruin your health by working too hard.

english: To Hear, To Understand, To Listen To, To Be Informed, To Consent
notes: "This is a weird word. It's like confirming you heard and understand something, but doesn't mean you agree. So, ""to consent"" isn't 100% accurate. So, it's kind of like saying ""to hear or ""to be informed." "You received (受けた) some information. Now, you are going to take that information that you received and then revolve it (回る) around in your head to think about it. Hmmm... hmm... Ok, I like what I'm hearing. I am going to consent what it is you said. I am going to be informed now that I received the information and have revolved it around my brain a bit. Thank you."

example_sentences.japanese: ご伝言を承りましょうか。
example_sentences.english: Would you like to leave a message?

english: To Make Dirty, To Make Something Dirty
notes: "汚れる is ""to get dirty."" This is when you make something dirty, aka ""to make dirty."" You know that this is the version where you make things dirty yourself because when you make someone dirty with all that poop you're flinging, they sue (す) you immediately. This happens a lot." "The reading comes from 汚れる, so if you know that you can read this."

example_sentences.japanese: 綺麗な涎かけが無くなっちゃった。うちの赤ちゃんが全部汚しちゃって。
example_sentences.english: We are out of clean bibs. Our baby boy got them all dirty.

notes: "越す is ""to go beyond."" Now you're going beyond your home and pulling everything with you to go to another home. You are trying to move / to move homes." "The readings come from 引く and 越す put together. Careful of that っ."

example_sentences.japanese: 「パパ、フグと私、結婚して日本に引っ越すつもりよ。」「俺の目の黒いうちはそんなことはさせないぞ。」
example_sentences.english: """Dad, Fugu and I are getting married and moving to Japan."" ""Not while I’m alive, you won’t."""

notes: "越す means ""to go beyond."" 追 is follow. If you are following someone, and then you go beyond them, you have overtaken them. That's why this word means to overtake." "The reading comes from 追う and 越す put together into one. You can overtake this word now that you know that."

example_sentences.japanese: 他の自転車走者を追い越す時、いつも挨拶代わりに手を振ります。
example_sentences.english: I always wave my hand to say hi whenever I pass other bikers.

notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means rot so the verb vocab version is to rot." "Remember the word 臭い, which means ""stinky""? When something rots, it becomes stinky, and all くさい."

example_sentences.japanese: 牛乳は腐りやすいんだから冷蔵庫の外に出しっ放しにしないでね。
example_sentences.english: Don’t leave milk out of the fridge because it goes bad easily.

english: To Run Alongside, To Run Parallel To
notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means run alongside so the verb vocab version is to run alongside." "Think about how you're sewing (そう) something, and your thread has to run alongside the edge of the cloth."

example_sentences.japanese: 川の両岸に沿って、ずうっと、美しい桜並木があるんです。
example_sentences.english: There are beautiful cherry blossom trees all along the river banks.

notes: "You know that 詰める is ""to stuff in"" and 込む is ""to be crowded."" So when you stuff something and crowd it up, you are going to stuff or to cram it in." This word uses the readings you learned with the kanji. If you remember your kanji readings, you'll be fine here.

example_sentences.japanese: なんとか洋服を全部スーツケースに詰め込めました。
example_sentences.english: I managed to cram all my clothes into my suitcase.

english: To Worship, To Pray To, To See
notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means worship so the verb vocab version is to worship." "You have to worship the ogre (おが), because if you don't it'll eat your face off."

example_sentences.japanese: 私の家族は、毎朝仏壇の前に集まって仏様に拝みます。
example_sentences.english: My family gathers in front of our family Buddhist altar to pray to Buddha every morning.

notes: "You'd think this one would have a much different meaning, considering it's tear and give birth. This word means bankruptcy, which seems a bit odd, but I guess there's another bankruptcy word with 産 in it too (倒産). That one is fall, and this one is tear.
