They're both pretty bad, and they both refer to bankruptcy." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の祖父は江戸時代の破産した百姓だという噂だ。
example_sentences.english: It’s rumored that his grandfather was a bankrupt farmer of the Edo period.

english: Be Late, Be Tardy, Late, Tardy
notes: "A slow carve is so slow. If you carve something slowly, it will take you a long time. You will be late with a slow carve like that." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 三日連続で遅刻してしまいました。
example_sentences.english: I was late three days in a row.

notes: "You can infer and measure all you want. If you do enough, you'll get some good conjecture and speculation off that inferring and conjecture." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の推測では、彼は宝くじが当たって、バハマに引っ越した。
example_sentences.english: My guess is that he won the lottery and moved to the Bahamas.

notes: "If you're mud drunk, you're so drunk you're rolling around on the ground. You are dead drunk." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 完璧に泥酔していて、方向感覚を失っていました。
example_sentences.english: I was completely drunk and lost my sense of direction.

notes: "I was too slow, so we'll have to prolong the time in which this product will come out. This is a delay :(" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: バスの大幅な遅延により会議に遅れてしまった。
example_sentences.english: The bus was delayed for a long time and I missed the meeting.

notes: "I am too slow so things have really begun to stagnate. What a delay." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: その動画を遅滞なく削除せよ。
example_sentences.english: Delete the video without delay.

notes: "Tear and break everything, taking it all down. Destruction! Demolition!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 兎小屋は火事によって破壊されました。
example_sentences.english: The rabbit hutch was destroyed by the fire.

notes: "You take your salary and buy oil. When you are doing this, you are fueling something." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 給油ポンプが車に届きません。
example_sentences.english: The fuel pump doesn’t reach my car.

notes: "When you enter prison that's imprisonment." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 初めて入獄した時、何故か安心感を得たんですよね。
example_sentences.english: When I was imprisoned for the first time, for some reason I felt secure.

notes: "If you let someone cut off your oil supply, it's probably because of your inattentiveness. You let your guard down." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチには油断をするな。奴は中々手強い男だぞ。
example_sentences.english: Don’t let your guard down around Koichi. He’s a really tough guy.

notes: "I jammed in myself and entered your personal life. Because I care, you know? I don't want you to be addicted to My Little Pony anymore, so this is an intervention." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 警察の介入により、事態は一層複雑化した。
example_sentences.english: Police intervention made the situation more complicated.

notes: "My introduce was jammed in there for you to hear. That is my introduction. Jammin' it in." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 「こんにちは。サーモンいますか？妹なんですけど。」「わぁ、イクラじゃない！！！」「わぁ、紹介してよ！」「こちらが、フグ。（フグを指さしながら）」「初めまして。」「鰐蟹とキンニクマは知ってるわよね！」「やあ、イクラちゃん。久しぶり。」
example_sentences.english: "Salmon-Roe: ""Hi, is Salmon here? I’m her sister."" Salmon: ""Oh my God, Salmon-Roe!"" Fugu: ""Oh, introduce us!"" Salmon: ""This is Fugu."" (Points at him.) Salmon-Roe: ""Nice to meet you!"" Salmon: ""And you know Crabigator and Kinnikuma!"" Crabigator & Kinnikuma: ""Hi."" Salmon-Roe: ""Long time, no see."""

notes: "Undress the prison from yourself, you're getting out of here, pal! Jailbreak!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の母親は彼に脱獄を強要した。
example_sentences.english: His mother forced him to break out of jail.

notes: "Perform your lecture. This is your lecture. This is your address to the people." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: その講師、講演会場にリムジンで登場したんだよ。
example_sentences.english: The lecturer came to the lecture hall in a limo.

notes: "Lecture of righteousness is still a lecture." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 講義の頭に、教授は私達がナイフにニックネームを付けているかどうかを尋ねました。
example_sentences.english: At the beginning of the lecture, our professor asked us if we have nicknames for our knives.

notes: "View and measure what you are watching. This is observation. It is no mere viewing, it is more than that." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 南極観測隊のメンバーになるにはどうすればいいですか。
example_sentences.english: How can I become a member of Antarctic exploration party?

notes: "A beforehand measure is when you make a prediction of something." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 科学者たちは、大地震の予測に失敗した。
example_sentences.english: Scientists failed to predict the massive earthquake.

notes: "If you exit from prison you are getting your release from prison. But, before you move on, let me tell you one thing: Hope is a dangerous thing. Hope can drive a man insane." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: そして、出獄の日が近づくにつれて、憂鬱になって、何故か危機感を感じたんです。
example_sentences.english: Then, as the day that I would be released from prison drew near, I became depressed and for some reason I sensed impending doom.

notes: "You carve then you carve again. So much carving until, wait, wow, it looks like something! All that carving became a sculpture!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彫刻を落として、真っ二つに割ってしまいました。
example_sentences.english: I dropped the sculpture and it broke in half.

english: To Be Drunk, To Be Seasick, To Be Carsick
notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means drunk so the verb vocab version is to be drunk.This drunk feeling also happens to some people in boats and cars. But we call that to be seasick or to be carsick. You aren't actually drunk, but you feel like you are (and you're probably gonna puke, yuck!)." "I'm not drunk, yo (よ). YO. I'm not drunk, yo. YO. Yo, I'm not drunk. Yo."

example_sentences.japanese: みんな船に酔ってしまい、そこら中に吐き散らかしていました。
example_sentences.english: Everybody got seasick and puked all over the ship.

example_sentences.japanese: 酔ってる時に車を運転するのは絶対にダメだよ。
example_sentences.english: Never drive when you are drunk.

notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means stagnate. The verb vocab version is to be overdue. This is probably because something that has stagnated is running late, and therefore causes it to be overdue." "The reading for this one is wildsauce. I'm going to leave this one to your capable hands. Just think of Tod (とど) and some coot (こお) doing something wild even though they're overdue for something else, or something. Anyways, best of luck to you on this one."

example_sentences.japanese: 家主が六ヶ月間家賃が滞っている男の家に出向くと、男は家の中で死んでいた。
example_sentences.english: The landlord visited a guy who was six months behind with his rent and found him dead in the house.

notes: "If 垂らす is ""to dangle something"" then this is to dangle or to drip. You're not doing the dangling, which is rare (れる), because usually it's you who's doing the dangling." "The reading is the same as 垂らす."

example_sentences.japanese: ほら！母乳だと乳が垂れるって言うじゃない？
example_sentences.english: Say! Isn’t it said that breastfeeding causes saggy breasts?

english: To Feign, To Wear, To Pretend
notes: "If you go to attire yourself, you're covering up who you are and trying to be someone else. You are trying to feign. You are trying to wear a lie. You are trying to pretend." "While you go to feign that you're someone or something else, someone calls you out on it: ""you so (よそお) much a liar!"""

example_sentences.japanese: 予想していた昇進が無かったが、彼は平気を装って昇進した社員たちにおめでとうと言った。
example_sentences.english: Although he didn’t get the promotion he had been expecting, he put on a good face and congratulated the people who did.

english: To Rehash, To Bring Up Again, To Drag Up, To Reheat
notes: "You steam something to return it to its previously warm state. This is when you go to reheat something. But we usually use it to talk about bringing something up again and again in conversations or arguments. That's why it means to rehash or to bring up again. You're bringing up memories from the past and steaming them up again." "The reading comes from 蒸れる and 返す. Combine this knowledge to reheat your memories."

example_sentences.japanese: またかよ。女はすぐ昔の話を蒸し返すよな。やってられないわ。
example_sentences.english: There you go again. Girls always bring up old issues. I don’t want to deal with that.

notes: "It is obsolete so we must stop it. No more of it anymore. This is abolition." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 死刑制度廃止には、賛成ですか、反対ですか。
example_sentences.english: Do you agree or disagree with the abolition of the death penalty?

notes: "I will accept and I have agreement in the matter. I have come to acceptance." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチはアメリカ合衆国の大統領になることを渋々受諾した。
example_sentences.english: Koichi reluctantly agreed to become the president of the United States.

notes: "We are of the same alliance. We are in an alliance." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: ああ、そういうことか。Tofuguは一番のライバル会社と同盟を組んだんだよ。
example_sentences.english: Oh, now I see what happened. Tofugu formed an alliance with its closest competitor.

notes: "I would like to offer my blood to someone else in the form of a blood donation." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 車が移動献血車に衝突するのを見ました。
example_sentences.english: I saw a car bump into the mobile blood bank van.

notes: "You have my consent and agreement. This is my consent and agreement." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 父は、私達の結婚を二つ返事で承諾した。
example_sentences.english: My father agreed to our marriage without hesitation.

notes: "I will permit this, and you have my agreement. Both of these things combine to be my consent." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: もし娘さんとの結婚を許可してくださるのなら、あなたに我が社の登録商標の使用を許諾します。
example_sentences.english: If you allow me to marry your daughter, I’ll give you my consent to use our company’s trademark.

notes:
"If you change something then exchange it, you are making a conversion or a change." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

"If we return and send back things, we will have done a return or restoration." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 太陽エネルギーを電気に変換する技術を開発した人に会ってみたいです。
example_sentences.english: I'd love to meet the person who developed the technology to convert solar energy into electricity.

example_sentences.japanese: 海外でもパソコンを使えるように変換プラグを買ってきました。
example_sentences.english: I bought a conversion plug so that I can use my computer overseas.

example_sentences.japanese: 平仮名がうまく漢字に変換できない時は、大体タイプミスが原因です。
example_sentences.english: If you can't convert your hiragana to kanji properly, it's probably because there's a typo.

example_sentences.japanese: 優勝旗が毎年返還されなくちゃいけないなんて、知らなかったよ。
example_sentences.english: I didn’t know that the championship flag had to be returned every year.

notes: "You dance, you step, you dance, you step. Good job! Now you're doing dancing." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 半年ぶりの舞踏会でした。
example_sentences.english: It was the first dance in six months.

notes: "I am reliant on you, I suppose. It is merely dependence." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 自分が携帯依存症だってことは認めます。
example_sentences.english: I admit that I’ve become dependent on my cell phone.

notes: "When something reaches normal, it has finished diffusion. Normal things aren't all bunched up and concentrated. Normal things are spread out nice and evenly, via diffusion." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: Tofugu思想を普及するための歌を作曲しました。
example_sentences.english: I made a song to spread Tofugu-ism.

notes: "I'd like to offer money, no strings attached. It's free. It's a donation." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 政治献金としていくらかお金を包んだ。
example_sentences.english: I wrapped some money up as a political donation and gave it to them.

notes: "You are obsolete so it's time for extinction. Now you're all wiped out, and this is extinction." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 核廃絶運動家たちは、核兵器を廃絶することは実現可能だと信じている。
example_sentences.english: The anti-nuclear movement believes that the abolition of nuclear weapons is feasible.

notes: "What I leave behind and transmit to you is your heredity. You have my genes, even after I'm gone." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. Since you didn't learn the on'yomi for 伝 before, here's a mnemonic to help you out. You keep records of your heredity in the den (でん). That's the best place for them. In the den."

example_sentences.japanese: 日本では、遺伝子組み換え食品にはパッケージへの表示が義務づけられています。
example_sentences.english: In Japan you are obligated to display whether foods are genetically modified on the package.

notes: "The thing we leave behind at a fault is a loss." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: この空港に遺失物取扱所があるかどうかをご存知ですか。
example_sentences.english: Do you know if there is a lost and found office in this airport?

notes: "Maintain what we have and put it on hold. We need to keep it up to date and fixed, so we need maintenance." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 車は維持費が高いし、今はまだそんな余裕はないな。
example_sentences.english: The cost of car maintenance is really high and I can’t afford that yet.

notes: "Cure and heal me. That is medical therapy." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 虫歯の治療をするために、五年ぶりに歯医者に行きました。
example_sentences.english: I went to a dentist to treat my cavities for the first time in 5 years.

english: Passing An Exam, Make The Grade, Passing The Exam
notes: "I reached the ordinal prefix number that represents a passing score on my test. This means I was able to make the grade and have a status of passing an exam!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: ねぇ、及第点って何点だったか覚えてる？
example_sentences.english: Hey, do you remember what score you need to get a passing grade?

notes: "An alliance promise is one that's made with a pledge or pact. Imagine making an alliance with someone, pledging your support." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグと盟約を結びたいんです。
example_sentences.english: We want to form a pact with Tofugu.

notes: "Take your finger and pluck out the one thing out of all the things that needs pointing out or identification. Yep, that's the one. Pluck that one." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ちょっと間違いを指摘させてもらってもいいですか。
example_sentences.english: Do you mind if I point out your mistakes?

notes: "If 薦める is ""to recommend,"" then the noun version would be a recommendation or some advice. This generally refers to a recommendation of a person or thing, not an action." "The reading comes from 薦める. Might I make the recommendation to learn that word first?"

example_sentences.japanese: そのスリッパは私のお薦めです。
example_sentences.english: Those slippers are my recommendation.

notes: "I believe I can trust you. That's why I put so much reliance and trust on you to do well." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は信頼できるような気がするし、早合点はしたくないね。
example_sentences.english: I don’t wanna jump to conclusions because he seems to be pretty trustworthy.

notes: "I am reliant on you and I trust you. Therefore, I have a request for you that I'd like to entrust with you." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 依頼は断られちゃうかもしれないけど、聞くだけ聞いてみたら。
example_sentences.english: Your request may be turned down, but it never hurts to ask.

notes: "Restore to the former self. This is restoration." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトがTofuguのシステム復旧のために今一生懸命頑張っています。
example_sentences.english: Viet is working his hardest to restore the Tofugu system right now.

english: Still, As Yet, As It Was
notes: "If you have a dependent nature, then even if you go off on your own, you're still going to ask for help. Dependent people still need help because that's just how they are." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 依然父の消息は不明です。
example_sentences.english: I still have no news about my father.

notes: "I will inherit at your consent. It's not just given straight to me at birth, though it kind of is. I get succession, but only if people say it's okay." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 王位継承者の暗殺を企てている者がいるとの噂があります。
example_sentences.english: There is a rumor that someone is plotting the assassination of the successor to the throne.

notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means obsolete and this word means to become obsolete." "Everything has to become obsolete. Even the biggest most fiery things, like a star, for example, will go obsolete at some point."

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトはカップケーキブームは既に廃れていると主張した。
example_sentences.english: Viet insists that the cupcake boom has already died out.

notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means dance and the verb vocab version means to dance, as well as to flutter." "Who is the greatest dancer of them all? China's previous ruler, Mao (まう)."

example_sentences.japanese: 彼氏の部屋、埃がすっごい舞ってて最悪だったんだけど、綺麗な花びらが舞っているんだって思い込むように頑張ってみたさ。ま、無理だったけど。
example_sentences.english: In my boyfriend’s room a bunch of dust was fluttering about and it was disgusting, so I tried to imagine that they were beautiful petals fluttering about instead. It didn’t work.

notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means inherit and the verb vocab version is to inherit." "You not only inherit one fortune, but two! You're lucky both sides of your family ""accidentally"" died at the same time. TWO (つ) fortunes! TWO! HAHAHAHA. Also, you can think of it like the つ of 次, because you are the ""next"" successor when you inherit something."

example_sentences.japanese: 日本では、通常は長男が一家の跡を継ぎます。
example_sentences.english: The oldest son usually becomes the head of a family in Japan.

english: To Spit Out, To Disgorge, To Spew Out
notes: "If 吐く is to throw up, and if 出す is to remove or hand over, then if you throw up and hand that throw up over to someone via your throwing up, you are going to spit out at them, or to spew out, or something gross along those lines. Then again, this word can be used to be like ""spit the info out already!"" too, so it's not all spitting for reals." "The reading comes from 吐く and 出す."

example_sentences.japanese: 男は舐めていた飴を吐き出しました。
example_sentences.english: The man spit out the candy he’d been sucking.

notes: "Trade is easy if you like trade and commerce." "The 貿 reading is okay, but the 易 reading is different from what you're used to. Just think about how a lot of the trade that comes in will come into the train station (駅). So if you want good trade, you'll want to be at the えき."

example_sentences.japanese: 貿易事務の仕事を探しています。
example_sentences.english: I’m looking for a job as the clerk of a trading company.

notes:
"Something that will exchange energy is something that pulls in air, takes out the bad stuff, and then outputs good air, exchanging it for the bad. That is ventilation." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

"If you scream wake up! at someone you can bet they're going to awaken. Screaming anything at a sleeping person would probably rouse them. They'll probably be mad at you though." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: ちょっと窓を開けて部屋の換気をしない？
example_sentences.english: Why don’t we open the window and air out the room?

example_sentences.japanese: 大学の入学式で、学生たちに飲酒やカルト宗教についての注意喚起が行われました。
example_sentences.english: At the university entrance ceremony the students were alerted to the dangers of alcohol and cults.

notes: "I respond to your recruitment with this application to try and join your group." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 応募用紙は裁判所でもらえますよ。
example_sentences.english: You can get the application form at the courthouse.

english: Attachment To, Tenacity, Obsessed With, Attachment
notes: "You tenaciously wear something. You have some kind of attachment to it. Some kind of tenacity that makes you obsessed with it." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. Unfortunately, you didn't learn the on'yomi reading for 着, which is ちゃく. Think about how you have a big attachment to chalk (ちゃく). Hold the chalk, love the chalk. You are obsessed with chalk."

example_sentences.japanese: 異常なほどお金に執着する男の小説を書いてみたいんだよね。
example_sentences.english: I’d like to write a novel about a guy who has an abnormal obsession with money.

notes: "A war struggle is the part in war where you have to struggle at each other. This is a battle." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 実際のところ、忍者は直接戦闘することをできるだけ避けた。
example_sentences.english: Actually, ninjas try to avoid combat as much as possible.

notes: "An explode attack is when someone attacks with exploding things, like bombs. This is a bombing." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: そのチョコレート工場は、爆撃を受けて粉々になりました。
example_sentences.english: The chocolate factory crumbled to pieces from the bombing.

notes: "When something begins to crumble and break, it will certainly collapse at some point. It just can't hold up under the pressure." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 今朝の俺のクソが大き過ぎて、トイレの床が崩壊したんだ。
example_sentences.english: My poop was so big this morning that the bathroom floor collapsed.

notes: "I pledge and promise to do that thing... so much so, I'm willing to sign a contract about it." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: あの事件が先方に契約を解除させたんだよ。
example_sentences.english: That incident led them to cancel the contract.

notes: "A fire burial is when you burn the body. You call this cremation." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 火葬のシステムは自動的に停止する訳ではありません。係の人が小窓から骨の様子を見ながら、終わったと思う時に止めるのです。
example_sentences.english: The cremation system doesn’t shut down automatically. The person in charge checks how the bones are doing from a small window once in a while and stops it when they think it’s done.

notes: "Whittle down and exclude this item from the list. Time to remove it. It's deletion." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: インターネット上からあんたの写真を全部削除するのは、時間はかかるだろうけど、俺の手に掛かれば不可能じゃないね。
example_sentences.english: It’s gonna take some time to delete all your pictures off the Internet, but it’s not impossible for me.

notes: "The sect of dispatch helps with all the dispatch and deployment duties." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: その派遣社員は、新しい職場の雰囲気をすぐに掴みました。
example_sentences.english: The temporary dispatch worker quickly got used to the atmosphere of her new office.

notes: "Explode with laughs, what explosive laughter." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. Since you didn't learn the on'yomi for 笑 with the kanji, here's a mnemonic. Who has come down with explosive laughter? It's the shogun (しょう)! The shogun just can't stop laughing."

example_sentences.japanese: 母さんと父さんを爆笑させるような、何かいいエイプリルフールの案はある？
example_sentences.english: Do you have any good April fool’s ideas to make our parents explode with laughter?

notes: "If you recruit gold you are trying to raise money, aka you are fundraising." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 一万円札を崩してもらうことはできますか？もしそれができるなら、千円札を募金します。
example_sentences.english: Could you break a ten thousand yen bill? If you can I’ll donate a thousand yen to your fundraiser.

notes: "A big resist is something he generally and usually does... at least in most cases. He's usually a big resistor, that one." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 大抵の外国人は納豆が苦手かと思いますが、私もその一人です。
example_sentences.english: I think most foreigners usually don’t like natto and I’m one of them.

notes: "On the second day, you experience your drunkenness a different way... in the form of a hangover." "The reading is 二日 and 酔い put together (the reading for that comes from 酔う)."

example_sentences.japanese: 二日酔いだし、足もつるし今日は最悪だよ。
example_sentences.english: I’m hungover and I also have a cramp in my leg. Today is the worst.

notes:
"To display and indicate something is to put up a notice or bulletin." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

"What indicates that you've been enlightened enough to reach enlightenment? A revelation! That's the only way you can know you've been enlightened enough." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: アヤは、レストランが臨時休業の掲示をしている紙に余白があるのを見つけては、そこに落書きをします。
example_sentences.english: Whenever Aya sees that a restaurant put up a notice about shutting down for a holiday and there is some space left on the paper, she draws doodles there.

example_sentences.japanese: それはまるで神の啓示のようだった。
example_sentences.english: That’s just like divine revelation.

notes: "I want to recruit some people, so let's gather them up and do some recruiting and solicitation to get them." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: Tofuguはまだブロガーを募集中ですよ。
example_sentences.english: Tofugu is still recruiting bloggers.

notes: "Whittle down and decrease something. This is a reduction or cutback, since you're whittling down and decreasing it." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: コストの削減に苦戦しています。
example_sentences.english: I’ll have a hard time reducing the cost.

notes: "My dialect has offended you? I will make reparation by giving you a reimbursement and some compensation. I'm sorry my dialect was so bad you couldn't understand the speech. Here's your money back." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 撮影中に漁師さんの網を誤って破いてしまったため、弁償しなくてはならなかった。
example_sentences.english: I ripped a fisherman’s nets by mistake while taking pictures, so I had to reimburse him.

notes: "We are ready to confront war, if we have to. We are going to start the resistance against your regime, confront you, and even make war." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 学生たちは、権威に対して徹底抗戦を強いられました。
example_sentences.english: The students were forced to resist to the bitter end against authority.

notes: "When you're boat drunk you have sea sickness." "The reading for 船 goes to ふな (probably because you're sick and can't spell). The 酔い comes from 酔う."

example_sentences.japanese: この薬で船酔いを克服しました。
example_sentences.english: I got over my seasickness with this medicine.

notes: "A one's self (自己) introduction (紹介) is a self introduction." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 自己紹介では、いつもすぐ言うことがなくなっちゃうんだよね。
example_sentences.english: Whenever I introduce myself, I quickly run out of things to say.

notes: "If you have to aim with your attack, you're probably shooting or sniping something with a projectile (like a gun, or something)." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 男は政治家を狙撃するために、そのホテルの部屋が見える場所までやってきた。
example_sentences.english: He positioned himself in view of the hotel room to snipe the politician.

notes: "If you self explode, it means you're blowing up yourself, and probably taking others with you. This is a suicide bomb." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 今月末までに、自爆テロを実行しなくてはなりません。
example_sentences.english: I have to commit a suicide bombing by the end of this month.

english: To Appeal For, To Invite, To Raise, To Grow Violent, To Become Stronger
notes: "The kanji is recruit so the verb vocab version would, you'd think, be 'to recruit,' but it's to appeal for or to invite or to raise. So, it's kind of like recruiting, but instead of people, you're recruiting for things and actions.This verb can also be intransitive (oh my!) and mean to grow violent or to become stronger. It's like all of that recruiting is happening inside of you and causing some weird things to happen to you!" "You'd like to appeal for two, no (つの), three things! Three!"

example_sentences.japanese: 妻への不信感は募るばかりです。
example_sentences.english: My distrust for my wife is only growing stronger.

example_sentences.japanese: みんなで募金を募りましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let's all appeal for funding together!

english: To Be Afflicted, To Be Afflicted With Illness, To Be Sick
notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means afflicted and the verb vocab version is to be afflicted." "I was afflicted with an ancient Egyptian disease that turned me into sun god Ra, but now I'm okay. I was a Ra (わずら), but now I'm just me again."

example_sentences.japanese: シェルターには、結核を患うホームレスの人がたくさんいます。
example_sentences.english: In the shelter there are many homeless people sick with tuberculosis.

english: To Be Shy, To Be Bashful
notes: "恥ずかしい is ""embarrassing."" This is the verb version. What happens when someone is embarrassed? They become shy and bashful. That's why this word is to be shy or to be bashful." "The reading comes from 恥ずかしい."

example_sentences.japanese: ストリッパーになると自分で決断したにも関わらず、彼女はまだ人前で裸で踊ることを恥ずかしがっているんだよ。
example_sentences.english: Although she was determined to become a stripper by herself, she’s still shy about dancing naked in public.

notes: "Weird that this kanji means bullet but the verb vocab version means to bounce. Just imagine someone shooting a bullet. What does it do when it hits the right materials? It's going to bounce." "If you're going to bounce something off that wall, it has (はず) to be made of rubber, otherwise it will just go right through. It has to."

example_sentences.japanese: 彼との会話がこんなに弾むなんて、思ってもみなかったわ。
example_sentences.english: I never expected such a lively conversation between the two of us.

notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means burial, so the verb version would be to bury or to inter." "We're going to bury you, so this is your new home (ほうむ) now, friend."

example_sentences.japanese: その事件の真相が闇に葬られるのではないかと心配しています。
example_sentences.english: I’m worried that the truth of the incident might be buried.

english: To Compensate For, To Make Up For
notes: "To make reparation is to compensate for or to make up for. Take responsibility for your actions and make up for everything." "When you go to compensate for what you did, you become too good for your own britches. You are too good now (つぐなう)."

example_sentences.japanese: たとえあなたが死をもって罪を償っても、問題は解決しないでしょう。
example_sentences.english: Even if you atoned for your sins with your own death, it wouldn’t solve the problem.

english: To Do A Favor, To Bless, To Give Out Of Pity, To Donate Out Of Charity
notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means favor and the verb vocab version is to do a favor for." "If you are going to do a favor for anyone, it's going to be for your good buddy meg (めぐ). Imagine a Meg you know (or know of) and imagine yourself doing a favor for her. Meg Ryan is so happy you're in her life."

example_sentences.japanese: 本日のTofuguの収益の全額が、恵まれない子どもたちに寄付されます。
example_sentences.english: All of Tofugu’s proceeds from today will be donated to underprivileged children.

english: To Put Up A Sign, To Put Up
notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means display, so if you're doing the action of displaying something, you're going to put up something, or, sometimes more specifically, to put up a sign." "You have to put up a sign for your newest invention, the car car (かか). It is a car made so that other cars can drive the car. Nobody wants to buy it, which is why you have to put up a sign."

example_sentences.japanese: ジェームズは、鉛筆削りの技術のレベルを上げるという目標を掲げた。
example_sentences.english: James set a new goal: to bring his pencil sharpening to the next level.

english: To Whittle Down, To Shave Off
notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means whittle down and the verb vocab version is to whittle down as well." "To whittle down or not to whittle down. Will have to take it on a case (けず) by case basis."

example_sentences.japanese: 歯を削る音ってのは、私にとっては最も不快な音の一つだね。
example_sentences.english: The sound of shaving down teeth is one of the most unpleasant sounds to me.

notes: "I steal by listening to what people say. I do this by wiretapping their phone and bugging their homes." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 誰かがTofuguのオフィスに盗聴器を仕掛けたのですが、私達は犯人も理由も分かりません。
example_sentences.english: Someone bugged the Tofugu office, but we have no idea who or why.

notes: "If you have a tenacious writing brush, you are doing a lot of writing. Also, if you write for a magazine you probably write a ton too, because they have to come out with new issues every week or month." "The 執 is a little altered, where しつ is shortened to しっ. You've seen this kind of thing before, so just keep this shortening pattern in mind and you'll be a-okay!"

example_sentences.japanese: 最後に短編小説を執筆したのはいつですか？
example_sentences.english: When was the last time you wrote a short story?

notes: "A cool cluster is something that has a cluster of cool-creating coolant. This device is an air conditioning." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 暑すぎだよ〜。ちょっと冷房付けてもらえないかな。
example_sentences.english: It's too hot. Could you turn on the air conditioning please?

notes: "You accept and consign the job. You are going to be entrusted with this property for the winter. Don't go into room 237." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 我が社にとってその受託契約を受注することがどんなに重要か、分かっているよな。
example_sentences.english: Do you know how desperately we need the brokerage contract?

notes: "I dodged being pregnant. Whew. Good thing I was taking my birth control." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 今年の新年の抱負の一つは、ちゃんと避妊をすること、です。
example_sentences.english: One of my New Year’s resolutions is to properly use contraception.

notes: "I'll think and consider this. I'll give it consideration." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You've learned them both already, so you should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の家族ではなく自分の家族のことを考慮してください。
example_sentences.english: Please consider your own family instead of mine.

notes: "If you distribute your considers, you will be giving consideration and care to whatever you're distributing these cares to." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: お母さん、大人って子供への配慮が欠けていると思わない？
example_sentences.english: Mom, don’t you think that adults lack consideration for kids?

notes: "To the committee I would like to consign these things. This is what I consign." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: そいつがさ、男の目隠しまではしたけど、残りの殺人業務は他の暗殺者に委託したって言うんだよ。
example_sentences.english: He says that he did blindfold the guy, but entrusted the rest of the murder to the other assassin.

notes: "Try to suppress and control the enemy. We must control them." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 生理前は、月経前症候群のせいで、感情をうまく抑制することができません。
example_sentences.english: I can’t control my emotions well before my period because of PMS.

notes: "Draw a copy of the world and you are making a depiction of the world." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: アヤは、Tofugu殺人事件を細部に渡って描写した。
example_sentences.english: Aya drew a detailed depiction of the Tofugu murder case.

notes: "This is going to suppress and stop what's coming at you. It's a deterrent." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: どの国が一番素晴らしい犯罪抑止モデルを有していると思われますか。
example_sentences.english: Which country do you think has the best crime prevention model?

notes: "A join kill is when in one play you get two kills (outs) in baseball, making it a double play." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 「ゲッツー」というのは、併殺を意味する和製英語です。
example_sentences.english: """Get two"" is a Japanese word derived from English meaning double play."

notes: "If you draw a drawing or painting, you will end up with a drawing or painting." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: クロード・モネは、点画法という、点描画法とは少し違った技法を得意としていました。
example_sentences.english: Claude Monet was very good at stippling, which is a bit different from pointillism.

notes: "If you escape death you have, well, an escape." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の弟は優し過ぎて犯罪者達の逃亡を助けてしまい、そのせいで逮捕されてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: My little brother is so generous that he aided in the criminals’ escape and was arrested for it.

notes: "A warm cluster is when you get a bunch of warmth together, and then use it to warm your home. This is indoor heating, kind of like the same way how an air conditioner is a ""cool cluster.""" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 何で暖房消したの？パイプが全部凍っちゃったじゃない。
example_sentences.english: Why did you turn off the heat? All the pipes are completely frozen!

notes: "Join and join with each other. This is a merger." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. Just remember that 合 is read as ごう here. Who orchestrated this merger? Good ol' grandpa ごういち."

example_sentences.japanese: アメリカ合衆国は、私が生まれた年にテキサスを併合しました。
example_sentences.english: The United States of America annexed Texas the year I was born.

notes: "Play music that will give me comfort, why then I should go see a musical performance to keep me nice and calm." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 千円くらいの、奏楽用のハンドベルはありますか？
example_sentences.english: Do you have a musical handbell for around 1000 yen?

notes: "If you perform and play music you are doing a musical performance." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: バンドが舞台で演奏をしている最中に、電球が切れてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: The light bulb burned out while the band was performing on stage.

notes: "Something that is contrary... this is the te-form version of contrary, meaning you're starting to say something, making this on the contrary." "The reading is like 変える, which is to change. So, if you change what the other person is saying to another way, then you're saying you're changing things. It has the same reading, so remember it that way."

example_sentences.japanese: 善かれと思ってしたことが、却って仇となって友人のストレスになってしまいました。
example_sentences.english: I just wanted to do the right thing but instead it backfired and I just stressed my friend out.

notes: "I want to suppress and pressure you! Muahaha! This is oppression." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 警察は、その暴動を抑圧するのにしばらく時間がかかりました。
example_sentences.english: It took the police a while to suppress the riot.

notes: "We got life by sending back our runner to home plate. That run allowed us a more life in this game, and maybe we'll win! It was all by reaching home plate." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 行方不明の英語教師は、足が凍傷になっていたものの、無事に生還しました。
example_sentences.english: Although his feet were frostbitten, the missing English teacher safely came back alive.

notes: "It is contrary to what I think is good. It is below my standards. Thus, rejection." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: Tofuguメンバー全員がバンジージャンプに挑戦するというアイディアは、速攻で却下されました。
example_sentences.english: My idea for all of the Tofugu members to bungee jump was quickly rejected.

notes: "A far consider is when you let your considerations go far from you so you don't think about how angry you are about what's going on in front of you. It allows you to have some restraint, since your considerations are far from here. It also allows you to decline things, since you're not considering the other person's feelings." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You've learned them both already, so you should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 質問があればどんなものでも遠慮なくおっしゃって下さいね。
example_sentences.english: Don’t hesitate to ask me any questions.

notes: "Send back to the origin means you are going to return to origins. Make a reduction down to the original." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 我々は円高還元セールを実施します。
example_sentences.english: We are going to have a strong yen reduction sale.

notes: "Take your rope and stretch it out to show where the cutoff is. This is when you rope off something. It shows your territory and turf. Don't cross this rope I've stretched out, it's my domain." "The reading is 縄 and 張る put together into one word."

example_sentences.japanese: 案の定、その場所はヤクザの縄張りだった。
example_sentences.english: Sure enough, the place was Yakuza’s territory.

notes: "If you usually lean yonder, in that direction, that will be your tendency." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本人は外国人と喋る時、英語訛りの日本語を話す傾向があります。
example_sentences.english: Japanese people tend to speak Japanese with an English accent when they talk to foreigners.

notes: "If you consign something to someone, you are going to entrust them with that item. Here you go, I entrust you." "The reading for this one is super weird, but I will entrust you with this knowledge, nonetheless. The reading comes from the on'yomi reading, which is たく, and is the one you learned. It doesn't make any sense, but that's how the ball bounces here."

example_sentences.japanese: 探偵を託して写真を全部渡したのが間違いでした。
example_sentences.english: It was a mistake to entrust all the pictures to that detective.

notes: "If 及ぶ is ""to reach"" then this is something similar. Now you're doing the reaching, and to reach something you have to exert yourself to do it. Also, you have to reach to the goal you're trying to reach." "The reading comes from 及ぶ, so if you know that, you'll reach the ability to know this word's reading as well."

example_sentences.japanese: 放射能汚染は人体にどのような影響を及ぼすと考えられているのでしょうか。
example_sentences.english: What effect do people think radioactive contamination has on the human body?

notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means bribe, but when you pay a bribe, you are going to pay something or to cover something, like a meal, or something like that." "You need to make a payment, make a payment now (まかなう) to cover the cost of this room."

example_sentences.japanese: もし今赤ちゃんができたら、俺の収入だけで家族を賄うのは無理だと思うんだよ。
example_sentences.english: I don’t think my income would be enough to feed my family if we had a baby now.

english: To Step Into, To Rush Into
notes: "To step on (踏む) and then to crowd (込む) something, you're really stepping into something. This is to step into or to rush into something." "The readings come from 踏む and 込む, put together."

example_sentences.japanese: ルームメートが、私のプライバシーに踏み込みすぎだと思うのよね。
example_sentences.english: I think my roommate invades my privacy too much.

notes: "If you believe you can consign your trust to someone, then you can trust them, or you are being entrusting." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はその証券マンを信頼して、投資信託に大金をつぎ込みました。
example_sentences.english: I trusted the investment broker and invested a lot of my money into the mutual fund.

notes:
"A temporary title is what you give something when you don't have a final title for it. it's a working name or a tentative name." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

"You're singing and you're chanting. It's a gay ol' time. You're singing and singing and singing!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: タイトルはまだ単なる仮称です。
example_sentences.english: The title is just a temporary name for now.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたの歌唱力をみんなに見せつけるために、このビデオをFacebookに投稿してもいいですか？
example_sentences.english: Can I post this video on Facebook to show everyone your skills as a singer?

notes: "If you try to consider (遣う) your words (言葉) you are making a choice of words." "The reading is 言葉 and 遣う combined together."

example_sentences.japanese: 誰かの言葉遣いを真似することは、外国語の良い勉強法です。
example_sentences.english: Imitating someone’s speech can be a good way to practice a foreign language.

notes: "A flock that has gathered is a crowd and multitude. Because, well, lots of things gathering." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 小さな男の子がジャスティン・ビーバーの物真似をし出したので、群集は大笑いをしました。
example_sentences.english: The crowd broke out in laughter when the little boy started imitating Justin Bieber.

notes: "A gun kill is a death by shooting." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 犬が飼い主に銃殺されるという悲しい事件がありました。
example_sentences.english: There was a tragic incident where a dog was shot and killed by its owner.

notes: "The employ task is employment." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: かつては多くの会社が終身雇用を保障していましたが、今ではそれが当たり前では無くなっています。
example_sentences.english: Many companies used to guarantee their workers a job for life, but that’s no longer a common thing.

notes: "To excuse and to exclude, that's exemption." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の祖父は心臓病を患っていたため、兵役を免除されました。
example_sentences.english: My grandfather was exempt from military service because he had a heart disease.

notes: "Allocate the truth more and more to make things better. The truth is, we need to allocate even more, until we've reached fullness." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: お客様と末永い関係が築けるよう、充実したアフターサービスをご提供しております。
example_sentences.english: We provide good after-sales service because we want to build long-term relationships with our customers.

notes: "If you hop and leap into the air, you probably are doing a jump and leap into the air." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: この授業は、生徒たちの跳躍力を伸ばすことを目的としています。
example_sentences.english: This lesson is aimed at improving students’ leaping, jumping, and hopping skills.

notes: "To fly and leap is leaping." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は陰謀論が好きなんですが、彼の論理はよく飛躍するんですよね。
example_sentences.english: He likes conspiracies, but there is often a leap in his logic.

notes: "You have an excuse that permits you to do what you want. It is a license and certificate allowing you to do this." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 「あぁ、自分がどれだけドライブが好きか忘れてたわ。免許更新しなくちゃ。」「おい、待てよ！お前の免許失効してるのか？ありえねえ。よし、それまで！今すぐ横につけて！」
example_sentences.english: """Ah. I forgot how much I love driving. I have got to get my license renewed."" ""Wait! Has your driver’s license expired? Omg. That’s it! Pull over right now!"""

notes: "A leaping move isn't just any kind of move, it's a lively motion or sometimes a throb." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: アヤの最新のTofuguキャラのイラストは、とても躍動感に溢れています。
example_sentences.english: Aya’s latest illustration of the Tofugu characters is very vibrant and lively.

notes: "When prosperity wakes up it will push through whatever it's in and create a protuberance or bulge. Just imagine it pushing out of the wall, trying to get out, making a bulge. So prosperous!" "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. Here's a mnemonic for the reading of 起. To get out of this bulge, you use a key (き). The key lets you get out."

example_sentences.japanese: 喉頭隆起は、その近くにある骨の形が仏様に似ていることから、喉仏としても知られています。
example_sentences.english: The adam’s apple is also known as the throat Buddha because the bone shape looks like Buddha.

notes: "Allocate electricity back to the battery with a recharge." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: もしよければ俺の車で携帯の充電ができるよ。
example_sentences.english: You can charge your phone in my car, if you’d like.

notes: "If you take what you recommend and announce it to the world, you are making a recommendation." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 人事部に辞職勧告を受けた後もなお仕事を続けていたら、窓際族に追いやられてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: After I got resignation advice from the personnel department and I still didn’t quit my job, I was transferred to a useless position.

notes: "I refuse. I am saying ""no."" That is my refusal." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は戦場に行く事を拒否したため、臆病者と呼ばれた。
example_sentences.english: He was called coward since he’d refused to go to the battlefield.

notes: "A leap when you advance on your enemy is a rush or dash or even an onslaught." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: Tofuguが今年、大躍進を遂げたのは何故だと思いますか。
example_sentences.english: What do you think made Tofugu take such a big leap forward this year?

notes: "I recommend this to you, so I'd like to invite you to try it. This is a solicitation or invitation." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 大学生活の最初は、部活の勧誘をたくさん受けました。
example_sentences.english: I got a lot of invitations to participate in club activities at the beginning of the university year.

notes: "If you take a supplement and allocate it to something else, you are providing a supplement, because that's what you do with supplements." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 帰る前にプリンタの紙を補充しておいてもらえるかな。
example_sentences.english: Could you refill the printer paper before you leave?

notes: "An excuse from taxes? That's a tax exemption." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 免税店がどこにあるかご存知ですか？
example_sentences.english: Do you know where the duty-free shops are?

english: To Be Discreet, To Be Careful
notes: "If you have humility you will try to be discreet." "Why are you going to be discreet? Because that tutu she (つつし) wears is really embarrassing."

example_sentences.japanese: 電車の乗客は、携帯での会話を慎むべきだ。
example_sentences.english: People on the train should refrain from having cell phone conversations.

notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means employ so the verb vocab version is to employ." "You are going to employ more people to your business so you can make more money and eventually buy a yacht (やと). That's the dream life, it is."

example_sentences.japanese: あなたを雇いたいのは山々ですが、就業許可証が発給されるのを待ってはいられないのです。
example_sentences.english: I’d like to hire you, but we can’t wait for your work permit to be issued.

hiragana: まぬかれる, まぬがれる
notes: "You are going to excuse yourself from the situation, and in order to do that, you have to escape from the person / thing trying to hold you there in order to avoid them." "In order to do that, you jump inside your man(u) car (まぬか) which is a car for a tough man(u) that needs to drive fast, just like you."

example_sentences.japanese: 後部座席に座ってシートベルトを締めていたので、私達は重傷を免れました。
example_sentences.english: We avoided serious injury because we sat in the backseat and wore our seat belts.

notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means refuse and the verb vocab version is to refuse." "What are you refusing? You are refusing a child, because children are all bad. You say ""子 bad, 子 bad"" over and over again."

example_sentences.japanese: 私のかかりつけのお医者さんは、私が大腸癌検査を受けるのを拒みました。
example_sentences.english: My family doctor refused to let me get the colorectal cancer screening done.

english: To Repay, To Refund, To Reimburse
notes: "払い is a ""payment"" and 戻す is ""to return."" If you return a payment, you are going to repay or to refund someone for their payment." "The readings come from 払い and 戻す."

example_sentences.english: On the highway, cars collided one after another.

"It's obsolete so I'm going to abandon it. This is annulment. You are sending something to disposal." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.english: Koichi returned safely and the village was filled with joyful voices.

example_sentences.english: Our yard is overgrown with weeds, so I’m going to mow them this weekend.

notes: "I praise you for what you did, so here's your prize to go along with my praise, a medal!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.english: When she tried to go up on the stage to get her prize, she tripped on the stairs.

example_sentences.english: The weather forecast was wrong and it started to rain while I was on patrol.

example_sentences.english: I’ve decided to go on a pilgrimage to sacred places around the world.

example_sentences.english: To turn on your cell phone you need to press the power button for five seconds.

notes: "Life, when it multiplies (multiply), is doing reproduction." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.
