example_sentences.english: My husband and I planted a maple sugar tree to commemorate our marriage.

notes: "If you undress from clothes you are undressing." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 脱衣する前に、鞄を脇へ置いたのは覚えています。
example_sentences.english: I remember I put my bag to the side before undressing.

notes: "A withdrawal is something you do to remove something from the past. It is a withdrawal or removal of what you did or submitted before." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. Look out for the shortened てつ."

example_sentences.japanese: 瓦礫の撤去に関するニュースをネットで読みました。
example_sentences.english: I read the news about removing rubble on the internet.

notes: "If you do a withdrawal of something it's like you're revolving back to how things originally were. This is a withdrawal or repeal." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. Look out for the shortened てつ."

example_sentences.japanese: ごめん。前言撤回するよ。
example_sentences.english: Sorry, I take back what I said.

notes: "A withdrawal of soldiers is a withdrawal of troops." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. Look out for the shortened てっ spot."

example_sentences.japanese: 私はその撤兵を恥じた事は一度もありません。
example_sentences.english: I never felt ashamed about the withdrawal of the troops.

notes: "A challenge for war? I accept this challenge. A challenge is always worth accepting!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: ありえねえ！お前ってほんと、超天然キャラだよな。なんで蝉の鳴き真似に挑戦なんてしてるんだよ？
example_sentences.english: No way! You really are such an airhead! Why are you trying to mimic a cicada’s shrilling?

notes: "Fasten everything into one. All together in one batch or lump." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. Watch out for the shortened いち."

example_sentences.japanese: 日本では焼き菓子作りとか料理の計量方法が違うんだよね。いっそ世界中の計量方法が一括で同じだったらいいのにね。
example_sentences.english: In Japan they use a different method of measurement for baking sweets and cooking. I think it would be better to have one way of measuring throughout the world.

notes: "If you untie the analysis, you are really just doing analysis to the analysis, if you catch my drift." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は踊りながらそれを解析してみました。
example_sentences.english: I analyzed it while dancing.

notes: "Take things apart into parts. Then, do analysis. This is analysis." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: それは先生の息の質の分析結果です。
example_sentences.english: That’s the result of the teacher’s breath quality analysis.

notes: "I'm going to twist this bullet and turn it around on you. You're the one I'm going to blame, which is why my blame bullet is twisted back at you." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: この金融危機について、誰が糾弾されるべきだと思われますか？
example_sentences.english: Who do you think is to blame for this economic crisis?

notes: "Distract me with a twist in what we're doing. Just imagine you're working on something. Then, you get distracted by a twist in whatever it is that you're working on. This little twist doesn't destroy everything, but it does cause a complication and confusion." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: この問題をこれ以上紛糾させたくないんです。
example_sentences.english: I don’t want to complicate this problem any more.

notes: "Time to overcome the clothes of our enemies. They all wear the same kind of clothes (let's say blue clothes) so we know that if we overcome the blue coated people, we will have won. It will be a conquest!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 徐々にホームシックを克服していってます。
example_sentences.english: I’m slowly getting over my homesickness.

notes: "Let's departure on our digging up of this site. It is more than just digging, we're going somewhere and learning new things with this dig. This is an excavation!" "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. Be careful of the 発 getting shortened."

example_sentences.japanese: ある日、金を求めて穴を掘っていると、大量の古代ギリシャのお宝を発掘しました。そこで、その幸運を分かち合う妻を娶ろうと決意しました。
example_sentences.english: One day, he excavated a large number of old Greek treasures while digging for gold, so he decided to take a wife with whom he could share his fortune.

notes: "A grip with your hand (onto another hand) is a handshake." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. With 手 just think back to other vocab words that use the on'yomi reading."

example_sentences.japanese: CDを買うと、オマケで握手券が二枚ついてきた。
example_sentences.english: I bought a CD that came with two handshake tickets as a bonus. (Handshake tickets are similar to meet and greet tickets.)

notes: "A lodge where you will stay overnight is lodging. It is where you will stay the night." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: まだ今夜の宿泊先を探しているんです。
example_sentences.english: I’m still searching for a lodging place for tonight.

notes: "You are mourning your fault. Because of your fault, you have gotten a loss and forfeit." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 介護施設に、どうやら記憶喪失らしいお婆さんがいるんだけど、その人がすっごく面白いのよ。
example_sentences.english: In the nursing home there is an old woman who seems to have lost her memory, but she is really funny.

notes: "One overnight is a one night's stay." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. Watch out for the shortened 一 and the rendaku in this one."

example_sentences.japanese: ねぇ、そう堅いこと言わないでさ。うちに泊まってけばいいじゃん。たったの一泊だけだよ。
example_sentences.english: Come on! Don’t be so stiff. Stay over at my place! Just for one night!

notes: "The fasten arcs are arcs that go around something to fasten these things all together. What are these things? They are (parentheses) and [brackets]." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. Also, watch out from the shortening.

example_sentences.japanese: 左の括弧を読む時は単に「括弧」と言いますが、右の括弧を読む時は「括弧閉じる」と言います。
example_sentences.english: "When people read the left bracket, they just say ""kakko,"" but when they read the right bracket, they say ""kakko-tojiru,"" which means ""close bracket."""

notes: "My challenge has made a departure and is being sent to the enemy. This challenge that I'm sending is a provocation to see if they'll take me up on my challenge." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 抗議者の一人が、警察を挑発するために火炎瓶を投げつけました。
example_sentences.english: A protester threw a Molotov cocktail toward the police during a riot to provoke them.

notes: "Wake up from your bed and get up. You are rising or getting out of bed." "The readings are the on'yomi readings for both of these. For 起, just remember how in order to get up out of bed, you have to be let out of your chains, which requires a key (き). Otherwise, you stay laying down forever."

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は起床時間になっても、まだいびきをかいています。
example_sentences.english: He is still snoring even though it’s time to get out of bed.

notes: "I want to take the whole and fasten it together. Take all the parts and put it together in a synthesis and recap of the information." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は情報を総括し、上司の注意を促すために報告しましたが、彼は聞く耳を持ちませんでした。
example_sentences.english: I summed up the information and reported it to my boss, but he wouldn’t listen.

english: To Be Burned, To Get Burned
notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means char, but the verb version is to be burned or to get burned. You're not doing the burning, of course, but you're getting burned (owch!)." "The times where you were burned were mostly when you were a kid (子). That's because kids aren't good at working with hot things."

example_sentences.japanese: 一定にかき混ぜることで、鍋の底が焦げることが防げるとお母さんが言っていたわ。
example_sentences.english: My mom told me that constant stirring keeps the bottom of the pan from burning.

english: To Begin To Blow, To Breathe Out, To Burst Out Laughing
notes:
"If 吹く is ""to blow"" and 出す is ""to remove,"" then you are removing your blowing. You need to begin to blow to do that!" "The readings come from 吹く and 出す."

"""To Remove"" an eruption it needs to burst out of the earth or volcano it's in." "Remember how you learned the word 吹き出す? Well this is read the exact same way and means almost the exact same thing. If you know one reading, you know both!"

example_sentences.japanese: 俺の新しい髪型を見て、あいつプッと吹き出したんだぜ。失礼だよな。
example_sentences.english: She chuckled when she saw my new hairstyle. That’s rude, isn’t it?

example_sentences.japanese: 今までためていた怒りが一気に噴き出した。
example_sentences.english: The anger that had built up burst out at once.

english: To Be Stormy, To Be Rough
notes: "The kanji is wild and the verb is to be stormy or to be rough. If something is wild, like a storm or something, then it will be stormy and rough, after all." The reading comes from the reading you learned with the kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: 美容師として働いている限りは、手が荒れるのはどうしようもありません。
example_sentences.english: My hands will be rough as long as I’m a beauty artist, there’s nothing I can do about it.

english: To Be Transparent, To Be Clear, To Be See Through
notes: "This is a combination of the words 透ける and 通る. When you are transparent enough to pass through other things, you're still going to be transparent and people will be able to see through you." The readings for this word are both kun'yomi readings. You've learned both of these readings by now so you should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女の手は透き通るほど白かった。
example_sentences.english: Her hand was so white it was almost transparent.

notes: "You know that 吹く is ""to blow"" and 込む is ""to be crowded."" So if you blow into something to the point where it's crowded, you are blowing into it, making this word ""to blow in." "The reading comes from 吹く and 込む."

example_sentences.japanese: 家はおんぼろで、嵐が来る度に雨風が吹き込むのが現実です。
example_sentences.english: The reality is that the house is so old that the rain and wind blows in whenever a storm comes.

english: To Challenge Someone, To Challenge Something, To Challenge
notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means challenge and the verb vocab version is to challenge someone." "I don't (いど) just challenge anyone, but when I challenge someone, it's for real. My challenging reflexes come from my Id (いど), after all."

example_sentences.japanese: 私はこの日曜日、有名なベーコン鑑定家に挑みます。
example_sentences.english: I’m going to challenge the famous bacon connoisseur this Sunday.

notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means dig and the verb vocab version is to dig." "If you are going to dig you are going to end up making a hole (ほ)."

example_sentences.japanese: クママンは中年の男やもめで、家業で金を掘っています。
example_sentences.english: Kumaman is a middle-aged, widower living and digging gold like his father before him.

notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means dilute and the verb vocab version means to dilute or to water down." "The reading comes from 薄い, so if you know that you'll be able to read this too."

example_sentences.japanese: この味噌汁はしょっぱすぎるよ。もうちょっと薄めてもらってもいいかな？
example_sentences.english: This miso soup is too salty. Can you water down a little bit?

notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means distract and the verb vocab version of this word is to distract and to divert." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: You need to divert and to distract Maggie (まぎ). "

example_sentences.japanese: 不快な気分を紛らすために、裁縫針で耳にピアスの穴を開けました。
example_sentences.english: I pierced my ear with a sewing needle to distract myself from my unpleasant feelings.

notes: "You've seen 逃げる and 逃す. This one is 逃れる. This one simply means to escape. So that's not too bad. The difference between this one and the other escapes is that it has to do more with luck." "This is the same reading you learned for 逃す, so you should be able to read this word as well."

example_sentences.japanese: 万が一ゾンビが実際に現れた場合を想定して、どうやってゾンビから逃れるのかを考えているんです。
example_sentences.english: I’m thinking about how to escape from zombies if they actually showed up.

notes: "To 駆ける is ""to gallop."" 回る is ""to revolve."" So if you're galloping around in a revolving fashion, you are going to run around." "The readings come from 駆ける and 回る."

example_sentences.japanese: レシピにサフランがいるって書いてあったから、あちこち駆け回って探したんだけど見つからなくて、結局今回はサフランは使わなかったの。
example_sentences.english: The recipe said to put in saffron, so I ran around searching for it everywhere, but I couldn’t find any, so I didn’t add saffron this time.

notes: "駆ける is ""to gallop"" and 込む is ""to be crowded."" If you gallop into someone and crowd them, you are going to rush into them." "The readings come from 駆ける and 込む."

example_sentences.japanese: 終電に駆け込み乗車をしようとしましたが、目の前でドアが閉まりました。
example_sentences.english: I was rushing onto the last train, but the door closed before my eyes.

notes: "駆ける is ""to gallop"" and 出す is ""to remove."" So if you gallop out to remove yourself you are probably going to rush out a little fast. Calm down and slow down, man!" "The readings come from 駆ける and 出す."

example_sentences.japanese: 彼に質問を尋ねた時、駆け出しただけだ。
example_sentences.english: When I asked him a question he just ran off.

notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means shake and the verb vocab is to shake." "If everything starts to shake what else will shake along with it? You (ゆ), of course."

example_sentences.japanese: カヌーを揺らないで！
example_sentences.english: Don’t rock the canoe!

english: To Tie Up, To Fasten, To Tie Together, To Bind
notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means fasten and the verb vocab version is to fasten or to tie up or to tie together." "You are fastening up the coocoo (くく) clock, so the coocoo bird doesn't come out anymore. That annoying coocoo bird."

example_sentences.japanese: どうしてこの文章を括弧で括ったんですか？
example_sentences.english: Why did you enclose this sentence in brackets?

notes: "Two overnights is a two night's stay." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 継母がうちに二泊泊めてくれって言ってるんだけど、どう思う？
example_sentences.english: My stepmother is asking if she can stay at our place for two nights, what do you think?

notes: "Unite it all together and fasten it. That is unification." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 俺たちはいつもリスク統括部の奴らとは意見が合わないんだよ。
example_sentences.english: We don’t always agree with people in the risk management department.

notes: "A sky attack is an air raid / air attack. Tora tora tora!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕が空を見上げると、ちょうど空襲が始まるところだった。
example_sentences.english: When I looked up at the sky, the air raid was just about to happen.

notes: "An attack attack is an attack or assault." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 警察の車は、暴走族に襲撃された。
example_sentences.english: A police car was attacked by a motorcycle gang.

notes: "The decision is split, causing a breakdown in all we've decided. A big ol' rupture." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: あの男は奴らの決裂を、牢屋の中で舌なめずりをしながら待っていたに違いない。
example_sentences.english: That guy must have eagerly waited out their breakdown from behind bars.

notes: "The consolation of a problem is when I show my condolences. It is my sympathy call." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 私達は毎週日曜日、セラピー犬たちと一緒に老人ホームを慰問します。
example_sentences.english: We visit a nursing home with therapy dogs every Sunday.

notes: "I show my consolation by apologizing. This is consolation." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 保険会社から受け取る慰謝料は、税務署に申告する必要がありますか。
example_sentences.english: Do I have to declare the consolation money I receive from an insurance company to the revenue office?

notes: "The tribute I offer is my contribution." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: どうしてG20は財政支援への貢献を否認したのですか。
example_sentences.english: Why did G20 reject financially contributing to the bailout?

notes: "A reverse attack is a counterattack." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: パックマンは、追ってくるモンスターを逆襲して食べ始めた。
example_sentences.english: Pac-Man counterattacked and started eating the monsters that were chasing him.

notes: "If you break and destroy something, that is destruction. That is annihilation." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: その都市は原爆により壊滅しました。
example_sentences.english: The city was annihilated by the atomic bomb.

notes: "Extinction where everything is destroyed is destruction. It is extinction." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 全ての種の鯨が絶滅の危機に瀕している訳ではない。
example_sentences.english: Not all species of whales are in endangered.

notes: "I will chastise you and give you penalty. I do this as a discipline. A punishment." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 違反者には懲罰が与えられる。
example_sentences.english: Violators will receive punishment.

notes: "Using violence I'm going to expose the truth! This is disclosure. This is exposure." "The reading for 暴 is strange and new, not what you learned with the kanji. Just think about how when there is disclosure or exposure of something, you are surprised. You can't believe that's the truth. You have to take a step back (ばく) to deal with the new information."

example_sentences.japanese: 暴露本の出版については現在再考中です。
example_sentences.english: I’m having second thoughts about publishing a tell-all book.

notes: "The illusion is destroyed. If your illusion is destroyed, that is disillusionment." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼氏が道端で立ちションしてるのを見ちゃってさ。もう、完璧に幻滅した。
example_sentences.english: I saw my boyfriend taking a piss in the street and I was completely disillusioned.

notes: "Destroy to death. If you are destroyed to this point, this will be your downfall and ruin." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: もしその超巨大火山が噴火をすれば、我々は滅亡を免れないだろう。
example_sentences.english: If the super volcano erupted, we would not be able to escape destruction.

notes: "When what you expose is exited out of hiding, exposed for everything to see... that is exposure. It can also refer to photographic exposure too, in case you were wondering." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 思い直して、肌の露出が激しいドレスを着るのは控えることにしました。
example_sentences.english: I thought better of it and refrained from wearing such a revealing dress.

notes: "Slap that bug and destroy it. Haha! I slapped all the bugs away. This is extermination." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 私達はみんな、飲酒運転撲滅運動をサポートしています。
example_sentences.english: We all support the eradication of drunk driving.

notes: "Things that chafe and grate have lots of friction." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 摩擦によって静電気が生じるんですか？
example_sentences.english: Does friction cause static electricity?

notes: "A courteous talk is a friendly chat. We all know that ""friendly chats"" are never what they seem, though... right?" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 来る10月22日に、マンションの住人の皆様との懇話会を予定しております。
example_sentences.english: We are holding a friendly get together for the apartment residents on October 22.

notes: "If you see 即 before a word, you know that it's probably something that happens really fast or instantaneously. That's why this is immediate or instant." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: すごく可愛いティディベアを見つけたので、即買いしちゃいました。
example_sentences.english: I found a super cute teddy bear and immediately bought it.

notes: "If something is moving towards sincerity then it indeed and really did happen. Absolutely." "My 事 (まこと) really did happen! Indeed it did!"

example_sentences.japanese: 誠に申し訳ありませんが、当ホテルは全室禁煙となっております。
example_sentences.english: I am very sorry, but smoking is prohibited in all rooms of this hotel.

notes: "A courteous discussion is a little more formal than a friendly talk (because it's a discussion), but it's still fairly informal on the discussion scale, making it an informal talk." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 授業参観日の先生との懇談の間、彼女はずっとハンカチを握りしめてていました。
example_sentences.english: She was tightly clutching her handkerchief throughout the friendly talk with the teacher on parent’s day.

notes: "An instant death is an instant death." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は潮津波に乗ってサーフィンをしようとしたが、残念ながら即死した。
example_sentences.english: He tried to ride tidal bore and surf it, but unfortunately he died instantly.

notes: "With a seal we're printing everything out. The seal is what prints the words on the paper, making this printing." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 我々の広告を上質の紙に料理のレシピと一緒に印刷すれば、みんなそれを冷蔵庫に貼っておいてくれるんじゃないかな。
example_sentences.english: We should print our advertisements on nice paper with cooking recipes so that people will keep them on their fridge.

notes: "You have consolation so now you can relax. What a great feeling this is. You now have solace and relaxation." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: うちの会社では、毎年強制参加の慰安旅行があります。
example_sentences.english: Our company has a mandatory recreation trip every year.

notes: "A part split is when things split into two parts. This is a split and division." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: その政党は三派に分裂したと思っていたんだけど、実際は四派に分裂していたんだね。
example_sentences.english: I thought the political party was split three ways, but it was actually split four ways.

notes: "An odd attack is an attack you don't expect. This is a surprise attack." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 敵の奇襲を予想できなかった。
example_sentences.english: We didn’t expect our rival’s surprise attack.

english: To Be Proud, To Be Arrogant
notes: "Take my majesty and stretch it. Your majesty is so stretched! That makes me so proud! That's why this word is to be proud or to be arrogant." "The reading is from 威 and 張る."

example_sentences.japanese: 昨年最高額の売上を上げて歴代最年少の部長に昇進したんだから、きっと優秀なセールスマンなんだろうけど、確実に今は組織のトップのような顔をして威張り散らしているからね。私はあいつの事が嫌いだし、今後も尊敬することはないと思うよ。
example_sentences.english: He must be a good salesman because he made the most sales during the past year and was promoted to be the youngest manager in the company’s history, but he definitely feels like the top dog right now and he’s being really arrogant. I don’t like him and I will never respect him.

notes: "The kanji means grate (as in, ""to grate"" on something). The verb vocab version is to chafe and to rub, which is pretty close." "If you're going to chafe on me like that, I'm going to sue (す) you. It's making me very uncomfortable."

example_sentences.japanese: ペティコートは、スカートが肌と擦れることを防ぎます。
example_sentences.english: Petticoats prevent skirts from rubbing against your skin.

notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means destroy and the verb vocab version is to destroy and to annihilate." "You are going to destroy the hoe roe. This is the roe that comes from the hoe tools. If they create too much roe, they will create too many hoes. And if there are too many hoes, bad things will happen."

example_sentences.japanese: 奴らはメディアで情報操作を行って、日本を滅ぼそうとしているんだ。
example_sentences.english: They are trying to ruin Japan by manipulating information.

notes: "Remember 群れる, which means ""to flock"" or ""to crowd.""? This also means that!" "The reading is a little different from 群れる, though. There's an extra ら in there. That being said, it's pretty similar, so you should be able to use one to remember the other after a few reps. You can also think about it this way: Everyone is flocking together in one place. Strange thing is, it's to a small 村 (むら). There's a 村 reunion going on, that's why."

example_sentences.japanese: 空港に到着するとファンが群がっていて、驚きましたよ。
example_sentences.english: We were surprised that fans had gathered to wait for us when we arrived at the airport.

notes: "The kanji means chastise but the verb vocab version is to learn by experience. I guess these are kind of similar. When you make a mistake, someone will chastise you, and then you will learn by experience (either via the experience or via the chastising)." "As a child (こ) you got a lot of chastising, I bet. A lot of learning by experience (of chastising)."

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女に三度も振られてるっていうのに、お前まだ懲りてないのか。
example_sentences.english: You got turned down by her three times already and you still haven’t learned, have you?

english: To Pass Through, To Pass Under, To Evade, To Dive Underwater, To Get In, To Go Underground
notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means conceal, but the verb vocab version is to pass through or to pass under. Technically, you're concealed, but it's a little more active. You're passing through unnoticed, or passing under something. You're evading." "Why are you trying to pass through without getting seen? Because there's a cougar (くぐ) hunting you, and if it sees you... well... you're dead meat."

example_sentences.japanese: うちの犬は、フラフープをジャンプして潜る技を身につけました。
example_sentences.english: My dog learned a trick to jump through a hula hoop.

notes:
"Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means sink so the verb vocab version is to sink. This is when you're doing the sinking." "When you sink something, like a battleship, you go on and say: ""she's (しず) sunk, I sunk her."" That's like your tagline, or something. You say it for some reason because you think it's cool."

"This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means tranquilize, so the verb version is what happens when you've already been able to tranquilize someone. It's to appease or to suppress." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: You want to appease her because she's (しず) SUPER mad. She's pissed and she's angry and she's going to beat you up if you don't find out how to calm her down!"

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はソファに身を沈めながら、アカデミー賞の授賞式の生中継を観ています。
example_sentences.english: He is watching the broadcast of the Academy Awards ceremony and sinking into the sofa.

example_sentences.japanese: 神の怒りを鎮めるには、生贄を捧げる必要があります。
example_sentences.english: In order to appease the god’s anger we need to offer a sacrifice.

notes: "Open a letter that's been sealed already, it becomes an unsealed letter." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 開封前の商品であればいつでも返品可って書いてあるけど、開封後に中身が壊れてたり、その商品が好きじゃなかった場合はどうなんだろう。
example_sentences.english: It says I can return unopened products at any time, but what if I opened it and the stuff inside was broken or I didn’t like it?

notes: "Extinction caused by a shout. You are making everyone else's voices go extinct, and you scream and shout over them. You are making an exclamation, gosh darn it." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. Careful of the shortening.

example_sentences.japanese: 誰かがジェットコースターの上で、「覚悟しろ！」と絶叫した。
example_sentences.english: "Someone screamed ""brace yourself!"" on the roller coaster."

notes: "A spicy win is a narrow victory. Kind of makes sense, right?" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: Tofuguは著作権侵害の裁判で辛勝しました。
example_sentences.english: Tofugu won a narrow victory in a copyright infringement suit.

notes: "A spicy hug is a hug that feels not so great. But, it's not really painful all at once, either. As you're receiving a spicy hug, you just have to show patience and endurance while it lasts." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You didn't learn the reading of 抱's on'yomi reading, so think about how much patience and endurance you need to learn how to be good at bowling (ぼう)."

example_sentences.japanese: 場違いだって思うかもしれませんが、私のためだと思って辛抱してください。
example_sentences.english: You may feel a little out of place, but please be patient for me.

notes: "Recreation and comfort are things you do for pleasure and amusement. So nice!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 娯楽小説を読むことの何が悪いって言うんですか？
example_sentences.english: What’s wrong with reading light novels?

english: Thunderbolt, Lightning, Bolt Of Lightning, Lightning Strike
notes: "Thunder that falls from the sky is a thunderbolt." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 落雷が直撃したのに、奇跡的に無傷だった。
example_sentences.english: Even though the thunderbolt was a direct hit, I was miraculously unhurt.

english: To Be Diverted, To Be Distracted
notes: "You know that 紛らす means ""to divert"" or ""to distract."" This is when you're not doing the action, now, making this word to be diverted or to be distracted." "The reading comes from 紛らす."

example_sentences.japanese: 解熱剤が他の薬に紛れちゃってて、どれがどれだか分かりません。
example_sentences.english: The fever medicine slipped in with other pills and I’m not sure which one is which.

notes: "You know that 焦げる is ""to be burned"" or ""to get burned."" This word however is when you're doing the burning, making it to burn or to scorch. You know this because when it comes to burning, you pull out all the stops. You use lots of gas (がす) to burn whatever it is you burn." "The reading comes from 焦げる, so if you know that you know this word as well."

example_sentences.japanese: いつもトーストを真っ黒に焦がしてしまう。
example_sentences.english: I always burn my toast completely black.

english: To Endure, To Conceal, To Hide
notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means endure so the verb vocab version is to endure." "Those who are able to endure are those who have had a lot of training. Who has had the most training of anyone? Ninjas. What group are they part of? The shinobi (しの)."

example_sentences.japanese: 父さん、どうして僕たちはアイツらの侮辱を忍ばなきゃならないの？
example_sentences.english: Why do we have to endure their insults, dad?

notes: "荒れる is ""to be stormy"" or ""to be rough."" This is when you do the stormy rough things. You go wild on everyone, trying to lay waste and to devastate everything around you." "The reading comes from 荒れる."

example_sentences.japanese: 昨夜車上荒らしにあって、マックを盗まれました。
example_sentences.english: My car was broken into last night and my mac was stolen.

notes: "逃す is ""to let go"" or ""to let escape."" If something escapes your seeing, then you are going to overlook it." "The reading comes from 見 and 逃す."

example_sentences.japanese: その法律に抜け穴があることを今の今まで見逃していました。
example_sentences.english: I hadn’t noticed that there was a loophole in the law until now.

notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means shake so the verb vocab version is to shake." "The reading comes from 揺る."

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチが木を揺さぶったので、ビエットは枝に掴まった。
example_sentences.english: Viet held onto the branch because Koichi shook the tree.

english: Betting, Gambling, A Gamble, A Bet
notes: "The noun version of gamble is gambling or betting or a gamble or a bet. Whatever you do, put it all on black 13. Trust me." The reading comes from the reading you learned with the kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: あいつとの賭けに勝ったよ。
example_sentences.english: I won a bet against him.

notes: "It's possible that it's considerably considerable. It's considerably, fairly, and quite... something. Also please note that this is almost always written in kana and not kanji. But, we're learning kanji here, so gosh darn it we're going to learn some kanji." The reading is the same as the reading you learned with the kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本で初恋の人にバッタリ出くわした時は、可也驚きました。
example_sentences.english: I was quite surprised when I bumped into my first love in Japan.

notes: "Remember how 戸籍 is the family register? This is referring to that, and that makes this word mean entry in family register." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 結婚式の前に入籍をする予定です。
example_sentences.english: We are planning to be entered in the family register before the wedding ceremony.

notes: "You stare at hope. It looks good. That is your prospect and view, as you stare at hope." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: そのホテルの部屋からは美しく青い海を眺望することができました。
example_sentences.english: We were able to view the beautiful blue ocean from our hotel room.

notes: "A stiff fix is when you fix something to be stiff. When you do that, it becomes rigid." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 死後どのぐらいで死後硬直が起きるんでしょうか。
example_sentences.english: I wonder how long after death rigor mortis sets in.

notes: "一斉 is simultaneous or all at once. Add the に in there and you're heading towards those things. For ""simultaneous"" that becomes simultaneously. For ""all at once"" it stays at all at once." "The reading comes from 一斉."

example_sentences.japanese: 派遣社員たちは、景気の悪化で一斉に解雇されることを心配しています。
example_sentences.english: The temporary workers are worried about being fired simultaneously in the recession.

notes: "If you kill bacteria you are performing sterilization. You're killing those bacteria." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. Watch out for the shortening.

example_sentences.japanese: トイレを殺菌する一番いい方法は何ですか？
example_sentences.english: What’s the best way to sterilize a bathroom?

english: To Be Destroyed, To Be Annihilated
notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means destroy so the verb vocab version is to be destroyed. You know you're not destroying things because of the beer (びる). You'd never destroy beer... but someone else might. Grrr." """THE HORROR!"" (ほろ) you cry, as your beer is about to be destroyed."

example_sentences.japanese: 地球がじきに滅びるんだとしたら、どうしてベーコンを食べるのを我慢しなくちゃいけないの？
example_sentences.english: If the earth is going to be destroyed, why should I resist eating bacon?

english: To Curse, To Put A Curse On
notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means curse, and the verb version is to curse or to put a curse on." The reading is the same as the one you learned with the kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: 夫が心的外傷後ストレス障害と診断された後、私はそれが誰であれその戦争を始めた人を呪いました。
example_sentences.english: After my husband was diagnosed with Post Traumatic Stress Disorder I cursed whoever it was that started the war.

english: To Earn Income, To Make Money
notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means earnings and the verb vocab version is to earn income, because you can't ""to income"" something. Can also be to make money." "You earn your income, and every time you're paid, you're given your money in a briefcase (かせ). Imagine getting your income from a briefcase, opening it up, and grabbing the money from within. Then, you have to give the briefcase back at the specified dropoff."

example_sentences.japanese: 現職の大統領が、前大統領よりもどれだけ多くのお金を稼いでいるか知っているかい？
example_sentences.english: Do you know how much more money the incumbent president earns than the former president?

english: To Get Cloudy, To Become Cloudy
notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means cloudy and the verb vocab version means to get cloudy or to become cloudy." "The reading is the same as the one you learned with the kanji. It also happens to be the same as 雲, which has a very similar meaning (clouds)."

example_sentences.japanese: ラーメンの湯気で眼鏡が曇っちゃうのが好きじゃないんだよね。
example_sentences.english: I don’t like it when my glasses get cloudy from ramen steam.

notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means bride and the verb vocab version is to marry, because you can't really ""to bride"" someone." "Imagine you're getting married to a valley girl. You're all like. Hey, I'm gonna marry you! And she's all like Tots (とつ), we gonna get, like, married! Imagine her saying more ""tots"" things (tots = short for totally in valley girl speak, at least in my imagination)."

example_sentences.japanese: 嫁ぎたての頃は、息子の嫁はかまととぶっていました。
example_sentences.english: Around the time they got married, my son’s wife pretended she was a prude.

notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means grate and this verb means to rub or to scrub. It will help to think back to 擦れる which means ""to chafe"" or ""to rub,"" which is more similar to this verb than the kanji meaning is." "This kanji shares the reading from 擦れる but it also has another reading, こする. Both are considered ""common."" Most likely, you'll use する's reading the most because it is the same as すれる's reading, but for now try to keep the other one in your mind as well."

example_sentences.japanese: 花粉症で目を擦ってたら、片方のコンタクトレンズが破けました。
example_sentences.english: I was rubbing my eyes because of my allergies and one of my contact lenses was torn.

hiragana: まばたき, またたき
english: A Blink, A Wink, Wink, Blink
notes: "A blink is a blink and a wink as well, depending on how many eyes you use." "A wink is all it takes to get the ""Ma butter"" (まばた) from the store. It's hidden, and they only bring it out if you do the wink."

example_sentences.japanese: 瞬きせずに、この絵を見続けてください。
example_sentences.english: Don’t blink and just keep looking at the picture please.

notes: "Ten thousand years old! That's a lot of time. This is the word for the turned-English Japanese phrase, banzai!" "The reading isn't the same as 万's normal reading. It's ばん instead of まん. But, since the word ""banzai"" is so well known, you probably can remember this reading."

example_sentences.japanese: トフグのコウイチに万歳三唱をしましょう！万歳！万歳！万歳！
example_sentences.english: Three cheers for Koichi of Tofugu! Hip hip hooray! Hip hip hooray! Hip hip hooray!

notes: "Secluded and closed off, putting you in confinement and imprisonment." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 専業主婦になってからというもの、まるで捕虜になって、台所に幽閉されてでもいるかのようだわ。
example_sentences.english: After becoming a housewife, it’s like I’ve become a war prisoner, confined to the kitchen.

notes: "The shelf, once established, makes up the construction and building of the building. Just think of a building that's being built. It looks like a little shelf, doesn't it? That's important because this type of construction usually goes over something between two things, like a bridge." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 今まで一度も橋梁を架設したことがありません。
example_sentences.english: I’ve never built a bridge before.

notes: "Take your pride and stretch it out. It's an exaggeration, because you've stretched your pride out pretty thin." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: レビューで今までで最高のカメラだとか何とか書かれてたけど、それはやっぱり誇張だったね。
example_sentences.english: The review said that it was the best camera ever, but it was an exaggeration just like I thought.

notes: "The departure of bubbles is when bubbles leave something, like a mouth. That's why this is foaming." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 発泡スチロールはこの袋に入れてもらってもいい？他のゴミとは分別して捨てるんだよね。
example_sentences.english: Could you put the styrofoam in this plastic bag? We throw away the rest of the garbage separately.

notes: "Shut up and kill your talking or I'll kill it for you. I'm not listening to this. I'm ignoring it." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 警察はその地域では多くの犯罪を黙殺しています。
example_sentences.english: The police ignore most of the crime in this area.

english: Killing With A Sword, Putting To The Sword
notes: "A slice kill is a killing with a sword. You don't want to hear this, if at all possible." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕のお気に入りのアニメキャラクターが斬殺されてしまった。
example_sentences.english: My favorite anime character was slaughtered.

notes: "If you thwart and stop something, you are an obstruction or hindrance." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: その証人が法廷で証言するのを、何としてでも阻止するんだ。
example_sentences.english: Do whatever it takes to prevent that witness from testifying in court.

notes:
"Thwart and damage the advancement of something. That's an obstruction and inhibition." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

"Neglect someone so much that you remove yourself from their inner circle and live outside of their life and it's called estrangement. You might never see them again. But that's okay with you, your relationship is too weird to fix now." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: カフェインを含む飲み物は、睡眠を阻害します。
example_sentences.english: Drinks containing caffeine inhibit sleep.

example_sentences.japanese: 学校ではずっと疎外感を感じていました。
example_sentences.english: I had constantly felt alienated in school.

notes: "This is the same as the kanji, rather. Can also mean better or instead." "Just think: rather than a bug (むし), how about an animal?"

example_sentences.japanese: お姫様よりも寧ろ猫になりたい。
example_sentences.english: I’d rather be a cat than a princess.

notes: "You sink down and shut up. You go into a silence and hush. This tends to be an awkward silence or hush." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 気まずい沈黙の後、私は塩の入った小瓶を掴みました。
example_sentences.english: There was an awkward silence and I grabbed a salt shaker.

notes: "If you enter ink into (your body), you are getting yourself a tattoo." "The reading comes from 入れる and 墨 combined together. Careful of the rendaku."

example_sentences.japanese: その入れ墨には今までいくら費やしているんですか。
example_sentences.english: How much money have you spent on tattoos?

notes: "Forging and tempering of things is tempering and forging of things. When you do this to your body, to get ready for the big race, it's called training. (Though body tempering sounds way cooler, don't you think?)" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 発音が一晩で上手くなる人なんていません。発音を上達させるには、継続的かつ正しい鍛錬が必要です。
example_sentences.english: Nobody can get perfect pronunciation overnight. To improve your pronunciation you need continuous and proper training.

english: To Be Proud Of, To Boast Of
notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means pride and the verb version is to be proud of or to boast of." "The hoe 子 (ほこ) is the kid who is carrying around a hoe all the time, swinging it around, doing dumb things with it. He's so proud of it, though, and it shows on his face. He's always boasting about his hoe skillz too."

example_sentences.japanese: この短編映画では、日本が世界に誇るロボット産業をテーマとしています。
example_sentences.english: This short film is about the robotics industry that Japan boasts of to the world.

english: To Shake, To Sway, To Tremble
