example_sentences.english: Could you sort out the extracted data by 5 o’clock?

notes: "Isolate and detached from everything else. This thing (or person) is in isolation and quarantine." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は二日酔いであまりにも酒臭すぎるので、別の部屋に隔離しています。
example_sentences.english: We have quarantined him to a separate room because he is hungover and reeks of liquor.

notes: "Pluck lucky ticket out to choose the winner of the lottery / raffle! Today I pluck... number 23! We've chosen a winner!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はあの病院の抽選で、胃のバイパス手術が当たったんです。
example_sentences.english: I won a gastric bypass surgery from that hospital’s raffle.

notes: "Cover your face. Not with your hands or a puppy, but with a mask! Okay, I guess you could cover it with a puppy mask, but that's all you." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 覆面のスーパーマンは、ボッロボロのマントを身につけていました。
example_sentences.english: The masked superman was wearing such a tattered cloak.

notes: "An intuition difference is a misunderstanding or wrong guess. Sorry! My intuition was off." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 「すみません、間違えました。違う人と 勘違いしました。」「正確には誰と間違えたんですか？お願いします。教えてください。」
example_sentences.english: """Excuse me, my mistake. I thought you were someone else."" ""Exactly who did you mistake me for? Please. Tell me."""

notes: "It's solely one. The only one. The sole one. Totally unique." "The reading for 唯 is the same as the one you learned with the kanji, though there is also a shortened version which has ゆい shortened to ゆ. The reading for 一 is one you haven't learned yet, wow! You're finally going to learn the second, rare on'yomi reading for 一! It wants to be the only reading now, so it eats (いつ) the other one. Oh no, you can't remember that other reading now. いつ is the sole 一 reading in your brain!"

example_sentences.japanese: あいつは奴の家族の中で唯一まともな人間だよ。
example_sentences.english: He is the only decent person in his family.

notes: "Fear mixed with confusion creates panic! You get a scare so bad, you're fearful and you don't know what to do." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You've learned them already, so you should be able to read this on your own!

example_sentences.japanese: 私が留守だった日、村は恐慌に包まれた。
example_sentences.english: The village was consumed with panic on the day I wasn't there.

example_sentences.japanese: 人生で二度もの経済恐慌を経験するとは思っていなかったよ。
example_sentences.english: I wasn't expecting to experience two economic scares in my lifetime.

example_sentences.japanese: 国全体が恐慌状態に陥った。
example_sentences.english: The entire country flew into a panic.

notes: "Intuition from my dialect tells me that I should pardon you. Give you forgiveness. You're lucky I speak this dialect." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 勘弁してちゃぶ台。今日は忙かったし、滅茶苦茶疲れているんだ。
example_sentences.english: Cut me some slack. It’s been a long day and I’m terribly tired.

notes: "Immersed to the point where it's transparent, because it's so soaked... that is total permeation and soaking and osmosis." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: こちらの化粧水は、お肌の奥深くまで浸透するということで、すごく人気が出てきています。
example_sentences.english: This face lotion is getting really popular because it deeply permeates into the skin.

notes: "Open up cultivation back on this land. It was closed before, due to it being a wasteland, but now it's time for reclamation and cultivation of this land." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 畑は違えど、新規市場を開拓するという点においては、前職とさほど変わりはないよ。
example_sentences.english: Although it’s a completely different field, there isn’t much of a difference in terms of cultivating a new market.

notes: "I'd like to infer and encourage this item to you. It is my recommendation. It is my endorsement." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: このカボチャのパイは、焼き上がりでも美味しく召し上がって頂けるのですが、私たちは御賞味の前に少し冷蔵庫に入れて頂くことを推奨しています。
example_sentences.english: This pumpkin pie is delicious right after it’s been baked, but we recommend refrigerating for a short time before eating it.

notes: "I've memorized this to the point of comprehension. It was my resolution to learn all this to comprehension. This way I have readiness." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は痩身手術を受ける覚悟を決めました。
example_sentences.english: I resigned myself to undergo weight loss surgery.

english: Slang, Common, Vulgar, Local Manners, Local Customs, Mundane
notes: "Things that are vulgar are things like slang, local manners, and just plain common stuff." The reading is the same as the one you learned with the kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: 貧乏から金持ちに成り上がった人は、俗に成金と呼ばれます。
example_sentences.english: People who went from rags to riches are commonly called nouveau riche.

notes: "The kanji means solely, and this means solely, but also other related things like only or merely. They're all pretty close, so try to remember a few!" "To spice up something you'd describe with words like only and simply use Ta da! (ただ) to spice it up. It's like magic! Now it isn't just a gift, it's a TA DA surprise gift."

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は私の母ではなく唯の付き添い人です。
example_sentences.english: She is not my mother, she’s just a chaperone.

notes: "Immersed in water. That sounds like submersion. Possibly like a flood, even." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 気温が上がるのは素晴らしいことだけど、私達は雪解け水による浸水を心配しています。
example_sentences.english: It’s great that the temperature is rising, but we’re worried about a flood from the melting snow.

notes: "Using our intuition we will come up with a plan. We'll be taking into consideration the information we have along with our intuition, so don't worry." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 様々な状況を勘案すると、私にとって仕事を辞めることがベストな選択だったんです。
example_sentences.english: Taking various circumstances into consideration, quitting the job was the best option for me.

example_sentences.japanese: 自分がされたり言われたりしたらどう思うかってことも勘案に入れるようにしてます。
example_sentences.english: I try to take into consideration how I would feel if things were said or done to me.

example_sentences.japanese: この投資に関して、どのようなリスクを勘案していますか。
example_sentences.english: What kinds of risks have you taken into consideration concerning this investment?

notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means inferiority and the verb vocab version is to be inferior to." "When thinking about cars, an automatic (おと) car is inferior to a manual car. Sure, manual is harder, but way more interesting to drive."

example_sentences.japanese: 今、彼は私のこと嫌っているから、私の立場は挨拶程度の人よりも劣っているってのははっきりしてるわ。
example_sentences.english: He hates me now, so I’m pretty sure that I'm even more inferior to him than a nodding acquaintance.

english: To Be Moist, To Be Damp, To Be Watered
notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means watered. When something is watered, it is moist and damp. That's why this verb is to be moist or to be damp or to be watered." "If you get moist and damp, then you're all (うるお) wet. It's just how it is."

example_sentences.japanese: このローションを使えば、あなたのお肌はプルプルに潤いますよ。
example_sentences.english: If you use this lotion it will moisturize your skin so that it’s firm and soft.

english: To Be Overturned, To Be Reversed, To Be Retracted, To Topple Over
notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means capsize but the verb version is what happens when a plan or idea capsizes. It going to be overturned. It was a bad idea, go back, don't do it or we'll all sink!" "Of all the ideas that need to be overturned, it's the ones from the 靴 guy (くつがえ). He thinks we should only wear shoes. Not shoes and nothing else, but shoes all over out entire bodies. Yikes, now that's an idea I'd like to be retracted, 靴 guy."

example_sentences.japanese: スポーツはずっとそんなに好きではなかったんですが、一度野球の試合を見に行った時にそれが覆りまして、今ではマリナーズの大ファンです。
example_sentences.english: I didn’t always like sports, but that was overturned once I went to see a baseball game and now I’m a big fan of the Mariners.

english: To Be Soaked In, To Be Submerged, To Be Flooded
notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means immersed. Things that are immersed are described by verbs like to be soaked in or to be submerged or to be flooded." "What is soaked and submerged in water (that shouldn't be)? It is your heater (ひた). It's all soaked and doesn't work anymore :("

example_sentences.japanese: お風呂で図書館から借りたホーソンの『巌の顔』を読んでいたんですが、うっかりお湯に浸ってしまったんです。
example_sentences.english: "I was reading Hawthorne’s ""The Great Stone Face"" that I borrowed from a library in the bath and thoughtlessly soaked it in bathwater. "

english: To Isolate, To Partition, To Separate
notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means isolate and the verb vocab version is to isolate or to partition or to separate. You get the idea, anyways." "Why did you have to isolate him from the rest of the soccer players? Because all he could do was headers (へだ) and that was getting pretty dangerous. He would head everything in his reach. He was going crazy with headers. He had to be isolated!"

example_sentences.japanese: 私のアパートでは、浴槽と洗面所はシャワーカーテン一枚で隔てられています。
example_sentences.english: In my apartment, the bathtub and the washroom are separated by a single shower curtain.

english: To Mow, To Reap, To Harvest
notes: "If you prune and take from what you pruned, you're going to mow or to reap or to harvest whatever it is you're pruning." "The reading is the reading you learned with 刈 and the reading from the vocab 取る."

example_sentences.japanese: 私の実家は農家で米を育てているので、今週末は稲の刈り取りを手伝わなきゃいけないんです。
example_sentences.english: My parents are farmers who raise rice so I have to help them harvest rice this weekend.

english: To Pity, To Have Mercy On
notes: "If something is pathetic then you should try to pity that thing." "Awww (あわ), you're so pathetic it's cute! I will pity you. Reading also comes from 哀れ."

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女のお婆さんが、「あの子の人見知りは哀れむべきものだ」とぼやくのを聞きました。
example_sentences.english: "I heard her grandmother grumble, ""That girl’s shyness should be pitied."""

english: To Prune, To Mow, To Cut
notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means prune and the verb vocab version is to prune (or to mow or to cut)." The reading is the same as the reading you learned with the kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: 草を刈り終わったから、放してやってよ。
example_sentences.english: I’ve finished mowing the grass, so turn him loose.

notes: "If you have comprehension, then you are probably going to realize something about something else. Comprehension leads to realization, after all." "You realized something so amazing that you couldn't believe it. That comprehension, wow! The realization was so big that you sat (さと) down in disbelief. If you didn't you would have fallen on the ground."

example_sentences.japanese: 背中の曲がったお婆さんは、不法滞在者として拘置所に拘留された時、そこで自分が死を迎えることになることを悟りました。
example_sentences.english: When the hunchbacked old lady was sent to a detention center for being an illegal immigrant, she realized that it would be where she met her death.

notes: "We're moving towards one approximation. It used to be more approximations, but now it's just one, and because it's just one it's not really an approximation anymore. It's unconditionally set. It's set as a rule." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 定額給付金は一概に良い事だとは言えない。
example_sentences.english: I can’t say that tax rebates are unconditionally good things.

notes: "A vow promise is the promise that you made with your vow. It's the oath you sweat to keep!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: こちらが誓約書となっておりまして、こちらとこちらにサインをして頂く必要があります。
example_sentences.english: Here is the written pledge. You need to sign it here and here.

notes: "Transport and exit these goods from here (by transporting them). Take it away. It's time to carry out." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 日曜の夜七時までに全ての作品を搬出する必要があります。
example_sentences.english: We need to carry out all of our work by 7pm on Sunday night.

notes: "When you flip your idea of something, you're changing how you think about it. That's why this word is change one's mind." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: この結婚について、絶対に翻意することがないことを誓います。
example_sentences.english: I swear, I will absolutely not change my mind about this marriage.

notes: "This is the noun version of the kanji and has the same meaning as well: coloring." "The reading has いろ (like 色) in it, then a ど, so think about an 色 dog, running around coloring things, because that's what an 色 dog does."

example_sentences.japanese: 父の弁当は、彩りについて全く考慮がされておらず、全部茶色だったので嫌でしたね。
example_sentences.english: I didn’t like my dad’s bento because he never really took coloring into account and all of it was brown.

notes: "When you revise something to make it correct you are doing a correction and revision." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: もし私の日本語に間違いがあれば、その場で訂正してもらってもいいですか？
example_sentences.english: If I make a mistake in Japanese would you mind correcting it on the spot for me?

notes: "A feeling of inscription is the feeling one gets when something so strong happens that it's like the feeling gets inscribed into your soul. This is something that left a very deep impression." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 私達は彼のピアノの演奏に深く感銘を受けました。
example_sentences.english: We were deeply impressed by his piano performance.

notes: "Drifting down the stream. Something that is doing this is drifting. It could also be the drift of something." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 帆が折れて、ヨットが海に漂流し始めた時は、ちょっと悲観的でしたね。
example_sentences.english: When the mast broke and my yacht started drifting out to sea, I got a little pessimistic.

notes: "Something has drifted to the point where it has arrived. Where do drifting things arrive? They arrive on shore (as they drift on top of water). That makes this word drifting ashore." "This word uses the on'yomi readings for the kanji. You'll need to remember the on'yomi reading of 着 for this word by looking back at the word 執着 where you first learned this reading."

example_sentences.japanese: 傷ついた赤ちゃん鯨が、とある砂浜に漂着するところを想像してみてください。
example_sentences.english: Imagine a wounded baby whale drifting ashore onto a sandy beach.

notes: "The embankment prevents the water from going over the edge. It's an embankment." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 水が堤防を越えそうになっているから、近づかない方がいいですよ。
example_sentences.english: The water is almost running over the embankment, so you should be careful.

notes: "My interest is stirred up! I'm feeling excitement and stimulation from all this stirring up, in fact!" "The reading for 興奮 is one you didn't learn with the kanji, though it's similar. Instead of きょう it's こう, so just think of how whenever you feel excitement, it's thanks to こういち. So just think of こういち exciting you in some way to remember this vocab's reading."

example_sentences.japanese: 止まれの標識を無視する度に、興奮するんです。
example_sentences.english: Every time I ignore a stop sign I get excited.

notes: "Using the grasp meaning of 把 and combining it with grip, you can tell you're grasping at something and then gripping it. I usually grasp then grip at things flying at me, which makes this word mean grasp or catch." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 正直、まだ事態の把握すら出来ていない状況です。
example_sentences.english: Honestly, I haven’t even been able to grasp the overall situation yet.

notes: "A wicked devil! Ugh, I hate those things. They're always a hindrance and intrusion. Just imagine a wicked devil hanging out in your house, eating your food, and sleeping on your bed. What a hindrance." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の邪魔をするな。一人で出来るよ！
example_sentences.english: Don’t stand in my way. I can do it by myself!

notes: "Something you do accidentally is hopefully something you do occasionally or once in a while." "For the reading, think about the word 弾 (たま), which means bullet, and how you occasionally shoot people with bullets when you're out hunting... but not too often. Dick Cheney level."

example_sentences.japanese: 偶にぎっくり腰になるんですよね。
example_sentences.english: I strain my back every once in a while.

notes: "You want people to express how they feel about you in a clear manner, so you demand they give you public acknowledgement. You want clear, concise public recognition for all of your amazing talents, skills, and for reaching level 50 of WaniKani. Maybe they'll throw you a parade!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 表彰式には出席せずに帰ってきてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: I came home without attending the awards ceremony.

notes: "We have to examine you during this epidemic... soooo, if you could come over here and just stay here for a long time, that'd be great. Yeah, it's kind of a quarantine, sorry about that." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: オーストラリアの検疫法はすっごく厳しいから、食べ物は何も持って行かない方が身のためだよ。
example_sentences.english: Australia’s quarantine laws are very strict, so you shouldn’t take any food there.

notes: "I need to consult you on this problem, if I could. I have a question / enquiry I'd like to ask you." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: その日は経済財政諮問会議が開催される予定です。
example_sentences.english: The Council on Economic and Fiscal Policy plans to hold a meeting on the same day.

notes: "I'm stirred up causing me to wake up. I'm stirring and rousing oneself." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女の一言が、彼を奮起させ、受験勉強をさせた。
example_sentences.english: Her one word roused him to study for the test.

notes: "I look up to heaven, and I am taken aback and amazed by it. It's just so amazing." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は真美がどれだけ速くベーコンを食べれるのかってことにびっくり仰天しました。
example_sentences.english: I was astonished at how quickly Mami could eat bacon.

english: To Accomplish, To Achieve, To Carry Out
notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means accomplish and the verb vocab version is to accomplish." "Everything you've accomplished can put stored in your single little pinky toe (と)... you haven't accomplished that much, apparently."

example_sentences.japanese: 諦めないで！やり遂げるんだ！お前なら出来るよ！
example_sentences.english: Don’t give up! Accomplish it! You can do it!

english: To Burn, To Be Lighted, To Be Lit, To Be Burning
notes: "This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means lamp, so the verb version is to burn or to be lit. Just like what you'd do with a lamp." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You haven't learned this reading yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you:Who wanted the candle to be lit? Tom (とも) Cruise. He's afraid of the dark so he always wants all the lights and candles in the house to be burning at all times."

example_sentences.japanese: あの部屋に明かりが灯るのを見たんだ。
example_sentences.english: I can see light burning in that room.

notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means drift and the verb vocab version is to drift." "You're going to drift away. Drifting drifting drifting. Then, you turn into a yo-yo and yell ""ta da yo-yo (ただよ)! Not sure why drifting turns you into a yo-yo, but imagine it and don't question it."

example_sentences.japanese: 焼き芋を食べた後のおならは、他のおならよりも長い間空気中を漂う気がするよ。
example_sentences.english: Farts after eating roasted sweet potatoes seem to hang in the air longer than normal farts.

english: To Flip, To Turn Over, To Flip Over
notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means flip and the verb vocab version is to flip or to turn over." "The here guy (ひるがえ) is the guy who's here right now. He's here, and he's ready to flip over."

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女のスカートが風で翻ったのは分かるんですが、その時の彼の心象を翻訳するのは私には難しすぎます。
example_sentences.english: I know her skirt fluttered in the wind, but rendering how I felt at the time is too difficult.

notes: "Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means threaten and the verb vocab version is to threaten." "I'm going to threaten you with your life if you have a bad odor (おど). Imagine someone with a bad odor, then threaten them."

example_sentences.japanese: その教師は何名かの男子生徒を刃物で脅したとして解雇されました。
example_sentences.english: That teacher was fired because he threatened some male students with a knife.

notes: "Flip the translation of a word from one language to another. That is the translation of that word (or phrase, etc)." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: ちょうど君の翻訳を見させてもらってたところだよ。
example_sentences.english: I was just looking over your translation.

notes: "To carry you and transport you. That's a form of transport. Could also be a carriage, which is also a form of transport." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. Watch out for the rendaku.

example_sentences.japanese: このレストランには、食事やその他の細々したものを運搬するためのミニエレベータがあります。
example_sentences.english: There is a mini elevator used to transport food and other small things in this restaurant.

notes:
"Things that transport and send you places are forms of transportation." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

"A sail runs boats along the sea by sailing! You can't run along the water unless the sail is out and catching the wind." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 搬送作業時に左肩を脱臼してしまいました。
example_sentences.english: I dislocated my left shoulder when I was doing conveyance work.

example_sentences.japanese: ほら、あそこにヨットが帆走しているよ。
example_sentences.english: Look, there’s a yacht sailing over there.

notes: "What's stuffed in the bottle? Jam you bottled for later! How could you forget?" "This word consists of the on'yomi reading for 瓶 and the kun'yomi reading for 詰 that you learned when you learned 詰める. You've learned them both so as long as you remember the rendaku, you should be able to read this word too! Just remember that 詰 is taking the め from 詰める with it in this word too. You can't see it, but it's there."

example_sentences.japanese: メープルシロップを瓶詰しています。
example_sentences.english: I’m bottling maple syrup.

english: Drying Up, Dry Up, Running Dry
notes: "Something that withers from thirst ends up drying up. If you let a plant dry up like this it might die if you don't water it soon." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You didn't learn this reading for 渇 yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you:If all of your plants are drying up you should just give them to your cats (かつ). Cats love to play with dried up plants. At least they won't go to waste."

example_sentences.japanese: もうすぐ石油は枯渇する。
example_sentences.english: The petroleum will dry up very soon.

notes: "An explanation that's bright is just a really clear and well developed explanation." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: これについて、正式に釈明をする必要がある。
example_sentences.english: You need to formally explain this.

notes: "Even if you untie an explanation it's still a pretty good explanation anyway. " This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: その解釈は間違っていると思います。
example_sentences.english: I think that explanation is wrong.

notes: "Soft prohibition isn't going to be as bad as jail or prison. They went soft on you, so you're only under house arrest. That's not so bad, right?" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は自宅軟禁下に置かれました。
example_sentences.english: She was placed under house arrest.

notes: "If you want to char fish for dinner it will dry up because of your own impatience. Charring fish takes time and if you're too uneasy and shove it too far in the fire it will dry out, burn, and get gross." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 度重なる事業の失敗で、すっかり焦燥しきっているんだ。
example_sentences.english: I’m thoroughly irritated with this repeatedly failing project.

notes: "Before you can give an explanation of who you are to someone you're about to meet, you have to nod or bow as a greeting first. It's rude to start explaining who you are before you greet them." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You didn't learn this reading for 会 yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you:When someone bows to you, you always feel a little uncomfortable, so you say, ""Eh"" (え) and try to get them to stop. You're so uncomfortable that you can't think of words and ""eh"" is all you can manage to get out."

example_sentences.japanese: 会釈をしたら会釈を返すのが礼儀でしょう。
example_sentences.english: You might have the decency to return my nod with a nod.

notes: "If your brain can't stop pouring out all the explanations your teacher gives you, you'll need to keep notes. That way when the information pours out of your head, you'll still have your comments and annotations to help you remember the teacher's explanations later." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: その場合は、注釈を付けてください。
example_sentences.english: In that case, please add notes.

notes: "You are determined to get an agreement out of people so you decide to be really positive with them. As long as you make it seem like everything is super great, and totally good for them, they'll end up agreeing with everything you say. " This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: どうして肯定も否定もしないんですか。
example_sentences.english: Why won’t you say yes or no?

notes: "If you call someone by screaming, you're probably trying to summon them like a magician would. Magicians have to scream their spells out in order for them to work. So you have to scream out their name when you call them if you want to summon someone." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 魔法使いを召喚しました。
example_sentences.english: I summoned a magician.

english: To Respectfully Call, To Respectfully Invite, To Respectfully Eat, To Respectfully Drink
notes: "This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means call, so the verb version is to respectfully call. It can also be used as to respectfully eat or to respectfully invite too. It's a really useful word like that. As long as you remember it's the respectful/honorific way of doing things you should be fine." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: If you want to respectfully call out to someone you need to make sure you don't look them in the 目 (め) because that's super rude. Always remember to turn your 目 away to show respect."

example_sentences.japanese: あなたのお姉さまは神に召されたのですよ。
example_sentences.english: Your older sister was called by the gods.

english: To Soak, To Steep, To Dip
notes: "This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means immersed, so the verb version is what happens when you immerse something in a liquid. It's to soak or to dip." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You already learned this reading when you learned 浸る, so you should know this one too."

example_sentences.japanese: どうして野菜を水に浸しているの？
example_sentences.english: Why are you soaking the vegetables in water?

english: To Till, To Plow, To Plough, To Cultivate
notes: "This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means plow, so the verb version is to plow or to till." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn this reading yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you:You need to till your land because you want to have a tiger yard (たがや). That's either when you have a yard full of live tigers, or you plant bushes and shape them into tigers. I hope it's the second kind of tiger yard. Either way, you have to plow the land to get it ready."

example_sentences.japanese: この機械で畑を耕すんですよ。
example_sentences.english: I’ll plow the field with this machine.

notes: "This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means wither, so the verb version is to wither or to die." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn this reading yet so here's a mnemonic to help you:How do you get plants to wither? You hit them with your car (か). It isn't very good for your car either, but the plants will definitely die, so problem solved!"

example_sentences.japanese: せっかく植えた木が枯れてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: The tree I took great pains to grow withered.

notes: "Animals exit the mountains into your land and never seem to die! They end up appearing frequently in your garden, eating all your yummy carrots and watermelons, and then make their exit back into the hills. They're infesting your home now and you don't know what to do!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本各地でクマが大量出没している。
example_sentences.english: Bears appear frequently in large quantities all over Japan.

notes: "Stand behind someone and embrace them. That's how you show them you're backing and supporting them. Do this to your local politicians. " This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: どうせ出馬者を擁立しようとしているだけだろう。
example_sentences.english: I’m sure that they are just trying to support the candidate.

notes: "A sealed chain won't break or open so it gets in the way of everyone, forming a blockade. This can happen at banks too and it will result in them freezing your account!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 銀行が潰れて、預金が封鎖されてしまったんです。
example_sentences.english: The bank was bankrupted and my account was frozen.

notes: "A cave in where everyone dies is still a cave in, just a really sad one." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 地震であそこの道路が陥没したそうです。
example_sentences.english: It looks like that highway over there collapsed from the earthquake.

notes: "If you take along a chain with you it's still a chain, it's just moving somewhere new." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: まずはこの負の連鎖を断ち切る必要があります。
example_sentences.english: First, you must sever ties with this negative chain.

notes: "Pierce someone when you stab them with a mighty charge with your sword. Better yet, hit them with your lightning attack!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 突貫工事で犬小屋を建てました。
example_sentences.english: We built the doghouse by constructing it at top speed.

notes: "A closed chain lets everyone know that a building or store is closing for good. It's got to lockout everyone so they won't try to get in anymore." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: このプールは今月で閉鎖されます。
example_sentences.english: The pool is closed this month.

notes: "When you are given cool treatment it's called a cold reception or inhospitality. This sucks." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は実力があるのにどうしてこんなに冷遇されているんですか。
example_sentences.english: If he’s so great then why did he get such a cold reception?

notes: "Those with leadership who want control will set out on missions of conquest and strive for world domination!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: わが校の野球部が、秋のリーグ戦を制覇しました。
example_sentences.english: Our school’s baseball club dominated the autumn league match.

notes: "If you encounter something difficult it's going to result in disaster. Especially if you're in a boat. Encountering really difficult water will result in a shipwreck! Ick!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 危うく遭難するところでした。
example_sentences.english: We narrowly missed having a disaster.

notes: "An embrace and a hug are pretty much the same thing. So you're still going to embrace and hug people!" "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You didn't learn this reading for 抱 yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you:Who gives the best hugs in the world? Harry Houdini (ほう)! He knows what it's like to be hugged too tightly because he's always in straight jackets. So his hugs are nice and gentle. Just the way you like them!"

example_sentences.japanese: その映画の、主役の二人が甘い抱擁を交わすシーンがとても美しかったよ。
example_sentences.english: The scene in that movie where the two leading actors exchanged a sweet embrace was so beautiful.

notes: "It doesn't matter what kind of treatment you get on your encounter with new people because it's the encounter itself that's scary! Don't worry, people are just people. They shouldn't make you nervous." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 悲惨な交通事故に遭遇しました。
example_sentences.english: I encountered a tragic traffic accident.

english: Endurance, Perseverance, Tolerance, Patience, Self Control
notes: "I get ridiculed a lot, but it makes me have really strong endurance. If you get picked on a lot, just say, ""I have patience and self control, and I can make it through this.""" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: おしっこを我慢するのは体に悪い。
example_sentences.english: Holding your pee is bad for your health.

notes: "When a volcano erupts with fire it makes a really big eruption. You should probably start running." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 富士山が噴火したらどうなると思いますか。
example_sentences.english: What do you think would happen if Mt. Fuji erupted?

notes: "An exhibit of things in a row only happens at an exhibition. Everything will be neatly lined up on display for you there." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたは、パン屋のむき出しの陳列についてどう思いますか。
example_sentences.english: What did you think of the bakery’s exposed exhibition?

notes: "You need to swell and stretch if you want to see any kind of expansion of your company. Growth can't happen without a little wiggle room." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 宇宙は膨張しています。
example_sentences.english: The universe is expanding.

notes: "If you fall during a cave in you'll fall along with everything around you. And that sinking feeling in your stomach is because... I mean, well you ARE sinking into the ground. " This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: トヨタが世界一から陥落したのは何故だと思いますか。
example_sentences.english: Why do you think that Toyota fell from being the best in the world?

notes: "When you obtain something acting like that person had died, it's called confiscation or forfeiture. Maybe if they were alive, you think, they wouldn't have let me take it. Well they are still alive so it's theirs and you can't keep it forever." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生に携帯電話を没収されました。
example_sentences.english: I forfeited my cell phone to the teacher.

notes: "Hunting where you hunt is still hunting." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You didn't learn this reading for 狩 yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you:The most importing thing when hunting is not to forget your hunting shoes (しゅ). Without your special shoes all the animals will hear your stomping feet and run away before you can get them."

example_sentences.japanese: この鳥の狩猟は禁じられています。
example_sentences.english: Hunting of this bird is prohibited.

english: Immersing Oneself, Immersing Yourself, Immerse Oneself, Immerse Yourself
notes: "All the extra things in your head die when you immerse yourself in one thing. That way the one thing you're focusing on is the only thing your brain hears." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You've learned them both already, so you should be able to read this word.

example_sentences.japanese: 好きなことに没頭できるなんて、幸せですね。
example_sentences.english: If you can immerse yourself in things you like, you’ll be happy.

notes: "You bury things into people who look like they've died. It's called implantation. They're not really dead though. This is surgery and they'll wake up and go about their lives with whatever that thing was that you put in them." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You didn't learn this reading for 埋 yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you:Wait that's not a person you're embedding things into. It's a bunch of mice (まい). I guess that's okay. Just don't go putting the mice into people. That's... don't cross that line."

example_sentences.japanese: 整形手術で二重の埋没手術をしました。
example_sentences.english: I had double eyelids surgically implanted with plastic surgery.

notes: "An orphan is standing alone in the streets. Orphans don't have any parents and most of the time they're friendless too. It's really sad." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: ある事件があって、職場で孤立してしまったんです。
example_sentences.english: The incident is isolated to their place of work.

notes: "When something erupts and shoots a bunch of water or lava out it comes out in a huge jet and sprays everything." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 催涙スプレーの噴射方法を教えてください。
example_sentences.english: Please show me how to spray tear gas.

english: Killed In Action, Death In Battle, KIA
notes: "When a person dies in a war they're considered to have been killed in action. There are lots of memorials around the world for people who died this way." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: たくさんの戦没した兵士たちがここに埋められています。
example_sentences.english: Many soldiers who were killed in action are buried here.

notes: "A country in chains is under a national isolation policy. They're bound and they can't visit anywhere else." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本が鎖国していたのはいつですか。
example_sentences.english: When was Japan in national isolation?

english: One Piece Of Sushi, One Sushi, Consistency
notes: "One sushi counter is counting one piece of sushi. This can also mean consistency, which make sense if you think about piece of sushi—each one should be as consistent as the last!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 最高級のトロを一貫だけ注文しました。
example_sentences.english: I ordered one piece of the highest grade of fatty tuna.

notes: "Your auspicious departure from another world is your origin story. You originally came from another place, and you had to leave there gloriously before you could enter this world." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: デコポンは日本発祥のみかんの品種です。
example_sentences.english: Dekopon is a kind of mandarin orange that originated in Japan.

english: Persistence, Accomplishment, Carry Through, Perseverance, Realization, Realisation
notes: "You have to pierce this piece of information into your brain until it finally penetrates, which takes a lot of persistence. Do that and it will be quite the accomplishment!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 大変だったけど、みんなで決めた計画を貫徹することができた。
example_sentences.english: It was hard, but we were able to carry through with the plan we had decided on together.

example_sentences.japanese: 十年前の夢を貫徹できなかったことを残念に思います。
example_sentences.english: I regret that I couldn't realize the dream that I had ten years ago.

example_sentences.japanese: 初志貫徹の心構えで頑張ります。
example_sentences.english: I’ll do my best to prepare to accomplish my original goals.

notes: "Exhibit your feelings in a petition. If you feel something is unjust you have to say something. Form an appeal and fight back!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 請願・陳情は、住民の意見や要望を反映させるための制度です。
example_sentences.english: A petition is a system to reflect the opinions and requests of the residents.

notes: "When you pierce some fabric with a needle it needs to pass through to the other side to actually pierce and penetrate it. Make sure it goes all the way through if you want to sew properly." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: ブラジャーのワイヤーが弾丸の貫通を防いでくれた。
example_sentences.english: My wire bra protected me from the bullet penetrating.

notes: "Hunting in secrecy is only done through illegal poaching. If you weren't poaching protected animals you wouldn't have to do it secretly. " This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: どうすれば象の密猟を防止できると思いますか。
example_sentences.english: What do you think can be done to prevent the poaching of elephants?

notes: "When you are given superior treatment it's called preferential treatment. This is the best way to be treated." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 高齢者を優遇しすぎじゃないでしょうか。
example_sentences.english: We shouldn’t give too much preferential treatment to older people.

notes: "You ridicule everyone but yourself because you have so much pride. When you talk about yourself you only boast because there's nothing to ridicule. That's how great you think you are." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 自分の不倫を得意気に自慢するとか、ありえないんだけど。
example_sentences.english: It’s impossible for me to proudly boast about my own affair.

notes: "Embrace your duty to defend your country and prepare for its protection and defense. You love your country, so you'll do what you have to in order to support its defense." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 君はどうして彼を擁護するような発言をしたんだい。
example_sentences.english: Why did you speak up to protect him?

notes: "This is the adverb version of the kanji quick, so it means quickly." "This actually uses the kun'yomi reading, but it's almost the same as the one you learned when you learned the kanji. It's just さっ instead of さつ. If you can remember that さつ gets shortened here, you'll know how to read this!"

example_sentences.japanese: 茜は颯と涙を拭った。
example_sentences.english: Akane quickly wiped away the tears.

notes: "Compensation reparations are still compensation and reparations! That's convenient." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 被害総額の全額を賠償してください。
example_sentences.english: Please compensate the full amount for all of the damages.

notes: "A building or civilization that dies and then falls is in a state of ruin and collapse. Like the Mayans or the Western Roman Empire. They fell pretty hard." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 本当に日本は没落していると思いますか？
example_sentences.english: Do you think Japan is really collapsing?

notes: "If you sink and die it's because you were sinking in the ocean or a pool or something. It's important to notice you're going down so you don't die like that." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: タイタニック号の沈没を予言していた人がいるんです。
example_sentences.english: There’s a person who predicted the sinking of the Titanic.

notes: "When something erupts out an exit it usually had to fight pretty hard to get to that exit. That's why it ends up spewing and gushing all over the place." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: ブラックホールからガスが噴出しているって本当ですか？
example_sentences.english: Is it true that gas spews out of black holes?

notes: "Exhibit what you want to mention in a loud, clear statement. You have to say it if you want people to listen." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: まず、被告人が冒頭陳述を行います。
example_sentences.english: First, the defendant will perform their opening statement.

notes: "If you take along your leadership into the next year, then you're on top for a few years in a row. You've won successive championships." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. Just watch out for は becoming ぱ."

example_sentences.japanese: 今までに甲子園を三連覇した高校はありますか？

notes: "Leisure with more leisure added on? That's a really quiet and leisurely life you've got going on!" The reading is just the on'yomi readings (which you learned with the kanji) twice in a row.

example_sentences.japanese: 退職後は田舎で悠々と暮らしたいな。
example_sentences.english: After retirement I want to live a quiet life in the countryside.

notes: "If you resemble someone who's cruel, you, well, you resemble them. Maybe you're really mean too. I guess only you can know that. But you do look like that other guy..." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You didn't learn this reading for 似 yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you:Which cruel guy do you resemble? Jesus (じ), of course. I mean, you look just like him. Look in the mirror if you don't believe me. Look, there he is. Wait, what do you mean he isn't a cruel guy? I guess you're the cruel one then. Sucks to be you."

example_sentences.japanese: 三冊の本は、どれも内容が酷似している。
example_sentences.english: All the content in the three volumes of the book resemble each other.

english: Self Control, Self Discipline, Self Restraint
notes: "If you're solemn by yourself, you have a lot of self control. You don't need anyone to tell you to be that way, you have your own self discipline." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 役員の不祥事発覚を受け、本日は全社員が営業活動を自粛致します。
example_sentences.english: With the staff scandal coming to light, all employees are to restrain themselves from doing business activities today.

notes: "Evaluate in a cruel way so you can lay some severe criticism down on your competition! It's not the nicest thing to do, and it's not very constructive for them, but it will make you look better. " This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: いちいち酷評を気にしてたら、何も書けないよ。
example_sentences.english: I can’t write anything if I pay an undue amount of attention to each severe criticism.

notes: "A rapid run is called a sprint or a dash." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 少年は、駅の構内を全力疾走していた。
example_sentences.english: The boys sprinted around the station.

english: To Follow, To Stick With, To Stick To, To Go Through
notes: "This is a combination of the words 貫く meaning ""To Go Through"" and 通す meaning ""To Let Pass."" So when you're trying to go through an area and also let someone pass with you, you start to follow them. Not intentionally, but you're both trying to go through at the same time so you decide to stick with them." This is a combination of two words you already know, so you should already know this too!

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は最後まで自分の信念を貫き通しました。
example_sentences.english: He stuck to his beliefs until the end.

notes: "This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means deviate, so the verb version is to turn away or to avert." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading.  You haven't learned this reading yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you:You want to turn away from this movie because it's not worth watching. I mean, it isn't bad, but it isn't good. It's just so-so (そ). But that's not enough to keep your interest."

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は颯と目を逸らした。
example_sentences.english: She quickly averted her eyes.

notes: "Accumulate and accumulate make accumulation!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本政府が巨額の国債を累積していることについて、あなたはどのようにお考えですか。
example_sentences.english: How do you think the Japanese government accumulated such a great amount of national debt?

notes: "What do you wear to heal a really serious injury? An adhesion. Okay, so you don't actually wear these, but your body makes them for your insides to wear so you can heal. Nice job insides!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 手術後の癒着リスクについて、きちんと説明はなされましたか。
example_sentences.english: Were the risks of adhesion after surgery explained accurately to you?

notes: "All you can do is consider your grief and how it's ruining your life. That's called anxiety, and it can be a real problem. You end up being concerned about everything, but don't worry. There are ways to combat it. You'll be okay!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: ズバリ、社長が現在抱える憂慮とは何ですか。
example_sentences.english: What is the company president concerned about now?

notes: "Dedicate yourself to doing the best at school by having perfect attendance! That's how you can show you're really dedicated to learning." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 今年の夏休みは、老人ホームで奉仕活動をしました。
example_sentences.english: This summer vacation I volunteered at a senior citizen’s home.

notes: "Dedicate your life to what you believe in and you'll have really strong belief and faith in whatever that thing is. Just try to dedicate yourself to something nice." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は日本国民全員が神道を信奉すべきだと思います。
example_sentences.english: I think all Japanese citizens should believe in Shinto.

notes: "Circulation in a loop is still circulation. Or rotation." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 血液の循環には二種類の経路があります。
example_sentences.english: There are two types of paths for blood circulation.

notes: "Bow your head to conceal yourself better than you were concealing yourself before. If you want to go into hiding you need to know how to lay low!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 我々はマフィアの潜伏捜査をすることになった。
example_sentences.english: We conducted an undercover investigation of the mafia.

notes: "Grieve for a pathetic situation by offering your condolences. Showing regret is the best way to handle it." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 哀悼の意を表して、黙祷しました。
example_sentences.english: I expressed my condolences and prayed silently.

english: Correspond, Fulfilling, Applicable To, Qualifying As
notes: "If the above is correct then please sign the corresponding line to agree with it. And make sure you correspond in a timely manner." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: この商品も、キャンペーンの対象に該当しますか？
example_sentences.english: Does this merchandise correspond with the target of the campaign?

notes: "Measure how much you've accumulated and you'll have a cumulative total. That total includes all the things you've bought since the beginning of time. Probably." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: このサイトでは、人気アプリの累計ダウンロードランキングを毎日更新しています。
example_sentences.english: I update the total download rankings for popular apps everyday on this site.

notes: "If you dedicate your entire supply of food to the gods it's called an offering, and it takes real dedication to do something like that." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.english: Why did the Prime Minister receive criticism for making an offering at Yasukuni Shrine?

notes: "If you want to erase and extinguish every lamp and every picture of a lamp in the world, just erase them all. Simple as that." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は怪我で一軍登録を抹消されたんだ。
example_sentences.english: His army registration was deleted due to the injury.

notes: "A healing cure will be great for healing sick people. " This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 虫歯が自然治癒することはありません。
example_sentences.english: Cavities don’t just spontaneously heal.

english: Look On, Sit By And Watch, Spectate
notes: "Nearby there is a beautiful view. Look on as the sun sets and the sky changes color. You would give up anything to be able to spectate this kind of thing all the time." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はイジメをただ傍観していました。
example_sentences.english: I only looked on at the bullying.

english: Loss Of A Close Game, Regrettable Defeat
notes: "Your team was about to win the game but you decided to be frugal with your shots near the end and it resulted in failure, making it a loss of a close game. If you had just taken those shots your team probably would have won. What a regrettable defeat." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: わが校は、惜敗でベスト8入りを逃しました。
example_sentences.english: Our school missed getting into the top eight by losing a close game.

notes: "Only accept new people moving in nearby once you've finished properly monitoring them! Tapping into their phones will probably help too, but don't tell anyone I told you to do that." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 警察は、犯罪捜査のために、通信の傍受を行うことがあります。
example_sentences.english: The police may perform correspondence monitoring for the sake of the criminal investigation.

notes: "Follow people who grieve by mourning with them. You don't want to be the only one who doesn't seem sad." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You didn't learn this reading for 追 yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you:You're mourning the loss of your pet pig. You can't help but yell SOOEY (つい) to the sky, hoping she'll come back to life. It doesn't work so you stay in a state of mourning for the rest of your life. She was your best pig friend, after all."

example_sentences.japanese: みんなで奴の追悼コンサートを開かないか？
example_sentences.english: Why don’t we open his memorial concert with everyone?

english: Move For A Different Job, Move For A Job
notes: "Proceed to a new place to do your duty. That's just a fancy way to say you're about to move for a different job. This is usually a job at the same company you're already at, it's just a different position for you." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 今度、中国に赴任することになりました。
example_sentences.english: I’ve decided to relocate to China now.

english: Murder, Killing, Denial, Erasure, Obliteration, Ignoring
notes: "Erase the fact that you killed someone by shaking your head in denial about the murder. No one will know." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: あの男は、組織に歯向かったため、社会から抹殺されたんだよ。
example_sentences.english: That man rose against the system and was erased by society.

notes: "You only have time to do one thing at dawn once. Dawn is really short so you can do whatever it is for a moment, but that's it." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: この話は一旦なかったことにしてもらえませんか。
example_sentences.english: Will you forget that conversation for a moment?

notes: "Overgrown prosperity is still prosperity. Why, it's even thriving. Nice!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 商売が繁昌するように、神社でお祈りをしてきました。
example_sentences.english: I went to pray at a Shinto shrine in order for the company to prosper.

notes: "To tranquilize souls you have to a have a mass repose of souls. Then their souls will move on to the next life and stop hanging around here, haunting umbrellas." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 星祭りは、平和を祈り、戦死者を鎮魂する儀式です。
example_sentences.english: Tanabata is a ritual to pray for peace and give repose to people killed in the war.

notes: "Your pudding congealed and is all hard. How on earth did it solidify like this? It shouldn't freeze unless you put it in the freezer. Unless, did you? Oh... " This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 煮詰めたジャムは、冷めてくると粘性が強まり、ゼリー状に凝固します。
example_sentences.english: When the jam I boiled cools it will become viscous and solidify into jelly.

notes: "Freeze and look at me. Your stare is giving me the creeps! You can move now. Hey. You can move now. Stop I said!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: タイプの女性がいたので、思わず凝視してしまいました。
example_sentences.english: She was my type of woman so I stared unintentionally.

notes: "Accumulate enough of a good reputation at your company in advance and you'll be able to have successive promotions. You'll be boss in no time! " This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は若くして部長に累進した。
example_sentences.english: He was promoted to section head at a very young age.

notes: "Tranquilize pressure with medication that helps with its suppression. Then you won't have to feel it anymore." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 警察が三日がかりでデモ隊を鎮圧しました。
example_sentences.english: The police suppressed the demonstrators by the third day.

notes: "Bow as you descend into enemy territory. This is how you have to surrender if you want to live. Keep your head nice and low and descend into their ranks." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 絶対にあいつらを降伏させてみせる。
example_sentences.english: I let them surrender unconditionally.

english: To Be Absorbed In, To Grow Stiff, To Be Devoted To
notes: "This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means congeal or freeze, so the verb version is to grow stiff. But it's also used to mean what happens when your emotions or interests freeze on one thing. You start to be absorbed in whatever that thing is. Try to remember both meanings." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: What have all your friends started to be absorbed in? Their 子s (こ). They all keep having kids and now that's all they seem to care about. Damn kids."

example_sentences.japanese: 妻の料理の盛り付けは、いつも凝っています。
example_sentences.english: I’m always absorbed in the arrangement of my wife’s food.

english: To Be Frugal, To Be Sparing
notes: "This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means frugal, so the verb version is to be frugal or to be sparing." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: You should try to be frugal when you go to the ocean (おし). There are lots of things to buy, like delicious food, sun hats, and tofugu dolls, but you really shouldn't spend all your money there. Try to plan on spending less when you head to the ocean next time, okay?"

example_sentences.japanese: お前がちょっとした手間を惜しんだために、全ての計画がおじゃんになったんだぞ！
example_sentences.english: You wouldn’t spare even a little time so all your plans fell through!

english: To Cover, To Hide, To Lay Upside Down, To Turn Over
notes: "This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means bow or lay, so the verb version is what when you try to cover or to hide something. You're doing the action to something, you're not the one hiding." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: Who's that you're trying to cover up? It's your fool (ふ) brother. He keeps doing embarrassing things and trying to get you in trouble. So you're trying to hide him with your jacket. Well we see him, we know he's a fool, so you can stop now."

example_sentences.japanese: どうして弟が犯罪者であることを伏せていたんだ。
example_sentences.english: Why would I cover up my younger brother being a criminal?

english: Undulation, Ups And Downs, Highs And Lows
notes: "Wake up, now lay down, now wake up again, okay now lay again. What you're doing is called undulation. If your emotions do it it's called ups and downs. Everyone goes through stuff like this sometimes." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 生理前はどうしても感情の起伏が激しくなってしまう。
example_sentences.english: Before my period I always get violent emotional ups and downs.

notes: "Say furthermore again and you'll be saying it all the more." The readings for this word are both kun'yomi readings. You've learned both of these readings by now so you should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたのことが尚更嫌いになりました。
example_sentences.english: I came to dislike you all the more.

notes: "Okay these words are really vague so this is kinda bad. I'm sorry. The readings for this word are both kun'yomi readings. You've learned both of these readings by now so you should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は、美しく、尚且つ頭も良いが、性格は悪い。
example_sentences.english: She’s beautiful, smart, and yet she has a terrible personality.

notes: "Hands beating together is actually applause. Though... you might be doing it wrong if you're actually beating them together." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 舞台が終わった後、拍手が鳴り止まなかった。
example_sentences.english: After the scene ended, the applause did not stop roaring.

notes: "A confused riot causes even more confusion. Soon there will be so many distractions happening, what with cars tipping over and fires starting, that no one will know which way is up!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 薬で意識が錯乱しているようでした。
example_sentences.english: Their consciousness seemed to be confused by the medicine.

notes: "You're full of delight. It's still delight though." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: ご満悦のようですね。
example_sentences.english: They seem to be delighted.

example_sentences.english: Well then, is there an agency the government has direct control over here too?

notes: "Some things happen outside of reason. They happen in addition to it. That's called divine providence. You can't explain it, but something outside of reason definitely influenced the things around you." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 誰も自然の摂理には逆らえないよ。
example_sentences.english: No one can defy the laws of nature.

notes: "If you're exhausted by all the evil things in your life you might die of exhaustion!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 人口が増えない限り、地方経済の疲弊が回復することはないでしょう。
example_sentences.english: It seems that the local economy will not recover from impoverishment unless the population increases.

notes: "Take children from their homes and squeeze all their talent out until they have nothing left. That's called exploitation, and lots of companies make money off of it. example_sentences.english: This agent is famous for considerably exploiting his guarantees.

notes: "If you still need more time to finish a project and you tell whoever is in charge beforehand you'll be able to get an extension. Then you'll be able to finish it." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.english: I suppose I’ll give you a three day extension.

example_sentences.english: Japan made a huge change from the postwar food shortage to a period of gluttony.

notes: "You thought you memorized what this picture looked like, but suddenly everything looks confused and different. That's because it's an illusion." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.english: I calculated my calorie intake for one day.

example_sentences.english: Anyway, let’s get in contact with the police station with jurisdiction first.

example_sentences.japanese: 牧場で搾乳体験をしてきました。
example_sentences.english: I personally experienced milking at the farm.

notes: "Towns destitute and scarce of food will end up in poverty and destitution." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.english: He lived in poverty and committed theft as a last resort.
