example_sentences.japanese: 子犬と戯れている少女の写真を撮りました。
example_sentences.english: I took a picture of the puppy and the girl playing with it.

notes: "Remember how you learned that 一遍 means ""once?"" Well if you add に and make it an adverb, it becomes at once." "This has the same reading you learned with 一遍 so you should be able to remember this too!"

example_sentences.japanese: 一遍にいろんなことを言われても、分からないわ。
example_sentences.english: If you say a bunch of things at once I won’t understand.

notes: "If you want to create a cast you need to learn casting first. Then you can make lots of neat art, crafts, and counterfeit money. Wait, no, don't do that last one. " This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You've learned both of them, so you should already know this word!

example_sentences.japanese: ここで、プラチナ・コインの鋳造をします。
example_sentences.english: Platinum coins are cast here.

notes: "Change and transition mean change and transition! Nifty." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 1996年から2013年までのトップ日本語学習サイト20の変遷を見てみましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let’s look at the changes in the top 20 Japanese language learning sites between 1996 and 2013.

notes: "You congratulate someone and celebrate by saying congratulations and having a celebration!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 慶祝の意を表して、乾杯！
example_sentences.english: To show our congratulations, a toast!

notes: "Usually if you're going to the left in Japanese, it's not a good thing. So if you transition to the left it's seen as a demotion. Going to the right is way better." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 田舎の支店に左遷されました。
example_sentences.english: I was demoted to a branch store in the country.

notes: "Your guts feel like they're falling when you experience a lot of discouragement. You know that sinking feeling you get in the pit of your stomach? That's your guts falling!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 息子は、受験に失敗して落胆しているんだ。
example_sentences.english: My son failed an exam and is discouraged.

english: For The Time Being, First Of All, At Once, Immediately
notes: "If you only take daring and you don't have any yourself, you only have it for the time being. It will go away if you can't make it yourself." This word uses the kun'yomi readings for the kanji. You learned both of these already, so you should be able to read this with no problems!

example_sentences.japanese: 取り敢えず枝豆とビールをください。
example_sentences.english: Edamame and beer for now please.

notes: "If a parent is friendly enough you can form a friendship with them, not just a kid/parent bond." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 親睦を深めるためのパーティーを準備しています。
example_sentences.english: Our friendship is deepening as we prepare for the party.

notes: "You despise this one guy so much that you want to humiliate him so you insult him in public. That wasn't very nice, but it did seem to embarrass him. I guess you won." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: こんな侮辱を受けて、黙っていろというのか。
example_sentences.english: I received the insults and remained silent.

notes: "Marry and marriage still make marriage. Congratulations! Wooh! Yay! " This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 婚姻届を役所に提出しました。
example_sentences.english: I submitted the marriage registration at the public office.

english: Move The Capital, Transfer The Capital, Relocation Of The Capital
notes: "If you want to transition the capital to a new, better place, you need to move the capital. This used to happen a lot way back in Japanese history. It's actually pretty interesting so you might want to read up on it!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 来年は、遷都1500年記念のイベントが開催されます。
example_sentences.english: Next year an event is being held for the 1500 year anniversary of the relocation of the capital.

notes: "If you select to talk to nothing but sand for a really long time, you're neglecting to contact anyone else. Your relatives miss you! Stop talking to sand and call them!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: ご無沙汰しております。
example_sentences.english: I haven’t seen you in so long.

english: Plot, Ulterior Motive, Secret Intention, Hidden Purpose
notes: "The soul and guts of a story lie in the plot! " This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: あわよくばおこぼれに預かりたいという魂胆が見え見えだよ。
example_sentences.english: You are so transparent. I can tell that you’re plotting to get a share of the profits if you get the chance.

notes: "A person who wanders because their lord was killed, is known as a ronin, or a masterless samurai. Now they're just like the rest of us, but they can't stop wandering because they have nowhere they belong.In modern times, ronin refers to those who failed their university entrance exams, waiting until for another chance to take the test again." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 受験に失敗し、浪人生活に突入しました。
example_sentences.english: I failed the exam and entered the life of a failed student.

example_sentences.japanese: お前みたいな浪人の要求には応じられないな。
example_sentences.english: We are unable to comply with the request of a masterless samurai like you.

notes: "Despise someone and your scorn for them just becomes even stronger scorn." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 叔母の言葉は、いつも軽い侮蔑を帯びている。
example_sentences.english: My aunts speech always has light traces of contempt.

notes: "Lightweight scorn, no matter how light, is still scorn. Those feelings are pretty strong no matter what." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You haven't learned this reading for 軽 yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you:You have more scorn and disdain for the KKK (けい) than any other group in the whole world. And I'm not going to argue with you, they're pretty hatable."

example_sentences.japanese: 私、あの人のこと軽蔑しているの。
example_sentences.english: I despise them.

notes: "If you tasted the air at a recital the flavor would taste like scrutiny. That's really what everyone is doing when they watch. They don't really want to hear you, they just want to judge you." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 結婚相手はよく吟味してから決めたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to decide on a spouse after a lot of careful investigation.

notes: "Spinning exploits sheep, but you keep spinning anyway because you're cold and you need the sweater you're making." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 牽切紡績とは、化学繊維特有の紡績方法で、綿からの紡績ではありません。
example_sentences.english: Kensetsu bouseki is a spinning method particular to synthetic fibers not spun from cotton.

notes: "Resident soldiers live in barracks when they've been stationed in another country. They have to serve their occupancy for a certain amount of time before they get to go back home." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: あそこには米軍が駐屯しているんだよ。
example_sentences.english: US armed forces are stationed over there.

notes: "Prohibition of something with a punishment so serious that you'll end up in mourning after is a taboo. " This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: よく、禁忌を犯すと手足をもがれると言われますが、これは本当でしょうか。
example_sentences.english: It’s often said that your hands and feet are plucked off when you commit a taboo, is that true?

english: To Become Hollow, To Be Dented, To Sink, To Collapse
notes: "This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means hollow, so the verb version is to become hollow and to sink" "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: You feel like you've started to become hollow when you have a head cold (へこ). You may be all stuffed up, but it's making you so sad that you feel hollow somehow."

example_sentences.japanese: 失恋で凹んでいます。
example_sentences.english: I’m sinking in unrequited love.

example_sentences.japanese: 早速新車を凹ませてしまって、凹んでいます。
example_sentences.english: I'm super sad because I made a dent on my new car already.

english: To Despise, To Disdain, To Make Light Of
notes: "This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means despise, so the verb version is to despise." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: Think of all the things you start to despise and to disdain. Now come up with some anecdotes (あなど) for each one of those things. Be sure to think in your head, ""I'm coming up with anecdotes for things I disdain, why am I coming up with anecdotes?"""

example_sentences.japanese: 子供だからといって侮らない方がいい。
example_sentences.english: You shouldn’t make light of it just because it’s a child.

notes: "This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means scorn, so the verb version is to scorn and to despise." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: You start to scorn your boss because she's been wearing that same sage suit (さげす) for a month now. She knows you want to wear a sage suit too but you can't wear the same color as her! It's really making you start to despise her. Uhg!"

example_sentences.japanese: あの男は、無意識に人のことを蔑んでいるのよ。
example_sentences.english: That man unconsciously looks down on people.

notes: "This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means spinning, so the verb version is to spin and to make yarn." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: Before you start to spin you have to let out two moos (つむ) as tribute to the cows that gave you their fur to make yarn out of. Go on, two moos, right now. Hey, out loud, not in your head!"

example_sentences.japanese: 昔はこうやって糸を紡いでいたんですよ。
example_sentences.english: A long time ago thread was spun in this way.

notes: "Remember how you learned that 凹凸 means ""uneven?"" Well spin something uneven around and it's still uneven! Just kinda backwards, just like this word!" "However, just because the meaning stays the same when you flip it, doesn't mean the reading does. Doing that actually made the reading change from on'yomi to kun'yomi readings! You haven't learned either of these yet so here's a mnemonic to help you:When you have the convex parts first and the concave parts second in something uneven is ends up looking like a deco box (でこぼこ). An art deco box that is. They have lots of stuff stick out of them on the outside, but you can open them up and put stuff on the inside."

example_sentences.japanese: 床がちょっと凸凹しているのが気になるね。
example_sentences.english: I’m worried that the floor is a little uneven.

notes: "Wander from stream to stream and you'll get really used to wandering. You'll love it so much that you'll convert to nomadism. The open sky is your home!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 全てのジプシーが貧しい流浪の民というわけではない。
example_sentences.english: That doesn’t mean all Gypsies are poor, nomadic people.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it probably uses the kun'yomi reading. You did not learn this reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you: If you're very tired and very giggly, you'll try to say your friend's name but start laughing right away so it ends up sounds like,  ""Hannah ha ha ha (はなは)."""

example_sentences.japanese: そのようなことが事実だとすれば、甚だ遺憾である。
example_sentences.english: If that sort of thing is true, I’m very sorry.

notes: "Release your worldly ties and wander the word. You'll get used to wandering and you'll spend the rest of your days roaming the world until you die. It's quite the life! But you can only do it if you let go of everything else." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 当時は、逃げるように各地を転々と放浪していました。
example_sentences.english: In those days I had to wander from place to place in order to escape.

notes: "If you wander around doing nothing at your own expense it will be a huge waste of money. It's not like you were doing or buying anything important, you were just wandering around, after all. " This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 妻の浪費癖がなかなか治らないんです。
example_sentences.english: My wife’s wasteful habits were not easily cured.

notes: "Worship in the morning, worship in the night, worship all day! Worship that WaniKani poster. Do it." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: どうして偶像崇拝を禁止するのですか。
example_sentences.english: Why do they prohibit idol worship?

notes: "Die in the past and it was death that you suffered from!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 社長の逝去は本当に大きなショックです。
example_sentences.english: The company president’s death was a really big shock.

notes: "Reckless concepts are just delusions. You shouldn't dwell on them, they probably aren't going to happen." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: いつも大金持ちになる妄想ばかりしています。
example_sentences.english: I’m always just fantasizing about becoming a very rich person.

notes: "Diarrhea that goes below you is still diarrhea, unfortunately. I hope it's going down into a toilet..." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 朝から下痢が止まりません。
example_sentences.english: The diarrhea hasn’t stopped since morning.

english: "Die At One's Post, Die On Duty, Die At Your Post"
notes: "If you want to become a martyr during your employment you need to die at your post. I don't know why you'd WANT to do that though." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: その刑事は、銃弾を浴びて殉職しました。
example_sentences.english: The detective took a bullet and died at his post.

notes: "You quit your job but with a pretty good excuse to back it up, so you get a dismissal instead of just quitting outright. If you're in the army and you do this it's called a discharge." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: あの大臣は罷免されたよ。
example_sentences.english: That cabinet minister was dismissed.

notes: "Hide and hide make hide! Lots of hiding going on around here. I think... I can't find anyone so I can only assume." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は犯人を隠匿していたんだよ。
example_sentences.english: She hid the criminal.

notes: "The final bullet of censure is impeachment. You've already been publicly humiliated and now you're being impeached because of it. Yikes." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 大統領の弾劾を求める大規模な反政府デモが開かれました。
example_sentences.english: A large-scale anti-government demonstration was held for the impeachment of the President.

notes: "Part of you is starting to secrete some kind of secretion. It's kinda gross, so maybe you should go to the doctor to check if it's normal." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 胃液は1日1～2Lも分泌されています。
example_sentences.english: Around 1-2 liters of gastric juices are secreted each day.

notes: "A bad kind of playing is when you tease or prank someone. It's mean and you shouldn't do it!" "The reading for this word is an exception. Here's a mnemonic to help you remember it:If you tease someone with a prank that makes them eat zoo rats (いたずら), you're a jerk. That's less of a prank and more like abuse. Cut it out."

example_sentences.japanese: 今子供達の間で流行っている悪戯ですよ。
example_sentences.english: Pranks are popular among children right now.

notes: "I promise this will be a really thrifty place because it's a thrift store! They wouldn't lie about that!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: いくらマイホームを買いたいからって、度を過ぎた倹約を強いるのはどうかと思います。
example_sentences.english: I don’t think it’s a good idea to force a higher amount of frugality on yourself just because you want to buy your own home.

english: To Adore, To Miss, To Yearn For
notes: "This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means yearn for, so the verb version is to yearn for. But that sounds kinda old fashioned, so you can just use to adore too." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: You realize you're starting to yearn for someone way more than you used to. ""Sh*t (した)... "" you say to yourself. This wasn't supposed to happen. Anytime you start to adore someone like that you always know you're getting into a bunch of sh*t you don't want to deal with. Damn these emotions!"

example_sentences.japanese: 私は彼のことを兄のように慕っていました。
example_sentences.english: I adored him like an older brother.

english: To Become Muddy, To Become Impure, To Become Cloudy
notes: "You already know that 濁す means ""to make muddy,"" but this is when you're the one getting muddy. It means to become muddy." "This has the same reading as 濁す. If you can remember that one, you should be able to remember this one."

example_sentences.japanese: 煙草の煙で部屋の空気が濁っています。
example_sentences.english: The air in the room is getting cloudy with tobacco smoke.

notes: "Torture may be a problem but that doesn't stop people from using torture to get their way." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 俺の姉は、マフィアから残虐な拷問の受けたんだ。
example_sentences.english: My older sister was brutally tortured by the mafia.

notes: "If you can't stop thinking about how much you yearn for someone, that yearning can drive you crazy. Try to keep it in check, and enjoy how you can hold such deep affection for someone." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 異国の地で、母への思慕を重ねています。
example_sentences.english: Being in a foreign country, I constantly yearn for my mother.
